items.html:
The BFCM season is around the corner. Most eCommerce brands have set up their special campaigns. But while most brands focus on marketing their individual products, they ignore subscriptions all together.

What if you could promote your Shopify subscriptions by setting up BFCM subscription marketing strategies?

Curious? We share 12 strategies that you can easily implement in your Shopify store this BFCM season.

Let’s get started!

TL; DR

  • BFCM subscription marketing strategies can help with recurring revenue and go beyond simple discounts
  • Risk-free trials: Offer 1-month trial subscriptions at discounted rates to reduce commitment fears and increase sign-ups
  • Mini subscription series: Create a 12-day experience with daily perks to build customer habits and drive conversions
  • Founders Club: Launch an exclusive tier for early BFCM subscribers with lifetime perks like early access and priority support
  • Gift subscriptions: Enable short-term gifting options (2-3 months) with personalized digital cards
  • Bundle with experiences: Add exclusive experiences like masterclasses to subscription boxes for enhanced value
  • Secret subscriber sales: Run exclusive BFCM deals only accessible to subscribers to convert one-time buyers
  • “Set and forget” positioning: Market subscriptions as stress-free holiday gifts for busy shoppers
  • BFCM vault: Create limited-edition products available only in subscription boxes to drive FOMO
  • Mix & match options: Let customers build personalized subscriptions to increase control and reduce risk concerns
  • “Freeze anytime” guarantee: Promote flexible pause/cancel options to reduce commitment anxiety during busy shopping periods
  • Mystery bonuses: Add surprise gifts to BFCM subscription orders and encourage unboxing content
  • Post-holiday renewal campaign: Offer incentives for long-term commitments tied to New Year’s resolutions to combat post-BFCM lulls
  • Focus on subscriptions during BFCM to build recurring revenue beyond one-time holiday sales, using tools like Appstle Subscriptions App for implementation

12 BFCM subscription marketing strategies you can implement before this year ends

Think beyond the tried and tested BFCM strategies, such as discounts and incentives; market your Shopify subscription plans, increase sign-ups, lifetime value, and engagement with these strategies.

1. “Try before you commit” holiday subscription

Customers want the least amount of risks when making purchases from sales. When it comes to subscriptions, they do not want to get locked into long-term commitments. This is one fear that keeps them away from signing up even though they may love your products. That’s why offering a risk-free trial of your subscriptions can drive customers to sign up. Here’s what you can do:

  • Allow customers to start with a 1-month trial plan during the BFCM period
  • Offer this subscription plan at a discounted rate to increase sign-ups
  • Set up an automated system that signs up customers after the trial period ends
  • Send a reminder to customers when the trial period is going to end

Pro tip: Install Appstle Subscriptions App and use its flexible billing and plan-switching features for this strategy

2. Offer a mini subscription series

Another BFCM subscription marketing strategy is to offer a 12-day experience of your subscription. Instead of a limited-time subscription, in a mini series format, customers can be offered a small perk, tips to use products, discounts, etc.

These perks create urgency and FOMO and the limited timeframe makes customers feel like it is a BFCM season special offer. The benefit of this strategy? The daily touchpoints for 12 days can turn into customer habits, and eventually, they might want to sign up.

3. BFCM founders club for early subscribers

Set up a subscription plan that has an exclusive tier that makes early subscribers feel special. Call it “Founders Club”. Offer a limited edition subscription badge to all customers who sign up during the BFCM time.

Offer lifetime perks to these subscribers, for instance, first access to new collections, exclusive content, special discounts, or priority customer support. When you provide customers a sense of belonging and recognition, they feel more obliged to sign up and stay for long.

4. Gift subscriptions with a twist

Enable customers to give your subscription to their loved ones. Make this offer even more appealing by allowing them to gift the subscription for just a few months, for example, three months or two months.

Implement this BFCM subscription marketing strategy by creating special promotion campaigns, creating digital cards that allow people to add personalized messages, etc.

Pro tip: Market this subscription gifting plan as a ‘gift that keeps on giving’, making it more appealing.

5. Bundle subscriptions with exclusive experiences

Enhance subscriptions by combining them with exclusive experiences. While your subscription boxes and deliveries will have products, every now and then, you could add in an experience with it.

For example, a wellness box might come with access to one-on-one wellness masterclass with an expert. Experiences add value, create emotional connections, justify premium pricing, and reduce price sensitivity in shoppers.

6. Run a secret sale for subscribers only

Create a BFCM secret sale that is accessible only to subscribers. Promote this sale via special campaigns before the BFCM season. This will encourage and entice customers to sign up. Create FOMO by sending targeted marketing messages, such as, “The best deals of the year only in the secret sale for subscribers.”

This BFCM subscription marketing strategy can help convert customers and one-time buyers into subscribers. Customers that like your products will definitely not want to miss this exclusive opportunity.

Pro tip: Make the deals worth it for people to subscribe and share a few of these deals in your marketing messaging.

7. Position subscriptions as ‘set and forget’ gifts

This strategy can be specifically targeted at stressed holiday shoppers. When you market your subscription plan as a stress-free gifting solution, it can lead to conversion. People are always short of time during the busy holiday season, and this strategy can drive conversions. Create marketing campaigns with messaging that highlights thoughtful gifting and long-term benefits to the receivers of the gift.

8. Create a BFCM subscription vault

Create a special inventory of limited-edition products for the BFCM season which are available only in subscription boxes. Do not provide access to regular customers to purchase these products individually.

By positioning it as an insider access, not available to regular customers, or for subscription vault members only, you can create urgency to sign up, FOMO, and scarcity. These aspects lead to more subscription conversions.

9. Introduce a ‘mix & match’ build-your-own subscription

When customers have flexibility, control, and freedom in subscriptions, their feelings of risk of being stuck reduce, and sign-ups increase. Allow customers to create their own personalized subscriptions by mixing and matching products.

For example, allow them to choose: 1 of product A, 3 of product B, and skip product C all together. You can also add a holiday season touch by creating themes. This sort of personalization not only increases average order value (AOV), but also makes subscribers feel more invested in building their own unique subscription boxes.

Pro tip: Appstle Subscriptions and Appstle Bundles can help implement this strategy.

10. Promote a “freeze anytime” subscription structure

Another BFCM subscription marketing strategy is to implement a “freeze anytime” subscription guarantee. BFCM is a busy time and customers mostly shop in a rush. In this frenzy, they may not want to commit to something like subscriptions.

However, if you promote subscriptions that they can stop or freeze anytime, you can increase the potential of subscription sign-ups. For instance, promote messages, such as, pause anytime, cancel anytime, etc.

11. Add mystery bonuses for holiday subscribers

Create BFCM special promotions for subscriptions. For instance, include surprise bonuses in all BFCM subscription orders. You can add exclusive samples, discount coupons, reward points, limited-edition merchandise, etc.

Also run unboxing campaigns for user-generated content to entice more customers to sign up. BFCM is a time when consumers end up shopping a lot, and these marketing tactics can easily entice them to sign up for your Shopify subscriptions.

12. Launch a post-holiday ‘renew and reward’ campaign

Another holiday subscription campaign idea is renew and reward. Once the BFCM sale period ends, there is usually a dull time. But there’s one BFCM subscription marketing strategy that can help reverse this lull. Offer special bonuses to subscribers who commit for longer-term subscriptions.

For example, offer incentives if customers sign-up for one year or two years. You can market this around New Year’s resolutions, saying how the same subscription can give them more this new year.

Why sell subscriptions during the BFCM sale?

Here’s how adding subscriptions to your BFCM strategy can help your brand stand out as well as ensure future success.

1. Increase customer lifetime value (CLTV)

Many shoppers discover new brands during the BFCM sale. Imagine your Shopify store attracts many such new, first-time buyers. However, there’s a high chance they may never return to your store. And that’s where lies the power of subscriptions to bring them back.

Offering an option of subscription while they checkout from the BFCM sale can provide an opportunity to convert one-time shoppers into long-term subscribers. In this process, you can ensure an increase in CLTV.

2. Customers tend to buy more during BFCM

Data reveals that shoppers have a high spending appetite during BFCM, with the average order value increasing from $120 during non-BFCM period to $159 during BFCM. During the sale time, shoppers are in a buying mindset – comparing deals, filling carts, and more open to trying something new.

For Shopify stores, this makes it the easiest time to introduce a subscription offer. A shopper who might hesitate to subscribe otherwise is far more likely to say yes along with a limited-time BFCM deal.

3. Get more value from your promotion spend

The more you advertise and promote the BFCM sale, the more sales and revenue you can expect. One way to recover the BFCM ad and promotional marketing spends is to include a subscription offer with the BFCM sale price.

Think about it, if customers only buy once, a large part of your spend may never be recovered. Subscriptions fix this by spreading the return over many orders. Customers acquired at a high cost during BFCM keep generating revenue, which also lowers the customer acquisition cost over time.

4. To build predictable, recurring revenue

While BFCM is a peak sales period for brands, the following months are some of the slowest sales periods. This is when subscriptions can help generate steady and recurring revenue. Recurring revenue from subscriptions helps you plan your inventory, cash flow, and other budgets. Therefore, selling subscriptions during BFCM is beneficial to your Shopify business.

5. To turn one-time buyers into loyal customers

Research shows that subscription-based models increase purchases, engagement, and retention. When first-time shoppers buy your products from the BFCM sale, they already have found your product worthy of a purchase. This is a good time to encourage them to sign up for subscriptions as they have a high perceived value of your product. Regular deliveries also have a psychological effect. They keep your brand in the customers’ radar and thus increase loyalty.

How to implement subscriptions into your BFCM strategy: step by step

BFCM is just around the corner. Follow these simple steps to incorporate subscription within your BFCM strategy.

Step 1: Install Appstle Subscriptions App in your Shopify store

Your first step is to install a subscriptions app compatible with Shopify and Shopify Plus. Appstle Subscriptions App is easy to set up. The app works with Shopify checkout, so you can allow customers to buy one-time products and subscriptions in the same order. And if you’re looking to migrate from another app to Appstle, the merchant support team will help you with a smooth transition at every step.

Tip: Install and test the app a few weeks before the BFCM sale. This will ensure you have time to fix any glitches and can be ready for the sale time traffic.

Step 2: Choose a subscription type

Next, you must choose a subscription type that suits your products and customer preference. Here are some types of subscription plans:

  • Replenishment: Customers get regularly used products (skincare, food, supplements, pet supplies) delivered automatically, often with a “subscribe and save” discount.
  • Curation: Customers receive a surprise or curated box of products at set intervals. This works well for gifting and for introducing customers to new products.
  • Bargain or access: Customers pay a fee or sign up for members-only deals and early access to new products.
  • Premium membership: Customers get exclusive perks such as free shipping, priority support, or special access to products.

Tip: If you’re new to subscriptions, start with one or two of your best-selling products, ones that customers already buy repeatedly. You can expand to more products after BFCM, once you see how customers respond.

Step 3: Set your pricing and BFCM subscription offers

During BFCM, shoppers are looking for the best deals. Hence, give them a clear reason to subscribe instead of buying once. Here’s how to price your subscription offers:

  • Choose offers you can afford. Only discount products that still leave you a healthy profit after shipping, packaging, and the discount itself.
  • Offer a BFCM-exclusive discount on the first order or the first few orders, such as a percentage off or free shipping for subscribers.
  • Add perks beyond the discount, such as a free gift, early access to new products, or bonus reward points.
  • Create tiered or bundled plans (for example, a bigger discount for a larger quantity or a longer commitment) to increase your average order value.

Pro tip: Keep the offer simple and easy to understand. Shoppers don’t have time during BFCM.

Ensure you can adjust pricing. Track what works during BFCM and refine the offer for the next sale

Step 4: Give customers flexibility and an easy way to manage subscriptions

Many shoppers avoid subscriptions because they fear being locked in. The best way to ease that fear is to make managing a subscription simple. Here’s what you can do:

  • With Appstle, customers can pause, skip, edit, or cancel their subscriptions on their own. They can also swap products, change quantities, update the delivery date, or update their payment details without contacting your team.
  • Make sure this flexibility aspect is visible. Mention it in your product pages, emails, and banners.
  • Automated notifications for orders, deliveries, and payments, so subscribers stay informed.
  • Set up failed payment alerts, so you don’t lose revenue to expired cards.
  • Structure a cancellation flow that asks why customers are leaving and offers alternatives such as pausing or skipping instead.

Step 5: Promote your subscriptions and keep subscribers engaged

Promote your BFCM subscription offer everywhere your BFCM audience will see it. Here are some ways to promote it:

  • Product pages: Make the subscription option stand out, with the savings clearly displayed.
  • Email and SMS: Send early-access messages to your existing customers and subscribers.
  • Homepage banners and popups: Highlight your BFCM subscription deal.
  • Social media and ads: Show what subscribers get, whether that’s a discount, a gift, or exclusive access.

Tip: After the sale, keep new subscribers engaged. Send exclusive deals, early access to new products, and samples in their orders. Use cross-sell and upsell offers related to what they already buy, and run time-limited offers for subscribers around their renewal dates.

Wrapping up: Take the first steps to implement subscriptions in your BFCM strategy

BFCM is around the corner. The earlier you start, the better you can plan and implement subscriptions. However, when planning, ensure you take a long-term approach. Your subscription strategy should stay relevant even after the BFCM sale. Moreover, you should be able to adapt and enhance the subscriptions as and when required.

items.html:
Ensuring subscription success requires many aspects to function smoothly.

To acquire, retain, and reactivate old customers in today’s fast-paced eCommerce environment, brands need to be equipped with AI tools.

Traditional automation merely follows predefined rules. But AI goes a few levels deeper – interpreting customer data, assessing customer behavior, making decisions, and taking actions that can drive subscriptions across the lifecycle.

For example, for subscriptions, AI agents can identify when a subscriber is losing interest, create real-time offers to keep them engaged, and drive subscription renewals, too.

In this blog, you will learn why AI agents for eCommerce subscriptions are essential, and how your brand can use AI agents to boost sales and retention.

Let’s get started!

What can AI agents actually do for subscription businesses?

AI agents do more than AI-powered recommendations. Agents go a level deeper to understand customers and their behavior. Here are some processes performed by AI agents.

1. Monitor customer and subscription behavior

AI agents follow defined goals, break them down into sequences of steps, and execute actions. For instance, AI agents have the capability to track customer and subscriber behavior, purchase patterns, and draw insights from this data.

2. Identify opportunities or risks

AI agents have the ability to remember contexts, make decisions, and execute actions, all based on how they are trained and the goal they are given. For example, if a subscriber shows signs of churn, AI agents trigger incentives to keep them from cancellation.

3. Decide what action should be taken

There are multiple ways a failed payment can be recovered. AI agents for eCommerce subscriptions have the ability to decide which action can be taken to drive a desired result. For instance, the subscriber can be sent prompts in real-time with alternative payment methods or can be sent a message telling them they could try again at another time.

4. Learn from outcomes and improve future decisions

AI agents have the ability to learn from outcomes. For instance, it can loop feedback into its processes and adapt future decisions. For example, if a customer repeatedly buys the same product at regular intervals, AI can recommend them to sign up for a subscription plan.

5. Work continuously

Rather than waiting for a marketer or a human to trigger a campaign, AI agents can work continuously on their own to perform tasks they are assigned. For instance, if the AI agent notices a change in subscribers’ consumption patterns, it recommends adjustment in cadence to ensure the subscribers’ preference is met.

8 ways AI agents can increase subscription sales and retention

AI agents and agentic commerce adoption has grown in 2026. 40% of large enterprises are scaling the use of AI agents. Here are 8 ways in which AI agents can increase subscription conversion and retention.

1. Identify shoppers who are most likely to subscribe

Research reveals that specific AI uses have led to 12.3% conversion compared to 3.1% without AI. Instead of targeting all shoppers to drive subscription conversion, brands can use AI to identify the ones most likely to sign up. This saves resources from getting wasted on people who might not subscribe.

So, how does AI help identify potential subscribers? Here are some things AI tracks:

  • Analyzes browsing and purchase behavior to understand interest and product needs
  • Notices shoppers who purchase products repeatedly and identifies patterns
  • Tracks purchase patterns to find products and matches them with natural replenishment cycles
  • Identifies customers who repeatedly purchase the same product
  • Identifies high-intent shoppers to send subscription promotions

2. Recommend the right subscription plan for each customer

Relevance is a key factor in eCommerce. And AI can help make subscription promotions and marketing more relevant by recommending the right subscription plan for each customer.

Studies reveal that AI improves relevancy by understanding customer requirements and only offering those recommendations that align with customers’ preference and needs. Removing choice overload can play a role in increasing subscription conversions.

Here’s how AI agents for eCommerce subscriptions can enhance relevancy:

  • By analyzing previous purchase frequency data, AI can choose plans that match the specific delivery frequency
  • AI can analyze data on order quantity, order value, product selection and understand which subscription tier to recommend to which customer
  • By tracking customers’ previous subscription behavior, AI can know which plan might be suitable for which subscribers

3. Personalize subscription offers in real-time

Research shows that personalization can increase sales by 25% and real-time data usage can increase conversion by 20%. AI agents for eCommerce subscriptions can help with personalization in real-time, which is more impactful than merely sharing AI-based recommendations.

Here’s how AI agents can enhance your subscription conversion:

  • Identify products to promote based on past patterns
  • Understand which benefits to emphasize for which customer based on their preference and requirements
  • AI can assess whether offering a discount is necessary to convert a customer or they’re likely to convert at the original price
  • AI agents can help personalize experience across the journey, from product discovery to cart to post-purchase customer interaction

4. Predict when a subscriber is likely to churn

Think like you’re a customer who’s about to unsubscribe from a brand and a brand doesn’t do anything to retain you. It gives you an impression the brand doesn’t care about you. But just a little coaxing, a small discount or a gift could have changed your mind. This is where AI agents for eCommerce subscriptions help.

Here’s how AI agents identify churn-risk signals to know when to trigger retention interventions:

  • AI agents monitor reduced engagement, skipped orders, and increased pause frequencies
  • If there’s an increase in gaps between purchases or there are failed payments
  • Assess customer support interactions and a changed sentiment of customers
  • Track if customers are visiting cancellation pages frequently

5. Intervene before customers cancel

Customers choose to cancel their subscriptions for various reasons. Every cancellation cannot be solved by offering a discount. Proper AI subscription management with the use of AI agents can help make personalized interventions that keep customers away from cancellation.

Let’s look at some common cases why subscribers cancel and how AI agents can intervene:

  • Too much product: One of the most common reasons for churn is subscribers realizing they aren’t able to use the products before the next delivery. AI agents can help identify these reasons and recommend reduced quantities in each order or an extended delivery period.
  • Too expensive: Some subscribers might find the existing subscription plans too expensive. AI agents can identify lower cost or smaller subscription plans that match lower budgets.
  • Too many products: At times, customers might still have products remaining from the last order, in this case AI can recommend pausing the subscription for a specific period of time.
  • Wrong product: Subscribers’ needs change and they may no longer require the products in their existing subscription. AI can enable product swap so they can continue using the same subscription plan.

6. Optimize subscription cadence based on actual customer behavior

Many eCommerce brands are integrating the usage-based subscription model. Subscribers pay for what they use. This makes subscriptions more beneficial to customers. For brands, it increases retention, customer satisfaction, conversions, and inventory planning.

Here’s how AI agents for eCommerce subscriptions help:

  • Track data and analyze reorder frequencies. For instance, how often customers order pet food. AI can offer a reorder frequency based on individual customer patterns.
  • AI can analyze data to understand product usage patterns and trigger replenishment reminders. For instance, one segment reorders coffee every two weeks, while the other in a month.
  • AI agents can identify customers receiving products too early or too late and recommend cadence changes that match their required frequency. For example, food and beverage or household consumables.

7. Recover failed payments and at-risk revenue

Another way AI subscription management helps significantly is to recover failed payments. While automated dunning by sending reminders and helping customers through the process is one way, today’s customers have evolved.

Each customer may need a different approach. And hence, the most appropriate recovery method depends on individual customer contexts. That’s what AI has the ability to understand.

  • Identify failed or expiring payment methods and recommends new modes
  • AI can determine the best recovery action based on individual cases
  • Send personalized messaging to improve conversion and retention
  • Adjust timing of reminders based on customer activity patterns
  • Escalate repeated failures to support teams for appropriate solutions

8. Reactivate former subscribers

At times, subscribers may not cancel, but simply remain inactive. What this requires is to reactivate subscribers. This is where AI can be used for subscription retention.

Reengaging old customers requires significantly lesser resources and effort compared to acquiring new customers, and hence, brands should not ignore reactivation. Here’s how AI agents can help you:

  • Identify why the customer is inactive and for how long. Then, recommend an approach to reengage them.
  • AI can recommend new products based on what the subscriber purchased earlier.
  • Based on the subscribers purchase patterns, offer a different subscription cadence.
  • Send a personalized win-back message based on their preference.

How AI agents for eCommerce subscriptions can connect the subscriber lifecycle

Here’s a snapshot of how AI agents can take relevant actions at different stages of subscriber lifecycle to increase conversions and retention.

Lifecycle stage Potential AI agent action
Visitor To identify subscription intent and how likely they’d be to sign up
First purchase To recommend subscription to a new customer
New subscriber Optimize onboarding to provide a better customer experience
Active subscriber Personalize offers to keep them engaged and retain them
At-risk subscriber Identify churn signals to approach with appropriate solutions
Cancelled subscriber Understand the reason and offer strategies to reactivate them
Churned subscriber Find reactivation opportunities via different channels

What data can AI agents for eCommerce subscriptions use to work effectively

Both single-purchase customers and subscribers leave a lot of data, which, when analyzed, can provide useful insights. For instance, data from purchase history, subscription history, product catalog, customer profile, and order frequency can provide an understanding into customers’ preference, needs, and purchase patterns.

Data such as skips and pauses, cancellation reasons, payment history, engagement data, customer support interactions, and website behavior provides deeper level insights into customers, their pain points, expectations, and more.

However, a study by MIT Sloan shows that companies lose between 15% to 20% revenue because of poor quality data. More data generated from your Shopify store does not automatically lead to better decisions for subscriptions. Paying attention to quality, consistency, and accessibility of the data matters more for the success of your AI subscription management.

Where AI agents should and shouldn’t make decisions

While AI can work autonomously for many processes, some decisions are best made by humans or through human-in-the-loop AI. Here are use cases for AI and AI+human decisions.

Use cases for AI autonomous decisions

  • Product recommendations
  • Cadence recommendations
  • Replenishment reminders
  • Low-risk retention interventions
  • Personalized messaging

Use cases for decisions that may require human oversight

  • Large discounts
  • Refunds
  • High-value customer interventions
  • Policy exceptions
  • Complex customer complaints
  • Significant pricing changes

How brands can start using AI agents without rebuilding their tech stack

AI and technology are evolving everyday. To integrate AI-powered subscription eCommerce, you do not need to rebuild your entire tech stack. Here’s how you can start using AI agents in a phased manner.

Phase 1: Identify one high-value use case

AI agents can help with multiple subscription processes. You don’t have to implement all of them at once. Pick one to begin with. For instance, do you want to gather churn predictions to increase subscriber retention, or is your goal to improve subscription recommendations and increase revenue?

Phase 2: Connect the required data

To make the most of AI agents, connect data from your Shopify subscription platform, Shopify store, customer data from different sources (customer profile, surveys, social media), and data from marketing tools.

Phase 3: Start with recommendations

Before you give full control to your AI agents, let them share recommendations. Have an AI and human mix of processes. This ensures you have control and can streamline how you implement AI.

Phase 4: Automate low-risk actions

In the next phase, start automating low-risk actions. For example, you can allow agents to execute predefined actions in your Ai subscription management. For instance, automate subscription renewal reminders and triggers.

Phase 5: Expand across the subscriber lifecycle

Slowly and steadily, you can allow AI agents to execute use cases across the subscriber lifecycle. Ensure you plan the cases and monitor AI performance at all stages.

The future of AI agents in subscription commerce

According to Morgan Stanley, AI shopping agents will add up to $115 billion to eCommerce by 2030. And Bain & Company estimates agentic commerce will hit up to $500 billion by 2030.

The use of AI has moved from mere data collection and analyses to understanding how subscribers think, act, and what they want. For instance, fully personalized subscription plans to triggering dynamic bundles for subscription conversion.

AI agents will contribute to trigger usage-aware replenishment and predictive inventory for subscriptions. Moreover, AI agents will coordinate across your Shopify store to ensure subscriptions are in sync with loyalty, CRM, customer support, and more.

AI agents for eCommerce subscriptions will move deeper into understanding subscriber needs and act autonomously on that understanding to drive sales and long-term customer lifetime value.

Summing up

Implementing AI for subscription management and retention takes your Shopify store from static automation to context-aware action. If you want to implement AI in subscription eCommerce, start with one measurable use case, track its impact, and expand to other use cases.

Are you looking to integrate AI agents in your Shopify subscription infrastructure? You will require a robust subscription tool that has the capability to integrate AI. Appstle Subscriptions App is designed to match evolving AI tool requirements.

items.html:
When sales slow down, most eCommerce stores reach for that one strategy – discounts across the site.

While this ecommerce discount strategy might drive temporary sales, it can often have a negative impact in the long run. Customers tend to stop buying at original prices and wait for sitewide sales.

Conversely, discounted bundles, even though offer products at a thinner margin, encourage customers to buy more. Bundles also enable brands to decide which products to offer on discount and how much.

In this blog, we compare bundle discounts with sitewide discounts across metrics. You’ll learn which discounting strategy—bundle discounts vs sitewide discounts—is better for your Shopify store.

Let’s get started!

TL; DR

  • Sitewide discounts cut prices on everything equally, fast to launch, but they erode perceived value over time and train customers to wait for sales instead of buying at full price.
  • Bundle discounts reward customers for buying more (e.g., “Buy 3, Save 15%”), they tend to raise Average Order Value while letting brands protect margins by choosing which products get discounted.
  • Profit margins: Sitewide sales discount every product equally, even high performers that didn’t need it. Bundles let you selectively discount lower-margin items while protecting your bestsellers.
  • Inventory movement: Sitewide discounts mostly boost sales of items that were already popular. Bundles can pair slow-moving stock with bestsellers to move inventory more deliberately.
  • Customer perception: Frequent sitewide sales can make customers question your “real” price. Bundles reframe the conversation around added value rather than a lower price.
  • Ease of use: Sitewide discounts are simpler and quicker to set up. Bundles take more planning (product pairing, thresholds, landing pages) but pay off with better long-term economics.
  • Best use cases: Use sitewide discounts for time-bound moments (BFCM, clearance, launches). Use bundles as an ongoing eCommerce discount strategy to grow AOV, protect margins, and increase customer lifetime value.
  • Hybrid approach: Many brands combine both, e.g., offering premium bundles during a sitewide sale to nudge customers toward bigger baskets without giving up all their margin.
  • Bundles are generally the more profitable long-term strategy, while sitewide discounts work best as an occasional, targeted tactic rather than a default.

Bundle discounts vs sitewide discounts: Understanding the difference

To understand the difference between bundle discounts vs sitewide discounts, let’s begin with the definitions of each of these strategies and how they are different from each other.

What are sitewide discounts?

A sitewide discount is applied to all the products on the site. For example, a 10% discount across the site, or flash sales with a countdown timer, or holiday sales, such as Black Friday, End of Season, etc. Sidewide discounts touch all eligible products, are easy to launch as it requires a single discount code, and it impacts all products equally.

What are bundle discounts?

Bundle discounts are offered on a bundle of multiple products, rather than on individual items. For instance, “Buy 3, Save 15%” or starter kits or mix-and-match bundles offered at discounts. For bundle discounts, brands get to choose the products that quality for discounts, and the incentives only unlock when customers add more to their cart.

The main difference is that sitewide discounts make everything cheaper, while bundle discounts make purchases worth it.

Comparing bundle discounts vs sitewide discounts across key metrics

An important process is to measure the metrics that move businesses forward. Measuring metrics helps understand which eCommerce discount strategy fits a given moment.

1. Average Order Value (AOV)

Sitewide discounts: Customers mostly buy what they came to buy. The discount lowers the price of the cart, but it doesn’t necessarily add more products. Customers only get a better price, not more products.

Bundle discounts: The incentive is tied to quantity, for example, buy 3, save 15%. This encourages customers to buy more products to reach the threshold. This increases the number of products as well as the value of their orders.

Bundle discounts tend to increase AOV because it increases the number of products customers buy at one time.

2. Profit margins

Sitewide discounts: Every product is sold at the same discount, regardless of its margin. A high-margin hero product and a low-margin loss-leader are discounted equally, which means the brand is giving away profit on items that didn’t need to be discounted at all.

Bundle discounts: You can control which products are eligible for bundling, hence, it’s possible to build bundles that have higher-margin items, or that only apply a discount once a certain volume is reached. This allows you to be strategic instead of a blanket discount.

Bundle discounts provide control over which SKUs are discounted, and by how much. This helps protect margins.

3. Inventory movement

Sitewide discounts: Typically, under sitewide sales, bestsellers tend to do well. These are the products that are already favorites and hence, sell easily when discounted. And so, slow-moving inventory rarely benefits.

Bundle discounts: Bundles create opportunities to pair a slow-moving product with a bestseller, or to promote complementary items that wouldn’t sell well on their own. This turns bundling into an inventory management tool, not just a pricing tactic.

Bundle discounts can be designed around products that actually need to move.

4. Customer perceived value

Sitewide discounts: When you offer a discount on everything, over time, it may change customers’ perceived value. If it’s often on sale, is the original price even real?

Bundle discounts: For bundles, you can send a different message, which lets customers know they’re getting more. This makes them think about the added value of the extra products in the bundle.

Customers often perceive bundles as offering higher value rather than lower priced products. Such value creation helps in building brand equity; quite opposite of what price reduction does, no wonder in bundle discounts vs sitewide discounts, bundling wins.

5. Operational simplicity

Sitewide discounts: Sitewide discounts have a single discount code, and hence, are easy to launch. One pre-set automatic percentage off at checkout, can be live across the entire store in minutes.

Bundle discounts: Bundle discounts require more planning, deciding which products pair well, setting thresholds, testing bundle logic in the store, and often building dedicated bundle landing pages or “Frequently Bought Together” widgets.

Sitewide discounts are easy and fast to implement compared to bundle discounts.

When do sitewide discounts make sense?

Whether you should use sitewide discount or bundle discount depends on your goals and what you’re using it for. For instance, sitewide discounts do well when you connect them to an event on the calendar. BFCM is a good time because customers are looking for deep discounts.

Another time to offer sitewide discounts is during end-of-season clearance sales, and when you want to move the inventory. Also, at times when you want to acquire new customers. Another time to implement it is when you want to phase out a product before a relaunch.

In each of these cases, the sitewide discount is solving a specific, time-bound problem, not functioning as an always-on growth strategy.

When do bundle discounts make sense?

Bundle discounts work well when brands want to build a more profitable sales pattern over time. Bundles increase AOV and also improve product discovery across the catalog. With bundles, you can cross-sell complementary products, and protect profit margins.

Bundles increase revenue through each and every customer, not just per transaction. Moreover, bundles make it easy to launch new products alongside bestsellers, which encourages larger purchases.

7 reasons bundles generate higher profitability

Here are 7 ways in which bundles can help your Shopify store generate more profit.

1. Customers buy more products per transaction

Bundles have more than just one product – two, three, five or more. Bundles are designed on the principle of buying more and getting more price benefits, as well as value. Thus, the average profitability per transaction increases.

2. Discounts are applied more strategically

With bundles, you can protect margins on certain products and choose which products to offer on discount. For instance, you might not want to offer heavy discounts on your hero products. Conversely, you can apply discounts on lower-margin products.

3. Bundle discounts improve product discoverability

Bundles make it easy for you to introduce new products to customers. For example, add a new product at a heavy discount in the bundle. Or, add a trial pack; for example, a new shampoo. Customers might never buy these new products individually, but as part of bundles, they’re easier to sell.

4. Bundles reduce dependence on deep discounting

Another reason bundles generate higher profitability is because bundles shift the customers’ attention from the discount to the value offered by the bundle. Instead of price cutting, bundles create value.

5. Bundles increase cross-sell revenue

Cross-selling is a key strategy for increasing sales and revenue. When brands recommend “Frequently bought together” products, these cross-sells feel more like convenience as the products are already naturally purchased together.

6. Bundles help move slow inventory

You can improve your inventory efficiency by combining slow-moving products with bestsellers in bundles. You don’t have to resort to a clearance sale kind of strategy by giving sitewide discounts.

7. Bundles can increase customer lifetime value

With bundles, you can introduce a broader set of products to customers. This can lead to more repeat purchases over the years because customers now have more reasons to come back to your store.

Hybrid strategies: Combining bundles and sitewide discounts

Many successful brands don’t rely on just one strategy. Rather, they combine both, applying each where it’s most relevant. Instead of answering the question of which strategy—bundle discounts vs sitewide discounts—is better, let’s look at some examples of how to combine the two.

  • Sitewide sale + premium bundle offers: The bundle offers a better effective discount than the sitewide rate, nudging customers toward higher basket sizes even during a broad sale
  • Bundle-specific incentives during BFCM: Layering bundle logic on top of a seasonal moment.
  • Tiered promotions: Strategies such as “spend more, save more” blend the simplicity of a sitewide structure with the basket-growth incentive of bundling.
  • Bundle-first merchandising: Where bundles are the default way products are presented, with sitewide sales reserved for occasional, clearly bounded events.

The goal of a hybrid approach is to capture the acquisition and urgency benefits of a broad sale while still protecting margin and basket size wherever possible.

Metrics to measure before choosing a discount strategy

The best way to design your strategies is to plan them around customer data. Here are some key metrics to measure:

  • Average Order Value (AOV): Is the cart growing, or just getting cheaper?
  • Gross Margin: what percentage of revenue is actually being retained?
  • Units Per Transaction: are customers buying more items, or the same amount for less?
  • Bundle Attach Rate: What percentage of orders include a bundled product?
  • Conversion Rate: Is the offer actually driving more purchases, or just discounting existing ones?
  • Customer Lifetime Value (CLTV): Are these customers coming back, or are they one-time discount shoppers?
  • Inventory Sell-Through Rate: Is the promotion actually clearing the products it needs to?

Bundle discounts vs sitewide discounts: Which strategy should you use?

Sitewide discounts can help you with short-term sales, for example, BFCM or end-of-season sales. But using it as your only strategy can do more harm. Customers tend to prefer waiting for sitewide sales rather than purchase products at original prices.

Bundle discounts are based on a more thought-through and deliberate approach, where customers buy more. In bundles, value becomes more important than discounts. For instance, convenience of buying a set of things together, getting complementary products together, and buying combinations that are most often bought together by customers.

In most cases, bundles are winners. If you’re looking to set up an effective eCommerce bundle strategy on your Shopify store, you will require a smart app such as Appstle Bundles & Upsells.

image.alt: How to Manage Thousands of SKUs in Enterprise Product Bundling for Shopify Brands

items.excerpt: For small Shopify stores, managing product bundles is simple. But for enterprise brands bundling products from multiple categories, markets, and channels can be complex. Apart from the challenge of creating thoughtful and appealing bundles, the challenges also include managing thousands of bundle combinations at the same time, maintaining inventory accuracy, customer experience, profitability, and more.…
items.html:
For small Shopify stores, managing product bundles is simple.

But for enterprise brands bundling products from multiple categories, markets, and channels can be complex.

Apart from the challenge of creating thoughtful and appealing bundles, the challenges also include managing thousands of bundle combinations at the same time, maintaining inventory accuracy, customer experience, profitability, and more.

In this guide, you’ll learn how enterprise product bundling strategies for Shopify brands and the systems to make it work.

A quick look at the key ideas in this article

  • Bundling gets exponentially harder at scale. A few SKUs and bundles are easy to manage by hand, but thousands of SKUs can’t keep up.
  • The biggest hidden challenges are: real-time inventory sync (one SKU can live in hundreds of bundles), consistent pricing logic, propagating product updates across bundles, reporting on which bundles actually drive revenue, and the sheer merchandising workload of managing bundles manually.
  • Build bundle rules instead of individual bundles.
  • Use dynamic bundles that adapt to inventory and customer choice, not fixed combinations.
  • Organize your catalog into bundle-friendly collections with clear tagging and hierarchy.
  • Use customer behavior data (frequently bought together, repeat purchases) to guide bundle creation.
  • Automate discount and pricing logic with tiered/volume/collection-based rules
  • Connect bundles across channels (online, POS, retail, wholesale) for consistency
  • Continuously measure performance, conversion rate, attach rate, AOV, revenue, and margin
  • Bundles aren’t just an AOV tool. They also drive product discovery, inventory clearance, new product adoption, customer acquisition (starter kits), personalization, and cross-category expansion.
  • Enterprise bundling requires flexible rule-based logic, real-time inventory sync, automated pricing, POS support, advanced analytics, and cross-channel consistency; spreadsheets and manual processes break down at scale.
  • Before scaling, ask: Can your platform handle thousands of combinations? How much bundling is still manual? Are bundles tied to live inventory? Do you know which bundles are actually profitable?
  • Success isn’t about creating more bundles. It’s about building a scalable system (rules, automation, data-driven personalization) that grows with the business. Tools like Appstle Bundles & Upsells are built to handle this automation end-to-end.

Why does bundling become more complex at enterprise scale?

When a store is small with just 20 SKUs and five bundles, it’s easy to manage everything. From choosing product combinations to pricing to monitoring performance.

But imagine thousands of SKUs across multiple collections, marketing, and fulfillment locations? A large number of products can lead to various kinds of complexity.

  • Combination explosion: Every new SKU added to the inventory multiplies the number of possible bundles that it can be a part of.
  • Inventory dependencies: A single SKU might be a part of hundreds of different bundles, so one stockout can affect the entire merchandising plan.
  • Pricing complexity: Different bundles may need different discount logic, which has to stay consistent across bundles and markets.
  • Merchandising complexity: Deciding which bundles to promote, and when, becomes an ongoing complex task rather than a one-time setup.

The challenges of managing thousands of enterprise product bundling combinations

As businesses scale, bundling may pose many challenges. Here are some of the most common challenges you should look for in your Shopify bundling business.

Inventory synchronization

A single SKU can belong to hundreds of bundles at once. If that SKU sells out, every bundle containing it needs to be updated, disabled, or reconfigured. This has to be done instantly, in real time and through an automated system, not manually.

Pricing management

When bundles are built manually, discount logic tends to become inconsistent. One bundle might be discounted 15%, another 20%, with no clear reasoning. At scale, this inconsistency erodes both profitability and customer trust.

Product updates

A single product change, for example, a new price, a discontinued variant, an updated image, can ripple across dozens or hundreds of bundles that include it. Without a system to propagate that change, bundles quietly go stale.

Reporting complexity

With thousands of bundle combinations live at once, understanding which bundles are actually driving revenue (versus just existing) becomes genuinely difficult without dedicated analytics.

Merchandising workload

One of the biggest challenges is that manually creating and maintaining bundles simply becomes impossible past a certain scale. A merchandising team can build and maintain dozens of bundles by hand. They cannot build and maintain thousands.

7 strategies for Shopify enterprise product bundling

Here are seven strategies you can apply for efficient Shopify bundle management.

1. Build bundle rules, not individual bundles

Automating bundle creation rules can reduce complexity. For instance, instead of creating three bundles from scratch, define rules that automatically create bundles. For example:

  • Any 3 products from collection A
  • Any 4 products from category B
  • Any 2 products from the same product line

Instead of manually building and maintaining hundreds of individual product groupings, one rule can generate hundreds of valid bundle combinations automatically. This automated system of creating bundles can help you scale without added manual processes, reduce ongoing maintenance, and adapt automatically as the catalog changes.

2. Use dynamic bundles instead of fixed product combinations

Dynamic bundles are created in real time based on customer behavior. Rather than fixed sets of products, dynamic bundles can:

  • Adjust automatically based on catalog changes
  • Let customers select the products they want in the bundle
  • Adapt to real-time inventory availability

Common formats include build-your-own-box offers, mix-and-match bundles, and collection-based bundles where any product from a defined group gets added to a bundle. This shifts the bundle from a fixed offer into a flexible tool that is more relevant to customers and the current catalog.

3. Organize products into bundle-friendly collections

For dynamic enterprise product bundling to work effectively, it is important that the catalog is planned and structured in a systematic manner. For this, brands need to create clear collection structures, consistent product tagging systems, and a defined product hierarchy. Here’s how this structure helps:

  • Bundles can be created based on collection or tag membership rather than manual product lists
  • Automation rules become easier to write and maintain
  • Merchandising teams can launch new bundle campaigns faster

4. Use customer behavior to determine bundle opportunities

Creating a strong data collection and analysis strategy for enhancing your enterprise product bundling strategy can ensure effectiveness and relevance when market trends change. For instance, when you gather data on frequently-bought-together patterns, repeat purchase behavior, and cross-category purchase patterns, you can keep the bundles more relevant.

Here’s how creating bundles based on customer data makes a difference:

  • Create bundles based on evidence rather than guesswork
  • It makes personalized bundling possible, for instance, offering different bundle suggestions to different customers based on their own purchase history
  • Data can help drive dynamic recommendations that update as customer behavior changes

5. Automate bundle discount and pricing logic

For enterprise brands that have thousands of bundles, manual price-setting is almost impossible. Moreover, it is a recipe for inconsistency and errors. Therefore, enterprise brands use smart bundling tools, such as Appstle Bundles & Upsells to build rules-based pricing systems.

Some of the rules for bundle pricing systems may be: Tiered discounts, volume discounts, and collection-based discounting rules.

Let’s look at some benefits of automating bundling logic.

  • Pricing stays consistent across thousands of bundles
  • Fewer manual pricing errors
  • Easier to scale new bundle campaigns without rebuilding pricing logic each time

6. Connect bundles across channels

Most often, enterprise brands have multiple sales channels. For instance, Shopify stores, Shopify POS, physical retail stores, and wholesale. Bundling strategies need to stay consistent on all channels.

This means thinking in terms of omnichannel merchandising and unified promotions. The same bundle logic and pricing rules apply whether a customer is shopping online or in a physical store. Disconnected bundle strategies across channels create confusion and inconsistent pricing, which harms customer trust.

7. Measure bundle performance continuously

Monitoring and measuring enterprise product bundle performance is key for ongoing success. Here are some of the metrics to measure:

  • Bundle conversion rate
  • Bundle attach rate
  • Impact on average order value (AOV)
  • Revenue contribution
  • Margin contribution

The goal isn’t to maximize the number of bundles in the catalog — it’s to continuously identify which bundles are actually working and optimize or retire the ones that aren’t. Bundle quantity is a vanity metric; bundle performance is what matters.

How enterprises use bundles beyond average order value (AOV)

Most brands think of bundles as a strategy to increase AOV. However, there are many other ways bundles can positively impact your business. Here are some:

  • Product discovery: Introduce customers to new or lesser-known products by pairing them with bestsellers.
  • Inventory management: Move slow-selling or excess stock by bundling it with high-demand items.
  • New product launches: Drive adoption of new products by bundling them into existing purchase paths.
  • Customer acquisition: Use starter kits or introductory bundles to lower the barrier to a first purchase.
  • Personalization: Offer custom bundle experiences tailored to individual customer behavior.
  • Cross-category expansion: Increase product penetration by encouraging customers to buy across categories they wouldn’t normally shop.

The tech stack you need for enterprise bundle management

Here are the tech and digital capabilities that you require for your enterprise product bundling strategy.

  • Flexible, rule-based bundle logic
  • Dynamic bundle creation and updating
  • Real-time inventory synchronization
  • Automated pricing and discount logic
  • Shopify POS support for in-store consistency
  • Advanced analytics and reporting
  • Support for high-volume transactions
  • Consistency across every sales channel

Questions to answer before scaling bundles in your Shopify store

First, get a sense of how much of your bundling happens manually, and which are the processes that can be automated via a bundling app. Understand the capability of your current eCommerce platform – can it support thousands of bundle combinations? If not, what apps or technology support would you require for that?

Apart from that, you must know if your bundles are connected to live inventory data. This means, will bundles change in real time based on sales and demand? Will your bundles be available only on your Shopify store or on other offline channels as well? These are some of the basic questions to begin with, before you get started with your enterprise product bundles.

Summing up

A successful enterprise product bundles strategy is not just about creating bundle volume. It is more about setting in place a system that will support your business in scaling bundles as your business grows.

For a successful bundling strategy, create flexible rules, automate pricing and inventory logic, use customer data to create dynamic bundle experience, increase AOV and drive revenue automatically through a robust bundling app, such as Appstle Bundles & Upsells.

Appstle Bundles & Upsells allows you to create multiple bundle types, automates discounts and pricing logic, tracks bundle performance in real-time and creates dynamic bundles, etc.

items.excerpt: Many brands invest heavily in product bundles on their ecommerce store but overlook how those same bundles appear in physical retail environments. The result? As ecommerce and retail continue to merge, creating a consistent omnichannel product bundles experience across channels is…
items.html:
Many brands invest heavily in product bundles on their ecommerce store but overlook how those same bundles appear in physical retail environments.

The result? Customers see different offers, pricing structures, and product combinations depending on where they shop.

As ecommerce and retail continue to merge, creating a consistent omnichannel product bundles experience across channels is becoming a competitive advantage.

This guide explores how brands can build an omnichannel bundling strategy that increases revenue, improves customer experience, and simplifies operations.

Let’s get started!

A sneak peek into the key strategies in this article

  • Omnichannel product bundle consistency means customers get the same pricing, offers, and product combinations whether they shop online or in-store, which builds trust and avoids confusion.
  • Common challenges include mismatched online/offline offers, inventory gaps between channels, undertrained in-store staff, fragmented tech systems, and disconnected performance reporting.
  • Key strategies for consistency: build a unified bundle strategy with clear goals and audience, standardize pricing and value across channels, use combined online/offline sales data to pick winning bundle combinations, and align merchandising teams on promotions and launches.
  • Make bundles easy to discover everywhere (PDP recommendations, checkout upsells, in-store signage and POS prompts), ensure inventory/fulfillment can reliably support bundle orders, and measure performance (attach rate, conversion, AOV, revenue) across channels rather than in silos.
  • Well-executed bundles also boost broader omnichannel KPIs like AOV, conversion rate, inventory turnover, and product discovery.
  • A dedicated bundling app (like Appstle Bundles & Upsells) can help unify bundle management across online and offline channels.

Why does bundle consistency matter in omnichannel commerce?

Today, commerce is complex. There are multiple channels that customers engage on. For instance, eCommerce stores, physical stores, pop-up shops, events, wholesale partners, and Shopify POS, among others.

Customers tend to engage on multiple channels at the same time. For example, discover bundles via social media, buy them via the website, and follow up via another channel. If every channel works in a silo, it will lead to inconsistency.

Inconsistency causes many problems. For instance, differing information on channels leaves customers confused. Inconsistency in pricing can lead to reduced trust and lower conversion rates.

Customers expect the same brand experience across the platform. Simple things such as uniform pricing and consistent bundle information can have a positive impact without trying hard.

The most common omnichannel product bundle challenges

With multiple channels come complexity and challenges. Here are some of the most common challenges around omnichannel product bundles.

1. Different bundle offers online and offline

What if you see a ‘Buy 3 Get 1’ offer online, want to touch and feel the product before buying, so you head to the physical store only to find the offer is not available in-store? You’d be let down, and might even feel like brands are tricking customers into buying things online without trying.

2. Inventory constraints

Inconsistent inventory between online and physical stores can also lead to confusion and customer dissatisfaction. For instance, you see a particular product in the physical store and decide, for convenience, to place an order via the app. But discover later that the product is not available online.

3. Staff awareness gaps

While brands find it easy to promote bundles online, quite often, in-store sales staff are not trained to push bundles or find it hard to sell them. Moreover, online and in-store bundle offers might have inconsistent messaging, leaving customers confused.

4. Technology limitations

Another key challenge for omnichannel product bundles is because of the systems used to manage bundles. Systems and tools for online and in-store bundles might be separate, which might lead to inconsistent bundle offers on the channels.

5. Reporting fragmentation

For a bundle strategy to be effective, you need to track and monitor its performance across channels – online and in-store. Moreover, you need a unified performance view. But this may be hard in an omnichannel set up.

7 ways to create consistent omnichannel product bundle experience

Here are 7 strategies to create consistency in omnichannel product bundle experience for customers.

1. Start with a unified bundle strategy

Creating a well-thought strategy is key to the success of your bundles. That’s because when your foundation is clearly designed keeping in mind your goals, the chances of failure lessen. Here are some factors that you should have clarity on:

  • Bundle goals: What do you want to achieve with your bundling strategy? Do you want to move slow stock, increase average order value (AOV), or introduce customers to new products? Your goals will define your strategy.
  • Target audience: Who is your target audience? Who are you building the bundles for? An audience-product mismatch can be a key reason for slow bundle sales. Define your target audience before you plan your bundles.
  • Product combinations: Choose the bundle products strategically. For instance, combine low-selling with most-popular, or products that complement each other. Avoid putting random products together as this may backfire.

To ensure consistency, answer these key questions:

  • Why does this bundle exist?
  • What customer pain point does it solve?
  • Who is this bundle for?

2. Standardize bundle value across channels

One of the biggest drawbacks of omnichannel product bundles is inconsistency in the value customers get from bundles from online and physical stores. For instance, if you offer the same bundle with two different prices or offers, online and in the physical store, customers will definitely get confused.

Here’s how you can ensure consistency:

  • Same offer: Make the same discount, benefits offer, online and in-store. When you do this, customers don’t feel cheated or dissatisfied. Even if you’re offering multiple ways to collect orders through BOPIS (buy online and pick in-store) or BOPC (buy online and pick up curbside), keep the approach consistent.
  • Same value proposition: Every customer shopping from your brand must feel valued in the same manner, regardless of the platform they’re shopping on. Ensure same bundle discount, same-value free gifts even though formats change.
  • Similar pricing structure: Offer online bundles incentives in-store and vice versa. This kind of similar pricing builds trust and drives customers from one platform to the other. Even though you may display or package bundles differently, the core pricing structure should be similar.

3. Use data to identify best-selling bundle combinations

As Seth Godin said, “Don’t find customers for your products, find products for your customers”, putting together different products for each bundle is a strategic activity, not a random thought. To ensure you have the best bundle combinations, follow these strategies.

  • Frequently-purchased-together products: One of the best ways to create a successful bundling strategy is to look at data from past sales. Which products are frequently bought together? For this, combine online and in-store data to design bundles. Integrating a good Shopify bundling app makes this easier, not only to refer to data but to ensure your data reflects changing patterns and trends over time.
  • Cross-category purchases: Which cross-category products are customers buying together? For example, a glass cleaner solution, a kitchen platform mop, and a long-handle broom being bought together for home upkeep. Look for patterns to get ideas for creating bundles of products from different categories.
  • High-margin combinations: A sure way to ensure high average order value is to have high-margin products in omnichannel product bundles. This ensures your online and physical store can meet its revenue goals and a lower gap between the two stores.

For all these strategies, use data from online and in-store separately, as well as analyze the combined data to discover patterns.

4. Align online and in-store merchandising teams

Imagine the product and sales team creating bundles to be launched but the marketing team for the physical store does not have any information about it. Bundle success requires collaboration between various teams. When every team is aligned and in sync with the plan, you can drive higher success rates for omnichannel product bundles.

Here are some factors to consider for omnichannel merchandising:

  • Shared promotions calendar: Running omnichannel bundle promotions can be a challenge if teams work in silos. Planning bundle promotions requires various teams—product, sales, marketing, order fulfilment, and logistics—to be in sync for planning online and offline promotional activities and offers.
  • Consistent messaging: An aspect for omnichannel businesses that builds trust and removes confusion is consistency in messaging across customer touchpoints. Whether it’s in-store or online, your offers, tone, voice, and core value proposition of the bundles should remain the same.
  • Product launch coordination: One of the most challenging aspects of omnichannel product bundles is to sync the launch. For instance, say you’re selling football kit bundles. You launch online. Customers visit your physical store to shop after trying on the kit. However, your in-store launch is delayed. This can seriously harm your brand reputation.

5. Make bundle discovery easy in every channel

One mistake that many brands make is they make bundles seem like an afterthought or a strategy to clear stock. When you mix bundles with single products, when you don’t highlight them and give them the attention they deserve, your customers will also perceive them as something that’s not as exciting.

One way to change this perception is to display bundles with equal importance as other products. And this goes for both online and physical stores. Let’s look at some factors to remember when displaying bundles.

  • Online: Include bundles in the product detail page (PDP) recommendations, personalize recommendations for customers, upsell bundles through the checkout page, and add them in landing pages. Also, create a separate page featuring only bundles.
  • Retail: In the physical stores, let bundles be at the forefront. Display signage and posters to promote bundles, and train the staff to recommend bundles. Another way to increase bundle sales is point of sale prompts (POS) at the billing counter.

The idea is to make it easy for customers to discover bundles wherever they’re shopping.

6. Ensure inventory and fulfilment can support bundles

Consistency also means being able to fulfil orders. For instance, a returning customer may want to buy the same bundle again but if you aren’t able to fulfil the order soon, it may reflect on your brand’s order fulfilment competency. Some of the challenges, such as bundle stockouts, component shortages, and inventory allocation for omnichannel product bundles, can be overcome.

Here are some best practices to follow:

  • Monitor bundle inventory separately: Mixing up single products and bundle products in the inventory can get confusing. It can lead to repetitions, and incorrect calculations. By monitoring bundle inventory separately, you can ensure bundle products never run out and are restocked based on need.
  • Forecast demand: Any successful order fulfilment process is based on forecast and planning ahead of time. Place restock orders before your bundle products run out. To do so, forecast demand based on past sales patterns.
  • Track bundle performance by location: Monitor bundle sales by location for online and physical stores. This can help you predict and forecast product requirements for restocking inventory in time.

7. Measure bundle performance across channels

Measuring bundle performance metrics, such as sales rate, return rate, average order value, etc., can give you an overview of what’s working, what’s not, and optimization opportunities.

But measuring online and offline bundle performance separately can create blind spots. Analyzing data from online and offline bundles in a unified manner can give a better picture of what’s required to reach omnichannel product bundle goals.

Here are some bundle metrics to track online and offline:

  • Bundle attach rate
  • Bundle conversion rate
  • Bundle revenue
  • AOV impact
  • Cross-channel performance

How product bundles improve omnichannel KPIs

Let’s understand how product bundles help improve some of the most important omnichannel KPIs.

1. Average Order Value (AOV): Instead of single products, you are selling more than one product per transaction, increasing AOV. Moreover, including a high-value product in a bundle can further increase AOV.

2. Conversion rate: When you strategically design bundles based on past sales patterns, seasons, trends, and customer preferences, you make purchase decisions easier.

3. Inventory movement: Omnichannel product bundles make it easy to get the inventory moving – slow-moving products, new items, perishable products, etc. can be moved in time when there are more than one sales channels.

4. Product discovery: Introducing new products to customers becomes easier with bundles. You can mix a new product with old bestsellers, create a bundle with new products and offer a discount or add small size sample products.

Summing up

The most successful eCommerce brands don’t look at bundles only as an online strategy. They combine offline channels as well. However, for an efficient omnichannel product bundle strategy, you need a smart bundling app for your Shopify store.

items.excerpt: For eCommerce brands, timing and speed are more important than you think they are. Is your focus on acquiring subscribers? If your answer is yes, you may need to change your eCommerce subscription strategy. Why? Because acquiring subscribers can be a long process.
