items.html:
The subscription landscape is highly competitive. And two of the critical factors of this business model are customer acquisition cost (CAC) and customer lifetime value (CLTV).

Both these are key metrics that need to be in balance for the business to be profitable. And to ensure a balanced CAC vs. CLTV ratio in subscription businesses, you require effective strategies and a deep understanding of how these two metrics work.

If you’re curious to learn about these subscription profitability metrics and how to apply them to your Shopify store, read this blog now!

TL;DR

  • A healthy CAC vs. CLTV ratio in subscriptions—1:3 to 1:5—is essential for profitability of subscription businesses.
  • To decrease CAC, combine referral and loyalty programs with subscriptions, build communities, offer tiered subscription plans, and combine bundling with subscriptions.
  • To increase CLTV, create personalized experiences using data analysis, implement upselling and cross-selling, offer flexibility, and reward long-term subscribers with exclusive perks.
  • Track KPIs such as monthly and annual recurring revenue, churn rate, customer segments, and product usage metrics.
  • Use analytics platforms like Appstle Subscriptions App to monitor and optimize CAC vs. CLTV ratio for subscription businesses.

Understanding CAC vs. CLTV in subscription business

Let’s get started by understanding the basics of customer acquisition cost for subscriptions and customer lifetime value.

What is CAC in subscription businesses?

Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) for subscriptions is the cost incurred to acquire a subscriber. In the context of subscriptions, it includes all expenses—marketing, sales, content creation, ad spends, social media spends, promotional discounts, operational, among others—divided by the number of new customers acquired during a specific period.

What is CLTV in subscription businesses?

Customer Lifetime Value is the total revenue a customer generates for a business throughout their relationship with it. CLTV can be calculated by predicting the period for which the customer will remain a subscriber divided by the total revenue they will generate. The revenue can include subscription fees, upsells, cross-sells, and other regular subscription purchases.

Why does CAC vs. CLTV ratio matter in subscription businesses?

The CAC:CLTV ratio determines whether your business is profitable and scalable or not. Let’s understand how and why this ratio matters.

A good CAC:CLTV ratio ensures that the revenue generated from each customer exceeds the cost of acquiring them. This gives a sense of the margin available for operations, growth, and profit.

In subscription models, this ratio becomes critical as subscriptions involve upfront investment to acquire subscribers. Unlike traditional business models where customers purchase products immediately, in subscription businesses, purchases take place over a period of time and repeatedly. While recurring business models increase CLTV, it is also essential to reduce its CAC.

The ratio also impacts businesses’ ability to scale marketing efforts. A good CAC vs. CLTV ratio in subscription provides comfort and confidence to businesses, as they can spend on marketing. Conversely, a poor ratio can hamper growth as businesses might not have enough resources for scale or growth.

What is a healthy CAC:CLTC ratio?

Typically, a healthy CLTV to CAC ratio for eCommerce subscriptions ranges between 1:3 to 1:5. This means, for every one dollar spent in acquiring a subscriber, subscription businesses should earn three to five dollars in CLTV. This ratio provides sufficient margins to cover various costs.

Subscription businesses that demonstrate high performance and have strong retention rates, are often able to achieve 1:5 or better ratios. Businesses that know how to minimize customer acquisition costs and maximize value from each customer relationship often have better ratios.

Key takeaway: Your target CLTV to CAC ratio should be decided based on your industry, product, and business goals. Higher margin products and services subscriptions can often reach CAC:CLTV ratio goals.

CAC vs. CLTV ratio in subscriptions based on industries
The ratios vary based on industries. For instance, the ratio in SaaS businesses is typically between 1:3 and 1:10. Higher ratios can be possible if the cost of providing service is lower, and if the customer lifecycles are longer.

Ecommerce businesses without subscriptions often have CAC:CLTV ratios of 1:4 to 1:6. However, in traditional businesses, the lifetime value calculation differs because of the unpredictable nature of repeat purchases, unlike in subscription formats.

CAC Vs. CLTV in subscription businesses

In this section, we explore strategies to decrease the customer acquisition cost for subscriptions, and to increase customer lifetime value for your Shopify business.

Strategies to lower CAC in subscription businesses

While running organic marketing campaigns and word-of-mouth marketing are some of the strategies that may help acquire customers, to compete in today’s subscription environment, you will have to think beyond these traditional strategies. Here are some strategies to consider:

1. Combine a referral program with subscriptions

A referral program helps increase customers. By combining a referral program with subscriptions, you can increase the potential of new subscribers. Word of mouth advocacy for brands builds more trust and confidence, and hence new customers are more likely to sign up.

2. Combine a loyalty program with subscriptions

Loyalty programs help increase loyalty, decrease acquisition costs, and increase CLTV. Loyalty programs offer benefits, encouraging customers to stay loyal. The more loyalty members you have, and the longer they stick to your brand, the lesser your acquisition costs.

3. Set up tiered subscription model

When the subscription model is tiered—for example, Silver, Gold, and Platinum—subscribers tend to stay more engaged and for a longer duration. For instance, subscribers in lower tiers would want to progress to higher tiers to get more benefits out of their subscription plans. They do so by making more purchases. Tiered subscription models help lower CAC.

4. Combine bundling and subscriptions

Bundles include two or more products or services. When you offer bundles as subscriptions, customers can get more value from it. The convenience of ordering bundles at discounted prices increases customer satisfaction and lifecycle. You can do so by integrating Appstle apps into your Shopify system

5. Provide flexibility

Allowing subscribers to easily change the frequency of subscription deliveries, for example, from weekly to monthly, quarterly, etc., can give them freedom and flexibility, making them stay for longer. When things are not rigid, customers will stay for longer.

6. Build a community

Building a community of subscribers increases the feeling of belonging and being part of an exclusive group of likeminded people. This leads to subscribers turning into brand advocates, and creating a network that attracts more subscribers. This can lead to decreased CAC.

7. Maximize convenience

Design the subscription customer experience (CX) and logistics in a way that it maximizes convenience and minimizes friction. This leads to more satisfied subscribers, flexibility, personalized experiences, and loyalty.

Strategies to increase CLTV in subscription businesses

From meaningful subscription plan pricing to upselling and personalization, here are some effective strategies to increase customer lifetime value in subscriptions:

1. Personalization

With digital subscription tools, you can now collect and analyze customer data, and use the insights for creating personalized experiences for subscribers. Data-driven personalization can help with LTV calculation for eCommerce.

For instance, collect data about subscriber order patterns, behavior and activities on the site, etc., and create offers and recommendations based on that data. When you provide what customers want, they stick with your brand for long, increasing CLTV.

2. Upselling products and services

Another way to increase CLTV is to upsell products and services via subscriptions. Upselling can not only increase the average order value (AOV), but also enhance the value subscribers gain from their orders.

For instance, offer a water tank cleaning service along with the monthly house cleaning subscription. With enhanced value and experience, your customers will tend to stay for longer, increasing CLTV.

3. Flexible subscription plans

By offering flexibility, you can significantly reduce the churn rate of subscriptions. And churn rate is directly connected to increasing CLTV. In subscriptions, you can offer flexibility in many different ways.

For example, flexibility by allowing subscribers to pause deliveries, change delivery dates, add or remove items from deliveries, choose different payment options every time, etc. Allowing them the flexibility to change subscription plans from paid to free to premium, etc., can also increase convenience, satisfaction, and hence, CLTV.

4. Use data-driven insights

When it comes to data, there’s no limit to what you can track online. By analyzing data, you can create personalized and more relevant experiences for customers. And it’s not just past purchases or current behavior you must track.

Track the content that subscribers engage more with, which perks are more liked by subscribers, which tier is performing better, etc. By tracking these and other such, not so obvious data, you can enhance personalization, and increase CLTV.

5. Offer rewards to long-term subscribers

Long-term subscribers often have the highest CLTV. One of the best ways to keep your most loyal customers is to create emotional bonds with them. Do so by rewarding them for their loyalty. Offer exclusive rewards to long-term subscribers on special occasions. For example, mark subscriber milestones with rewards, offer exclusive experiences, or personalized service for them. This will boost loyalty and CLTV.

Tools and metrics for tracking CAC and CLTV

In this section, we explore formulas, calculation methods, subscription tools, and metrics that you can apply in your Shopify business.

Formulas and calculation methods

The formula to calculate CAC is simple. Add all the expenses related to customer acquisition and divide it by the number of customers acquired during that period. Therefore, it is critical to attribute all relevant costs and count new acquired customers properly.

For subscription businesses, customer acquisition cost can include expenses, such as paid advertising, content creation, marketing, salaries, technology, tools and subscriptions, promotional discounts, etc.

For calculating CLTV, you have to take into consideration many variables, for example, average revenue per user, gross margin and customer lifespan, etc. To calculate CLTV, multiple average revenue per user with gross margin and divide by churn rate.

Subscription business KPIs to monitor

Here’s a list of subscription business KPIs you should track. These subscription profitability metrics can help you find gaps in your business, optimize, grow, and scale.

  • Monthly recurring revenue (MRR)
  • Annual recurring revenue (ARR)
  • Churn rate
  • Customer segments acquired during a specific period
  • Product usage metric
  • Customer support ticket frequency

Dashboards and reporting solutions

Ecommerce subscription businesses require efficient, smart analytics platforms that can combine data from multiple sources and analyze it to provide accurate CAC and CLTV. Many advanced subscription tools also provide real-time data analytics and subscription profitability metrics.

Appstle Subscriptions App is a preferred tool used by thousands of Shopify merchants. The app offers integrated reporting solutions that provide subscription-specific metrics. Appstle app can also be customized for specific business requirements.

Wrapping up

A healthy CAC vs. CLTV ratio in subscriptions is key for ambitious and growth-oriented Shopify businesses. A higher CAC and lower CLTV can cause imbalance and have a negative impact on the business profitability.

And to manage and track both these metrics, you require an efficient subscriptions app with the required capabilities.

Appstle Subscription App has built-in features to complement Shopify platform and third-party apps. The app not only helps Shopify and Shopify Plus stores set up subscription plans, but also manage subscriptions to ensure a healthy CAC and CLTV ratio.

items.html:
At a time when organic marketing reach is extremely low and the only thing that seems to get traffic is paid media, there’s one star strategy that still remains powerful – community.

Communities bring a sense of belonging, connecting like-minded customers through common identity, kinship, and affinity.

In this blog, we explore all about community driven growth for Shopify stores through memberships.

Curious to get into community-driven marketing for your business?

Let’s get you started!

TL; DR

  • Community-driven growth for Shopify stores creates loyal customers through exclusive memberships, increasing a sense of belonging, brand affinity, and shared interests with like-minded members.
  • Shopify brands must implement community-driven growth via eCommerce membership models as it has many benefits. Collect customer insights by tracking member conversations, increase retention through better experience, turn members to brand advocates, organically growing your brand, and save costs.
  • Membership programs drive brand advocacy by offering members exclusive perks, through word-of-mouth recommendations by members, and by instilling a feeling of identity within members.
  • Membership programs help increase average order value, customer lifetime value, and reduce churn, leading to compounding effects of memberships.
  • Membership programs must have the key features, such as tiered membership structure, VIP access, exclusive drops, etc.
  • By combining the features of Shopify platform with Appstle Memberships App, you can create higher engagement, long-term member commitment, and increase ROI from your membership program.

What is community-driven growth?

Community-driven growth is a result of creating groups of customers, offering exclusivity, belonging, affinity, and a space for shared interests. Members of the community receive many benefits, leading to more engagement, and eventually more profits, more customers, etc.

Let’s understand this with an example. Nike Run club is a membership program that engages members through its fitness tracking app. Members have access to exclusive products and member-only experiences.

Nike measured the impact of this membership program. The brand reached 30% of its revenue through the membership app, revealing that its app members spent 3X more than customers on other channels.

Like Nike, there are many eCommerce brands adopting community-driven growth strategies to meet various goals, including higher retention rates, increase profits, improve brand awareness, etc.

Source

Why Shopify brands are adopting community-first strategies

Creating member communities has many benefits for brands, some direct, some indirect. Here are some ways in which community-building helps brands:

1. Gather insights into customer preference

By following and observing what members discuss, brands can collect insights into customers’ preferences. Brands can collect these insights from the various platforms that the community members are a part of, for example, the membership portal/platform or app, social media communities, online community platforms, or during physical events. Additionally, Shopify brands can run targeted surveys.

2. Increase customer retention and loyalty

When customers have good experiences with brands, they tend to stay loyal for the long-term. According to a 2025 study by Forrester, a strong brand experience (BX) and customer experience (CX) fosters loyalty and higher lifetime value. And brands that focus on building loyalty, grow about 2.5 times faster than their competitors.

3. Improve brand reputation

Over time, members become brand ambassadors, not only discussing your brand within the member community, but outside of it, too. Members tend to talk about your brand and refer it to people in their circles. When some members are satisfied with the membership program, they will share positive reviews with other members, enhancing your brand reputation.

4. Decrease customer support costs

When members interact with each other, they tend to answer queries by other customers. This can help reduce your customer support costs. According to a Gartner study, brands that integrate communities can reduce customer support costs by 50%. Well-managed communities can pitch in by answering queries, thus reducing your support load.

The role of eCommerce membership models in building advocacy

Memberships create opportunities for including brand advocacy strategies in your Shopify stores. Let’s understand how exactly membership programs help do this.

1. Offering exclusive perks leads to advocacy

Memberships may start with transactional benefits for customers, but they often lead to emotional connections. When you offer members special perks, such as discounts, early access to new launches, and member-exclusive event invites, members feel a sense of exclusivity.

This feeling of belonging to a special group leads to a deeper engagement with the brand, other members, and all that you have to offer to members. This leads members to advocate about the brand, discuss it, and recommend it to friends. This sort of brand advocacy strategy requires creating a special community of your most loyal customers, for example, through memberships.

2. Memberships encourage word-of-mouth referrals

Membership programs can bring organic and structured referrals from your existing members. Members who are satisfied and happy with the program, tend to talk about your brand in their social circles.

Moreover, they might also bring up your brand name as a recommendation on social media platforms. This sort of word-of-mouth marketing can lead to traffic to your site and lead to new customers.

Apart from organic referrals, you can integrate a structured referral program within the membership program. For instance, encourage existing members to refer to new members. In return, offer incentives.

In both cases — organic and structured referral programs — word-of-mouth recommendation coming from trusted people carries more credibility than paid adverts.

3. Psychological aspect: Identity-driven loyalty

Another reason for community-driven growth for Shopify stores is related to consumer psychology. When your customers become members, they often start considering themselves as a part of your community. For example, they’d say, “I’m a Nike Run Club member”, or “I’m an Amazon Prime subscriber”. This sort of affliction and connection with brands creates loyalty and long-term associations.

Eventually, long-term memberships become less about perks and incentives, and more about belonging to a community. The shared interests, exclusive experiences, and special benefits become a part of members’ identity, leading to loyalty. This sort of loyalty is hard to break even when your competitors offer more perks.

How memberships lead to long-term revenue generation

Membership programs are an effective strategy for community-driven growth for Shopify stores. Let’s understand how memberships drive revenue.

1. Membership perks tied to AOV

You can encourage members to spend more by planning the perks smartly. However, you must also ensure the perks offer members value. Let’s see how to do it:

  • Create perks that entice and encourage customers to spend more
  • For example, Amazon Prime offers free shipping on orders above $25. This encourages customers to shop more to avoid paying shipping charges
  • Costco has a bulk-only model that leads to higher AOV
  • Set spending thresholds for free shipping, reward points, and exclusive access, etc.
  • Offer discounts on bulk or large-volume orders
  • Create member-exclusive bundles, increasing AOV
  • Tiered rewards is another way to unlock higher spending
  • Run time-sensitive discounts to create urgency

2. Stickiness and reduced churn from exclusivity

Creating exclusive experiences for customers has many benefits. It increases the perceived value of your brand, leads to stronger emotional connections, and increases loyalty. These factors lead to long-term revenue generation. Here’s what you can do:

  • Implement annual membership fees, offer points, and a tiered structure. These factors make it hard for customers to leave as they feel like they have invested a lot in it to leave abruptly
  • Integrate social communities into the membership experience. When members connect at a personal and emotional level, they tend to stay longer as they’ve made connections, and do not want to leave
  • Offer progressive benefits. For instance, members that stay for a year, receive 500 reward points, members who stay for two years, receive 1000 reward points, etc. As the value of your rewards increase, members would find it hard to leave
  • Offer members-only products and services that are not available to regular customers
  • Design a tiered membership in such a way that members would lose their membership status if they do not shop for a specific threshold annually

3. Customer lifetime value (CLTV) uplift

Membership enhances customer relationships over time. It also increases customer engagement, and their commitment for the long term. These factors eventually lead to higher CLTV. Here’s how you can increase CLTV with memberships:

  • Set up strategies to extend membership renewals. This will mean low churn rate and active members
  • Offering exciting membership perks and continuous engagement can lead to increased purchase frequency
  • Design strategies to increase average order value (AOV). Over time, these strategies compound
  • Cross sell products by using data and by offering product recommendations
  • Combine a referral program with memberships. This brings more members and increases CLTV

Implementing community-driven growth via Shopify membership programs

Here’s how you can get started with a community-driven membership program for your Shopify store:

1. Include key membership features

Including some strategic features in your membership program can provide many opportunities to build and engage member communities. Here are some features:

  • Membership tiers: By creating a tiered structure, you can increase engagement and excitement. Having a multi-tier structure enables you to offer exclusive perks to each tier. Higher level tiers get more benefits. Thus, members try to progress to upper tiers by engaging and shopping more. This also increases their long-term commitment.
  • VIP access feature: Another feature to include is VIP access. For instance, provide priority customer support to members, early access to sales, exclusive content, invitations to member-only events, and personalized experience. These ensure exclusivity and higher satisfactory levels.
  • Exclusive drops strategy: Provide exclusive products and services to members. For example, limited-edition products, seasonal collections, pre-order privileges only for members, flash sales, etc. By creating new exclusive experiences, you can enhance the value perception of the membership and customers will tend to stay for long term.

Customer communities are powerful when implemented strategically. Setting up and managing memberships requires many elements to work in sync. And that’s why integrating a membership app is critical.

You buy a mattress and see a recommendation for a mattress cover. A quick search for a t-shirt can end up with a purchase of a set of 5 t-shirts.

Product bundles are everywhere. Brands are leveraging the power of bundling to increase profits.

In this blog, we take a look at how product bundles are helping brands increase sales, what are the most effective Shopify product bundling strategies, and how to implement bundling in your store.

Let’s get started!

TL; DR

  • Product bundling creates combos and packs of related or complementary products and services offered at a discounted price as one bundle/pack.
  • Shopify product bundling leverages psychological principles, such as price anchoring and easy decision-making and increases average order value (AOV) by 30 to 50%.
  • Effective product bundling strategies include tiered bundlings, build-your-own bundle, seasonal bundles and AI-powered dynamic bundles.
  • Brands such as Mylkables (plant-based milks) and YuMove (pet supplements) use product bundling strategies to increase sales and AOV, manage inventory, and build loyal customer bases.
  • Appstle Bundles & Discounts App helps Shopify brands set up and manage bundling, pricing transparency, tracking performance metrics, collecting data, increasing conversion rate, AOV, and profits.
  • Beyond discounts, bundling is more a strategic approach to increase sales, improve inventory management, and create competitive differentiation in the industry.

What is product bundling in eCommerce?

Product bundling is a marketing and sales strategy where brands group together multiple products and sell as one bundle. Bundles often have a discounted price. The products may be related and complementary, or variations of the same item. For example, a back-to-school bundle with a bag, a lunch box, books, and pencils. Another example of a bundle is a set of five t-shirts.

While traditional bundles in physical stores are often limited to the products available in the store, eCommerce bundling offers more freedom and flexibility, as products need not be present at the time of online sales. Ecommerce bundling need not to be managed manually, but with smart apps, for example, Shopify product bundling apps.

Example: Camera kit with accessories, card reader, LED, lens, and more.

Types of bundles

There are different types of bundles, such as:

1. Build-your-own bundle

Customers can pick multiple items and create their own bundle. For example, keep one high-value product mandatory and allow customers to pick three other products from a curated set of products or any product from your site. This increases average order value (AOV).

2. Cross-sell and upsell bundle

By grouping together complementary or related products, you can encourage customers to buy a bundle that adds value to their purchase as well as increase AOV on your Shopify store. For example, bundle a phone with a protective screen guard, and a case.

3. Fixed bundle

In fixed bundles, you can add either different types of products or variations of the same product. Allow customers to buy the products individually too, but when bought as a bundle, offer them a discount.

4. Theme or seasonal bundle

Theme bundles include related or complementary products based on a theme. For example, a winter skin care bundle with a moisturizer, cleanser, and lotion. Another example is a gift set for baby girls and baby boys.

5. Subscription bundle

A popular Shopify product bundling strategy, in the subscription bundle model, customers received a box with curated products on a recurring basis. For example, a curated tea monthly subscription box. Customers only

6. Buy-one-get-one bundle

In this bundle type, customers get a free product when they buy a particular item. For example, buy one bottle of soft drink and get one free, or buy one phone and get a smart watch for free.

Why Shopify product bundling matters for merchants

The benefits of offering bundles go beyond increased revenue. Here’s why bundling matters to Shopify merchants.

  • Bundling helps merchants increase AOV as customers end up buying more than just one product. This does not require additional marketing, making it an effective conversion rate optimization (CRO) strategy
  • When existing customers buy bundles instead of single products, the revenue increase with the same traffic volume
  • Bundling helps merchants manage inventory better. For instance, merchants can add slow-selling items in bundles to sell stock
  • Merchants can optimize their inventory with the help of bundles. For instance, create seasonal bundles to sell season-based inventory
  • Offering bundles can help create unique value proposition (USP) and a competitive differentiation

The psychology behind product bundling

Bundles and combo packs encourage customers to make more purchases. So what exactly is the psychology behind bundling, and how do bundles work? Here’s how.

Price anchoring

Price anchoring is a strategy that creates a high initial price point or value anchor, which makes a discounted bundle price offer more attractive. It works on the principle that we tend to “anchor on the first piece of information we encounter”, to make purchasing decisions.

When you bundle products and services, you can create a price anchor with the original price of a product when bought individually. For instance, a bundle of 5 t-shirts offered at a price of INR 4500, and the same t-shirt bought individually at INR 500.

When customers buy the bundle of t-shirts, they will anchor it against the price of a single t-shirt. This sort of anchoring and comparing makes bundles more appealing to customers.

Discounts drive urgency without hurting margins

Even though merchants offer discounts on bundles, it doesn’t mean they are losing profit margins. In fact, when planned strategically, bundles can balance discounts with profitability.

When merchants bundle a high-margin product with low-margin products, it balances out discounts and profitability.

Another factor to note is that even though merchants offer discounts based on the number of items in a bundle, their profit margins increase because bundles increase the AOV compared to single-product sales.

Moreover, bundles can lead to the feeling of urgency and FOMO in consumers. For instance, if there’s a limited-edition bundle or seasonal bundle that will be available for a limited time, customers feel the urge to buy the bundles immediately. This increases sales and profitability.

Bundling case studies: How brands increased sales with bundling

Let’s get into the details of how and why bundling works for Shopify brands by looking at some real-life examples and bundling case studies.

Case study 1: Mylkables

Mylkables is an Australian brand that offers alternative milks. Apart from offering single products and subscriptions, the brand offers many types of bundles. The bundles include multi-pack offers as well as bundles with different types of milks.

The brand’s Combo Deals and Multiple Box Deals collections offer reduced pricing, encouraging purchases of larger quantities. Mylkables plans bundles strategically, allowing customers to choose multi-packs of the same item or try varieties by choosing bundles with a variety of milks.

Why Mylkables Shopify product bundling works:

  • The combo offers increase AOV
  • With the multi-pack bundles, customers get to try new products they might not have tried
  • Increases brand loyalty and repeat purchases
  • Subscription of bundles increases revenue as well as repeat purchases
  • Customers have many varieties to choose from, keeping monotony away

2. Case study 2: YuMove

Yumove is a pet supplements brand that offers supplements to address various pet health issues. However, their USP is they also offer supplements for humans. The brand caters to the needs of different types of pets, offering supplements for various ailments. Their ‘Dog and Me Bundle’ offers supplements for pets and humans.

Why YuMove bundling strategy works:

  • The bundling strategy extends across multiple life stages and supplement needs at each stage
  • The bundles often include complementary products so customers can try new items
  • Its subscription option makes it easy for customers to make purchase decisions for convenient long-term purchase
  • Having a wide range of supplements makes the brand a complete solutions provider, increasing sales

Bundling strategies that drive 30%+ sales growth

If you’re waiting to get started with Shopify product bundling, here are some tried and tested strategies that have helped brands increase sales by 30% and more.

1. Tiered bundles

Tiered bundles strategy works on the structure where the more customers buy, the more discount they get. For instance, ‘Buy 2, save 5%’, Buy 3, save 10%’, and so on. It works on the principle of progression of value, encouraging customers to buy more. Customers can maximize savings by choosing higher tier bundles.

To implement tiered bundles strategy on your Shopify store, follow these points:

  • Carefully calculate profit margins for each tier
  • Calculate eCommerce bundle discounts in a way that it encourages customers to purchase more and increases your profit
  • Add higher-margin products based on tiers, making it easier to sell high-value products

2. Build-your-own bundles

Build-your-own bundles strategy enables personalization. Customers can choose the products they want to add to the bundles. This Shopify product bundling strategy works well for brands that have an extensive inventory with many products and categories.

Here’s what you should do:

  • Categorize your inventory in a thoughtful way
  • Communicate about the value of these bundles to customers
  • Keep it simple so that customers understand it
  • Example: Choose any 3 products from our organic collection for 15% discount

3. Seasonal bundles

Seasonal bundles are based on purchasing patterns seen around specific times of the year. For example, during the Holiday Season and Christmas, or during school reopening time. Seasonal bundles are often for a limited time and hence there’s an urgency around them.

Here’s what you can do with seasonal bundles:

  • Create seasonal bundles based on timing and relevance
  • Use customer data from the past to create bundles
  • Launch the bundles much in advance
  • Create FOMO and urgency by offering limited-time offers
  • Example: Valentine’s Day bundles, back-to-school bundles, monsoon bundles, etc.

4. Dynamic bundles

In the ever-changing eCommerce environment, it is critical to have a pulse on your customers’ needs at all times. The best way to do so is AI. With AI, you can create dynamic bundles, even in real-time. AI-based bundles use data analysis and insights to create bundles of products customers want.

Here are some AI-based dynamic bundle tips:

  • Create dynamic bundles based on customer behavior, purchase history, and browsing patterns
  • Offer personalized dynamic bundles to increase sales
  • Choose a Shopify product bundling app that offers AI-based features
  • Continuously optimize your dynamic product bundling strategy by collecting and analyzing data

How to implement bundling on Shopify

items.html:
Subscriptions have taken over every industry, whether digital content or eCommerce. However, within subscriptions, Shopify stores can implement different revenue models.

Prepaid, pay-as-you-go, and some stores also employ hybrid models.

In this blog, we explore the critical question: prepaid vs. pay-as-you go Shopify subscriptions: which model works best for Shopify

Let’s get started!

TL; DR

  • With prepaid subscriptions, customers pay upfront. This model works best for established and high-value product brands, offering predictable cash flow and lower churn rate. However, it requires higher customer commitment.
  • With pay-as-you-go subscriptions, customers pay for the products and services they use, over time. This model works well for new brands offering experimental products. It makes customer acquisition easier. However, it has higher churn and less predictable revenue.
  • Choose the prepaid subscription structure if you have established products, price-sensitive customers, or B2B customers, and if you need a predictable cash flow.
  • Choose pay-as-you-go if your brand is new, has seasonal products, a younger target audience, and if your priority is customer acquisition.
  • Consider hybrid revenue models by offering both tiered discounts and loyalty incentives to maximize benefits of each approach. By taking a hybrid approach, you can transition customers from pay-as-you-go to prepaid, over time.

Understanding prepaid vs pay-as-you-go subscription models

Before we dive into the pros and cons of these two Shopify subscription models and which one works best for various industries, we’ll first understand the two models in detail.

What are prepaid subscriptions?

In prepaid subscriptions, customers pay in advance, upfront, for the entire subscription period. For example, pay the annual fee for newspaper subscription for the whole year. Prepaid subscriptions provide customers access to products or services they subscribed for, for the subscription period. Subscribers do not need to pay any extra charges.

Prepaid subscription benefits to customers include discounts, free shipping, freebies, etc. For Shopify merchants, prepaid subscriptions mean immediate revenue, increased cash flow, and long-term commitment by subscribers.

Example:

What are pay-as-you-go subscriptions?

In pay-as-you-go subscriptions, customers pay on a recurring basis, for example, weekly, monthly, or annually. Customers have to pay only for the products or services they use. For instance, monthly internet subscription, where customers pay for what they use.

This subscription model offers flexibility as customers do not have to pay a fixed amount. Moreover, they can stop their subscriptions based on their needs. For customers, pay-as-you-go subscriptions offer the benefits of flexibility. For Shopify merchants, this model makes it easy to attract new subscribers due to the lower commitment expectations. Brands can cater to a wider customer base and continuously engage with customers.

Example:

Industries for prepaid and pay-as-you-go subscriptions

Benefits of prepaid subscriptions

Here are some of the benefits of prepaid subscriptions for Shopify merchants:

1. Predictable revenue

In prepaid subscriptions, Shopify stores receive an upfront payment. This provides revenue predictability and cash flow, which can be helpful for budgeting and planning future expenses and investments.

2. Inventory planning

Predictable revenue and long-term commitment from subscribers helps with inventory planning. You can get a better sense of product or service requirements by clients and can fulfil them with better planning and management.

3. Higher upfront revenue

Customers pay the entire subscription amount upfront at the start of the tenure. This means Shopify brands can collect higher upfront revenue and plan how to use the cash for various business needs.

4. Customer commitment

Since subscribers pay upfront for a specific period (week, month, year), you have committed customers. Once they pay, customers might not leave you mid way, leading to less churn. This also provides you more opportunities to engage them and encourage them to renew their subscriptions.

5. Reduced operational cost

Frequent billing cycles means more operational work. But in prepaid subscriptions, customers pay once. This requires fewer billing cycles and processes, simplifying Shopify merchants’ work. This can also help you plan your subscription pricing strategy.

6. Lower churn rate

Customers have a better cost predictability and can budget for the next billing cycle to renew their subscription. This reduces churn rate for Shopify stores. Moreover, incentives such as freebies and other perks also influence subscription renewal decisions.

Benefits of pay-as-you-go subscriptions

Here are some benefits of pay-as-you-go for Shopify merchants:

1. Lower barrier to entry for customers

As customers have the option of paying in parts over the course of their subscription period, they feel more comfortable about signing up for the subscription. If the subscription fee is high in the beginning, customers tend to hesitate to commit.

2. Charge more for high consumption subscribers

Some subscribers might use more than the others. In this case, you can charge subscribers according to their usage. In the prepaid method this may not be possible. You can also collect usage-based data and insights from your subscription platform.

3. More flexible and customer-friendly

Pay-as-you-go subscription structure is more customer-friendly. Customers feel more comfortable as they have to pay for only what they use. Moreover, they are not bound or tied to a long-term commitment and can choose to unsubscribe based on their preference.

4. Scalability

Another factor that Shopify brands consider between prepaid vs pay-as-you-go subscriptions is the benefit of scaling in the pay-as-you-go model. Brands can increase revenue by scaling services as per customer demand and usage. Moreover, brands can also scale down if needed, saving costs.

Prepaid vs pay-as-you-go subscription: Drawbacks of each model

While both the Shopify subscription models have benefits, they do have some drawbacks, too.

Drawbacks of prepaid subscriptions

  • When dissatisfied customers raise refund requests, it can disrupt cash flow and operational processes
  • Dissatisfied subscribers may share negative reviews about your brand, damaging reputation
  • If your products or services are seasonal, subscribers might want to pause or stop in between
  • As prepaid subscription requires long-term commitment, it can get hard to get customers to sign up
  • Lower initial subscription conversions can lead to longer sales cycles for the business

Drawbacks of pay-as-you-go subscriptions

  • This structure tends to see a higher churn rate, which makes revenue forecasting challenging
  • Cancellation is easy and hence Shopify brands have to constantly be on their toes, prove value, invest in marketing, and engaging customers
  • Less working capital for operations and other business expenses compared to the prepaid structure
  • The payment processing fees can compound with frequent transactions, leading to lower profits
  • This model can lead to involuntary churn, which requires advanced retention tools and planning

Example:

Which subscription revenue model is best for your Shopify store?

Both these revenue structures have pros and cons. So which one is most suitable for Shopify stores? Let’s determine that for your Shopify store:

1. Product-related considerations

The type of products you offer can influence the success rate of the revenue structure. For instance, if your products are high-value and established, customers may be more willing to pay upfront and commit for the long-term.

However, if your product line is new and experimental that customers haven’t used, the pay-as-you-go model will help reduce risk for customers and work better for you. Also, for seasonal products, the pay-as-you-go model is more suitable as you can avoid untimely churn and disruptions.

Prepaid: High-value and established products and services, essential consumables

Pay-as-you-go: New product line, experimental products, seasonal products, essential consumables

Example:

2. Customer behavior

Another key factor when deciding prepaid vs pay-as-you-go subscriptions is related to your customers’ behavior. If your customers are conscious about price and on a budget and prefer lower monthly commitments, the prepaid model is more suitable.

Also, for customers who prioritize convenience, the prepaid model works better, as you can reduce recurring billing cycles. The B2B industry is known to prefer the prepaid model as it eases budgeting and taxation processes.

However, if you have younger customers who have limited spending capacity and prefer more flexibility, the pay-as-you-go subscription structure is more suitable.

Prepaid: Price-sensitive customers, convenience-focused, B2B

Pay-as-you-go: Younger demographic with limited budget

3. Industry considerations

Your Shopify store’s position in the market and in your niche can also help you decide which pricing model would be best for your business. For instance, if your brand is established and known and can leverage trust, it would be easy for you to sell prepaid subscriptions.

However, if your brand is new, the pay-as-you-go subscription structure would be more beneficial to you. Depending on your industry, if your focus is more on offering value, the pay-as-you-go model would work better.

Conversely, if your brand positions itself as a premium name in your niche, it is better to go for a prepaid structure as it also enables you to offer discounts based on tiers.

Prepaid: Established, premium positioning

Pay-as-you-go: New brands, value-focused brands

4. Hybrid models

Many Shopify merchants take the hybrid approach, combining the benefits of both the models. For instance, merchants offer flexible prepaid options by allowing customers to pause subscriptions, offer refunds with a processing fee, offer credit systems for unused portions, and allow customers to make changes to their subscription mid-way.

Shopify merchants also use the tiered subscription approach, offering progressive discounts. For instance, 10% on quarterly payment, 20% on annual payment, and offer premium features to customers who pay the entire amount upfront.

You can also offer loyalty-driven prepaid incentives. Offer prepaid discounts once subscribers successfully pay a few monthly cycles. This helps to retain them. Additionally, you can offer prepaid rewards to long-term pay-as-you-go customers.

Prepaid vs. pay-as-you-go Shopify subscriptions: What will you choose?

Choose the subscription revenue model best suited to your business based on the pros and cons, your industry, and customer preference.

However, once you choose, you have to integrate the revenue system within your Shopify store with the help of a smart subscription app.

items.html:
Most eCommerce beauty brands offer some sort of loyalty program to customers. When done right, membership and loyalty programs can benefit brands in many ways.

From increasing sales and customer lifetime value (CLV) to increasing loyalty, the benefits of beauty loyalty programs are many. And some brands have aced their loyalty programs.

For instance, Lancome. In this blog, we breakdown its loyalty program to learn tips, strategies, and best practices.

Let’s get started!

TL;DR

  • Lancome offers an effective beauty loyalty program that is loved by its customers.
  • The loyalty program is simple with three tiers – Rose Gold, Gold, and Platinum.
  • The brand has designed easy ways to earn points.
  • The benefits of the loyalty program go beyond transactions, for example, free shipping, personalized recommendations, and exclusive access.
  • Tiered structure and gamification motivates customers to reach higher levels for better perks.
  • Welcome bonuses, referral rewards, and first-purchase incentives attract new customers.
  • Tier-specific perks and exclusive access make members feel special.

What is the My Lancôme Rewards Beauty loyalty program?

Lancome is a beauty brand that offers cosmetics, skincare, perfumes, and more. It is among the most popular international beauty brands. The brand has a successful loyalty program that offers its customers reward points, and other benefits, such as free shipping, a birthday gift, member only offers, and more.

Lancôme loyalty program analysis and strategy breakdown

Here are the features and strategies that make Lancome’s loyalty program stand out and why customers love the brand so much. Apply these beauty brand membership tips in your Shopify store.

1. Simple loyalty program structure

Customers look for simple and easy experiences with brands. Complicated structures can keep them away from interacting with brands. Lancome has created a simple loyalty structure. Customers can earn points, get rewards, and enjoy the benefits of the membership.

For instance, the loyalty program is complimentary. Members earn 10 points for every $1 they spend, as well as additional points for various activities, such as sharing reviews, enrolling in auto-replenishment, etc.

The tiered loyalty program has three tiers:

1. Rose Gold Tier

Customers in the Rose Gold Tier can earn up to 1900 points annually. They receive perks, including free shipping on orders worth $49 and more, a 20% discount as a birthday gift, and early access to promotions and launches.

2. Gold Tier

The Gold Tier is for customers who earn up to 6,499 points, offers free shipping on all orders, and a 20% birthday discount along with 100 bonus points.

3. Platinum Tier

The Platinum Tier offers the most perks. Customers who earn 6500 points annually can

Takeaway: Lancome’s tiered structure is gamified in a way that encourages customers to earn more points for more benefits. Such gamification not only offers more points to customers, it also increases their engagement levels and keeps them interested. A key requirement in the over-saturated world of eCommerce loyalty and membership programs.

2. Easy ways to earn points

The loyalty program has been designed in a way that customers can earn points easily. This sort of instant gratification encourages customers to earn more points. Here are the activities for which customers get points:

  • Points for every $1 spend
  • Points for signing up for text messages
  • For completing a virtual service
  • Bonus points for first purchase
  • For writing a review

Takeaway: Lancome’s points system has many small elements that make it stand out. It has engagement integrated within the points structure (customers are expected to perform an activity and engage to earn points). Besides, the welcome offer of bonus points plays a key role in attracting new customers.

3. Benefits beyond points

With every brand offering a rewards program and points, these perks no longer satisfy customers. Today’s customers expect non-transactional perks, too. Think personalization, community, exclusivity, special events, surprises, social causes, and more.

Here’s how Lancome meets these member expectations:

  • Free shipping on orders
  • Birthday discount
  • Early access to sales and launches
  • Members-only offers
  • Bonus points on special days
  • Welcome bonus points

Takeaway: Shopify beauty stores can offer benefits that are not related to purchases. Emotional connection helps drive loyalty more effectively than points.

4. Gamification

Lancome’s loyalty program is gamified with a tiered structure. Gamification helps make membership programs more interesting, ensuring members stay excited.

Lancome has three tiers, differentiated by the number of points customers earn annually. To jump to a higher tier, members have to make more purchases, and earn more points. It works on the principle of motivation. Customers strive to get recognized and participate in game-like experiences.

Takeaway: By creating clear tiers and differentiating by exclusive perks, you can increase engagement and motivate continued participation by members.

5. Customer acquisition features

Customer acquisition rate is a key metric that brands measure continuously. Lancome loyalty program has implemented certain features that focus on customer acquisition. For instance, offering bonus points as a welcome incentive. New members also get discounts and free samples for joining the membership program.

Apart from welcome incentives, the brand has also set up a referral program. The program is designed to encourage members to refer friends. In return, both the referee and the referred customer get points. This enhances customer loyalty and attracts new members.

Takeaway: Combining loyalty programs with referral programs attracts new customers and leverages existing loyal members as brand advocates. This is a cost-effective customer acquisition strategy.

6. Exclusivity

One of the most essential elements of loyalty programs is exclusivity. Customers want to feel special and exclusive. Lancome understands this customer need. The brand offers perks that are exclusive to each of its three tiers.

For instance, some of the exclusive benefits members enjoy are limited-edition products, first access to new launches, sales, and more.

Takeaway: Offering exclusive perks creates a sense of special status and belonging to the brand. It makes members feel valued and distinguished, driving retention and aspiration to progress to higher tiers.

7. Seamless mobile experience

Today’s savvy customers expect brands to offer the most convenient experience on all platforms, web and mobile. Lancome loyalty members can easily access and use the loyalty membership via mobile devices.

The loyalty program web page is optimized for mobile with effective UI and UX, ensuring members have a smooth omnichannel experience, even when they access the website on a small screen.

Takeaway: Mobile-optimized experience leads to more engagement, removes friction, and enhances satisfaction levels.

Takeaways from My Lancome Rewards beauty loyalty program and how to apply them to your program

Lancome beauty loyalty program takeaways How to apply these beauty brand membership tips in your Shopify store
Simple three-tiered loyalty structure
  • Create 2-3 simple tiers with benefits
  • Use a smart loyalty app
  • Set achievable point thresholds
  • Use attractive tier names
  • Ensure each tier offers meaningful value
Multiple ways to earn points
  • Offer welcome points to increase sign-ups
  • Reward referrals and reviews
  • Create seasonal point multipliers
  • Incentivize non-purchase behaviours
Benefits beyond transactions
  • Offer exclusive access to new products
  • Create member-only content
  • Provide personalized recommendations
  • Host virtual or in-person member events
  • Offer expert consultations or styling sessions
Gamified loyalty program
  • Add progress bars for tier advancement
  • Create point challenges and missions
  • Use badges for achievements
  • Add surprise and delight elements
Customer acquisition focus
  • Offer bonus welcome reward points
  • Implement double-sided referral incentives
  • Create limited-time joining bonuses
  • Make first-purchase rewards attractive
  • Use social proof to encourage sign-ups
Exclusivity
  • Create members-only product collections
  • Offer early access to sales and launches
  • Develop tier-specific exclusive content
  • Provide premium customer service for top tiers
  • Use exclusive branding and messaging
Omnichannel experience
  • Optimize loyalty pages for mobile devices
  • Create responsive design for all screen sizes
  • Integrate loyalty features into mobile app
  • Provide consistent experience across channels
  • Make point checking and redemption effortless

Summing up – Set up a successful loyalty program

This Lancome loyalty program analysis offers the various features and strategies that make the program one of the most effective programs loved by customers.

If you’re looking to revamp or set up a new loyalty program on your Shopify store, apply these strategies. However, remember to keep your program relevant to your customer needs. Hence, start by one or two strategies and keep experimenting as you go.

items.excerpt: Did you know 97% of eCommerce traffic leaves without making purchases. This is a major problem for online stores across industries. items.html:
Did you know 97% of eCommerce traffic leaves without making purchases. This is a major problem for online stores across industries.

Is there a way to increase first-time visitor sales and repeat purchases?

There is! Bundled subscriptions can increase first-order conversion rates.

In this blog, we explore all about subscription bundles and how you can maximize conversions from it.

TL;DR

  • 97% of eCommerce visitors leave without making purchases, making first order conversion rates a critical challenge.
  • Bundled subscriptions is an effective strategy, combining multiple products into recurring deliveries, offering higher perceived value and convenience.
  • Subscription bundles offer cost savings to customers, convenience, increase product discovery, provide predictable revenue to Shopify stores, and help with customer retention.
  • Implementing an effective subscription bundle strategy for increasing first order conversion rates involves steps such as identifying products for bundles, designing the structure, deciding pricing for each tier, and optimizing checkout.
  • Bundled subscriptions help increase first purchase conversion rates by combining discounted bundles with the convenience of recurring deliveries, leading to benefits for customers and Shopify brands.

What are bundled subscriptions?

Bundled subscriptions combine bundles and subscriptions. The bundle contains multiple products, which is sent as a recurring delivery to subscribers. Unlike single-product subscriptions, bundles offer many different products/ services that address different customer needs.

Offering bundled subscriptions is an effective strategy to boost conversions and increase repeat sales. It has a higher perceived value and is more convenient for customers.

Example

Why do bundled subscriptions work?

When you combine bundles and subscriptions, the potential for sales increases as it provides the benefits of both elements. Let’s understand all the key reasons why bundled subscriptions are effective for Shopify stores.

1. Convenience

With subscription bundles, customers have the convenience of receiving all products they need in one delivery. They do not have to wait or worry, nor do they have to keep ordering these products repeatedly.

2. Cost savings

Customers get discounts on bundles as opposed to when they buy single items separately. This price benefit motivates customers to buy more. Moreover, over time, they save a significant amount of money.

3. Product discovery

Bundled subscriptions also lead to new product discovery. You can add new items in the bundles, which customers may not have used before. Adding one new product with every delivery can help you introduce new products to customers.

4. Easy decision-making

When you offer a curated and personalized selection of products to customers, it reduces decision fatigue, making first-order conversion rates higher. Today’s customers prefer personalized recommendations and experiences such as bundled subscriptions.

5. Predictable revenue

Subscriptions create recurring revenue for your business. Moreover, bundled subscriptions increase average order value (AOV). These aspects create predictable and recurring revenue for your Shopify store.

6. Long-term customer relationships

When customers start experiencing benefits such as convenience, cost-savings, personalization, and a seamless buying journey over time, they feel more satisfied. This leads to less churn and more retention, leading to long-term customers.

Example: Beauty brand bundled subscription

Let’s understand more about how bundle subscriptions increase first-order conversion rates with an example of a beauty brand implementing this strategy.

A beauty brand created three bundle subscription tiers:

1. Basic: Cleanser + moisturizer ($25 per month)

2. Complete: Cleanser + moisturizer + serum + mask ($25 per month)

3. Premium: Cleanser + moisturizer + serum + mask + exclusive treatments ($50 per month)

The brand then integrated other elements into these bundle subscriptions. For instance, sharing educational content about skincare, offered seasonal variations in the subscriptions, created a community of subscribers, and ensured efficient customer support.

How to implement bundled subscriptions to increase first order conversion rates?

Subscription bundle strategies work well when done properly from the start. Here are the steps to follow to set up your Shopify bundle subscriptions.

Step 1. Identify bundling possibilities

Analyze your existing product catalog and customer data to identify bundling opportunities. For instance, find out which products are often bought together, which items complement your star products, and which products when bundled together can solve customers’ problems.

Apart from product pairing insights, understand customers shopping habits, analyze competitors’ bundle offering, gather information from customer support queries, and more. All this information can throw light on which products you could bundle together for subscriptions.

Example:

Step 2: Design your bundle structure

The next step is to design your bundled subscription strategy or structure. You will have to decide on factors such as the number of tiers, pricing for each tier, which products and how many will you include in each tier, etc. Let’s look at an example of a tiered bundle subscription strategy.

1. Entry-level bundle subscription

In this tier, you can offer 2 to 3 products, keep the lowest pricing to make it easy for customers to sign up and for you to increase first order conversion rates. In this tier, you could offer your most popular star products at a nominal discount rate, for example, 15%. Having your fast-selling products in this bundled subscription leads to higher conversions because customers already like those items.

2. Premium bundle

This bundle can include 4 to 5 bestsellers combined with complementary items. For instance, if your skincare products are top sellers, add a cosmetics product in the bundle. Offer the best value proposition in terms of discounts and savings, for example, 20% discount. You could also include one premium product in this bundle, to increase the potential of first order conversion rates.

3. Ultimate bundle

In the last tier, offer more than 6 or 7 products that are high-value and exclusive. This bundle should offer the highest discounts, for example, 30%. Moreover, include limited-edition or seasonal products in the bundle and appeal to your most engaged and loyal customers.

Step 3. Decide your pricing strategy

Design your pricing strategy in a way that it offers maximum value to customers but at the same time, does not eat into your profits. For instance, you could offer a 20% to 35% discount but your profit margin should still remain 40% to 50%.

Try a different percentage rate and figure which one is most lucrative. You could also consider subscription-based pricing. For example, an additional 5% off on weekly subscriptions.

Some other things to implement are psychological pricing tactics, such as charm pricing, show per-unit pricing compared to bundled pricing, offer multiple subscription period options, and create urgency with limited pricing, etc.

Step 4. Create multiple product-pairing strategies

There are many different ways in which you can bundle products. And while one pairing concept might work better than the other, it is always good to have a few different strategies. This ensures you cater to all potential clients and increase first order conversion rates.

For example, you can take the complementary approach. Combine coffee beans with a grinder and filters. Or pet food, treats, and supplements. Another way to bundle items is to take the problem-solving approach. Identify customer problems and bundle together all the products that can help solve that problem. For example, travel essentials bundles.

Step 5. Checkout optimization for bundled subscriptions

Checkout is the stage where there are the highest number of customer dropouts. To drive more first order conversion rates, optimize your checkout process. Let’s look at some ways of eCommerce conversion optimization for the checkout process on Shopify stores:

  • Keep checkout minimal to a few steps, for example, 3 to 4 easy steps
  • Provide the guest checkout option
  • Display bundle savings prominently
  • Display the benefits of subscriptions, example, free shipping, discounts, etc.
  • Display trust signals, such as testimonials, badges, etc.
  • Provide an easy cancellation option
  • Optimize for mobile with a mobile-friendly checkout flow

Metrics to track for improving first order conversion rates

To consistently improve first purchase conversion rates, you have to put in continuous effort. Tracking and measuring key metrics can help you find gaps and double up on aspects that are working well. Here are some metrics to track.

1. Conversion rate

Measure conversion rates of bundles – the percentage of visitors who purchase bundles. You should also measure first-time buyer conversion rate, and cart abandonment rate. Measuring AOV of bundles and single products can also help you with conversion optimization.

2. Subscription metrics

Measure customer lifetime value (CLV) to track long-term value of subscribers. For measuring monthly revenue from bundled subscriptions, track monthly recurring revenue (MRR). By measuring time to second purchase, you can get a sense of how quickly first-time subscribers return for more.

3. Engagement metrics

Engagement metrics are an indicator of how much time and interest customers are giving to your bundled subscriptions. You can measure metrics such as email open rate, click-through rates of emails, customer satisfaction scores, and referral rates.

Wrapping up – how to improve first purchase conversion rates for your Shopify store?

Setting up a subscription bundles strategy can help increase first order conversions on your Shopify store. However, it has to be efficiently planned and managed.

For that, you need a smart app like Appstle. Appstle Subscriptions App and Appstle Bundles & Discounts can provide a comprehensive set of features required for a successful bundle subscription strategy.

items.excerpt: Subscriptions have taken over every industry. Brands selling products and services are offering subscriptions. But there’s one strategy that has potential to increase eCommerce subscription conversions — free trials. In this blog, we explore how free trials help with eCommerce customer…
items.html:
Subscriptions have taken over every industry. Brands selling products and services are offering subscriptions. However, with increasing competition in the subscription market, increasing conversion rate has become harder.

But there’s one strategy that has potential to increase eCommerce subscription conversions — free trials.

In this blog, we explore how free trials help with eCommerce customer acquisition, its pros and cons, how to set up an effective free trials structure for your subscription business, and more.

Let’s get started!

TL;DR

  • Free trials can lead to subscription conversions, when done right.
  • Free trials for subscriptions help reduce risk perception, demonstrate value, build trust, and enable data collection, which has a positive effect on eCommerce subscription conversion rate.
  • Free trials have some drawbacks, such as operational complexity, lower perceived value of free things, and conversion timing pressure that could negatively impact conversion rate.
  • A successful free trial strategy involves a strategic structure with premium-feature access, a smooth onboarding experience for customers, continuous engagement tactics, a psychology-driven design, and A/B testing for features and flows.
  • To design and set up a free trial strategy for subscriptions requires the integration of a smart tool such as Appstle Subscription App, enabling subscription conversions with multiple key features.

What are eCommerce subscription free trials?

You might have come across free trials when exploring a new product or service. For example, Spotify, software solutions (Canva, ChatGPT) have free trials of their premium plans, etc. Free trial is a subscription marketing tactic that allows brands to offer their services, or some of the services for free. Free trials are typically for a fixed duration, such as a week, 15 days or 30 days. Customers can choose to sign up for paid subscriptions after the free trial period ends.

Free trials for eCommerce subscription conversion

pros and cons

Free trials have many benefits as well as disadvantages for eCommerce brands. While free trial helps drive eCommerce subscription conversions, at times, it can also deter customers from signing up. Let’s look at its pros and cons.

Subscription free trial pros

1. It impacts customer psychology

When customers have the option of a free trial before signing up, it removes the risk element, making it easy for them to do a trial of the new service. The psychological safety factor is beneficial for brands when targeting high-value subscription plans, launching complex software that requires initial learning, and services competing against market competition.

2. Brands can demonstrate value

Unless customers try, they will not know how good your product/service is. With free trials, you can demonstrate your product’s true value. When customers try your product, they can compare its features with what they read in the marketing material. Moreover, they can experience the user interface and know how your product can resolve their problems. Free trial is a strategic pricing tactic that helps you enhance customers’ perceived value of your subscription plans.

3. Help with building trust

When customers have free trials and like the product, it helps build trust and confidence in the brand. Many times, this can lead to social proof for the brand. For instance, the customer sharing a video of their free trial. Besides, customers might also bring word-of-mouth referrals, increasing subscription conversions for eCommerce brands.

4. Data collection and personalization

Apart from direct subscription marketing, free trials also help with data collection. By offering free trials, brands can gather customer data, specifically, behavioral data. This data and insights can be used to create personalized onboarding experiences and targeted campaigns for marketing. Additionally, brands can also use data for product improvements.

Subscription free trial cons

1. Misuse of free trial

Not all people who take free trials are genuine. Some may repeatedly use the free trial offer using different names and email ids, some may use the free trial just for research purposes, and some may take all the benefits of free trials but never convert. This is one of the biggest subscription free trial strategy drawbacks.

2. Operational complexity

Free trials can add to the operational costs. For instance, brands with tiered subscription models have to offer customer support, incur infrastructure costs, spend on fraud management and prevention, and process payments, among other processes, to each tier. This increases operational complexity.

3. Lower value perception

It is human psychology – we perceive free things as being of low value. This can impact customers’ decision to sign up for subscription plans. Also, free trials can make it difficult for brands to justify premium pricing.

4. Conversion timing challenge

Free trial periods are often for a limited time. This can lead to the feeling of urgency or rushed decision-making for customers. Customers may not be ready to make sign-up decisions within the specified time.

How to set up effective free trials for eCommerce subscription conversions

Setting up an effective subscription free trial strategy is key to driving conversions. Here is a step-by-step guide for your Shopify subscription business.

1. Define your objectives

When setting up free trials for your subscriptions, create a strategic plan from the start. That begins by defining your subscription goals. For instance, if your goal is to educate your target audience or is it to drive conversions? Based on this, you will set up metrics to measure, such as conversion rate, customer lifetime value, and churn rate, etc. Your goals will also define your target audience – new customers/markets, or existing customer base.

2. Define free trial structure

Define the structure of the free trial. It is essential to have clarity of the structure if you want to maximize eCommerce subscription conversions. Here are the factors you must decide upon:

  • Set the time limit for free trial – 7, 14, or 30 days
  • Decide feature access for free trial
  • Usage based trial – access until a specific threshold
  • Hybrid structure – combine time and feature limitations

3. Set up account management

Decide the account management system. This step is critical as it directly impacts your Shopify conversions. Ensure the sign up process is easy, including social login, and a short form. Also, indicate trial period status on different pages and throughout the customer interface. By setting up automated billing transitions, you can increase conversions. Use a smart tool such as Appstle Subscription app to set up and manage subscriptions.

4. Optimize onboarding

After the sign up process, the next important step in the onboarding. It’s the stage where you can set the foundation of your relationship with customers. Here are some tips to follow:

  • Share different features one by one
  • Engage them with guided tutorials and interactive walkthroughs
  • Introduce milestone-based engagement campaigns
  • Integrate systems to flag low engagement so you can work on further optimization

5. Set payment systems

Another critical aspect that impacts eCommerce subscription conversions is the payment infrastructure. A few features you will have to decide on are whether you want a pre-authorization or post-trial billing system, choose the different payment methods and support required, considerations for international pricing and currency, and subscription management and modification features.

6. Conversion optimization

When you run free trials, you have to ensure customers end up liking your product and there are maximum conversions. Here are a few ways to do so:

  • Identify the moment when free trial users notice value in your product
  • Collect that of user behavior to gain insights on actions that lead to conversions
  • Design your onboarding flow in a way that it drives actions you want from users
  • Offer personalized recommendations based on user profile

7. Continuous engagement

Once your customers are onboarded, it’s time to ensure they remain engaged with your product, are curious, and want to discover more of it. How do you do that? Introduce your product features progressively one by one throughout the trial period. Regularly communicate with them, for example, ask them if they require help. Additionally, keep sharing educational content with them and provide them access to communities and peer groups you’re created.

8. Run subscription conversion campaigns

To drive more conversions, consistent effort is a must. Try these conversion strategies:

  • Run conversion campaigns on multiple channels – email, SMS, WhatsApp, etc.
  • Focus on demonstrating value through your messaging, not discounts
  • Create urgency without pressurizing customers
  • Offer personalized incentives based on customers’ usage patterns

9. Run A/B tests

To ensure your systems align with customer preference and lead to more conversions, run A/B tests. For instance, try different trial periods and identify which trial periods lead to more conversions. Also try out different onboarding sequences, for example, guided and automated. Another test you could run is to share credit card details and without sharing. You can also test different communication timings to identify which brings more conversions.

Conversion psychology: why free trials work for subscriptions?

Offering free trials for subscriptions impacts customer psychology in many different ways. From reciprocity principle to endowment effect, here are some ways in which free trials affect human psychology and drive conversions.

1. The endowment effect

People who engage in free trials of products and services, often integrate them into their workflows. This makes it difficult to stop or discontinue using it. The result? Discontinuing might seem more like a loss than as avoiding a purchase. This is endowment effect psychology, where people value something more if they own it.

2. Social proof and commitment consistency

When free trial users share about their experience on social media or customize the product, it strengthens their commitment, increasing the likelihood of conversions. Also, when the free trial involves others (for example, a work team), it increases conversion potential.

3. Loss aversion psychology

Once we try something that seems to be working well, we often fear losing those set workflows, data, and settings. This need for not losing access leads to more conversions.

4. Reciprocity principle

It is human nature – once we agree to take something free, we feel obliged to make the purchase and convert. When you offer a free trial, it leads to a psychological willingness to buy the subscription.

Ecommerce subscription conversions example

Let’s understand how free trials increase conversions with an example from the subscription industry.

An e-learning subscription platform offered professional development courses. The platform offered a free trial with limited features for the duration of 30 days. Even though the platform saw high signups for the free trial, it failed to lead to higher conversion rate.

The brand decided to run an A/B test with a different free trial structure. In the other structure, the brand offered a free trial for a shorter duration (one week) and access to all its premium features.

The result: The platform saw a higher conversion rate in the second structure, which was for a shorter duration but with all its premium features.

Takeaways:

  • Customers perceive higher value in premium subscription plans that have advanced features
  • Longer duration free trials do not always lead to more conversions. They may have a reverse effect on conversions, making customers take undue advantage of the free service

Summing up: free trials to increase eCommerce subscription conversions

Do free trials increase trial to paid conversions? Yes, they do, provided the subscription free trial strategy is well defined and planned. In this blog, we’ve discussed how you can drive more conversions through free trials.

However, to ensure your free trial strategy functions smoothly, you will require a smart partner, such as Appstle Subscriptions App.

The app is designed to help you set up and manage subscriptions, including free trial plans. The app allows different types of subscription plans, easy subscription management, billing and payments, customization, and other features.
