items.html:
While most brands set up bundles to sell products in bulk and volume, the pricing and discounting strategies often fail to provide maximum gains.

The best bulk discount strategies have to take into account various factors, such as market demand, customer preference, technology, among others.

In this blog, we take a comprehensive look at Shopify volume discount, what it is, trends, how to set up volume discounts on Shopify and more.

Let’s get started.

TL;DR

  • Volume discounting refers to reduced or discounted pricing when customers buy large quantities.
  • Trends in volume discounting include AI-powered dynamic pricing, mobile-first design, personalization, and real-time inventory management.
  • Shopify volume discount strategies, such as Tiered discount, fixed discount, and seasonal discounts are the most effective.

Volume discount benefits Shopify brands by increasing AOV, reducing cart abandonment, and increasing customer retention rates.

What is volume discounting?

Volume discounting refers to a reduced price offered on the purchase of a large quantity. For instance, when customers buy a bundle of 10 instead of buying just one piece, they get a discounted price. This is volume discounting.

Volume discounting is a key sales and marketing strategy in many industries. For example, groceries, fashion, health and wellness, stationery, cosmetics, among others.

Volume discount overview and trends 2025

Ecommerce brands continuously enhance strategies to sell products in volume and bulk. For instance, AI-based discounting, personalization, and more. Here are some trends that will help you plan your Shopify bulk pricing strategy.

1. AI-powered dynamic pricing

AI tools integrated within Shopify stores have the intelligence to automatically adjust discounts based on inventory levels, demand, seasonality, and customer behavior. Merchants are using machine learning and AI to offer dynamic pricing and volume discounts.

2. Mobile-first design

50 to 70% of customers start their shopping journey by checking prices on their mobile phones. With an increase in mobile commerce, brands are optimizing volume discounts for touch interfaces and small screens. Since a large amount of traffic comes from mobile devices, creating a mobile-first design for volume discounts is a must.

3. Personalization

Customer segmentation helps brands offer personalized experiences. Brands offer different volume discounts to different segments. Segmentation is based on purchase history, location, customer lifetime value (CLV), etc.

4. Real-time inventory integration

The inventory accuracy rate of an average retail store in the US is just 63%. Shopify stores that integrate real-time inventory management using digital tools are able to reach higher accuracy levels. What is more, they avoid overselling. This helps maximize revenue from the inventory. For example, volume discounts adjust based on real-time inventory levels.

Appstle Bundle & Discounts for Shopify bulk pricing strategy

Appstle Bundles & Discounts App is designed for Shopify and Shopify Plus stores to increase AOV and revenue with strategic product bundling and volume packs. The app enables multiple bundle types and helps boost sales with targeted discounting.

Appstle Bundles & Discounts features:

  • Tiered volume pricing with unlimited discount tiers
  • Volume discounts for different product categories
  • Dynamic discounting based on inventory – increasing discounts with increasing quantities
  • Customization for color, font, layout, and positioning
  • Mobile-responsive design for all devices
  • Real-time notifications to customers about savings
  • Analytics to track performance across all analytics platforms
  • A/B testing for different discount structures
  • Automatic inventory management based on stock levels
  • AI-powered revenue optimization, for example, recommendations

Shopify volume discount pricing strategies

Depending on the industry and product type, you can offer volume discounts in various ways. Some of the effective strategies for bulk discounts for Shopify stores are tiered pricing and fixed discounts. Here, we explore some volume pricing strategies.

1. Tiered discount strategy

A straightforward strategy based on volume, in this method, you offer more discounts on larger volumes. For example, 3 to 5 pieces (5% discount), 6 to 10 pieces (10% discount), and so on and so forth. This kind of volume discounting encourages customers to purchase more in order to avail better prices, and thus, increases the AOV.

2. Fixed volume discount

Fixed volume pricing offers a pre-defined fixed discount on a specified number of pieces. For example, 1 piece ($10), 5 pieces $45 ($9 each piece), 10 pieces $80 ($8 per piece), and so on and so forth. This sort of volume discounting helps increase AOV and maintain margins on smaller volumes.

3. Seasonal volume discount strategy

Yet another Shopify volume discount strategy is designed around seasons. Seasonal bundles and volume discounts can be based on festivals, events, annual occasions, etc. For instance, selling large volumes or bundles during the festive season. Here’s an example:

  • 15% volume discount on gift purchases during the festive time
  • Free shipping on bulk orders
  • After the festival, clearance volume pricing 20% discount

Best practices for volume discounting in 2025

With increasing competition in the eCommerce space, and evolving digital technologies, it is essential for Shopify brands to follow the best practices to offer volume discounts. In this section, we look at the best practices and tips you must follow in 2025.

1. Mention the value clearly

The most effective way to drive volume sales is to clearly show savings to customers. Here are some tips to follow:

  • Show total savings amount with the bundle or pack
  • Display per unit savings
  • Show original price of single unit and discounted price when bought in bulk
  • Use a progress indicator. For example, ‘Add 1 more item to save 20%’
  • Optimize layout for mobile so that discount tables are easily scrollable

2. Use psychological pricing techniques

Use tactics to influence customers’ purchase decisions via psychological effect. Here are some tactics of psychological pricing.

  • Implement odd-even charm pricing, example, if the price is $50, write $49.99
  • Use FOMO tactic – Limited time offer extra 5% on bulk orders
  • Display social proof, example, 80% of customers buy the pack of 10
  • Run flash discounts on packs and bundles, example, 10% off for the next 2 hours

3. Implement customer segmentation

Segmenting customers into different categories enables you to offer discounts based on segments. When promoted to target segments, it can increase sales. Here are some tips:

  • Create a segment of new customers
  • Create lower threshold requirements for new customers
  • Offer higher discount and free shipping to new customers
  • Create a segment of returning customers
  • Offer loyalty-based discount, early access to bulk promotions, exclusive pricing, etc.
  • Create a segment for B2B customers
  • Offer custom volume pricing to B2B customers

4. Cross-selling integration

An effective technique for Shopify volume discounts is cross-selling. With cross-selling, you can increase AOV, increase customer satisfaction by offering more discounts, and improve the overall experience for customers. Here are some ways to implement cross-selling for bulk discount on Shopify.

  • Suggest bundles as a recommendation to reach volume thresholds for discounts. For example, these could be complementary products
  • Apply discounts based on category of products. This can help increase variety in one bundle or pack
  • Automate upselling and cross-selling. For example, set automated prompts – Buy 1 more item to unlock 10% discount

Automate inventory management

When integrating volume discounts on Shopify stores, proper management of the inventory is critical. Any gaps and errors in inventory management can disrupt your sales chain and impact site performance. Here are some tips to follow:

  • Automate volume discounts based on inventory levels
  • Set volume discount rules based on seasons and inventory cycles. Use past data
  • Use high volume discount strategy to clear slow-moving inventory

Benefits of Shopify volume discount

Implementing Shopify bulk pricing strategy has many benefits for your store. Let’s look at some here:

1. Increase average order value

Volume or bulk pricing offers lead to customers adding more products in order to reach a discount threshold. This leads to higher revenue and increased customer lifetime value.

2. Reduce cart abandonment

Another noticeable benefit of Shopify volume discounts is reduced cart abandonment. People feel encouraged to make purchases when they see savings potential. Moreover, automated discount applications in the checkout process removes friction. Mobile-optimized sites improve bundle user experience, leading to reduced cart abandonment.

3. Higher customer acquisition and retention

Discounted prices attract customers. Continued discounts via subscriptions help with retention. When customers who buy in bulk get discounts, they become repeat customers. Moreover, they also share referrals and bring potential customers.

4. Competitive advantage

Offering wholesale pricing on Shopify helps brands differentiate from competitors. Higher discounts and benefits increase value perception in the market and hence, brand growth.

Important factors for offering volume discounts

Factor in these important aspects when planning your Shopify volume discounts.

  • Pricing laws: Consider pricing laws based on industry, product, location, and other factors. Certain regions have restrictions on pricing and regulations to follow. It is critical to follow pricing laws in order to avoid penalties
  • Disclosure requirement: Clearly mention specific aspects, such as quantity requirements, eligibility, expiration dates, usage limitations, return and refund policies, etc.
  • Tax regulations: Consider tax calculations in discounted prices. Follow tax compliance based on location and industry, and maintain proper documentation
  • International VAT: If you serve international locations, factor in compliance and VAT regulations, and other costs when offering volume discounts
  • Data protection: Another important factor to consider in Shopify volume discounts is the protection of customer data,compliance with GDPR, CCPA, and more.

Wrapping up – how to set up volume discounts in Shopify in 2025

Offering volume discounts is the best strategy to increase sales and AOV. However, it is critical to craft effective strategies, understand your target audience, implement data-driven campaigns, and consider various other factors.

To do so, you will require a smart app, such as Appstle Bundles & Discounts App. The app has in-built features that help with setting up, automation, data analysis, and marketing for Shopify volume discounts.

items.excerpt: TL;DR If you’re a luxury brand or aspiring to reach that position, focusing on your loyalty program is essential. In the luxury industry, points and discounts do not build loyalty. Then what does? Think unique experiences, exclusivity, personalization, and trust. Learn how to build a luxury loyalty program for your brand, and how to make…
items.html:
TL;DR

  • Luxury loyalty programs’ success is based on exclusivity, experiences, tier-based exclusive benefits, and personalization, not traditional points or discounts.
  • Global luxury brands Louis Vuitton offers omnichannel loyalty programs featuring blockchain authentication, monthly intimate salons and master craftspeople interactions. Hermes takes an informal relationship-based loyalty approach.
  • 78% of affluent consumers consider loyalty programs essential. Success comes from creating exclusive communities and memorable experiences based on money-can’t-buy principles.

If you’re a luxury brand or aspiring to reach that position, focusing on your loyalty program is essential.

In the luxury industry, points and discounts do not build loyalty. Then what does? Think unique experiences, exclusivity, personalization, and trust.

Learn how to build a luxury loyalty program for your brand, and how to make it a success.

Let’s get started.

Trends in luxury brand loyalty programs

Studies show that up to 28% of luxury goods sales will be online. And 78% of affluent individuals consider loyalty programs an essential for brand relationships. This makes it critical for brands to focus on loyalty programs, both online and physical. Another study shows paid loyalty programs drive more engagement than free programs. Let’s understand how luxury brands build loyalty in this age of high competition.

1. Experiential elements

Luxury loyalty programs engage high-end customers through cultural events, such as private viewings of new collections, exclusive member clubs, and more. These experiential rewards provide a sense of community with likeminded people and build a community of customers that may extend into personal networks.

2. Tier-based structure

Luxury brands create exclusive circles of customer segments by offering tier-based loyalty programs. Depending on the program structure, customers can either be paid members if the program is paid, or join tiers in a more organic way, by making purchases, interacting and engaging with brands.

3. Sustainability

Luxury loyalty programs are not only about gifts anymore. Consumers like to be associated with programs that have a sustainability aspect, such as social and environmental causes. Loyalty members participate in charitable events, follow ethical consumption, and choose brands whose values they align with.

4. Personalization

Luxury brand loyalty programs integrate personalization in various creative ways. Using customer data, brands understand customer needs, offer relevant experiences, and create unique experiences exclusive to loyalty customer segments. Studies show that offering exclusive loyalty benefits and personalization has shown a 2 to 4% gross margin point increase in loyalty programs.

Luxury loyalty programs case study

Most luxury brands have loyalty programs. However, their programs tend to be extremely unique and exclusive. Here are some luxury brand loyalty examples to learn from.

Case study 1 – Louis Vuitton

Louis Vuitton’s My LV loyalty program is omnichannel, integrating online and physical experiences. Here are some features that make this luxury loyalty program effective:

  • It’s a global program, offering benefits that go beyond geographic location limits. For instance, members traveling to other countries can receive personal shopping appointments at flagship stores.
  • The brand organizes artist interactions. Loyalty members can interact with its master craftspeople, enabling members to commission personalized pieces as well as learning crafts and techniques.
  • The brand has incorporated blockchain authentication for members purchasing limited-edition pieces. Members receive blockchain-based authentication certificates that become part of their digital collections.
  • The brand organizes monthly salons that bring together 25 members to experience art, architecture or design. These intimate gatherings encourage connections between members, offering a feeling of community.

Case study 2 – Hermes

Hermes loyalty program does not follow a formal loyalty program structure. Its program does not have a clear points or tier-based structure. Rather, the loyalty program is relationship-based, built over time, and customer engagement. Here are some key points:

  • The brand builds relationships with its customers over time, via multiple interactions. Then, based on their purchase history and preferences, customers are offered coveted and exclusive items that are not offered to other customers.
  • The brand truly focuses on exclusivity. Their loyalty program is invisible and yet designed to create exclusivity. This makes the most exclusive and unique products more desirable to customers.
  • The Hermes experience is fluid, without any rules. The loyalty experience keeps changing from customer to customer, based on their relationship with the brand over time, offering exclusive loyalty benefits.

How to build and implement a luxury loyalty program

Wondering how luxury brands build loyalty programs? While there’s no single text book to follow, each brand has to design unique and exclusive loyalty programs to cater to the luxury market. Here are some steps to follow.

1. Design a unique program

Based on your industry and products, create a unique loyalty program. Start by conducting an audit of your brand’s USP’s and assets. Create your program around these USPs. These cannot be replicated by other brands and hence, can be influential in creating a luxury loyalty program unique to your brand.

2. Create customer segments for loyalty tiers

Think beyond demographic can psychographic data to segment customers. For example, try to understand customers’ cultural interests, lifestyle patterns, aspirational goals, etc. These aspects can help you create more relevant and personalized segments of customers, leading to a more successful loyalty program.

3. Plan your tech infrastructure

Customer data is the starting point for creating a unique customer experience for your loyalty members. And for collecting and analyzing data, you need tools. Hence, plan and design your technology stack in a way that it helps you meet your requirements and loyalty goals. From personalization to privacy and discretion, choose tools that enhance all these factors.

4. Bring in exclusivity

The core idea behind luxury loyalty programs is exclusivity. Create a few experiences for each segment that is exclusive to that tier. Make each of these experiences intimate and exclusive to each tier. This heightens the exclusivity factor as well as helps your program scale.

5. Set up customer service for your loyalty members

The key to a successful loyalty program is keeping it human-centered. Ensure your customer support is on point. Train personnel to offer special treatment to loyalty members with sophistication and cultural awareness for high-end consumers.

6. Feedback integration

Best-in-class luxury loyalty programs ensure their members feel heard. The best way to do so is to gather feedback and address it appropriately. Set up feedback collection systems for capturing and understanding your members’ needs.

7. Soft launch of your luxury loyalty program

Once all these essential elements are in place, it’s time to launch your loyalty program. Do this in parts. Soft launch it for a select set of customers. Gather their feedback and reactions. Enhance and refine the program before you launch it for everyone.

8. Integrate cultural calendar

Today’s customers expect greater value in the way meaningful brand interactions, personalized offers, and culturally-relevant experiences. Ensure your loyalty program calendar aligns with the different loyalty members’ cultural calendars, seasonal trends, fashion calendars, etc.

9. Continuously refine and enhance

Conduct regular reviews of your luxury loyalty program to track member engagement, program effectiveness and relevance. By doing so you can find gaps, identify aspects that aren’t working, and optimize your program for better results.

10. Scale your luxury loyalty program

Once your loyalty program is set up, slowly, scale it. Maybe you want to take it international, develop partnerships with other luxury brands to offer more perks, and add new technologies to offer an advanced digital experience.

Success metrics to measure for luxury loyalty programs

While Hermes has an informal loyalty approach, Gucci has a free program and Louis Vuitton a paid one. Whatever the structure of the program, every luxury brand measures specific metrics to ensure they offer the best experiences to their loyal members. Here are some metrics to measure.

Example: Rolls Royce loyalty program called Whispers

1. Engagement metrics

Measure different types of engagement metrics, such as cultural participation rates – are members participating in experiential perks? Measure the depth of customer relationships across touchpoints. Also, measure how your loyalty members advocate for your program in their social circles.

2. Customer lifetime value

To get a sense of conversion rates and customer lifetime value, measure various factors. For example, purchase frequency, average order value (AOV) and retention rates. Track the performance of experiential offerings and how it leads to conversions. Track members’ brand advocacy and social influence.

3. Cultural capital accumulation

Measure how your luxury loyalty program influences members’ family and social circles. Does your program enhance your brand’s future position by influencing those around your members? Understanding this can help you grow your program and secure its future.

Luxury loyalty program future trends and predictions

Just as the regular eCommerce market, the luxury online market is also seeing rapid changes. And these changes are reflected in their loyalty programs too. Here are some future trends and predictions for luxury loyalty programs.

1. Gamification

Luxury loyalty members expect greater social engagement incentives. Gamification in the loyalty program can lead to more interactions, boost engagement between members, create fun experiences and encourage participating. Thanks to Shopify loyalty program apps, gamification integration is easy.

2. Sustainability

There’s a growing trend of luxury loyalty programs incorporating sustainability aspects within the programs. For instance, eco-friendly rewards, environmental initiatives, collaborating with organizations to support causes that align with loyalty members’ values.

3. Omnichannel integration

Customers use multiple channels to interact with brands. And hence, offering an omnichannel experience in your loyalty program is extremely important. For instance, integrate online and offline channels.

4. Digital and data-driven experience

With technology and AI evolving rapidly, it’s a must to integrate digitalization in loyalty programs. Utilize data to gauge customer preferences and to enable personalization. The best way to do this is to integrate a smart Shopify loyalty program app that offers digital and data capabilities.

5. Hyper-personalization

Premium customer loyalty programs focus more on personalization. From providing tailored luxury experiences using AI and data to offering highly personalized recommendations and event invitations, data-based personalization can be as creative and in-depth as required.

Summing up – setting up luxury loyalty programs

The luxury market has expectations that are different from the regular market. Luxury loyalty programs members are more inclined toward personalization, exclusive experiences, and other forms of exclusivity.

These aspects make data, AI, and digital capabilities a must-have in your Shopify store. And that’s where Appstle Loyalty & Rewards App comes in.

items.html:
If you’re a Shopify store owner or marketer, you know how hard it is to convert a visitor to a customer.

In the competitive eCommerce market, it is essential to maximize conversions and revenue from each visitor interaction. One strategy to increase revenue is embedding subscriptions with Shopify one-click upsells.

That means, make offers to customers soon after they make purchases to sell subscriptions.

This blog explores Shopify one-click upsells for subscriptions, what it is, how to add one-click upsells on Shopify stores, the drawbacks, and how you can get started to increase your Shopify store revenue.

TL;DR

  • This article explains how to convert each one-time customer to a long-term subscriber, generating recurring revenue and maximizing ROI.
  • Combining Shopify one-click upsells with subscriptions is easy with subscription and upsell apps.
  • Ecommerce brands that implement one-click subscription upsells tend to be more profitable. The article shares examples, tips, and takeaways you can easily apply to your store.
  • Learn which success metrics to track and measure to optimize your Shopify store for maximum profits.

What are one-click upsells?

Ever received an email from a brand immediately after making a purchase offering another product at a discount? This is an example of a one-click upsell.

You can offer one-click upsell product recommendations soon after customers make purchases. These can be sent via email, WhatsApp, on the post-purchase page, or other channels. With this strategy, you can offer complementary products, upgrades, or subscriptions.

In this strategy, the one-click factor is important as it removes the other steps in the process, enabling customers to make purchases with a single click. They do not have to re-enter their payment details.

Compared to the traditional upselling process where customers have to repeat the entire checkout process, the one-click upsell feature helps improve conversion rates. This optimized subscription check-out process offers better conversions and ROI.

That’s because instead of selling products, you are offering customers the convenience of making recurring purchases, most often, at a discount. This creates more and predictable revenue for your brand.

Benefits of one-click upsells with subscriptions for Shopify brands

Upselling is an effective sales strategy. Combine it with subscriptions, and you can increase revenue, improve retention rates, and more. Here are the benefits of integrating one-click upsells with subscriptions.

1. Increased revenue

With Shopify one-click upsells, you can convert one-time customers into recurring subscriptions. This leads to increased revenue from each customer as well as higher customer lifetime value (CLV).

2. Improved customer retention

With subscriptions, you can engage customers for the long-term as most people tend to sign up for at least three months, six months, or annual subscriptions. Additionally, if they are satisfied, they renew their subscriptions. This helps increase retention rates.

3. Predictable cash flow

Shopify subscription integration with one-click upsells brings recurring revenue. Subscriptions have a predictable revenue attached. This can help you plan your inventory and business better.

4. Better customer experience

Both upsells and subscriptions offer additional value to customers. This leads to enhanced customer experience. And higher customer satisfaction rates have a positive impact on many areas of business.

How to add one-click upsells on Shopify with subscription integration?

Follow these steps to set up one-click upsells with subscription integration on your Shopify store.

Step 1: Choose your Shopify Subscription app

Your one-click subscription upsell success will depend on how efficient your subscription platform is. Appstle Subscription App is one of the most preferred platforms. When choosing the app, look for these features:

  • Easy set up process
  • Seamless migration from other apps
  • Multiple types of subscription
  • In-built marketing features, such as upsell, cross-sell, discounts, etc.
  • Quick checkout
  • Automated alerts and notifications
  • Customization features
  • Easy subscription rules control

Step 2. Install and configure your subscription app

The next step is to install your subscription app and configure it with your Shopify upsell app if the two apps are different. If you have an upsell feature within your subscription app, set it up based on your upsell strategy.

  • Install your chosen app, for instance Appstle Subscription App
  • Connect your subscription app with the upsell app if they are separate
  • If upsell feature is integrated in your subscription app, create upsell funnels
  • Create your post-purchase upsell experience using Appstle Subscriptions

Step 3. Design your upsell offers

Your Shopify one-click upsell strategy will drive results only if your upsells and offers are relevant to customers. Let’s look at how you can make subscriptions relevant.

  • Subscription upgrade offers: To convert one-time customers into subscribers, offer a discount on subscriptions or free shipping to encourage them to sign up. By converting them, you can increase AOV and recurring revenue.
  • Complementary subscription products: Offer complementary or related products when customers make a purchase. For example, if a customer buys a coffee machine, upsell a coffee subscription to them.
  • Bundle subscriptions: Offer bundles that include the purchased item with other products delivered regularly via subscription.
  • Maintenance and care subscriptions: Depending on your products and industry, offer a subscription for ongoing maintenance, part replacement, accessories, etc.

Step 4: Configure payment processing

To ensure seamless transactions for one-time purchases and subscriptions, ensure your payment processing system is set up for both types of transactions. Here are some steps to follow:

  • Verify your payment gateway supports recurring billing
  • Configure automatic retry for failed subscription payments
  • Set up tax and other calculations for recurring orders
  • Set up secure storage of customer payment information in the Shopify upsell app

Step 5: Set up customer communication

Set up automated communication and notification systems for various channels, such as email, SMS, WhatsApp, etc. Here are some notifications you should automate:

  • Welcome messages to onboard new subscribers
  • Billing notifications for recurring subscription fee
  • Renewal reminders for subscriptions
  • Upsell follow-ups for ongoing communication

Examples of upsell and Shopify subscription integration

Now that you know how to add one-click upsells on Shopify stores with subscription integration, it’s time to look at some real-world examples for inspiration.

Example 1: Glossier Beauty

Glossier is a beauty brand that implemented an upsell and subscription strategy. For example, when customers bought skincare products, the brand offers a skincare routine subscription. Here are some takeaways from this example:

  • Send post purchase subscription upsell immediately after checkout
  • Offer incentives, such as discount or free shipping on subscription
  • Include a few sample size complementary products in the first subscription
  • Communicate a clear value proposition to subscribers to keep them engaged

Example 2: Health supplement store

A health supplement brand offers supplements for one-time purchase as well as subscriptions. The upsell offer appears on each product page. The brand mentions the one-time purchase cost and the discounted cost when subscribed. Here are some other takeaways from this example:

  • Let customers choose subscription delivery frequency from various options
  • Highlight convenience and cost savings
  • Offer a free gift, such as a small travel pouch to keep supplements

Common mistakes of one-click upsell and how to avoid them

To maximize returns from your Shopify one-click upsell and subscription strategy, avoid these common mistakes. Better still, turn these mistakes into opportunities. Here’s how.

1. Offering too many options

Customers often experience decision paralysis when they have too many options to choose from. Hence, limit the number of upsells. Offer only relevant subscription upsells. Also, create a clear value proposition that makes decisions easy.

2. Not timing upsells

Offering upsells too early or too late can impact customers’ purchase decisions. One of the best times to offer a subscription upsell is soon after the customer makes the purchase because they are still in the buying mindset.

3. Offering generic subscriptions

Offering subscription upsells that are irrelevant or not related to the original purchase might not encourage customers to subscribe. Hence, create relevant and targeted or personalized upsell subscription offers. Use customer data to offer personalized upsell offers.

4. Not optimizing for mobile

Missing out optimizing upsell pages for mobile can also lead to poor conversion rates. For instance, customers may receive your upsell offers on WhatsApp and click on the link. However, if the link is not optimized for mobile, they may just close the page. Therefore, it is essential to optimize the upsell pages for mobile.

5. Not creating clear subscription terms

When subscription terms are not clear to customers or when they come across surprise terms or costs, they may feel deceived and may not want to continue. Hence, create transparent terms about billing cycles, shipping costs and timelines, and cancellation policies.

Success metrics for Shopify one-click upsells

To ensure your one-click upsell strategy is on track, consistently measure relevant performance metrics. Here are some metrics to measure.

1. Upsell conversion rate: Calculate the percentage of customers who signed up for the subscription via your upsell offer. Upsell funnels that are optimized well achieve better results.

2. Average Order Value (AOV) increase: Track the AOV before and after customers turn into subscribers following your Shopify one-click upsell offers.

3. Customer Lifetime Value (CLV): Measure the CLV of customers who are subscribers and those that aren’t. Track CLV continuously to understand any changes. For example, if there’s a dip, you can optimize and focus on strategies to increase CLV.

4. Monthly recurring revenue: Tracking the monthly recurring revenue from your subscription upsells can help in business planning and growth.

5. Subscription retention rate: Track and measure subscriber retention rate. If there’s a drop, find out the reason for churn and optimize.

6. Subscription fulfillment accuracy: Monitor how accurately your subscription orders are fulfilled compared to one-time purchases.

Wrapping up

Ready to set up your one-click upsells with subscriptions? The key is to implement this strategy and continuously optimize it. To do so, you will need an efficient Shopify subscription app – Appstle Subscription App.

The app is designed for Shopify and Shopify Plus stores and has several built-in features to support one-click upsells.

items.html:
If you offer product bundles in your online store you already know how bundling as a strategy helps increase average order value (AOV).

Now what if you could do the same in your brick and mortar store? Offer product bundles that customers can purchase in-store.

It’s possible, thanks to Shopify POS Bundling.

This blog will guide you how to extend bundles to in-store sales with Shopify POS bundling.

What is Shopify POS bundling?

Shopify POS bundling is a feature in Shopify’s Point of Sale (POS) structure that enables creating and selling bundles at physical stores. With this function, stores can bundle multiple products together and offer them as a bundle during the checkout process.

This bundle POS feature allows stores to bundle related products together and them as one unit at a discounted price. It supports different types of bundles, such as fixed bundles, flexible bundles, etc. This can be used for seasonal bundles, gift sets, or bundling complementary products. You can create bundles from your Shopify inventory and sell them through your retail store.

Shopify POS Bundling allows different types of bundles, making it easy to approach your in-store bundling strategy in a way which suits your customer segments. WithShopify POS, you can set up fixed bundles, mix and match bundles, tiered bundles, add-on bundles, and more.

Shopify POS features and capabilities

Let’s explore more Shopify POS features and capabilities:

  • The POS system offers real-time inventory syncing, with automated stock and inventory updates, from the online as well as physical store.
  • It offers flexible payment methods, such as carts, digital wallets, etc.
  • Merchants can access comprehensive reports and analytics based on combined data from the online and physical stores.
  • Shopify POS integrates and works well with other third party apps and hardware.
  • Shopify POS bundling is available at different pricing plans based on the needs of different businesses.

Shopify POS bundling benefits

Integrating Shopify POS for bundling has many benefits. Here are some:

1. Consolidated data

Implementing Shopify POS bundling provides unified data from the online and physical store. This makes managing inventory, sales, and marketing easy and more effective. Combined data and information helps streamline operations. Moreover, real-time synchronization streamlines inventory and prevents overselling or stockouts.

2. Effective scalability

Shopify POS bundling also enables businesses to scale and grow. By offering bundles online as well as in brick and mortar stores, you can increase AOV on both channels. Moreover, data and insights from both channels can offer insights that help make data-based business decisions.

3. Customer experience

Customers get a better and more convenient experience as they can make purchases online and in-store. Data collection and analysis helps offer personalized experiences and bundles to customers.

Implementing Shopify POS bundling: step-by-step

If you’re considering omnichannel eCommerce for your Shopify store with in-store features, here’s how you can implement Shopify POS bundling.

Step 1: Plan and prepare

  • The first step to planning Shopify POS bundling is to get an understanding of how bundles are performing on your site. Analyze which bundles perform well, check conversion metrics, AOV, what feedback customers are sharing, etc.
  • Next, conduct inventory assessment. Ensure you have enough stock for bundle components.
  • Your staff and team members will also require training. For instance, they should know how to present bundles, how to process bundle sales in the POS system, etc.

Step 2: Technical considerations for Shopify POS bundling

  • To begin with, create bundles in the Shopify admin panel and ensure they are marked as available for POS. Ensure correct pricing, inventory tracking, etc.
  • Make sure your POS app is configured to the bundles. Organize bundles, create custom collections, tag bundles for easy processes.
  • Set up payment and tax configuration processes to manage bundle discounts and tax calculations.

Step 3: Store integration

  • Create displays in the store to highlight and showcase bundles. Alongside, show savings and its value proposition if bought as a bundle.
  • Train your in-store staff to identify bundling opportunities based on their interaction with customers.
  • Provide material and information to in-store staff that helps them in better communication about bundle value and benefits.

In-store bundling tips and best practices

To ensure your omnichannel eCommerce experience with online Shopify and brick and mortar stores is seamless and efficient, follow these useful tips.

1. Communicate value clearly

Your customers should easily understand the benefits and value of buying products as bundles. Clearly display the savings and convenience aspects. Also, use different tactics to display discounts and savings. For instance, show the original price, strike it out, and show the discounted bundle price.

2. Offer flexibility

Customers might prefer to create their own bundles or request for specific bundles. Give them the flexibility by addressing their requests. This means you should have multiple bundle configurations ready in your store.

3. Ensure seamless checkout

Your Shopify POS bundling system should be set up to make the checkout process easy. Moreover, your staff should know now to troubleshoot if there are issues during bundle checkout.

4. Real-time tracking

Setting up real-time tracking can help you avoid situations such as stockouts and delays. By monitoring your bundle inventory in real-time, you can know which products are available and those that are close to stockouts.

5. Forecasting adjustments

Your POS bundle sales can impact the demand, supply, and inventory of individual products. Hence, plan your inventory, purchasing, and related tasks by considering bundle-driven increased demand for products.

6. Sync online and POS

Ensure you synchronize the different channels via which you sell bundles, for instance, online and POS systems. This will help avoid overselling bundle components and any misinformation.

7. Proper staff training

When offering Shopify POS bundles, ensure your staff is trained and knowledgeable about the bundles, the savings, benefits, and value to customers. They should also practice upselling techniques while interacting with customers. Moreover, your staff should know how to solve minor issues related to POS bundles.

8. Measure revenue metrics

One of the most important metrics to track is the revenue. What is the bundle penetration rate, track the AOV increases over a specific period of time, and revenue from different channels (Shopify and brick and mortar stores). Also compare revenue between channels to optimize.

9. Track customer metrics

Your Shopify POS bundling strategy has to be designed with your customers at its center. Hence, measure your customer satisfaction score, the return rate and abandonment rate for bundles, repeat purchases, customer feedback, etc. Measuring this will help you offer what customers want.

10. Continuous optimization

Collect customer feedback, conduct reviews and surveys and run A/B tests for bundles to enhance your Shopify POS bundle performance. To do so, you can automate the process using your Shopify bundling app and create in-store systems to identify patterns, analyze data, and optimize.

Wrapping up

By integrating Shopify POS bundling in your Shopify store, you can connect your online and physical stores. The POS system can help increase AOV, sales, enhance customer experience, and scale your business across channels.

To ensure your Shopify online and in-store bundling strategies are in sync, integrate a smart bundling app – Appstle Bundles & Discounts App.

Appstle Bundles & Discounts App features:

  • Targeted bundles and discounting
  • Real-time customer data analytics
  • Seamless Shopify POS integration
  • Upselling with conversion-optimized templates
  • Integration with subscriptions and recurring orders
  • Customization and personalization

items.html:
Customer acquisition cost (CAC) is the amount you spend on acquiring customers. It is a critical metric that determines your business profits.

The bad news: The average eCommerce CAC is rising. This could be because of one or multiple factors in your eCommerce business.

From higher competition and marketing costs to poor product-market fit to ineffective pricing strategies in your subscriptions and memberships.

To help you reduce customer acquisition costs in your Shopify store, this blog focuses on strategies you can implement in subscriptions and memberships.

Curious to know more? Let’s get started!

Why eCommerce CAC is rising and its challenges

According to a study by Harvard Business Review, acquiring new customers costs 5 to 25 times more than retaining existing customers. Customer acquisition costs are rising. 57% of retailers say it’s one of the biggest threats to their sales goals. But what exactly are the reasons for its rising costs? Let’s find out.

1. Increased competition

There are 28 million active online businesses in the world. More and more businesses are competing for the same customers. This is leading businesses to spend more on marketing, promotions, and customer acquisition campaigns. Besides, increasing costs of resources, advertising, etc. adds to CAC.

2. Ineffective customer targeting

Another reason the average eCommerce CAC is rising is because of ineffective customer targeting. Lack of personalization in marketing messages, poor targeting, lower engagement rates, and not using data strategically are some of the reasons for increasing marketing costs and CAC.

3. Customer behavior is changing

Due to an overload of information and options, customers’ engagement is decreasing. Brands are finding it harder to capture their attention. Moreover, customers’ expectations have increased. They expect more sophisticated and personalized experiences. Privacy issues are another reason customers are wary of interacting with multiple brands. All these factors are leading to a higher CAC.

4. Product and pricing factors

Lack of product differentiation, poor product-market fit, and inappropriate pricing can lead to lower engagement and sales. These factors tend to increase customer acquisition costs as they may require more marketing costs.

How eCommerce subscriptions and memberships reduce CAC?

Ecommerce subscriptions and memberships are marketing strategies that help increase recurring revenue, nurture long-term customer relationships, and hence, reduce customer acquisition costs. Let’s understand how they help do so.

Ecommerce subscriptions

How subscriptions reduce customer acquisition cost

Subscription models are based on the concept of recurring or repeat purchases at predefined intervals. Here’s how subscription can lower customer acquisition costs:

  • Subscriptions focus on retaining subscribers/customers rather than only acquiring new customers
  • With subscriptions, customers get into long-term association with brands. This increases customer lifetime value (CLV) and reduces CAC
  • Happy subscribers end up advocating for your brand, bringing new customers for free. This reduces CAC
  • Subscriptions help businesses gather insightful data about customers’ behavior, helping with targeted marketing. This improves customer retention, and lowers CAC

Example

Subscription features that help increase retention and reduce CAC

Offering basic and traditional subscription models that only offer discounts does not attract customers anymore. Customers want an all round excellent subscription experience. Here are some features that you must consider for your Shopify subscription model.

1. Convenience

Subscriptions provide customers the convenience of receiving products and services on a regular basis without having to repeatedly place orders. This sort of convenience leads to longer associations with the brand and reduces the need to spend on acquiring new customers.

2. Flexibility

Ecommerce subscribers have the flexibility and freedom to swap, pause, or change products when they want to. This offers a certain level of comfort, leading to a better customer experience.

3. Tiered subscription options

Subscriptions can have different tiers, which makes it easy for customers to choose a tier based on their preferences. Different tiered subscription levels and pricing offers customers the ability to choose what fits their requirements.

How to structure eCommerce subscriptions to reduce customer acquisition cost?

Here are some tips to structure your subscriptions in a way that they help reduce CAC.

  • Price subscriptions strategically in a way that it offers lifetime value as well as benefit on individual transactions. Price in a way that you recover CAC within the first few months.
  • Offer flexible subscription models for better CAC. For example, multiple frequency options – weekly, monthly, quarterly. Allow customers to make changes easily.
  • Bundle complementary products and services within subscriptions. This helps increase the average order value (AOV).
  • Design a tiered subscription model that caters to different customer segments. This can help increase lifetime value as customers can upgrade or downgrade plans based on their needs.
  • Automate data-driven personalization to offer personalized benefits to customers based on their behavior patterns. It can increase retention and reduce customer acquisition cost.
  • Design subscription CX and logistics in a way to maximize convenience and minimize friction. Automate tasks using an intuitive subscriptions app, such as Appstle Subscriptions App.

Ecommerce memberships

How eCommerce memberships lower CAC

Memberships are designed to enhance customer experience and drive customer loyalty. These aspects help reduce CAC. Here’s how:

  • With memberships, you can increase upsells and cross-selling, increase AOV and reducing CAC
  • Loyal members end up spending more over time, increasing value to your business
  • Membership programs offer incentives and perks that help retain customers, reducing CAC

Example

Membership features that help increase retention and lower CAC

Here are some eCommerce membership features that lead to enhanced customer experience, increased retention, and lower customer acquisition cost.

1. Personalized incentives

Since memberships last for a long period, Shopify merchants are able to collect customer data and use the insights to offer personalized incentives. For instance, free shipping, personalized discount, early access to collections, etc.

2. Community and groups

Memberships offer a feeling of belonging and community with other like-minded members. This sort of emotional connection leads to greater customer satisfaction and hence longevity.

3. Higher engagement

With features, such as personalized product recommendations, new incentives, freebies, and special benefits, membership programs provide consistent engagement to customers.

How to structure eCommerce memberships to reduce CAC?

Follow these tips to structure memberships in a way that it helps increase retention and reduces CAC:

  • Identify various customer segments. Creating segments helps in deciding perks and benefits for each segment. It will also help you price your membership plans based on the various segments.
  • Understand what motivates customers to make purchases. Collect feedback, conduct online surveys, and listen to members to understand what perks and benefits they experience.
  • Define membership validity – monthly, annual, or lifetime. Doing so will help you proactively run campaigns to get them to renew, engage, and stay for long.
  • Have a clear value proposition. Show members the benefits and value in the long run. For instance, if the membership fee is $100, show them how they would save $200 – $300 instead.
  • Price membership plans strategically, based on data and competitor analysis.
  • Integrate your membership plan within your Shopify store and experiences by using an efficient Shopify membership app – Appstle Membership App.

Wrapping up: reduce CAC with Shopify subscriptions and memberships

If you thought your Shopify subscriptions and membership models only help increase sales and revenue, you’re wrong. There’s a hidden benefit they offer – reduce customer acquisition cost.

items.excerpt: Wondering why your Shopify bundles average order value (AOV) isn’t increasing? Or why the bundle sales are going down? Could the root cause be unidentified Shopify bundling issues? items.html:
Wondering why your Shopify bundles average order value (AOV) isn’t increasing? Or why the bundle sales are going down?

Could the root cause be unidentified Shopify bundling issues?

In this blog, we discuss the most common Shopify bundling issues that merchants tend to miss, how they impact conversions, and the solutions to overcome those issues.

Curious to know?

Read on!

1. Pricing and discounting bundles

Pricing bundles in a way that they are profitable can be tricky. Many brands struggle to increase AOV. That’s mostly because of poor pricing strategies, which is a common Shopify bundling issue.

But what kind of discounts should you offer on bundles? Offering too much can eat into your profits, and too little might not be enough to generate sales.

Another challenge that businesses face related to pricing is technical. Shopify’s default features may not be sufficient for strategic pricing. Pricing complex bundles requires more expertise.

This is why you need to integrate other apps that help with profitable pricing, and discounting. For example, Appstle Bundles & Discounts App is an intuitive tool built for bundles. The app provides dynamic discounts features.

2. Shipping, order fulfillment and inventory management

Imagine your Shopify store receives orders for 100 bundles but you are not prepared or equipped to fulfill more than 50 orders at a time? Non-fulfillment of their orders can leave customers frustrated.

Shipping and order fulfillment is a crucial element of bundles. It involves many tasks, such as updating SKUs, dispatching orders, and addressing fulfillment gaps.

Moreover, in bundles, customers can end up buying multiple SKUs. And so, if your bundle inventory is not in sync, it can get really messy. For instance, you could end up over-selling products, delaying shipments, leading to unhappy customers.

Not planning shipping order fulfillment is a common Shopify bundling issue. Additionally, poor inventory management is also related to this issue. Many shopify stores make the mistake of not using automation for order fulfillment and inventory management, and hence fail because they try to do everything manually.

The solution: Integrate a bundling app on your Shopify store that has the capabilities to manage shipping, automate bundle inventory sync, order fulfillment, communication to customers, and other processes.

3. Choosing products to bundle together

Another common Shopify bundling issue that many brands face is deciding which products to bundle together. Should you bundle products that customers usually buy together? Or should you create data-driven bundles based on other findings? It’s tricky.

Here are some solutions to this Shopify bundling issue:

  • Collect data from your past orders. Look at the purchase history to identify products that customers bought together. For example, a face cleanser, toner, and moisturizer can be clubbed into a skincare bundle
  • Bundle a high-value product with other fast-selling, low value items. This way, you can ensure a high average order value and keep your bundle profitability steady
  • Create seasonal bundles. Not only does it create excitement for trying seasonal products, but also causes FOMO and urgency for customers to buy the bundles before the season passes or the bundles get sold out

4. Making bundles seamless and error-free

One of the biggest Shopify bundling issues is that brands create profitable bundles but ignore the other factors around it. For instance, marketing or setting up customer support for bundles, or promoting bundles so consumers discover them.

Here are some bundle error fixes you should work on to drive traffic and sales from bundles:

  • Feature bundles prominently on your Shopify store. Create a dedicated page or section just for listing bundles. Ensure each bundle page is comprehensive with information, discounting details, etc.
  • Make sure your bundle inventory sync is automated and efficient. If it isn’t, it may cause problems, such as over orders of bundles, delayed shipping, error in sending notifications to customers
  • Automate customer support for bundles, train support agents to respond to bundle related queries, and find quick solutions to any problems that arise on the Shopify store. Your technical team should be able to fix any issues on the bundles pages quickly
  • Use retargeting, social media promotions, email marketing for bundles, collaborate with influencers, and other marketing strategies to ensure your bundle offers get seen by your target audience

Source

5. Not personalizing bundles

81% of customers prefer personalized experiences from brands. A study byMcKinsey has found that personalization can increase ROI by 10 to 30%. And this stays true when it comes to bundles. If your customers see bundles with products irrelevant to them, they will abandon your site faster than you can imagine.

Focus on making bundle-buying experience as personal as possible. How do you do that? Here’s how:

  • Integrate a Shopify bundling app, such as Appstle Bundles & Discounts, which has in-built personalization features
  • Use data from customers purchase history, browsing behavior, etc. to identify their likes, dislikes, preferences, and market trends
  • Use advanced AI and automation tools to help with creating personalized experiences by tailoring bundles to individual customer needs
  • Offer different types of bundles, such as dynamic bundles (based on real-time browsing behavior), create your own bundle or DIY bundles (customers can pick and choose products), mixed bundles (club fast-selling products with other products)

Troubleshooting for Shopify bundling issues

Wondering where to begin to find what is going wrong with your Shopify bundling strategies? Here’s a guide that will tell you how to troubleshoot, what information to find, and how.

1. Bundle inventory sync issues

If you notice overselling and mis-match of information in the front-end and inventory, it’s time to figure out why. Here’s what you can do:

  • Check if inventory settings are not configured
  • Third-party app integration with your Shopify inventory
  • Error in automating stock alerts based on your inventory
  • Any manual updates not reflecting in your inventory

2. Bundle pricing and discounting errors

Do errors such as incorrect discounts, delay in updating bundle component pricing, and mis-match in currency conversion crop up in your Shopify store? Here’s what you should do:

  • Check if there are any discount logic faults
  • Hardcoded bundle pricing not reflecting
  • Tax calculations not included in bundle pricing
  • Check bundle pricing rules

3. Issues with bundle components

If the bundle components are not displayed properly or some products are missing, it’s time to troubleshoot. Follow these steps and bundle error fixes:

  • Look for any theme compatibility problems
  • Identify missing or corrupted product data
  • Run tests in default Shopify themes
  • Contact Shopify bundle app support
  • Look for conflicting liquid tags
  • Check if CSS isn’t hiding bundle elements

4. Bundle checkout and cart issues

Are there checkout issues, are bundles splitting into individual products at checkout, or are the discount codes not applying at the time of checkout? Fix these issues to provide a smooth bundle experience to customers.

  • Check if cart drawer customizations are causing structural problems
  • Identify issues with payment gateway incompatibility
  • Review discount code rules and related conflicts
  • Ensure bundle products maintain correct groups
  • Test cart functionality on different devices and browsers
  • Try the checkout process with different bundles
  • Verify payment gateway and shipping calculation settings

5. Problems with data analytics and reports

If you’re facing issues with tracking bundles sales, individual components, and others related to data and analytics reports, here’s how you can find the root cause and bundle error fixes:

  • Check it the analytics tracking is not configured properly
  • Identify problems with third-party app integrations
  • Is the custom tracking code missing?
  • See if bundle products have unique SKUs
  • Set up custom tracking for bundles
  • Create product tags to categorize bundle products
  • Create custom reports
  • Check if the Shopify bundle app is connected to Google Analytics

Wrapping up: Have you identified Shopify bundling issues in your store?

To ensure a smooth and uninterrupted bundles experience to your customers, you have to constantly monitor performance on your Shopify store, identify errors, and engage in Shopify troubleshooting.

Not doing so can show us errors, delays, slow page loads, non-fulfilment of orders, and more such issues on your site. To provide a smooth bundles experience, integrate an efficient Shopify bundling app.

FAQs

What are some reasons bundles fail to increase AOV?
Poor pricing strategies, traditional discounting strategies, and not setting clear goals from bundles can lead to low AOV.

Which is the best strategy to bundle products together?
Identifying which products to bundle together is a common Shopify bundling issue, which can be solved by using past data and trying out different strategies, such as mixed bundles, seasonal bundles, DIY bundles, etc.

What causes bundling checkout issues?
Bundling checkout problems can be caused due to lack of regular eCommerce troubleshooting and maintenance.

Why aren’t my Shopify bundle sales showing correctly in analytics?
The reasons could be many, such as missing or incorrect configuration of analytics tracking, third-party app integration issues, bundles lacking unique SKUs, etc.

How to ensure Shopify bundle inventory sync?
Consistently monitor inventory sync settings, verify configurations, third-party app interactions, and automation settings to ensure your Shopify inventory is in sync

items.html:
Loyalty programs have been an integral part of eCommerce brands’ loyalty strategies. However, reward programs have transformed over the years.

Moving from only transactions to building emotional connections, and offering highly personalized experiences. Brands that have kept adapting to customer preferences and market trends, have the potential to drive customer lifetime value.

This blog explores the loyalty program of one such brand loved by customers all over the world – H&M’s loyalty strategy.

We’ll break down H&M’s customer rewards program, understand how and why the loyalty program changed, and how Shopify brands can apply these learnings to enhance their programs.

Let’s get started!

What is the H&M loyalty program?

H&M is a world renowned fashion and apparel brand that offers clothing, accessories, and footwear for men, women, and kids. H&M’s loyalty program is considered one of the best eCommerce loyalty examples. It is free and offers exclusive benefits to members, such as points, discounts, perks, and more.

The loyalty program is digital but members can earn points for shopping online as well as in store and on the brand’s mobile app. The H&M loyalty strategy has evolved over the years as the brand has incorporated many changes to adapt to customer needs and market trends.

H&M loyalty strategy breakdown
The H&M loyalty program is much loved and popular amongst customers because of many reasons. In this section, we look into the many aspects and elements of the loyalty program that make it so special.

1. Easy sign up process

H&M’s loyalty program is free. Customers can join the program by visiting the membership page on the website, visit the store, or download the app and become a member.

The loyalty program page on the website provides all the necessary information. Customers can easily find answers to their questions from the FAQs section. Customers can see their available points on the website or the app.

The sign-up process requires few details, such as customer email, a password, and birthdate. Members can also add their name and address if they wish to. What is more, as soon as customers join the customer rewards program, they receive a discount reward or points credited to their account.

2. Offers many benefits to members

H&M loyalty strategy is designed in a way to provide multiple benefits and perks to customers. Unlike some loyalty programs that offer just points, H&M offers much more. Here are the different benefits of its loyalty program:

  • Points on every purchase online and in store
  • Member exclusive prices and discounts
  • Member event invites
  • Early access to shopping events
  • Klarna pay now or later option

3. Two tiers – Core and Plus

Less is more. Today, consumers are bombarded with multiple choices, which leaves them with decision fatigue. Moreover, having too many options complicates things. H&M loyalty strategy is custom designed with two tiers – Core and Plus.

Both tiers differentiate from each other based on the perks and benefits included in each tier. Core is the basic tier, while Plus is the premium tier. Customers can reach Plus tier once they earn 500 Points. This tiered strategy can also help increase repeat purchases on Shopify stores.

1. Core member benefits

  • Free shipping over $40
  • Member exclusive prices
  • Partner promotions
  • VIP event invites
  • Early access
  • Klarna pay now or later

2. Plus member benefits

  • All benefits of Core members
  • Early access to collections and sales
  • Exclusive experiences
  • Exclusive Plus member offers
  • Premium giveaways

4. Simple process to earn points

Another reason why this customer loyalty program is so popular is because it has made earning points simple and easy. Customers earn 1 point for every $1 spent online or in store.

Moreover, customers receive bonus points for non-transactional actions, such as for participating in their sustainability and circularity initiatives. Making it easy to earn points has many benefits:

  • If gives customers confidence
  • Immediate gratification
  • Builds trust
  • Increases excitement and engagement
  • Adds an element of playfulness

5. It has a sustainability/ circularity element

Fast fashion is one of the leading environmental issues around the world. H&M is one of the few brands that supports the cause of sustainability and circularity. And H&M’s loyalty strategy combines this cause with the loyalty program.

Members can drop off old clothes in any H&M store. Members are rewarded a 15% discount reward for every bag full of clothes they deposit at the store The clothes are recycled and reused.

This strategy of combining a social or environmental cause with the membership program is something worth exploring for Shopify loyalty programs that want to align with the values and preferences of the current generation.

6. Seamless mobile app experience

Customers can shop via H&M’s mobile app. Members can log into the app to get an overview of their loyalty membership – points collected, expiry date of points, etc.

Customers can make purchases via the app as the brand has their entire collection available on the app. Moreover, the app also enables customers to look for nearby stores, which provides a hybrid experience for those customers who prefer to try on clothes before making purchases.

Members can use the points accumulated whether they shop via the app, the website, or the store. However, for promotional reasons, the brand may also offer points exclusively for shopping via the app. When incorporated into Shopify loyalty programs, all these factors help increase repeat purchases on Shopify stores.

A comparison of H&M’s loyalty strategy: then and now

Recently, H&M made some significant changes to its loyalty program. One of the reasons H&M rewards program is considered amongst the best eCommerce loyalty programs is its ability to adapt and keep evolving. In this section, we look at what those changes are, how it impacts the program, the customers, and the brand, and why these changes were brought about.

Changes made to the H&M loyalty strategy:

  • The brand discontinued the 25% birthday discount and the 10% loyalty program joining discount
  • H&M loyalty program members now receive ongoing pricing benefits on selected products
  • Members get early access to limited editions and other special collections
  • Styling consultations, in-store event invites, and members-only previews
  • Integration of online and in-store experience, leading to a smoother customer experience

H&M loyalty strategy: Key takeaways for Shopify loyalty programs

1. The days of only giving discounts and points to loyalty members are gone. Today’s savvy consumers expect more – emotional connection, community, personalized experience, proactiveness, and more.

2. Brands must continuously measure the success of their loyalty program and experiment with new strategies. A traditional loyalty program is not enough to engage diverse customer segments.

3. Keep the loyalty program simple and easy for customers to understand and engage with. An overload of options and complex structures can put customers off.

4. Combine online, in-store, and mobile app systems so the customers can have a seamless, omnichannel experience. Functioning in silos can damage and stagnate rewards programs.

Takeaways from H&M loyalty strategy How to apply it to your Shopify loyalty program
Using data for Shopify loyalty programs
  • Use data to build real connections with loyalty members
  • Invest in smart Shopify loyalty apps and tools
  • Consistent data collection and analysis
  • Understand members’ needs and behaviors
Relevancy and real transformation
  • Copy-pasting loyalty programs from one industry to the other does not work
  • Get clarity on what loyalty means for your brand/li>
  • Know what will make your customers advocates of your brand and participate deeply
  • Take a long-term approach for your loyalty program
Creativity and innovation
  • Constantly evolve and grow your loyalty program. Embrace continuous change and creativity to keep up with the times
  • Explore new technologies – AI-based personalization, gamified loyalty experiences, and AR and VR
  • Consistently collect member feedback, analyze program performance, and try new strategies
Personalization and engagement
  • Offer more than points. For example, bonus points for non-transactional activities
  • Integrate initiatives and causes that align with customers’ values
  • Build a community, for example H&M’s Plus tier gets to experience VIP events

How to get started with your Shopify loyalty program?

H&M’s loyalty strategy has been successful over the years because of multiple reasons. First, the brand knows how to tap into customers’ needs and preferences. Second, the brand keeps adapting to change. Third, it utilizes technology to offer the best customer experience.

H&M loyalty strategy offers many tips and tactics that you can use for your Shopify loyalty program. And implementing these strategies is easy, thanks to tools such as Appstle Loyalty & Rewards App.

Appstle Loyalty & Rewards App features:

  • Allows multiple program types
  • Gamification features
  • Data-driven personalization capabilities
  • Easy integrations with third-party marketing and other apps
  • Data safety and security features

If you’re looking for a Shopify loyalty app that can help you implement H&M loyalty strategies on your store, explore Appstle.

items.excerpt: Bundles are in itself an effective strategy to increase average order value and sales. However, if you ignore bundles on your Shopify store, its returns may diminish. items.html:
Bundles are in itself an effective strategy to increase average order value and sales.

However, if you ignore bundles on your Shopify store, its returns may diminish. And instead of generating revenue, bundles might end up being a cost to your store.

To ensure that bundles keep giving you returns, it is essential to keep monitoring and optimizing their performance.

In this blog, we look at bundle UX optimization strategies that can increase conversions on your Shopify store.

Let’s get started!

How does bundling help increase CRO?

To understand how bundling helps increase conversion rates, we must understand its benefits. Before we get into Shopify CRO tips, here are some the benefits of offering bundles:

1. Leverage fast-moving and sell slow-moving products

Combining fast-moving products with unsold stock from the inventory can help you clear old, slow-moving stock. To increase conversions, use data from customer behavior, browsing history, and cart history. Bundle products customers browsed or added to their carts but didn’t buy in the past.

2. Reduced marketing costs

Marketing a bundle containing 10 products is cheaper than marketing those 10 products individually. Moreover, marketing bundles through creative strategies also has many benefits. For example, influence marketing for bundles can increase awareness, and social media marketing comes at affordable costs.

3. Higher perceived value and price opacity

It’s human psychology; we attach more value to bundles because they have more products and almost always at a discounted price. Moreover, when bundled smartly, bundles help remove negative impacts of pricing. For example, bundling low-price products with one large high-price product can enhance the value of the low-priced products.

Bundle UX optimization strategies for Shopify

Bundling products and services definitely has many advantages for Shopify stores. And there are many ways to create bundles. However, simple bundling of products doesn’t impress customers and may not drive conversions. To increase sales, try these CRO strategies.

1. Create dynamic bundles

Dynamic bundles, created using customer data, provide more value, personalization, and hence, satisfaction to customers. For instance, if a customer has added a few items to their cart, you could create a bundle including those products and offer it at a discount.

Dynamic bundles not only increase average order value (AOV) but also conversion rates. Here how you can optimize bundle UX with dynamic bundles:

  • Track customers’ viewing and browsing behavior and create bundles out of it
  • Create bundles based on cart activity
  • Have ‘complete the look’ or ‘frequently bought together’ recommendations
  • Create bundles based on purchase history and products often bought together

Example:

2. Optimize for mobile

Mobile commerce accounts for 63% of total global eCommerce. Consumers are increasingly choosing to make purchases from mobile devices. And hence, it is essential to pay attention to optimizing bundle pages for the small screens.

Here are some factors to consider for creating mobile-first bundles:

  • Create a responsive eCommerce design for bundles on your Shopify store
  • Ensure the navigation and simple and easy for small screens
  • Optimize images and content for speed
  • Streamline the checkout process, making it easier for customers to complete purchases
  • Since the product pages have more products and information on each bundle product, make the layout and content easy to read

3. Consider offering seasonal bundles

Ecommerce sales tend to fluctuate based on seasonal trends. Hence, during low sales periods, introducing seasonal bundles can help you maintain conversion rates. However, whether you can offer seasonal bundles or not depends on your product and industry.

Here are some tips on how to enhance UX with seasonal bundles:

  • Include new products that are available for a short period in seasonal bundles. For example, a monsoon bundle with accessories and essentials
  • Offer discounts to increase conversions of seasonal bundles
  • Promote bundles via marketing strategies, such as influencers, social media, etc.
  • Combine fast sellers with seasonal products to make the bundle more valuable

4. A/B testing of bundles

One of the best methods to assess bundle popularity and increase conversion rates is to run A/B testing. And with bundles, there are multiple ways to do this, compared to single products. Here are some A/B testing ideas for bundles:

  • Create different bundles and promote to segmented target audience
  • Try different CTAs to identify the ones that grab customers’ attention
  • Place CTAs strategically in the product page layout
  • Try A/B testing with the way you display bundle pricing. Price display strategies, such as odd-even can impact conversion rates
  • Try split testing product photos to see which photos attract more attention and conversions

5. One-click add-to-cart UX

One-click checkout makes shopping faster and easier for customers. Factors such as single clicks as opposed to many, pre-filled forms for payment and address details, and a streamlined checkout flow makes conversions faster.

Here’s how one-click checkout can help with bundle UX optimization.

  • Provide a more satisfying shopping experience to customers by reducing things they need to do
  • Less friction in the checkout process can lead to decreased cart abandonments
  • One-click add-to-cart UX is useful when customers are shopping from their mobile phones as it makes the shopping process easier

6. Add user generated content on bundle product pages

User-generated content (UGC), such as reviews, bundle-opening videos, and content about how customers used bundle products can help other customers make purchases. Nearly 80% of consumers get influenced by UGC.

Here’s how to utilize UGC content for bundles:

  • Show bundle-opening videos on the product page layout
  • Collect reviews from customers who have bought bundles
  • Ask customers to share how they used bundle products together
  • Use UGC in marketing campaigns on other platforms, such as email, social media

7. Create limited-time offers on bundles

Scarcity, FOMO, and limited-time offers are tried and tested strategies to increase eCommerce sales. And these strategies work! Customers do not want to miss out on opportunities. Moreover, when we humans gain a benefit, it has a psychological effect on us.

Here are some ways to use limited time offers for bundle UX optimization:

  • Create limited-time offers on bundles
  • Show timers on bundle product pages
  • Display the number of bundles left
  • Show real-time sales data, such as ‘Offer lasts for 1 hour’

8. Offer bundle subscriptions

Depending on your product type, whether or not it is a recurring need, create subscription bundles. For instance, Microsoft Office is sold as a bundle of software. A bundle of health supplements can be sold as a subscription that can generate recurring revenue, thus increasing conversions.

Here are some Shopify CRO tips for subscription bundles:

  • Offer exclusive bundle incentives on subscriptions
