items.excerpt: When it comes to bundling, we mostly tend to think of a set of 5 t-shirts or a yoga bundle with a few products. Ever thought of a bundle of t-shirts and a digital style guide? Or a yoga bundle with a yoga mat, bag, and a yoga app subscription? Digital and physical product bundling…
items.html:
When it comes to bundling, we mostly tend to think of a set of 5 t-shirts or a yoga bundle with a few products.

Ever thought of a bundle of t-shirts and a digital style guide? Or a yoga bundle with a yoga mat, bag, and a yoga app subscription?

Digital and physical product bundling is not new. But it is not common either.

While some brands have figured out how to create exciting digital and physical bundles to increase average order value (AOV) and sales, many brands struggle to launch such bundles.

If you’re a Shopify brand that’s looking to offer digital and physical bundles or are wondering how to enhance your existing phygital bundles, read this blog for strategies, tips, best practices, and more.

Benefits of digital and physical product bundling

A bundling strategy focused on combining digital and physical products can not only make your bundles stand out from the crowd and increase consumer interest, it can also be a revenue model that helps grow the AOV and profits. Whether you sell digital on Shopify and want to add physical products to your bundle or the other way around, here are the benefits along with tips:

1. Increases average order value

One of the most significant advantages of bundling is it increases the average order value (AOV). When customers end up buying more than just one product, it has a direct impact on the order value.

Expert tip: Bundle compatible digital and physical products that make customers’ life easier. Make it a bundle that solves problems, increasing its sales potential and AOV.

2. Increases sales and revenue

Bundling physical and digital products together offers upselling and cross-selling opportunities, leading to increased sales and revenue. Upselling and cross-selling bundles also leverage customers’ interests, making it easier to drive sales.

Expert tip: Make it easy for customers to understand the bundle value, how much they will save, and how the products complement each other.

3. Better inventory management

Using an efficient Shopify bundling app can help maximize automation and AI-based inventory management. Bundling physical and digital products requires the inventories of both these products to be in sync. Inventory management teams can

Expert tip: Integrate a smart Shopfify bundling app that has features such as multiple bundle types, automated discounting, marketing and communication features, data analytics, real-time analytics, among others.

4. Enhances search visibility

Bundling two types of products — digital and physical — increases search visibility. For instance, people searching for one of the products will end up discovering the other product and more, via the bundle. This increases the number of people your product listing reaches.

Expert tip: Come up with creative product pairings and clearly explain how the two complement each other. Don’t leave customers confused or wondering how to use the two together.

5. Increases perceived value for customers

When customers get to buy two or more necessary products as one bundle at a discounted price, its perceived value increases. Price sensitive customers look for more than just low prices. They pay more attention to value.

Consider value-based pricing, dynamic pricing, and other strategies focusing on delivering value rather than simply offering the lowest price. Contrary to popular belief, price-sensitive shoppers often look for value rather than the lowest prices.

Expert tip: Experiment with value-based pricing, dynamic pricing, and other strategies when offering bundle discounts.

6. Reduces decision fatigue for customers

When you pair a digital and a physical product that enhance the functionality and usability of the other, customers are bound to feel impressed and satisfied. Paying less than what they would pay if the products are purchased individually, is a key factor in speeding purchase decisions.

Expert tip: Clearly present all the plus points of the bundles, such as comparative price benefits, use cases, and how it will change the customers’ life.

Here’s an example of an innovative strategy for digital and physical product bundling. A graphic novel that comes in both digital and physical form, combined in a bundle. While the digital version gets released first, the physical version is shipped to customers at a later date.

Strategies for digital and physical product bundling

Combining physical and digital products in a bundle is more than just putting together two or more items. Here are the different strategies you can use to meet different business goals.

1. Bundling complementary products

This is one of the most common thought processes when developing bundles. Pairing products and services that are complementary naturally increases the bundle’s utility and perceived value.

For example, smartphones are bundled with digital products or services, such as cloud storage or streaming services. This enhances the capability of the physical product (smartphone) and solves one of the most common problems, lack of storage.

Another example of digital and physical product bundling that complements each other is a physical fitness equipment bundled with workout apps, and nutrition apps.

2. Bundles with experiential components

Based on the industry and product type, you can even create bundles that offer experiences, not just digital components that enhance utility. Adding experiential elements can create emotional connections and engagement opportunities.
For instance, luxury brands often bundle digital elements, such as behind-the-scenes access, personalized digital experiences, exclusive content, bundle ebooks with products, and one-on-ones with celebrities with physical products.

3. Convenience and efficiency bundling

Many times customers experience limitations with products. As a solution, they may have to buy digital products that make it easier to use the physical product. Thus, bundling for convenience and efficiency makes customers’ lives easier.

For instance, software companies bundle hardware with software that is pre-configured for use with the physical hardware. This also removes technical complexities. Moreover, customers do not face the difficulty of looking for the right software and making separate purchases.

Here’s an example of a physical and digital bundle. The Bose Sound Bar is a physical product that can be operated with the digital app

Digital and physical bundling best practices

To ensure maximum returns and engagement, here are some best practices and tips to apply to your eCommerce hybrid bundles.

1. Pricing bundles strategically: Convey clear value proposition through your bundle pricing. Ensure profitable margins for your Shopify store.

2. Implement tiered bundling: Allow customers to choose from different tiers based on their requirements for physical and digital products.

3. Integrate digital and physical product fulfillment: Coordinate physical inventory and digital delivery systems. Create a system that ensures both digital and physical elements are delivered based on customer expectations.

4. Having backup alternative products: When one component of a bundle becomes unavailable, you should be able to offer an alternative or modify the bundle to ensure customer satisfaction.

5. Communication and onboarding: Communicate the real value of the bundle to customers so that they know how to maximize the usability of the bundle. Explain physical product set up and digital activation while onboarding customers.

6. Using data analytics: Track and analyze which digital and physical product bundling strategy is working. Track various metrics such as customer satisfaction score, customer lifetime value, etc.

Digital and physical bundling industry wise use cases

In this section, we explore how various industries are applying digital and physical bundling strategies to maximize sales, engagement, and customer satisfaction.

Technology

Technology and electronics brands can easily create digital and physical product bundles. For example, every physical electronic product can be paired with a complementing software that enhances the purchase value for customers and for the brand. Moreover, such bundling can also create a recurring revenue potential for brands, as customers may need to upgrade the software or digital elements.

Examples of digital and product bundles:

  • Gaming console bundled with game subscriptions, digital content, etc.
  • Smartphones paired with cloud storage, streaming services
  • Kindle bundled with ebook subscription

Fashion

Fashion products such as clothes and accessories can be bundled with digital styling services, stylings apps, and virtual fitting technologies. Such bundles not only increase engagement but also increase the potential for offering personalized experience to customers.

Here’s what you can bundle:

  • Curated subscription box service including physical products and digital styling advice
  • Physical products with digital fashion magazine subscriptions

Health and wellness

One of the industries that leverages bundling well is the health and wellness sector. Brands offer lifestyle solutions via bundles, such as fitness equipment with nutrition or progress-tracking apps, coaching sessions, etc. This helps increase recurring revenue.

Here are a few examples:

  • Fitness equipment with nutrition apps, workout tracking software
  • Health supplement subscription with health tracking app
  • Bundle ebooks with products

Education

Bundles for education, training, coaching can include physical books, ebooks, progress tracking apps, certification tracking systems, and more. Education digital and physical product bundling creates a more engaging experience for learners, students, and teachers.

Here are some examples to create education hybrid bundles:

  • Physical books and papers with digital learning apps and tools
  • Physical products with digital tracking systems, apps, and tools
  • Books with online courses, mentorship programs, and digital resources

Wrapping up: How to set up digital and physical product bundling on your Shopify store?

Depending on your product type and industry, you can set up digital and physical product bundles on your Shopify store by trying out various strategies, discounting methods, and bundling options.

However, start with one or two such bundles, rund A/B tests, monitor their performance, optimize, and then take your bundling strategy forward.

items.html:
The average attention span is shrinking. Did you know it affects your customers too when browsing your site?

Yes! Generic product recommendations are not enough to grab their attention anymore.

Today’s customers expect personalized shopping experiences that meet their specific needs and preferences.

Giants like Amazon and Netflix have trained customers to expect personalization.

This applies to bundles as well. So, when creating bundles, ensure you make the bundles relevant to different customer segments.

How do you do that?

With data and analytics. By collecting and analyzing customer data such as purchase history, browsing behavior, spending capacity, and personal preferences, you can create various customer segments.

Next, you can create personalized product bundles that align with these different segments. This increases the potential of sales, increases revenue, average order value (AOV), and customer satisfaction.

A well planned strategy for dynamic Shopify bundles can become a strong revenue-generation vertical for your business.

In this blog, we explore all about personalized product bundles, strategies, how to set it up, smart bundling tools to use, and more.

Let’s get started!

What are dynamic bundles?

Dynamic bundles are created based on customer data. For instance, bundles are created based on purchase history, browsing behavior, etc. Data collected with the help of Shopify tools is used to extract insights that can help create bundle offers.

For example, using AI-powered tools, you can monitor customer behavior. If customers are browsing certain products a lot, combine those products and sell them as a bundle, at a discount.

What’s happening here? You’re putting together products that customers like and selling it as a package. This increases the perceived value of the bundle. Moreover, there’s a discount on the bundle. This also increases its sales potential.

Automation tools help personalize bundling from curation to promotion to discounting. Dynamic bundles for Shopify stores increase AOV, customer satisfaction, sales and revenue.

So what’s the difference between dynamic and static bundles?

Unlike dynamic bundles, static bundles are not based on any customer data. Static bundles are simply put together and do not have the potential to change.

Example:

Creating bundles based on purchase history

Purchase history data provides various insights that can help personalize bundles. From returning customers to new customers, upselling and cross-selling, purchase history data can be used in multiple ways. Here are some:

Segmenting returning vs. new users

Returning customers and new customers have to be approached differently. For instance, for returning customers, you may have to create bundles that are based on their past purchases and preferences. Whereas for new customers, you will have to focus on product discovery and value proposition.

So, if you want to create conversion-focused bundles, get into the details of how to approach returning and new customers:

  • Returning customer: Create bundles based on their past purchase history, budget and affordability, seasonal buying patterns, product preferences, etc.
  • New customer: Consider creating bundles based on data from similar demographic segments from your website, browsing behavior, and popular combinations.

Upselling and cross-selling strategies

Dynamic bundling strategies offer potential for upselling and cross-selling. The key to this is understanding customers’ journey, behavior, and purchase, and creating upselling and cross-selling recommendations via bundles.

For instance, a customer has recently bought a display rack for their house. Depending on your product inventory, offer a bundle including a floor rug, bookends, a lamp, etc. Sell it as a room makeover bundle at a discount.

Smart product pairing ideas

Bundling obvious products together is one strategy, but not the best one. If you want to create more value for customers, think more strategically, and try these dynamic bundles on your Shopify store.

  • Use data analysis to identify unique products bought together by customers, which you may have missed or never thought about
  • Create seasonal and event-based dynamic bundles. For this, continuously collect and analyze data from your store
  • Use geographic and demographic information to create bundles based on location

Using browsing behavior to influence bundles

There’s a lot of data you can extract from your Shopify store. But to design your bundles for personalized shopping experience, focus on browsing behavior data: Here are some tips:

1. Tracking viewed products

Monitor the products customers view, the amount of time they spend on product pages, products they zoom in, read descriptions of, and how they navigate. Tracking these activities in real-time can provide opportunities to offer AI-based recommendations in real time.

How to use this information? Create dynamic bundles including the products customers browse, create multiple bundles and show comparisons, and create unique bundles for customers who like to discover new products.

Example:

2. Creating product recommendations based on cart activity

Cart activity is one of the most important factors to track on eCommerce stores. Because it shows intent. Customers who are interested in buying add products to the cart. This makes them your potential target customers for bundles.

Use bundling strategies to offer the products in the cart as bundles. Pair those products with other high-value items to upsell and cross-sell. Set-up real-time dynamic bundle offers. You can also target these customers later if they abandon the carts.

3. Implementing “complete the look” or “frequently bought together”

Commonly used by many eCommerce stores, ‘complete the look’ and ‘frequently bought together’ are bundling strategies that help influence customer psychology into making purchases. While one increased the perceived value of products, the other functions on social proof.

Make these strategies more impactful for dynamic bundling by personalizing messaging, images, and pricing and discounts based on customer segments and preferences.

These conversion-focused bundling strategies can be applied to all products and industries. However, these tactics work well for fashion, apparel, home decor, home appliances, accessories, etc.

Tools that enable dynamic bundling on Shopify

AI-driven bundling tools are the key to offering personalized bundles. When your bundles are more relevant to customers, its conversion increases. There are many powerful tools that process data efficiently, and some, in real-time, too. Here are some tools that make dynamic bundling more impactful with AI-based recommendations.

  • WISER: Smart product recommendations and dynamic pricing strategies

Impact of eCommerce personalization on conversions

Before we get into the details of how personalization impacts conversions, let’s look at some statistics:

  • 71% of customers expect personalization from brands
  • Businesses that get personalization right generate 40% more revenue
  • 89% of businesses see personalization as a key to success
  • 67% of consumers want businesses to give them relevant product recommendations
  • 78% of customers that experience personalization are likely to refer brands to friends

Study also shows that companies that are able to leverage personalization and extract value out of it, grow 40% faster than those that don’t.

Source

How to apply A/B testing for personalized product bundles?

Let’s learn about how to run A/B tests to offer dynamic bundles.

Step 1: Create variations of your product bundles. Try various bundling ideas and strategies to build bundle recommendations.

Step 2: Randomly assign customers to view some bundles based on their location, time of browsing, etc.

Step 3: Track which bundles are getting more clicks, more sales, more browsing. Also track which bundles customers are abandoning in carts.

Step 4: Track key metrics such as conversion rate, AOV, revenue per customer, new customers, old customers, and which bundles are star performers

Step 5: Test one variable at a time and segment your customers to understand how different segments respond to personalized bundles

How to reduce bounce and increase cart size for Shopify bundling strategies?

To maximize ROI from your bundling strategy and ensure long-term success, try these methods to reduce bounce and increase AOV.

  • Monitor your site speed. If it has slowed down, improve the speed. Lower speeds lead to increased bounce rates
  • Create engaging bundles that make customers browse, explore, see images, and read bundle descriptions. Increased engagement can provide more opportunities for you to offer dynamic bundle incentives and close sales
  • Ensure your Shopify store is mobile-friendly and your bundles pages are designed for a small screen. This can help reduce cart abandonment as customers can shop from anywhere, any time
  • Create attractive bundles and promote them effectively. Use targeted marketing campaigns, personalized messaging, and automation. Install a smart bundling tool that offers these capabilities

items.excerpt: Ecommerce sales tend to be 10X around events and certain seasons. Take for instance BFCM sales. The event marks the highest sales for many brands. items.html:
Ecommerce sales tend to be 10X around events and certain seasons.

Take for instance BFCM sales. The event marks the highest sales for many brands.

Ecommerce shopping has its highs and lows; peak seasons and slow periods. Customers generally tend to buy a lot more around key dates, seasons, and specific times of the year.

As customers buy a lot, one strategy that can be beneficial for both customers and Shopify merchants is product bundles.

Why so?

Bundles increase the perceived value of the customers’ purchases, are convenient, and offer price benefits.

For brands, seasonal Shopify bundles increase sales, customer satisfaction, and revenue.

However, there’s a lot that goes into creating bundles for seasons and events. In this blog, we explore all about creating seasonal Shopify bundles.

Curious to learn? Let’s go!

Identifying key retail dates for your niche

One of the first steps to planning seasonal bundles is to identify key dates/seasons. But these will also depend on your product niche, locations you deliver to, etc. Let’s look at a few ways to go about holiday bundle ideas:

1. Common, global events

Common events such as BFCM sales, Valentine’s Day, Mother’s Day, back to school, etc. are potential dates for offering bundles. Since the dates of these events are fixed, you can plan much in advance.

Here’s a pro tip to stand out from the crowd and increase event-driven sales: Don’t bundle common items available on every other eCommerce store. Take the approach of emotional storytelling. For example, for V-Day, put together items that lead to spending quality time together, offer bonding activities, acts of love, etc.

Example: School-themed bundles

2. Industry-specific dates

Another seasonal Shopify bundle idea is to tap into your industry-specific dates. For example, if you’re a sports brand that sells clothing and accessories, identify key dates in the year and create relevant bundles. Show customers you’re an industry expert. Here are some ideas:

  • Yoga bundle for yoga day
  • Running bundle for the annual marathon day
  • Sport-specific bundles, for example, tennis bundle during Wimbledon

3. Plan your eCommerce marketing calendar in advance

Planning ahead can ensure you have enough time to market and promote your bundles via different platforms. Moreover, it also gives you time to adjust and optimize to increase event-driven sales from bundles:

Here are some tips:

  • Plan for global and local calendars
  • Run A/B tests for the bundles
  • Optimize for maximum ROI
  • Upgrade your Shopify tools in time for a seamless experience

Bundle ideas by season/event

Now let’s look at some bundling ideas you can use to create bundles based on seasons or events.

1. Holiday gift bundles

Holiday seasons offer multiple opportunities to create bundles. Most customers go through something called choice paralysis – find it hard to choose gifts. You can solve this problem by offering thoughtful bundles and increasing sales. Let’s look at some holiday bundle ideas:

  • For Christmas, create experience bundles with gourmet hot chocolate, luxury blankets, candles, etc.
  • For the Holiday Season, put together travel kits, bags, travel accessories, etc.
  • Offer a considerable discount on the bundle, for example, 20 to 25%, which makes it valuable and increase AOV

Example: A tea brand offer Christmas tea bundles for gifting

2. Back to school kits

Another opportunity to create seasonal Shopify bundles is during school reopening. Customers buy all sorts of products for schools and if combined together in a bundle, it can offer considerable price benefits and savings. Let’s look at some different ideas to create back-to-school bundles.

  • Back to school bundle for boys and girls
  • School basics bundle, with bag, lunch box, water bottle
  • Stationery kit bundle
  • Art and creative bundle
  • School sports bundle, with shoes, clothes, towel, etc.

3. Cross-sell opportunities for themed bundles

Seasonal Shopify bundles are also an opportunity for cross-selling products. Rather than selling a single product, encourage customers to buy more via bundles. The trick? Put together complementing items and position them as complete solutions. Here’s what you can do:

  • Use customer data to identify products bought together
  • Create seasonal themed bundles from these products
  • Example: A fitness brand can create travel sports bundles, yoga retreat bundles, hiking vacation bundles, etc.

How to automate bundle launches?

One of the best features for eCommerce stores is automation. From bundle launch to marketing to discounting, you can automate all the processes related to bundles. Here’s how:

1. Scheduling launches and taking bundles live automatically

Bundling apps offer automation features, including Shopify bundle scheduling. This allows you to plan and prepare for bundle launches much in advance, so you don’t have to leave all the tedious work for the last minute.

Here are some aspects to keep in mind for Shopify automation for bundle launches:

  • Ensure you choose an app that has Shopify bundle scheduling features
  • Set up pricing changes, inventory allocation, etc.
  • Craft a compelling promotional message
  • Choose an optimal day, date, and time, and pre-configure in advance
  • Use advanced bundling features that allow you to launch bundles in sequence, where tiered bundles become available at specific interval

2. Set timers for expiry

Another key factor to think about when automating your seasonal Shopify bundles is to set timers for its expiry. By offering limited-period seasonal bundle offers, you can create FOMO and urgency, increasing sales.

Here’s one way of setting timers:

  • Start with full availability when you make all bundle available
  • As they get sold, set up a ‘limited number remaining’ status
  • Next, set up ‘final hours’ for specific discounts on the bundles
  • And the last stage, automatically remove the bundles from the Shopify catalog

3. Email/SMS integration for announcement

Once you automate bundles, it’s also important to ensure your customers know about these. That’s where integrated Shopify automation communication comes in. Think email, SMS, WhatsApp messages, etc.

Smart Shopify bundling apps help with data collection, analysis, and segmenting customers based on the data. You can also set up personalization for bundle announcements based on customers’ past purchases.

Promotional tactics for seasonal bundles

Once you set up and automate your bundles, it’s time to promote and market them. Because unless you market your Shopify bundles, your target audience may not even know about them.

1. Landing pages, countdown timers, FOMO tactics

Since seasonal and event-based bundles are not regulars, you will need to create special promotional campaigns. You not only have to make customers aware about these bundles, but also ensure they buy it within a specific period. Here are some tips:

  • Create a landing page with images showing the complete bundle, strategic CTAs, countdown timers, social proof, etc.
  • Include different FOMO elements to encourage customers to buy the seasonal Shopify bundles in time, for example, limited-time bonus items that disappear at specific intervals, etc.
  • Keep it authentic by using real inventory data, real customer reviews, etc.

2. Collaborate with influencers and partners

Depending on your products and industry, you can partner with influencers and other brands to create and offer bundles. Doing so can help you expand your reach and grow your customer base. Here’s how you can make this exercise more meaningful:

  • Create co-branded bundles with influencers and other brands
  • Create exclusive campaigns to promote these seasonal Shopify bundles
  • Make the bundle experiential by adding experiences to the bundle along with products
  • Engage in cross-promotion with the influencer or brand

3. Offer exclusivity to loyal customers

One way to increase sales from seasonal bundles is to offer exclusive access and incentives to loyal customers. Here are some ideas:

  • Create tiered exclusive offers and access. For instance, different loyalty levels receive different bundle benefits
  • Create members only bundles that include exclusive, limited-edition products
  • Combine other marketing tactics such as referrals for your loyal members

Wrapping up: get started with seasonal Shopify bundles

There are many opportunities round the year to create seasonal bundles. From festivals to global events to special days, you can truly succeed with your bundling strategy if you plan it strategically.

One of the most important parts of strategic planning is to plan ahead. And thankfully, if you know your yearly calendar, you can not only plan, but also schedule bundle campaigns in advance.

However, to schedule and automate, you will require a smart bundling app that has various features to market, promote, collect data, and optimize campaigns.

Bundles work well for both eCommerce merchants and customers.

Customers like the discounted price benefits and added value, while merchants get opportunities to upsell, cross-sell, and try other profit-making tactics.

However, many merchants take bundle pricing too lightly. The result? They end up making pricing mistakes that hurt profits.

For instance, over discounting and miscalculating margins.

The best way to maximize ROI from bundling is to balance value perception with margin preservation.

In this blog, we explore the many ways to get pricing right for bundling.

Want to grow bundling revenue from your Shopify store? Try these bundle pricing strategies.

Understanding bundle pricing margins

Before we jump into bundle pricing strategies, let’s understand pricing margins, how to calculate margins, and Shopify tools that can help with it.

How to calculate product pricing margins?

To calculate Shopify bundle discounts correctly, it is important to keep in mind a few best practices for long-term success.

  • Include all direct costs associated with the bundle. For example, cost of products, shipping, warehousing, storage, payment processing, etc.
  • Another factor to consider to calculate product margins is to strategically group products for bundles in a way that it helps increase the average order value (AOV)
  • Maximize the value perception of the bundle for customers by strategically selecting products and presenting price benefits. For example, mention the original price if products are bought individually compared to the bundle price

Set a margin threshold

One bundle pricing strategy that many experts recommend is to set a margin threshold. Meaning, set a bundle margin that does not go below a minimum acceptable figure. For instance, say you set a 20% margin threshold for each bundle. You can choose a margin threshold depending on your product type and industry.

A related strategy for Shopify bundle discounts is to set margin thresholds based on product sales volumes. For instance, high-volume products can have a lower margin threshold, and low volume, seasonal, or niche products can have a higher margin threshold. This strategy helps ensure AOV as well as average profit earning.

Example:

Tools useful for product pricing margins

There are multiple apps in the market for eCommerce discounting, tracking profitability, etc. For instance, Shopify and Shopify Plus have built-in basic features that help with product and bundle pricing. Additionally, you can integrate various third-party apps with Shopify.

Appstle Bundles & Discounts App is designed for Shopify and Shopify Plus stores to increase AOV with smart product combinations. The app helps increase products with targeted discounting. Along with the option to set up multiple bundle types and discount options, the app helps track bundle performance, so you can optimize it in real time.

How to calculate bundle pricing: step-by-step

Now let’s understand bundle pricing strategies through some examples.

Additive vs. perceived value pricing

Additive pricing for bundling involves adding prices of all individual prices and then offering a discount on it. For example, a coffee bundle that includes a coffee machine ($200), a coffee mug ($20), and a packet of coffee ($10) sums up to $230. It is sold at a bundle price of $20 discount at $ 210.

Additive pricing is easy and straightforward for brands to understand and communicate to customers. It clearly highlights the overall savings on a bundle. However, it may not be able to convey the added value customers perceive.

In the perceived value method, bundles are priced based on the customer’s value perception of the bundle. Here, prices of individual products are not added. This leads to profitable bundles. However, it is hard to understand the perceived value customers place on a bundle.

Example:

What to include in bundle pricing?

What are the factors to consider when working out your Shopify bundle discounts? Here are all the costs you must consider in order to reach a profitable price for your bundles and avoid over-discounting or charging less.

  • Bundle packaging cost, such as boxes, protective material, larger boxes, etc.
  • Shipping cost, such as dimensional weight
  • Handling time, including picking and packing cost
  • Quality control costs, such as inspection of products, bundles, or shipment

Effective bundle pricing strategies

Bundle pricing might seem simple and straightforward, but it isn’t. If not priced strategically, it can lead to loss. There are multiple strategies to price bundles, based on product type and industry. Here are some effective approaches to pricing bundles.

1. Tiered discounts based on cart value

Tiered eCommerce discounting involves setting dynamic discounts based on the items in the bundle. In simple terms, customers who buy larger bundles get more discount, and smaller bundles get lesser discount. This type of bundle pricing strategy helps increase AOV. It also helps preserve margins on smaller bundles.

Let’s understand tiered discounts through an example:

Tier 1: $100 to $200 bundle value – 10% discount

Tier 2: $200 to $300 bundle value – 15% discount

Tier 3: $400 to $500 bundle value – 20% discount

2. Psychological pricing

Psychological pricing works on the principle of influencing customers to make purchases via psychological tactics around pricing. For instance, how you present pricing, how you display discounts, and how you convey the value of a bundle to customers can lead to purchase decisions.

Let’s look at some psychological bundle pricing strategies:

1. Price display-based strategy

The way you display pricing and discount can influence customers’ perception. For instance, showing the price of individual products compared to bundle price can highlight savings. When customers see how much they can save, they tend to make purchases faster.

2. Odd-even and charm pricing

One of the most common pricing strategies that works well is charm pricing or odd-even pricing. For example, if a bundle costs $50, make it $40.99. This gives a perception to customers that they’re paying less, even though it’s just a slight decrease. Customers also tend to buy products that have prices ending in an odd number.

Example:

3. Flash vs. evergreen bundle discount

Another bundle pricing strategy plays around with time and urgency factors. We’re talking about flash and evergreen discounts.

Flash bundle discounts are offered for a short duration, creating urgency as these are for a limited time. With flash pricing you can offer higher discounts as this strategy works well for clearing inventory.

Evergreen discounts refer to consistent discounts that are available all the time. In this strategy, the discounts are moderate. This strategy focuses on long-term customer value and margin preservation.

Avoiding common bundle pricing strategy mistakes

While setting Shopify bundle discounts looks easy, small mistakes could hurt your pricing strategies. Let’s look at some:

  • Avoid stacking bundle discounts with other promotional offers as this could turn into losses. For instance, if you offer bundle discount, first-time purchase discount, and another discount on the same purchase, you may end up with losses from such sales.
  • Don’t underestimate fulfillment costs. For instance, bundle costs include packaging, storage, higher shipping weights, complex return processing, etc. Hence, always add a fulfillment cost to your bundles to avoid facing losses on these sales.
  • Another bundle pricing strategy mistake to avoid is product mix mismatch. When you combine mismatched products in a bundle, the potential of its sales decreases. Hence, use customer purchase history data to identify products that would go well together in a bundle.

items.html:
With increasing competition in the eCommerce market, merchants are trying innovative strategies to offer new experiences to customers.

One such creative strategy is combining multiple Shopify elements, for instance, bundles, subscriptions, and loyalty programs.

While all three are individually effective marketing strategies, when combined, they offer various benefits.

In this blog, we explore how bundle and subscription integration with loyalty programs can help increase revenue, improve customer lifetime value (CLV), and drive higher retention rates.

Want to learn how to implement this strategy in your Shopify store?

Let’s begin!

Why bundle and subscription integration?

Subscription, bundle, and loyalty program, each has a different value-add for customers. For eCommerce brands too, these three elements offer specific advantages.

For instance, subscriptions provide convenience of automating recurring revenue on Shopify; bundles increase average order value (AOV); and loyalty programs improve long-term customer-brand relationship and repeat purchases.

Now imagine if these three are integrated into each other. Integrating the three strategies helps:

  • Improve customer lifetime value (CLV)
  • Make customers’ shopping experience exciting
  • Develop deeper brand loyalty
  • Drive recurring revenue for Shopify stores
  • Combines the benefits of all three – value, convenience, and loyalty

One of the best examples of bundle and subscription integration is streaming subscriptions.

Bundle and subscription integration: recurring revenue for Shopify stores

In this section, we explore how integrating bundles and subscriptions helps Shopify stores and customers, and how to go about it.

Benefits of offering bundles on a subscription model

1. Increase average order value

Bundles include multiple products, typically, at a discounted price. This perceived value appeals customers to purchase more, thus, increasing AOV. Add to it, the convenience of subscriptions that allows customers to make recurring purchases. Recurring bundles in subscriptions means increased AOV.

2. Improve customer retention

When customers feel satisfied with their purchases, they tend to stay loyal to those brands. This has a positive impact on the customer retention rate. Customer retention tools make it easy to include bundles in subscriptions and offer cross-selling opportunities, enhancing the perceived value of the subscription box.

Additionally, discounted pricing, upselling, and personalization via tailored product selection, all lead to more satisfaction and stronger brand and customer bonds.

3. Recurring income

Customers who tend to sign up for subscriptions tend to be more loyal and show more engagement. The fact that they signed up for long-term subscription means they like the brand and the products. For brands, this helps generate recurring revenue.

Add bundles to subscriptions, and it leads to not only increased AOV but recurring high revenue. This also enhances operational efficiency for brands by making orders predictable, which helps with inventory management.

Bundle and subscription integration: use cases

While a combination of bundles and subscriptions has many benefits, it may be suitable for some products and industries, more than it is for others. Let’s look at the best use cases for combining bundles with subscriptions:

  • Daily consumables, such as tea, coffee, groceries, and other food items. These are recurring purchases and can lead to good bundle ideas
  • Pet supplies, such as treats, pet food, pet grooming products, toys, etc., making pet management convenient and easy for pet parents
  • Personal care products, such as skincare, moisturizer, shampoo, etc., can be clubbed into bundles. They can also be personalized based on customer needs

Example:

Combine bundles and subscriptions with Appstle

Appstle Shopify app makes it easy to combine bundles with subscription. The Shopify loyalty app is designed for Shopify and Shopify Plus stores, with built-in features that reduce technical complexity and automate processes. Here are some Appstle features:

  • Flexibility to create bundles that can be offered as one-time purchase as well as subscription
  • Set discount levels for bundle purchases
  • Automatically adjust bundle availability based on stock levels
  • Prevent overselling, maintaining accurate inventory
  • Delivery frequency options for bundle subscriptions
  • Customer self help for adjusting delivery schedule, skip deliveries, modify bundles, etc.
  • Automated communication throughout subscription journey

Bundle and loyalty integration: rewarding smarter

Just like bundle and subscription integration, bundles combined with loyalty programs also offer unique and specific benefits. Let’s explore all about integrating bundles and loyalty programs.

How to use bundles to reward loyal customers

  • Offer incentives on bundle purchases to loyalty members
  • Offer a bundle as reward to VIP loyalty program members
  • Provide exclusive access to bundle deals only to loyalty members
  • Customize loyalty programs to implement creative strategies
  • Create exclusive bundles for high-tier loyalty members that aren’t available to other tiers
  • Create bundles with premium products, limited-edition items, and unique

How to offer points on bundles

There are many ways to offer points on bundles via loyalty programs. For example, a straightforward approach is to offer points based on the bundle price, just like you do on normal purchases.

Another way to offer points on bundling strategies is to assess the average order value (AOV) and whether there’s potential for repeat purchases of these bundles by the same customers. In such cases, you could increase points.

Tiered loyalty programs can have their specific points accumulation structure. For instance, standard points on small bundles and bonus points on larger bundles. Customers can also be offered points based on the tier they belong to – more points for higher tiers.

How to set up bundle subscription integrations

Setting up bundle subscription integrations with loyalty programs can seem complicated as there are multiple elements involved. Here are some tips and steps to follow:

App combinations that work well

Effective integrations require tools that offer API connections and integration capabilities. For example, Appstle Subscriptions App integrates easily with Shopify’s built-in bundle features. Moreover, Appstle also integrates with third-party apps such as Smile.io, LoyaltyLion, and Yotpo, among others. Let’s look at how some of these integrations help:

  • Smile.io and Appstle integration enables earning and redeeming points on subscription bundles. It makes automatic points allocation for recurring subscription orders and redemption easy. It also enables tier-based access to subscription bundles
  • Integrations help automate workflows, which help bundles in many ways. For instance, automating loyalty points on purchase of bundles, updating customer tier status, personalized notifications.

Key settings to check for integration

Check these settings in your bundle and subscription integration structure to ensure smooth functioning and clarity for customers.

1. Discount hierarchies

If integration is not done properly, it could lead to complications. For instance, it’s essential to set hierarchies for discount so that customers receive maximum price benefits. To ensure this, ensure you synchronize discounts carefully.

2. Renewal management

Another factor that can get complicated in bundle and subscription integration is renewal management. When customers renew subscriptions, loyalty tiers, points balance, and bundle availability should also change or update based on individual cases. Automated systems should account for these changes.

3. Update discounts, points

Also, when customers’ tiers change based on their purchase, their subscription accounts should get updated with relevant pricing, bundle availability, and loyalty points applicable. It is essential to synchronize these processes when there’s a subscription, bundles, and loyalty program integration.

4. Messaging and notifications

When subscriptions, bundles, and loyalty programs are integrated, notifications and messages have to be sent across platforms. For instance, a subscription renewal may impact loyalty points balance and bundle availability. Hence, the messages should go across all platforms involved. This ensures customers are informed about every detail.

Avoid overlaps between bundles, subscriptions, and loyalty program

Since many features of the three strategies may be similar, it is important to avoid overlaps. Follow these best practices and tips.

1. Incentive stacking

How many perks customers can receive when the three elements are integrated is based on individual businesses. For instance, some Shopify stores might want to offer more benefits than other stores. Incentive rules should be clearly set via the integrated apps and also communicated to customers.

2. Clear communication

Your subscription, bundles, and loyalty programs may have different policies. And hence, it is important to inform customers how the three function when integrated. For example, there could be limitations or exclusions.

3. Test how integrated elements function

The number and kind of transactions that occur on your Shopify store can vary widely. Hence, it is important to test incentive combinations when you set up loyalty, bundle and subscription integrations. Test for different scenarios that involve various combinations.

4. Tracking and monitoring

Consistently track and monitor to understand how customers use incentives, which incentive combinations are customers using, and how it impacts your profit. This data can help you optimize incentives structure. Use Shopify loyalty app to automate tracking.

Wrapping up – bundle and subscription integration with loyalty program

When implemented strategically, subscription, loyalty, and bundle integrations can help grow your Shopify business via innovative ways. And that’s where the key is – to think of the three as interconnected and not as separate.

Think of creative ways to combine the three, extract targeted data, and consistently optimize this new strategy to grow and scale your business.

You can apply this integration strategy easily with the help of Appstle. Appstle offers all three tools and advanced integration capabilities. Moreover, Appstle’s customization features can help you create a truly unique integrated experience like no other.

Explore Appstle for integrating subscriptions, bundles, and loyalty programs.

items.html:
Data analytics is playing a key role in crafting eCommerce strategies.

Every purchase, click, view, and action taken by eCommerce visitors is tracked. The resulting data and insights are used to craft multiple strategies.

One of the ways data is used is to create bundling strategies.

Unlike simple bundling of the past that was based on guesswork, now, Shopify merchants and marketers use data to create targeted bundles.

Thanks to data and analysis tools in the market, creating data-driven bundles has become easy. Bundle performance analytics combined with smart tools provides winning strategies for business growth and profitability.

In this blog, we explore data-driven bundling strategies, tools, and how to implement these in your Shopify stores.

Curious? Let’s explore more!

Data-driven bundling strategies for high-performing bundles

You can extract different types of data from your Shopify bundles set up. Once you identify high-performing products or bundles, you can convert that information into sales-driven bundling strategies. In this section, we explore some effective bundle performance analytics approaches and use cases.

1. Track bundle metrics

While there are many different metrics you could tack from high-performing bundles, if you spread yourself too thin tracking too many, you may not be able to use it effectively.

The solution: Limit the metrics you track.

Let’s focus on a few metrics such as:

  1. Conversion rate
  2. Average order value (AOV)
  3. Units per transaction.

By tracking conversion rate, you can get an understanding of which bundles are high-converting. These bundles are more popular amongst customers. Either its price is attractive or products are valuable. However, you must also calculate the profitability.

Another bundle performance analytics to track is average order value (AOV). Your bundles AOV should keep increasing. Even a slight and gradual increase can have a big impact on your revenue. And if AOV isn’t increasing, it means it’s time to make your bundling offers more exciting.

Next, track the number of items customers purchase – units per transaction. Bundles that have multiple related products tend to sell more. Tracking this can also increase cross-selling opportunities.

How to use Shopify analytics and app dashboards to track bundle metrics?

Shopify has built-in bundle performance analytics features. Use the analysis reports to gain insights into sales performance, customer behavior, etc. For more detailed Shopify bundle reporting, you must integrate a bundling app, such as Appstle Bundling & Discounts.

Further, it is essential to create custom reports for deeper bundle analysis. For instance, you could set up tracking for specific SKUs, track different customer segments based on bundles they buy, etc. Review these custom reports periodically to identify patterns and opportunities.

Here’s how you can use data for bundling:

  • Which products are customers buying together? Can you create a bundle of those items?
  • What products are customers buying one after the other through separate purchases? Can these be clubbed together in bundles?
  • Which are your most-bought and popular high-value products? Add one high-value product in each bundle and increase AOV.
  • Bundle high sales, low value products in a bundle to increase conversion rate.

Example:

2. Personalize bundles based on data

Personalized shopping experiences attract customers. No doubt!

Studies show 80% of customers are more likely to make purchases when brands offer personalized experiences.

But eCommerce merchants tend to ignore this strategy for bundles.

That’s because the idea of personalizing bundles with multiple products for various customer segments comes across as complex. But it really isn’t.

Use these different strategies to personalize bundles:

  • Analyze bundle purchase history to understand customer preference
  • Identify browsing patterns and use the information to provide personalized recommendations
  • Use cart abandonment data and bring back customers with personalized offers
  • Gather data about products frequently bought together by customers and create a bundle of those items

Another strategy is to segment customers by intent or lifetime value (LTV). For instance, high-value customers might be more inclined towards premium bundles, while others might go for discounted bundles. Here are some segments you could consider:

  • High-value
  • Budget customers
  • New customers
  • Existing customers

Bundle personalization can be effective if you collect and analyze data efficiently. For this, you will require smart eCommerce analytics tools that help track custom behavior, collect data, analyze it, and share Shopify bundle reports.

Pro tip: Start with broad segments to create personalized offers. Continuously collect data to refine segments for deeper personalization.

3. Optimize bundle pricing with real-time data

Customers want better pricing and savings every time they shop. And so, when you price your bundles strategically, you can increase conversion rate.

Let’s explore how to go about pricing bundles based on data.

  • Apply real-time data analyses for better bundle pricing
  • Run A/B tests for different bundle prices
  • Create many different bundles with the same products but price them differently with various discount levels
  • Try different discount presentation methods. For example, percentage discount, fixed amount discount, etc.
  • Set up dynamic pricing based on inventory levels. For example, low-stock products at a higher price
  • Pricing based on seasonal demand. Use eCommerce analytics tools to track seasonal pricing from previous years as well
  • Add more high-stock prices in bundles and offer discounts on these bundles
  • Track discount and conversion rate of bundles to identify the right balance
  • Automate dynamic pricing and real-time pricing via your Shopify bundle app
  • Offer limited-time pricing to create urgency and FOMO

Getting started with data-driven bundling

While data-driven bundling has many advantages for Shopify stores, implementing it requires a thought-through process. Here are some steps to follow:

  1. Define clear goals for your Shopify bundling strategy. For instance, increasing AOV, clearing dead inventory, improve conversion rate, or improving long-term profits
  2. Define short-term and long-term goals to measure progress
  3. Set up customer behavior tracking and data collection systems by using smart bundling apps, such as Appstle
  4. Review bundle performance analytics and metrics weekly, analyze customer feedback
  5. Periodically adjust pricing based on conversion data
  6. Monthly, analyze customer segments, run A/B tests of bundles
  7. Start small with two or three bundles with fast-selling products
  8. Build the bundling strategy with a focus on customer value proposition
  9. Continuously optimize using Shopify data and insights

Bundling strategy breakdown: SaltyTubCo

Here’s a case study of the bundling strategy of SalthyTubCo, a wellness and self-care brand that offers bath salts. The brand uses Appstle Bundles & Discounts to manage its bundles. So what makes this brand’s bundles stand out? Let’s find out.

  • StaltyTubCo has a dedicated page for bundles. Since all the products are listed on this page, it makes discovering products easy. Also, it makes purchasing easy
  • Customers can pick any four products of their choice and make it a bundle. This activity of adding items to the bundle also adds an element of fun to the shopping experience. Unlike other bundles that have pre-selected products, here, customers self choose what items they want in their bundles
  • The four-product bundle offers a 25% discount. The individual products have varying prices, so customers can choose any four products of their choice based on their budget. This allows customers to choose the same product multiple times or mix and match products
  • The USP of its bundle is not just the discount, it is personalization and customization. Customers can pick the products they want in their bundle. This flexibility and customized experience enhances the appeal for customers and potential for conversion

Create data-driven bundles with Appstle Bundles & Discounts

How well you capture and utilize data from your Shopify bundles can be the differentiating factor between you and your competitors.

The strategies detailed here can help you move from traditional bundling to a data-driven bundling approach, offering several benefits.

Maximize ROI from your Shopify bundles with continuous tracking, bundle performance analytics, and experimenting with different sales-driven bundling strategies.

However, tracking, data collection, analysis, reporting, and automating bundling processes will require a smart tool, such as Appstle Bundles & Discounts App.

  • Set up strategic and targeted product bundles
  • Multiple bundle types and discounting options
  • Real-time granular data analytics
  • Seamless Shopify POS integration
  • Dynamic bundling
  • 24x7x365 customer support for Shopify merchants

items.html:
Bundling is not a new strategy. eCommerce brands have been implementing it for years. However, basic bundling isn’t enough to hook customers anymore.

Traditional bundling has many limitations. For instance, lack of personalization, emotional disconnect with customers, and the inability to match customer preference, among others.

With increasing competition in the eCommerce space, brands are trying new and innovative Shopify bundling strategies to engage customers and increase sales.

Not only do these strategies increase customer loyalty, they also help increase the average order value (AOV), eventually, contributing to increasing profits.

So what are these strategies? And can you implement them in your Shopify stores?

In this blog, we explore four such advanced Shopify bundling strategies that you can try on your store.

Let’s get started!

Must try advanced Shopify bundling strategies

Here are four strategies that can help your Shopify business grow via bundling.

1. Build-a-box bundles

Most people associate bundles to a few different products selected by the store and sold as one pack or bundle. But bundles can also be put together by customers too. Yes! That’s a build-a-box bundle.

This Shopify bundling strategy has benefits for both customers and Shopify brands. For customers, it enables personalization, provides flexibility, higher satisfaction, convenience, and price benefits

For Shopify businesses, it leads to higher conversion rates, improved data insights, increased sales, and customer loyalty.

Some products for which build-a-box bundles work well are:

  • Snack boxes: customers can choose snacks of their choice for a fixed price or variable price bundle
  • Beauty and self-care kits: customers can pick cosmetics, self-care products, beauty products, make up, etc. based on their skin type and requirements
  • Apparel packs: customers can pick garments and accessories based on their size, color, style preference
  • Gourmet gift boxes: select coffee, tea, chocolate, wines, alcohols, etc.

Now, there are a lot of build-a-box apps that support bundling on Shopify stores. But you must choose the ones that are relevant for your Shopify store.

Some build-a-box apps preferred by Shopify merchants are:

  1. Appstle Bundles & Discounts: Appstle offers comprehensive and user-friendly features in the app, such as Shopify bundles, mix and match buncles, BOGO, Buy x Get Y, frequently bought together, bundle builder, custom bundles, and options for upsell, volume discount, etc.
  2. Bundler: Provides easy to create and manage product bundle options, mix and match bundles, upselling, etc.
  3. Selleasy: Enables upselling and cross-selling, frequently bought together features, product recommendations, etc.

Here’s an example of a gardening build your own bundle:

2. Mystery box bundle

Mystery boxes are based on the concept of offering a surprise to drive customer engagement. As the name suggests, these are bundles or boxes that have surprise products. Customers are not aware of the bundle contents.

Mystery box Shopify strategy works well because it creates value and adds excitement to an otherwise simple shopping experience. Going beyond transactional, these boxes offer an experience. This psychology is proven by a brand that saw only 15% return rate as opposed to the industry’s normal return rate of 40%.

That said, how you price mystery boxes on Shopify is critical. Here are some pricing strategies you could apply:

  • Keep the value proposition in mind when setting prices
  • Typically, brands offer products that are twice or thrice the value of the box price
  • Clearly communicate and visually show the value and price proposition
  • Personalization is a key Shopify bundling strategy. Customize mystery boxes for different customer segments

Further, lower your risks by doing this:

  • Have detailed product category descriptions
  • Share images of product examples
  • Make return policy and returns easy
  • Provide efficient customer support

Example:

3. Subscription bundles

Another effective Shopify bundling strategy is subscription bundles. This bundling strategy brings predictable revenue for Shopify stores. With subscriptions, customers enter into long-term association with brands and receive period deliveries.

Subscriptions help brands build deeper relationships with customers. This ongoing association also offers multiple opportunities for brands to interact and engage with customers. Subscriptions not only increase customer lifetime value (CLV), but also reduce acquisition costs.

Another key advantage of subscriptions is the potential to gather data from subscriber history and offer personalized subscription bundles. Shopify brands, too, can create customized subscription experiences using tools like the Appstle Subscriptions App.

Appstle makes it easy to customize subscription bundle plans. For instance, merchants can set up different types of Shopify subscriptions – build a box, fixed bundles, curated subscription bundles, and more. Moreover, Appstle features allow customers to change, edit, and customize their subscription bundles.

To retain your subscribers, try these best practices:

  • Keep your Shopify product bundling strategy exciting by consistently adding something new
  • Add surprise elements, such as new products, samplers, discount coupons, etc.
  • Allow flexibility of changing, swapping, pausing, and customizing subscriptions

4. Wholesale bundles

Bundles are not only for D2C brands. Bundling is an effective strategy for bulk buyers and wholesalers in the B2B segment. Consider this statistic: The global B2B eCommerce industry is expected to reach USD 13.68 trillion this year, and USD 60.62 trillion by 2034.

However, B2B Shopify wholesale bundles require a slightly different strategy. First, as a wholesaler you will have to understand your business customers’ needs well. You will have to club assorted products together that meet retailer customers needs.

For instance, if your customers are salons, you will have to create professional-use beauty products from multiple brands in a bundle.

Another aspect of Shopify wholesale bundles is to have access control. In wholesale business, pricing and product availability keep changing based on the market. And hence, it’s critical to have access to change the pricing and availability of your bundles on your Shopify store. For this, use a Shopify bundle app, which allows complete access and control, such as Appstle Bundles & Discounts.

Example: Bundles offers wholesale fashion bundles to brands

When and how to mix these Shopify bundling strategies

Now that we know some effective strategies, let’s understand how to use them. If you want a profitable Shopify business, you will have to apply multiple strategies to cater to different customer segments.

Let’s look at some strategies:

  • Mystery boxes to cater to customer segments that like to discover and use new products
  • Build-a-box-bundles for customers who prefer to have control and flexibility and find value in this form of bundles
  • Subscription bundles for customers who prefer convenience, price benefits, and long-term streamlined shopping experiences
  • Wholesale bundles to cater to businesses that prefer buying in bulk for price benefits

Let’s explore these strategies further with an example.

Here’s how a beauty and cosmetics brand can implement many of these Shopify bundling strategies.

Wholesale Bundles Create wholesale bundles of most-popular products, products that require to be cleated from inventory – use A/B testing and market trends Cosmetics retailers, salons, individual make up professionals, theatre companies Discounted pricing on each bundle

Wrapping up – ready to implement Shopify bundling strategy on your store?

By applying these different strategies – subscription, build-a-box, wholesale, and mystery bundles – you can take your Shopify business to the next level of growth.

However, experiment with one or two of these strategies rather than implementing all of them in one go. Try A/B testing, see which strategy works best for your customers, products, and industry.

items.excerpt: A quick online search about eCommerce membership benefits and perks shows hundreds of resources. But they’re all saying the same thing – discounts, offers, free-shipping. items.html:
A quick online search about eCommerce membership benefits and perks shows hundreds of resources. But they’re all saying the same thing – discounts, offers, free-shipping. And these run-off-the-mill benefits aren’t enough for members, not anymore.

Customers expect members-only perks on eCommerce stores. In this blog, we take a look at membership programs from the customers’ perspective, which is more about psychology, exclusivity, shared value, and culture.

Read about member-only perks strategies for small, mid-sized, and large enterprise brands that can really make a difference to membership programs today.

Member-only perks for small to mid-sized eCommerce businesses

Typically functioning on small budgets and fewer resources, small and mid-sized businesses require a balance between value and cost when planning member-only perks for eCommerce. Here are some effective strategies:

1. Experience over discounts

Gone are the days when offering discounts was enough to attract members. Today’s loyal members expect more engaging membership perks, such as experiences and things that add value to them.

According to a research report, customers crave for:

  • Emotional bonds – a sense of shared values and identity
  • Social bonds – connection to communities
  • Structural bonds – practical factors that make staying easier
  • Financial bonds – incentives that provide tangible value

Here are some ways to offer experiential perks:

  • Personalized recommendations, tailored content, and personalized communication
  • Community experiences via exclusive member communities, forum, and events (online and in-person) that foster a sense of belonging
  • Convenience via hassle-free shopping, fast deliveries, easy access to products and benefits, etc.
  • Members also want a feeling of exclusivity by receiving unique and exclusive Shopify perks

Example: Ikea membership offers experiences such as free tea and coffee every weekend, just-for members food offers, free family workshops, and protection against broken products.

2. Leverage automated cashback and store credit

With automated cashback, you can return a percentage of money to your customers. You can do so either via cash or store credit. Automated cashback and store credits help in many ways – increase repeat purchases, and loyalty. Here’s what you can do:

  • Offer a percentage of the amount customers pay as cash back. For example, 10% cashback on all purchases
  • Offer store credit on every purchase, on special occasions (birthday, anniversary), and at times as surprise gifts

3. Design a tiered membership program

With tiered membership programs, you can offer multiple levels, each with specific perks and benefits. With this structure, you can incentivize spending to entice customers to progress to higher tiers, enhance customer retention, and loyalty.

Another way to manage tiered membership is to allow customers to choose their preferred tiers by way of a membership fee. This flexibility and freedom can make customers feel satisfied and exclusive.

Here’s how to go about tiered membership member-only perks for eCommerce:

  • Low tier: Offer benefits such as discounts, points, and store credits on purchases
  • Mid tier: Offer exclusive discounts only to these members, early access, and personalized offers
  • Top tier: Offer premium perks, VIP access, dedicated customer support

4. Partner with complementing brands

The perks you offer today will become boring at some point. You have to keep changing and adding new perks. How do you do that? One way to do it is to partner with complementing brands and make them a part of your membership perks.

For example, if you’re a bicycle brand, partner with an accessories brand or sports wear brand. Offer discounts or gifts from these brands to your members. It not only increases your brand awareness, it also expands the customer base for both brands.

Do this:

  • Offer early access to new launches of your partner brand
  • Organize shared events exclusively for your members
  • Partner with new brands from time to time to keep your membership exciting
  • Offer discount coupons for the partner brand to your members

5. Automate perks delivery

Using technology to automate your membership program perks and benefits can not only streamline the process, but also enhance the membership experience for customers. Moreover, automating using an efficient Shopify membership app can save time, resources, and reduce manual work for your team.

Here’s how to use automation for membership perks delivery:

  • Set up automated points, store credits, and cashback systems
  • Send automated notifications and alerts for perks delivery
  • Provide automated customer support to members via a dedicate chat widget
  • Set up automated email marketing for perks delivery

6. Incorporate gamification

With game-like experiences via gamification, you can increase Shopify customer engagement, sales, and loyalty. Gamification involves fun games, instant rewards, challenges, badges, and other exciting elements.

For example, Nike ran the FuelBand campaign. The brand asked members to track their fitness progress to earn points and compete with other members. The gamified campaign led to community building and loyalty.

Source

Here’s how you can offer eCommerce member-only perks via gamification:

  • Offer points for purchases, product reviews, social media follow and engagement, referrals, etc.
  • Automate badges for various actions, such as when members cross a certain shopping threshold, or when they complete a specific number of years of being members
  • Improve relevance by personalizing gamification experience for members
  • Run contests as part of membership gamification

7. Limit perks to high-value actions

While you want to offer members perks and rewards for many small actions, there’s another strategy you must try. Limit eCommerce member-only perks to high-value actions only. For instance, offer rewards only when customers make large purchases, or share successful referrals. This way, you can increase Shopify customer engagement and make customers feel more closer to the brand.

There are many benefits of this strategy. It enhances program sustainability, and makes members more valuable to your brand.

Here are some ideas for this strategy:

  • Offer perks for large purchases only or free shipping on orders of large value
  • Offer rewards to members who initiate successful referrals for the membership
  • Offer perks to members who promote your brand via various channels

Member-only perks for mid to enterprise eCommerce businesses

Mid-sized to large enterprises usually have more budgets and resources to allocate to exclusive and premium membership perks. However, you can make your membership programs more valuable by using these eCommerce member-only perks strategies.

1. Offer exclusive, high-perceived-value access

To engage customers in membership programs of large enterprises, offer exclusive and high-perceived-value perks and benefits. For instance, you must think beyond rewards and points.

Here are some ideas:

  • VIP access to new launches
  • Dedicated support
  • Priority shipping and handling
  • Exclusive sneak-peek for to-be-launched products
  • Exclusive content, webinars, etc.
  • Customized solutions and experience
  • Limited edition products

For example, BMW runs the program, Joy Ride. Members save money on service and maintenance. The best feature of the program is that savings keep increasing as the car ages. This increases member loyalty.

2. Multi-tier program with premium benefits

Design a multi-tier membership program that ensures high ROI. For instance, the different tiers should cater to different high-value customer segments. It should encourage repeat purchases and loyalty. Moreover, it should bring in predictable revenue via the different tiers.

But when you’re designing this multi-tier program, ensure you clearly identify the different customer segments, clearly communicate perks in each tier, and track membership metrics for each tier separately

Here are some ideas of premium perks and benefits:

  • Offer access to limited-edition products, brand partnership offers that are not available to other tiers
  • Member-exclusive events for each tier. For example, behind-the-scenes tours, exhibitions, VIP curated experiences, etc.
  • Personalized experiences. For example, if you’re a fashion brand, offer the top tier members styling and personal shopping guide agent

Example: Nordstrom offers a four-tiered profitable loyalty program with exclusive perks for each level.

Source

3. Data-driven personalization

In enterprise-level membership programs, you can take personalization to the next level. How? By using data. Your high-value members will expect special and exclusive membership experiences. By collecting targeted data, you can offer exclusive Shopify perks and personalized experiences.

Here are some personalized data-driven eCommerce member-only perks ideas:

  • Customized gifts on special occasions
  • Exclusive, luxury benefits
  • Networking and meet and greet events with other members
  • Exclusive resources and content based on members’ preference
  • Flexible support and services based on members needs
  • Personalized product recommendations
  • Targeted discounts and exclusive bundles based on their past purchases

4. Omnichannel experiences

One of the advantages for enterprise-level businesses is the availability of budgets and resources to create comprehensive assets. For instance, when building your membership program, you can incorporate all channels and create an integrated system by investing in technology.

Here are some ideas to create omni channel membership experiences:

  • Connect multiple channels – online and offline stores, apps, social media, etc.
  • Maintain a consistent experience between different channels
  • Use a Shopify membership app that can handle scalability
  • Set up automated data analytics
  • Provide an integrated omnichannels experience where activities on all channels are in sync

5. Recurring revenue models

The basis of a successful membership program is members make repeated purchases, engage on a regular basis, and have a valuable long-term and ongoing association.

To enable a recurring revenue model via memberships, here are a few best practices:

  • Segment your members based on tiers, needs, preferences, and other parameters. Then create targeted recurring revenue models
  • Communicate clear value propositions to your members and make sure they find value in the membership
  • Enable multiple payment options. Flexibility leads to higher satisfaction and loyalty
  • Integrate smart technology and membership apps to helps you manage memberships and recurring income
  • Automate recurring revenue via your membership app

6. Leverage technology

It is easier for large enterprise and mid-sized businesses to incorporate and integrate membership platforms into their eCommerce systems. Leveraging technology can help automate processes, create seamless flows, lead to higher engagement, and overall a better membership experience.

Here’s what you should look for in membership tools:

  • The ability to automate tasks and processes
  • Scalability capabilities to ensure your business can grow
  • Create different types of membership programs based on your market
  • Offer innovative eCommerce member-only perks

How Appstle Memberships App can help offer member-exclusive perks

To run a successful membership program, you will have to think ahead of time; think like your customers; and beyond simple perks. Try the strategies that are relevant to your business and customers. Also, keep experimenting with new eCommerce member-exclusive perks ideas. Appstle is one of the most preferred membership apps for Shopify and Shopify Plus brands. The app provides a comprehensive set of features for small, mid-sized, and enterprise-level businesses.

Here are Appstle Memberships App key features:

  • Exclusive member perks, such as content, discounts, VIP benefits, community, etc.
  • Secure and stable memberships infrastructure leading to seamless functions
  • 24x7x365 customer support
  • Seamless integrations with third-party apps
  • Customization via Appstle Enterprise Plans

If you’re looking to launch a new membership program or enhance an existing program, explore Appstle.
