items.html:
Subscription models are one of the most effective strategies for the growth of eCommerce brands. The subscription industry has seen rapid growth and innovation in recent years. Shopify tiered subscription models are a key strategy in this eCommerce marketing mix.

That’s because tiered subscriptions offer many benefits, including increasing customer lifetime value (CLV). However, leveraging tiered subscriptions to increase CLV requires thoughtful strategies.

In this blog, we explore some of the most effective strategies for Shopify tiered subscription models along with action points you can easily try for your Shopify store.

Let’s get started!

What are Shopify tiered subscription models?

Shopify tiered subscriptions are pricing models that have different levels or tiers. Subscribers can sign up for their preferred tier to buy products or services on a period basis. Generally, for example, monthly, quarterly, or half yearly, etc.

Each subscription tier has a specific price point and offers specific benefits and perks. Typically, lower tiers get basic benefits, while higher tiers get more attractive and valuable perks.

Shopify tiered subscription models usually have two, three or four tiers. For example, Silver, Gold, and Platinum. The names of tiers change depending on the industry. For example, for the B2B industry, names such as, Starter, Growth, and Scale, are more appropriate.

In Shopify tiered subscription models, each tier has a different name, and different features, benefits, and perks. Customers can choose their preferred tier based on their budget, spending capacity, needs, and the perks, thus enabling brands to cater to different customer segments.

Here’s an example of an eCommerce tiered subscription model.

Ulta Beauty is a cosmetics and beauty products brand that caters to a wide range of audience. Its subscription program offers three tiers based on spending by customers.

How to increase customer lifetime value via tiered subscriptions?

Most eCommerce merchants think setting up a tiered subscription model on Shopify is enough to get recurring income flowing in and keeping customers happy forever. However, that’s not the case. Setting up an attractive subscription business is only the beginning. You will have to set up subscription model strategies to make customers stay and increase customer lifetime value. Here are seven effective ways to increase CLV for tiered subscription plans.

1. Cater to diverse customer segments

The basis of tiered subscription models is multiple levels or tiers; for example, Basic, Pro, Premium. Each tier has its own features and pricing. And each tier is designed for a specific customer segment.

With tiered structures, customers can choose a tier based on their budget. For instance, if it is a paid subscription model, it’s easy for customers to pick a tier based on their budget. Conversely, if it is a free subscription model, customers can do what it takes to progress to higher tiers.

With tiered subscription models, you can cater to various customer segments by offering different tiers. Customers can downgrade or upgrade to different tiers based on their needs, reducing churn, an effective eCommerce retention strategy.

2. Tiered subscriptions encourage upgrades

Another way in which tiered subscription models increase CLV is via plan upgrades. Existing subscribers can be incentivized to move to higher tiers. A strategy that is much more profitable than acquiring new subscribers. Existing subscribers allow you to build revenue over time, increasing customer lifetime value.

Some ways to encourage upgrades:

  • Offer incentives to subscribers to upgrade plans
  • Keep improving perks in the higher tiers to entice lower level subscribers to want to upgrade to higher tiers
  • Introduce gamification in your subscription model to encourage subscribers to engage and spend more
  • Offer incentives such as discounts to encourage subscribers to upgrade their levels
  • Make it easy for subscribers to upgrade to higher tiers via your Shopify subscription app

3. Improving customer retention through personalization

Personalization can generate 40% more revenue for brands. When you give customers control and choices over their subscription, they feel more satisfied because their needs are met. This leads to loyalty and retention.

Personalizing subscriptions for customers involves making different aspects relevant to their preference. While offering different subscription tiers is a way to personalize, further creating micro segments of subscribers can help improve retention.

Here are some subscription model strategies for personalization:

  • Offer curated subscription boxes based on customer preference
  • Share personalized product recommendations
  • Allow customers to choose delivery frequency
  • Use data to personalize experience at multiple touchpoints
  • Offer discounts to long-term subscribers encouraging them to commit for longer

4. Use data-driven insights for marketing and product development

It’s essential to conduct multi-layer data analysis of your subscribers. For instance, not only should you track which tiers are more popular, analyzing which type of content gets more engagement can also help you with marketing and product development.

Here are some ways to use data from and for subscriptions:

  • To offer personalized and relevant offers and deals
  • Use data to understand customer preference and spending capacities, then use these insights to create tiers based on your target audience segments
  • Refine perks, features, pricing, and marketing strategies in different tiers to match customer needs
  • Align features and perks of each tier to its target audience

5. Optimizing customer acquisition cost

Typically, higher-tier subscribers have a higher customer lifetime value than lower tiers. Hence, your customer acquisition strategy should be tier-specific. Optimize each tier based on the CLV it would generate from those subscribers.

For instance, if the customer acquisition cost of your Premium tier (top most) is $500 while it is just $100 for Starter tier (lower), it would still make sense for you to focus on acquiring more subscribers in the Premium tier as this tier will generate higher revenue. Moreover, this tier values your brand more and hence is more likely to stick with you longer, increasing customer lifetime value.

Now let’s look at some ways to optimize CAC for your tiered subscriptions:

  • Allocate a higher budget for higher tier CAC because the higher tiers are going to be more profitable
  • Set up predictive analytics for your Shopify subscriptions. This will help you identify high-value potential subscribers in the early stages of their journey
  • Higher tier subscribers are more likely to share referrals. Create referral programs for the higher tiers

6. Reduce churn and improve loyalty

Tiered subscription structures provide many reasons subscribers should not cancel their plans. For instance, they can downgrade to a lower tier instead of canceling. And they should have the flexibility to pause their plans for a short term if they wish to.

Moreover, Shopify brands can refine subscription experience by referring to customer data and enhancing offers and perks. Here are some ways to reduce churn to increase CLV in Shopify tiered subscription models.

  • Clearly communicate the benefits and perks of the plans so subscribers know its real value
  • Ensure the perks and benefits of different tiers do not confuse customers
  • Create a proactive and real-time communication set up. For example, if customers are reaching usage limit, inform them beforehand
  • Provide flexibility. When customers know they can pause deliveries, change products, make swaps, they feel more comfortable with the subscription
  • Continuously measure your retention and churn rate to optimize subscription model strategies

7. Strategic pricing and tier naming

Another effective subscription model strategy is pricing and naming the tiers. One of the most influential factors in subscription models is pricing – the annual or monthly subscription fee, the savings, monetary value of perks, etc. When pricing is competitive, it has a higher perceived value in the market.

Pricing and naming strategies involve factors such as behavioral psychology and market positioning. So how to go about pricing and naming strategy of your subscription plans?

  • Name the tiers strategically to communicate value propositions, for example, Starter, Growth, Scale.
  • Provide tier comparison tables on your website or subscription page to make decision making easy for potential subscribers
  • Your subscription pricing should cover your costs and also provide a profitable margin
  • Measure the immediate conversion impact as well as the long-term effectiveness of your naming and pricing strategies

Improve Shopify tiered subscription models with Appstle

Whether you’re launching a fresh Shopify tiered subscription model or in the process of enhancing it to increase CLV, you will need to try different strategies. Your subscription strategies should depend on your specific products, industry, and customer preference.

To set-up and run an efficient tiered subscription model, you will require a smart tool to help automate functions, complement your existing tools and skills, and make your subscription business a seamless journey for you. That’s where Appstle comes in.

Appstle Subscriptions App is designed for Shopify and Shopify Plus brands. The app helps build subscription models of various types, including tiered subscription models. Here are some key features of Appstle:

  • Multiple types of subscription plans: Create different types of recurring payment subscription plans, for instance, tiered subscription plans, flat-price subscriptions, usage based plans, curated box subscriptions, and more.
  • Customization features: Tailor Shopify subscription plans based on your brand, products, industry, and customer preference.
  • Flexible billing: Provide options for one-time purchase or recurring billing for products, improving sales and increasing customer lifetime value.
  • Loyalty features: Integrate loyalty features and referral programs within your Shopify tiered subscriptions, reducing cost of acquisition and churn, increasing CLV.
  • Scale with data analytics: Make informed business decisions based on in-depth growth analytics and subscriber history data from across different subscription touchpoints.

Install Appstle Subscriptions App to manage and scale your tiered subscription model.

FAQs

What is a tiered subscription model?
A tiered subscription model offers multiple levels with specific features and perks in each level. This type of subscription plan helps eCommerce merchants cater to various customer segments.

What is the difference between subscription and one-time purchase?
Subscriptions involve recurring payments for period product or service deliveries. One-time purchases involve a single payment.

How to calculate customer lifetime value?
To calculate customer lifetime value, multiply your average revenue per customer by average customer lifespan.

How does customer segmentation help in a tiered subscription model?
By segmenting subscribers based on their needs, preferences and other parameters, Shopify brands can cater to their specific needs and build stronger relationships, leading to loyalty and improved CLV.

items.excerpt: Enterprise eCommerce brands that implement headless commerce experience several benefits from it, such as improved site performance, greater agility and scalability. items.html:
Enterprise eCommerce brands that implement headless commerce experience several benefits from it, such as improved site performance, greater agility and scalability.

Headless commerce provides more freedom and control to large and ambitious brands as its front end and back end are separate from each other. Many competitive businesses choose to implement headless commerce infrastructure for its benefits.

In this blog, we explore what is headless commerce subscription, its advantages for Shopify businesses, and why ambitious businesses must consider headless commerce for subscription models.

Let’s get started!

Understanding headless commerce for Shopify

Before we explore the many ways in which headless commerce enhances or helps subscription businesses, let’s get clarity on what headless commerce is and how it functions.

Headless commerce separates the front end and back end of your Shopify website. For instance, the front end, which includes all the visual aspects that your customers can see and interact with, are disconnected with the back end.

The back end of your Shopify store includes all the systems, the structure, and logic that enables your website to function. In headless commerce, these two aspects are separate and disconnected, and function independently. Thus, giving more flexibility and freedom to merchants.

Among the many brands that have implemented headless commerce for various business goals are Amazon, Walmart, Nike, Toyota, Tesla, and McDonalds. These large enterprise brands have utilized the benefits of headless commerce for different purposes, such as for scaling their business, for providing omnichannel experiences, for customization, and more.

Now let’s understand the advantages of headless commerce for subscriptions and how it can help with eCommerce subscription innovations.

Advantages of headless commerce subscription systems for Shopify stores

Apart from the obvious benefits, such as more agility and freedom, eCommerce subscription brands can utilize headless commerce for many more advantages. Let’s explore the many advantages of headless commerce and ways in which you can maximize the capabilities of headless commerce.

1. Highly customizable subscription models

With the frontend and backend being disconnected, headless commerce provides flexibility and customization possibilities for subscriptions. Traditional platforms, where the front-end and backend are tightly knit, do not offer such flexibility. Here are some examples:

  • You can control the content and content structure you show to subscribers
  • Create personalized customer experiences via content based on the segment you are targeting
  • Set up variable billing cycles and customized shipping schedules
  • Offer customized subscription options based on customer preference
  • Create unique subscription flows for individual customers or segments
  • Design user interfaces from scratch, adapting to changing customer needs without disrupting the entire system

By implementing headless commerce for your Shopify store, you can improve subscription UX in multiple ways. For instance, Tesla is known to use headless commerce to allow customers to choose materials and colors to customize their cars.

2. Agility to adapt and innovate

The subscription market is rapidly evolving, leading to new trends and rising customer expectations. With headless commerce, subscription brands can easily update features based on market trends.

For your Shopify store, this means keeping customers happy and engaged, and meeting their needs and preferences. Here’s what you can do with headless commerce subscription:

  • Introduce new products rapidly
  • Change product pricing
  • Change billing and invoicing features
  • Experiment with new features without disturbing the current process flow
  • Launch new subscription deals with minimal technical overheads
  • Add subscription functionalities
  • Create more personalized experiences based on seasonal customer demands
  • Run A/B testing with ease to optimize subscription features

Here’s an example: Staples, the office supply retailer wanted to do away with the siloed catalog experience. It implemented headless commerce, which enabled customers to place orders by number and order history for faster reordering.

3. Seamless omnichannel subscription management

With headless commerce subscription, you can offer consistent experience across the subscription touchpoints. For instance, subscribers browsing or interacting with you via your mobile app or website or WhatsApp, get the same consistent information.

For brands, this can help in improving subscription UX, increased customer satisfaction, more sales, and overall better performance on the subscription website and app. Here’s how it helps your subscription model:

  • All customer and subscription data is accessible via APIs, ensuring a consistent experience on different channels, such as website, app, in-store, etc.
  • Real-time synchronization keeps subscription status, billing information, and inventory levels updated across channels
  • Customers can start a subscription on one device and seamlessly continue management on another without any disruption
  • Send personalized offers and recommendations based on customers’ subscription history
  • Access to subscriber history and data from all channels to support teams
  • As subscription preferences change, the inventory and fulfillment systems automatically adjust across channels

For example, if you have online and off-line stores and want to offer a seamless omnichannel experience to your subscribers, you could do so with headless commerce. Your customers could navigate your physical store via your mobile app as well as place orders.

4. Customer control and self service

With headless commerce subscription, brands can enable higher levels of self-service for customers. Subscription management tools can give subscribers control over their subscription accounts.

For Shopify brands, this can reduce customer support overheads. Moreover, it can increase customer satisfaction, leading to more sales and new customers via word-of-mouth by existing satisfied customers.

  • Subscribers can change delivery schedule, pause deliveries, or change orders
  • Subscribers can change payment methods, billing preference, etc., enhancing checkout process
  • Change subscription plans, upgrade or downgrade based on preference
  • Change language and currency based on location and preference
  • Reactivate paused or canceled subscriptions

For example, McDonalds used headless commerce to allow its customers to pay using the Chinese instant messaging service WeChat.

5. Scalability and platform agnosticism

Headless subscription commerce makes it easy for businesses to scale. When the different elements of the front end and back end are separate, they can each grow independently. This enables scalability.

For instance, when each element is independent, you can make changes to it separately without disturbing the other elements or the flow. This way, you can select the most effective tools for each of your Shopify subscription store features. Here’s how headless commerce helps with eCommerce subscription innovations:

  • Scale features separately, for instance, features like billing, analytics, etc.
  • Integrate various platforms and tools to manage subscriptions
  • Easily upgrade one element or component without having to rebuild the whole subscription system
  • Introduce new products or pricing models
  • Easily manage increased transactions by making changes to only the back end
  • Expand to new markets by implementing location-specific features
  • Run A/B tests on specific components only

Here’s an example: Walmart uses headless commerce to enable customers to shop faster. It built a unique app-like website, increasing company revenue.

6. Enhanced data integration and analytics

Headless commerce also allows you to integrate data across different departments and systems. This leads to better analytics. For example, information from subscription sign ups, billing, marketing, customer support, and inventory, all can be integrated for better analytics.

Moreover, this also helps with predictive modeling and strategic, data-driven decision making. Here are the advantages of headless subscription commerce for data and analytics:

  • Synchronize data in real-time across processes, for example, invoicing, shipping, marketing, order management, etc.
  • Deep customer behavior analytics that combines subscription, purchase, and engagement history data
  • Calculate precise customer lifetime value based on data from various components
  • Collate data from your Shopify subscription app and website for more accurate analytics and reports

For example, if your Shopify subscription page is facing slow load times due to heavy data, you could reduce load time with headless subscription commerce. You can create a system that keeps front end and back end data separate as well as synchronized it when required.

7. Reduced operational complexity, faster time to market

The eCommerce subscription market is vibrant where customers expect new and innovative experiences. Headless subscription commerce enables brands to stay agile and adapt quickly to market trends.

For subscription businesses, this means reduced operational complexities, and faster processes. Here’s how headless commerce helps:

  • Launch new subscription products, offers, and deals in less time
  • Incorporate features requested by customers, making advanced customization possible
  • Implement platform upgrades independently without disturbing the entire subscription system
  • Allow front end and back end teams to work independently and simultaneously
  • Introduce dynamic pricing models and subscription tiers quickly
  • Easily test and change subscription features without disrupting the entire system

For example, say there’s a new payment method in the market. You can implement and integrate it without having to disturb the front end and back end process flows.

Ready to implement headless commerce subscription on your Shopify store?

Whether you have an established Shopify subscription business that needs an upgrade or you want to set up a new subscription model for your business, headless commerce subscription is definitely worth exploring.

Not only does it provide freedom and flexibility, it also enables other features, such as omnichannel experiences, customization, personalization, customer self-service options, etc.

The app is designed to provide merchants the capabilities to customize, personalize, and create intuitive shopping experiences that complement the advantages of headless commerce.

items.html:
Almost every eCommerce brand has a loyalty program. And customers are part of more than 10 loyalty programs on average. However, customers end up engaging with just a few.

The reason? Most loyalty programs fail to stay relevant to customers. They offer run-off-the-mill perks. Customers lose interest because the programs lack value.

One strategy to ensure relevance and long-term customer loyalty is customization.

In this blog, we explore effective customer loyalty program customization strategies that you could apply to your Shopify store for maximum ROI and growth.

Read on!

Data-driven customer loyalty program customizations

If you’re not using data from your Shopify store, you’re losing out on many opportunities to engage your customers. Consider this: 63% of US-based customers are willing to share their personal details in exchange for rewards. Data can help you gain a better understanding of customers, and give them what they need. This increases conversions. Let’s look at some ways to use data for customer loyalty customization.

1. Tailored rewards and offers

Your most loyal customers expect you to know them, understand their needs and preferences. To create personalized loyalty program experiences on Shopify, offer customers tailored rewards.

For example, the outdoor apparel brand North Face has a loyalty program, XPLR Pass. Its loyalty members can use reward points towards experiences, such as unique trips. This helps build a stronger connection between the brand and its customers.

2. Personalized communication

Loyalty programs also provide many communication opportunities. For instance, send regular updates regarding points, expiring points, new offers, etc. By gathering data from individual customer accounts, you can send out personalized communication via email, SMS, WhatsApp, etc.

For example, send automated emails to individual customers mentioning their accumulated reward points and how close they are to the next tier. This customer engagement tactic will encourage them to earn more points and progress to the next tier.

3. Milestone recognition

Another way to utilize customer data is to track customer milestones and acknowledge them. For example, when a customer reaches a reward point or spending threshold, celebrate the milestone by offering personalized offers. This can help brands deepend the emotional connection with customers. Use the eCommerce loyalty strategy for your VIP and special customers to increase the potential of them sticking with you for a longer term.

Tiered loyalty structure with behavioral insights

Creating a tiered structure is another strategy that can enhance your customer loyalty program customizations. There’s a lot you can do when you have different loyalty tiers. You can offer multiple options to cater to customer segments, create dynamic adjustments based on customer behavior, and more. Let’s look at some ways to offer customized experience via tiered loyalty structures.

1. Multiple tiers with increasing benefits

When you have multiple tiers, you have access to data for multiple segments. Now what if you provide the same benefits to each tier? It’s not going to add any value to customers in the higher tiers.

But what if your tires have increasing benefits? For instance, say you have three tiers – silver, gold, and platinum. Customers in gold get more benefits than silver, and customers in platinum get the most benefits.

A multi-tiered set up helps with these loyalty program features:

  • Customize benefits based on tiers
  • Offer increasing benefits to higher tiers
  • Distinguish between loyalty members based on tiers
  • Create campaigns to entice customers to progress to higher tiers

2. Dynamic tier adjustments

Another strategy for customer loyalty program customizations based on your customers’ behavior patterns is to make dynamic adjustments. Meaning, make changes based on data insights.

For example, if you see that customers are taking too long to jump from one tier to the other, it’s possible that you’ve made it too hard for them. The solution? Make changes, make it easier for customers to move from lower tiers to higher tiers, with speed.

Some customer behavior that you could measure are spending habits, transaction frequency, spending thresholds year-after-year, engagement levels, etc. Use this data to make dynamic adjustments. This will keep your loyalty program engaging.

3. Tier-specific perks

One of the easiest ways to customize your loyalty program is to create multiple tiers and offer specific and exclusive perks and benefits to each tier. The lowest tier gets the least number of perks, while the top-most tier gets the most number of perks.

Many brands with tiered loyalty programs follow this strategy. Some of the exclusive benefits they give to different tiers are more points, bigger discounts, first access to new collections and sales, exclusive events, etc.

For example, cosmetics brand Sephora offers loyalty benefits in the form of savings, samples, and experiences. All three tiers get different types of these three benefits.

Flexible and customer-choice rewards

8 out of 10 customers that are part of loyalty programs prioritize flexibility in earning and redeeming loyalty rewards. From flexible shipping to tailored rewards to redemption, there are many ways to ensure flexible and tailored rewards experience. Let’s explore some.

1. Reward variety

One of the best eCommerce loyalty strategies is to let customers choose their rewards. When you do so, you make them feel like they’re in control. For instance, you can allow customers to choose from discounts, free samples, experiences, event invites, etc. Doing so makes the loyalty benefits more relevant to customers, enhancing customer loyalty for Shopify stores.

2. Multiple earning channels

Another customer loyalty program customization strategy is something simple but often ignored – setting up multiple ways to earn points. Different customers have their individual preferences. For example, some might make more purchases, and others might be more active on social media talking about your brand. Use these customer preferences to your advantage by creating multiple ways to earn reward points. For example, for purchases, for referrals, social media follow, likes, shares, comments, sharing reviews, etc.

Omnichannel integration

To ensure a more streamlined and unified customer experience, you can set up an omnichannel system where various channels are in sync with each other. Here’s how omnichannel integration can help with customer loyalty program customizations.

1. Seamless experience across channels

When your loyalty program members interact with you through different channels, they should have a seamless and cohesive experience. For instance, if a customer has interacted with you on the app, your customer support agents should be able to access that interaction history.

Research by the Harvard Business Review shows, when “loyal members encounter service failures-shipping issues, problems with returns, stockouts and the like-they get more upset than customers who are not members”.

Integrating loyalty program functionality across channels can make it easy for customers to earn and redeem points across channels. Moreover, if they have any issues, omnichannel set-up can lead to a quicker and more seamless solution.

2. Unified customer profiles

Let’s take an example. Your loyalty member earns reward points via your online store. Their next purchase is in-store and they earn more points. These points should somehow be added and appear in your customers loyalty profile. Synchronizing data across channels can ensure consistency and a unified experience for customers.

Exclusive access and community building

Seth Godin emphasizes, “Build a tribe, not a buyer base”. Building communities for your loyalty program can enhance personal and emotional connections, and create deeper meanings beyond transactions. To leverage community as a tactic for customer loyalty program customizations, explore these strategies:

1. Members-only events and content

An effective strategy for enhancing customer loyalty on Shopify stores is to facilitate a community experience for customers. For instance, private sales for VIP loyalty members, exclusive product launch parties, and other such special events can make customers feel exclusive and special. Also, share exclusive content to increase online engagement and participation.

For example, the automobile brand BMW organizes numerous exclusive events for its loyalty program Experience Club – curated art exhibitions, racing events, music concerts, culinary and tasting sessions.

2. Community engagement

The idea behind community-focused loyalty program features is to build emotional connections, where a group of people feel connected, heard, and can share with each other. Creating platforms for community engagement lead to higher personalized experiences.

There are many different ways brands can facilitate loyalty member communities — online, in-person, via WhatsApp groups, social media platforms and other channels. These communities allow members to share tips, ask questions to each other, raise concerns, share reviews and experiences, etc.

For example, the sports brand Skechers facilitates the GoRun club, a city-based community for loyal members interested in running.

3. Gamification

An exciting strategy for customer loyalty program customizations is to incorporate gamification. It adds personalized experiences, such as instant gratification, provides opportunities for participating and winning challenges, etc.

For instance, some gamification elements you can incorporate in your Shopify loyalty program strategy are badges, challenges, and achievement tracking. These not only make participation fun, but also encourage customers to purchase and engage more.

For example, Nike’s training app offers personalized workouts to members, gamifying their progress – a loyalty program feature that has helped the brand grow its community of loyal members.

Clear transparent communication

Nothing puts off customers more than the feeling of being cheated or lied to. This is what makes clear and transparent communication more important than you might imagine it to be. Let’s look at some ways in which you can ensure clear communication with your loyalty members.

1. Progress updates

Sending regular updates to loyalty members keeps them engaged and tuned into your program. For example, you can send them updates about their accumulated points, rewards earned with each action, and how many points they need to progress to the next tier or unlock surprise gifts.

You can send updates via different channels based on customer preference. For example, email, SMS, WhatsApp, Messenger, etc. Also, let customers know about expiring points so they are not in for a surprise if their points lapse.

2. Multi-channel messaging

When you use communication channels that are preferred by customers, it positively impacts your loyalty program. For instance, brands have seen higher engagement, conversions, and stronger customer retention.

Incorporating multi-channel communication is easier when your Shopify loyalty program app allows easy integrations. For example, set up messaging via email, SMS, WhatsApp, Messenger, push notification, among other channels. Also, optimize messaging times based on customers’ preference.

Robust technical infrastructure for customer loyalty program customizations

In this day and age, your loyalty program is only as good as your technical infrastructure. The market is full of customer loyalty program apps and platforms, but you must find one that’s most useful and relevant for your Shopify store. Then, apply these strategies:

1. Reliable and scalable platform

When planning your Shopify customer loyalty program, ensure you take a long-term approach. If your business and loyalty program has to scale, you should be prepared. One of the basic elements that will help you scale is your loyalty program app or platform.

For example, your app should be able to manage real-time updates as the numbers scale, fraud prevention, and smooth integration with POS and CRM systems are a must. From payments to invoicing to messaging and rewarding, ensure you have a strong infrastructure to manage all this.

2. Automation and AI

Automation and AI are a must to offer personalized loyalty program experiences on Shopify. For instance, real-time messaging via customers’ preferred channels is the most basic form of technical capability that customers expect from brands.

You can use AI and automation in many ways to offer personalized marketing messages and offers, dynamic offers to reduce churn, among others.

Ready to kick start your customer loyalty program customization strategies?

There are a lot of strategies that can help you effectively run your Shopify loyalty program. However, you must choose those that are relevant to your brand and your customers.

And to ensure a strong foundation, use a smart app, such as Appstle Loyalty & Rewards.

Appstle enables you to set up customized loyalty programs with points, store credits, referrals, rewards, and VIP perks. The app has features that help automate building brand loyalty and customer retention.

items.html:
With increasing competition, eCommerce brands find it hard to retain customers or increase loyalty rates.

Most brands have loyalty or rewards programs on their Shopify stores, a marketing strategy that has high potential to increase engagement, profits, and loyalty.

However, few brands get their loyalty programs right.

One brand that has been running a successful rewards program is Starbucks. Remember the stars you accumulate every time you buy a coffee or a sandwich at Starbucks?

In this blog, we breakdown the Starbucks loyalty strategy, and list down takeaways and tips that you could implement in your rewards programs.

Let’s get started!

What is the Starbucks loyalty program?

Starbucks is an American coffee chain with presence all over the world. The brand has set up a rewards program that is popular amongst its customers. Customers earn reward points everytime they make a purchase online or offline at any of its outlets.

The points collected can be redeemed against future purchases. Apart from points, the rewards program also offers other perks and benefits, such as drinks customization, free gifts on birthdays, free refills, among others.

Starbucks loyalty strategy breakdown and lessons

One of the most popular and talked about, Starbucks loyalty program offers many lessons and tips that eCommerce brands can implement in their rewards programs. In this section, we breakdown the Starbucks loyalty strategy and gather tips and takeaways, which you can apply to Shopify loyalty programs.

1. Starbucks Rewards has two tiers

Starbucks offers two loyalty tiers – Green and Gold. Keeping it minimal and simple, the brand makes the strategy straightforward. Here’s how it works.

Customers have to keep collecting “stars” (reward points) by making purchases, and progress through the levels. Every dollar spent earns customers reward points. When customers reach 450 stars in a year, they progress to the Gold level. The stars are valid for 12 months.

Green level: Once customers join the Starbucks loyalty program, they join from the Green level. In this level, customers earn points on every purchase, get reward points on birthdays, can get free refills on coffee and tea, etc.

Gold level: When customers earn 300 points in the Green level, they progress to the Gold level. In this tier, customers earn more perks and benefits, such as personalized and customized brews. Additionally, they can redeem points towards other perks.

Tips and takeaways:

  • Keep the number of tiers or levels to minimum, making it easy for customers to understand the loyalty program. Too many levels could confuse customers and make the experience tedious
  • Keep benefits and perks exclusive to each tier so that members can enjoy exclusivity and it encourages them to progress to higher tiers to earn those benefits
  • Customize tier names to match your branding, for instance, Starbucks levels are called Green and Gold to match its brand colors

2. Starbucks customer rewards program is free

Both paid and free rewards programs have pros and cons. For instance, when loyalty programs are paid, it may see limited sign-ups. However, only serious customers would sign-up, making it easy to attract only genuine customers.

Conversely, free reward programs attract a large number of customers to join, leading to more popularity. However, this could backfire as brands would spend more on campaigns targeting a larger number of people instead of a concentrated segment.

Benefits of free loyalty programs as a brand loyalty tactic:

  • Broader reach and easy sign-ups
  • Lower entry barrier leads to more engagement
  • Helps create a positive brand perception
  • Leads to a broader customer base and potential for word-of-mouth marketing
  • Increases repeat purchases, profits and lifetime customer value

Starbucks rewards strategy is to offer the program free. This makes it easy for the brand to attract more customers to the loyalty program. Once signed up, customers climb up tiers when they spend a specific amount in a year.

Tips and takeaways:

  • Decide whether you want to keep your loyalty program free or paid based on your product type, industry, and customer preference
  • Price your loyalty program in such a way that even if it is a significant amount, customers see value in it in the long run. This will encourage customers to pay and join
  • Make the joining and payment process seamless and easy, leading to good customer experience. Remember, first impression is the last impression

3. Easy joining process

Another critical factor in any kind of customer rewards program, subscriptions or membership programs is the joining process. A confusing and lengthy joining process can deter customers from signing up, while an easy, quick sign-up process makes it that much easier to bring customers on board.

Starbucks loyalty strategy considers this factor. The loyalty program is easy to join. All that customers have to do is download the Starbucks app, which is available for iOS and Android users, or sign up via the website.

Starbucks website has a dedicated rewards page, from where customers can join the program by simply clicking on a link. Customers are only required to share their name and contact email to sign up.

Tips and takeaways:

  • Ensure the sign-up process is easy and simple
  • Provide multiple ways to set up, for example, via website, phone app, etc.
  • Make the process short and fast, as a lengthy process can keep customer away
  • Assure customers of security and data privacy during the sign-up process

4. It is a well-structured loyalty program

When planning customer rewards programs, brands must take a long-term view. And that’s something that Starbucks loyalty strategy has done. It is well-planned and structured in a way that leads to long-term returns.

In Starbucks rewards program, new members begin with the Green level. When they accumulate 450 stars within 12 months, they automatically progress to the Gold tier, which is the higher level.

This simple and straightforward structure is designed in a way that motivates customers to earn more points until they reach 450 stars so they can enjoy the benefits of the Gold level.

However, the Gold level inclusion is not permanent. To maintain it, customers have to collect 450 stars a year. This encourages them to spend more to earn the required stars. For Starbucks, this ensures continuous revenue and higher customer lifetime value.

When customers continue to spend more and remain members of the Gold level, the brand also increases loyalty rates.

Tips and takeaways:

  • Set up an expiration system of points or tiers. This will keep customers spending more to continue being part of the higher tier
  • Think long-term when designing and planning your Shopify loyalty program
  • Use a Shopify rewards and loyalty app that provides features for long-term success
  • Create consistent revenue opportunities via multiple ways to earn rewards

5. Customization possibilities

Customization and personalization features are key to providing good customer experience. This is another effective feature in the Starbucks loyalty strategy. These brand loyalty tactics for Shopify stores can positively impact customers’ perception of brands and increase repeat purchases and revenue for the brand.

Starbucks has incorporated customization features in its customer rewards program. Loyalty members can customize their beverages, food, and merchandise. For instance, customers with 25 stars can customize their beverage; those who collect 100 stars can redeem their points by choosing from brewed hot or iced coffee, hot steeped tea, bakery items like cake pops and cookies, or packaged snacks.

Customers who collect 200 stars can redeem them for any handcrafted beverage from the standard menu, such as lattes, macchiatos, or frappuccino blended beverages. Members can also select hot breakfast items like sandwiches or oatmeal.

300 stars can get customers more substantial food options, allowing members to customize their lunch experience with packaged salads, lunch sandwiches, or protein boxes; while with 400 stars, customers can select merchandise items valued up to $20, including signature cups, drink tumblers, and other branded items.

Tips and takeaways:

  • Set up personalization and customization features in your Shopify loyalty program
  • Focus on customization as a value proposition
  • Provide personalization options based on different tiers
  • Create meaningful ways for customers to redeem loyalty points

What food and beverage brands can learn from Starbucks loyalty strategy

If you’re a food and beverage brand that’s looking to improve customer loyalty, you can take inspiration from Starbucks loyalty strategy. Let’s look at some key learnings and inspirational factors:

  • Keep your loyalty structure simple, tiered, and with minimal levels. This approach adds clarity. Customers can understand your program easily and know what to do to enjoy the program benefits. Food and beverage brands can set up tier thresholds that encourage repeat purchases, while offering increasingly valuable benefits at higher levels. This creates a clear path of progression, motivating customers to spend more.
  • Prioritize transparency in your Shopify loyalty strategy. Food and beverage brands must design a rewards system that is clear, and is transparent about the benefits in each tier. Customers should be able to view their accumulated stars, know how they can earn more points, and how they can redeem points.
  • Food and beverage are recurring purchases for customers. By removing the fees to join your program, you can maximize program participation rates and increase repeat purchases. This can lead to higher customer lifetime value. With this approach, you can also capture data from a broader customer base while creating more opportunities for engagement.
  • Another important Shopify loyalty tactic that food and beverage brands must consider is to streamline the sign-up process. You could create multiple entry points through mobile apps, websites, or in-store options. Also, ask for minimal information. Frictionless processes can drive more participation.

How to launch your Shopify loyalty program for success

The Starbucks loyalty strategy has numerous lessons and tips that you can implement in your Shopify loyalty programs.

Whether you want inspiration for tier-based loyalty structures or the kind of perks and benefits you could create for customers, there’s a lot you can learn from the strategies shared above.

But merely designing a good rewards program is not enough, you have to ensure it is managed well and includes all the features that help attract and engage customers.

items.html:
With increasing competition and fight for customer attention, eCommerce brands are trying various strategies to increase engagement and scale their business.

One such strategy that’s particularly gaining momentum is membership programs. Brands across industries are designing innovative membership programs that go beyond products and transactions. These membership programs are designed to engage customers, build member communities, and offer unique experiences to members as benefits.

A brand that has designed an effective membership program, loved by customers, is Lululemon. In this blog, we breakdown the Lululemon membership strategy, what makes it stand out, why customers love it so much, and what are the lessons you can implement in your Shopify membership programs.

Read on!

What is the Lululemon membership program?

Lululemon is an athletics clothing and accessories brand that offers premium products for men and women. Lululemon has a free eCommerce membership model that provides access to various perks and experiences without requiring a purchase threshold or annual fee. The brand offers various types of perks that go beyond discounts, making it more attractive to its customers. The program is designed to build a community of members and to increase customer engagement.

Lululemon membership strategy breakdown

Lululemon is a popular brand of athleisure clothing and accessories for men and women. The brand has multiplied its popularity with an effective membership program. In this section, we breakdown the Lululemon membership strategy and extract key takeaways that you can implement in your Shopify membership strategy.

1. Easy and multiple sign-up options

When you make it easy for customers to sign-up, the conversion rates can increase. Lululemon has made the membership sign-up process easy. Besides, the brand provides multiple ways for customers to sign up.

Customers can sign up via the website, through the iOS app, or in store. And the process is simple. All that customers need to provide is their name and email address.

2. The membership is free to join

Customers can join the Lululemon membership program for free. Making eCommerce membership models free is one of the biggest factors that can lead to more sign-ups. However, this can also lead to bogus sign ups, hence, may require careful vetting.

Making memberships free has many benefits. For starters, it is an effective customer retention strategy, because when members do not have to pay a fee, they do not mind continuing their membership.

Also, with free membership models, you can reach a wider audience, collect customer data, and potential for future marketing. Free memberships also help build loyalty and increase customer retention, and encourage more frequent purchases.

3. Many benefits and perks

One of the biggest factors that attracts customers to join memberships is the special benefits or perks. When customers receive exclusive benefits, they feel special. Lululemon membership strategy includes multiple perks and benefits for customers, making it more attractive for customers to join the program.

Some of the perks include early access to product drops, exchange or credit on sale items, select Peloton classes, membership events, receipt-free returns, and free hemming, among others.

The brand also partners with other brands and offers perks in collaboration with those brands. This way, there’s always more – products and brands – for members to explore and try.

4. Easy access and navigation

To ensure a good experience for customers, brands must make navigation and access as easy as possible. That’s what Lululemon membership strategy prioritizes.

Once customers create a Lululemon membership account or sign into their account, they can access and navigate the membership benefits from their account. Whether they are on the website or on the membership app, they can easily access their membership information.

When you design your membership program strategy, ensure the UX, navigation and access are

5. Clear explanation of membership program on one page

For Lululemon, its membership program is not an afterthought. The brand prioritizes the membership program and hence, it has a dedicated page for it on the website.

The membership page has all the details of the program. From links to sign up for the membership to details about benefits to FAQs, and more.

Providing all important information in one place makes it easy for customers to find information and clear their doubts.

6. An FAQs section for the membership program

Lululemon membership strategy prioritizes clarity and transparency. The membership page has not one but two FAQs sections. One section answers the general questions about the program, while the other answers questions related to partner perks.

One of the key factors that helps customers feel comfortable and build trust in brands is when brands share clear information with customers. Among other ways brands share information is live chats and easy access to contact channels such as phone and WhatsApp.

7. Access to product drops

Lululemon membership strategy has many features that offer priority and exclusive access to members. For instance, members get exclusive and early access to new product releases and limited collections before they become available to the general public. This creates a sense of exclusivity and rewards members who want to stay ahead of trends in athletic apparel.

8. Experiences beyond products

Today, customers expect much more from special programs, such as memberships and Shopify loyalty programs. Merely products and transactional experiences do not cut it for brands or customers any more. Lululemon membership strategy provides this key takeaway for brands that want to stay ahead of their competitors.

Lululemon offers its members access to virtual fitness classes and wellness content. This digital integration highlights the brand’s commitment to building a community of members that believe in an active lifestyle. This is an effective lesson by building communities on Shopify stores.

The brand also offers hemming services to members in their stores. A benefit that enhances product customization and fit. This service addresses a common pain point for athletic wear consumers while demonstrating Lululemon’s attention to detail and commitment to customer satisfaction.

9. Digital integration and experience

Lululemon membership strategy is fully integrated with Lululemon’s mobile app and online platform, offering a seamless experience across digital and physical touchpoints. This omnichannel approach of the brand reflects its attention to customer preference and expectations.

items.excerpt: Competition in eCommerce is only increasing. Brands are constantly trying innovative ways to increase revenue. items.html:
Competition in eCommerce is only increasing. Brands are constantly trying innovative ways to increase revenue.

One strategy that has proven to be powerful is exclusivity. eCommerce memberships help brands create exclusivity.

Exclusivity taps into human psychology, makes consumers feel special, creates a community of select people, and increases the perceived value of customers’ engagement with brands.

Exclusivity as a psychological tactic gives eCommerce brands multiple ways to tap into revenue generation. In this blog, we look at the various strategies to monetize exclusive memberships for Shopify stores.

Why does exclusivity work?

Implementing exclusivity strategies helps brands enhance the perceived value of its membership programs. For instance, when something is available to everyone, it is considered regular. However, when the same thing is made exclusive for a select few, its value increases.

It is human psychology. We like to feel special, exclusive, and stand out from the crowd. Whether this feeling of exclusivity is through price, invitation, special benefits, or timing, when something is rare and scarce, we value it more.

Moreover, we also like to be part of communities, something that membership programs are able to create for customers. Customers are willing to pay more for such exclusive experiences. And for brands, membership programs offer opportunities to create these exclusive experiences as well as monetize them.

Let’s look at some reasons why customers pay for exclusivity:

  • The feeling of being special and VIP
  • Access to limited-availability products
  • Connection with like-minded communities
  • Learning opportunities and inside knowledge

Consider these statistics:

  • In 2023, 75% of US consumers belonged to at least one membership program. (McKinsey)
  • 57% of customers say quality and value are the main reasons to consider paid memberships. (KPMG)

Strategies to monetize exclusive membership access

Merely setting up a good membership program will not help you generate revenue. You will have to implement different strategies to transform memberships into revenue. Here are four such strategies to monetize exclusive memberships.

1. Early drops

Early drops or exclusive access to new products makes customers feel exclusive. This exclusivity encourages them to make purchases. Early access is one of the most common tactics used by eCommerce brands to cater to their VIP and premium members.

Human beings are wired to seek exclusivity and feeling special. For brands, this is a great way to monetize exclusive memberships. For instance, Nike’s SNKRS app offers its members exclusive access to limited-edition products. The brand has seen increased sales as well as a reduction in customer acquisition costs.

Here are some tips to set up exclusive access campaigns:

  • Create a buzz through teaser campaigns, such as countdowns, hints of upcoming releases, etc.
  • Create segments or tiers for early access. For instance, VIP members get access 48 hours early, regular members get access 12 hours early and general public get access to the products only ones it is launched
  • Send personalized email and SMS notifications with links to the early drop product pages
  • Display FOMO elements, such as scarcity indicators, real-time inventory countdown, etc.

2. Generate revenue through content

Shopify brands offering memberships can also generate revenue through content. For instance, when brands focus on establishing expertise in their industry subject matter and create a compelling story around their brand, they can monetize content strategically and generate membership-based revenue.

Here are some ways you can monetize exclusive content marketing via your memberships:

  • Offer your members paid educational courses
  • Offer how-to-guides and product usage tips
  • Create a paid newsletter with exclusive content for members
  • Run exclusive content marketing campaigns for members only
  • Create behind-the-scenes content around product development
  • Create a subscription model for your exclusive content; example, newsletter
  • Offer member-only discounts on certain types of content

By offering exclusive content to members, you can build deeper relationships, and provide value beyond transactions. Moreover, when customers see added value in your memberships, it can increase the retention rate, thus, leading to higher customer lifetime value.

Example

3. Paid memberships

Membership programs can be paid or free. Creating paid membership benefits programs can help you build a community of high-value customers. Paid membership programs are an effective revenue stream for brands, helping brands monetize exclusive memberships.

One of the best examples of paid memberships is Amazon Prime. The brand charges an annual membership fee. This fee brings recurring and predictable revenue, increases the CLV, increases purchase frequency of customers, and lowers customer acquisition costs. All these factors lead to more revenue.

However, a critical factor in paid memberships is the pricing or the fee. Let’s look at some ways to price membership programs:

  • Create multiple tiers or levels and different price points. For instance, silver tier $100, gold tier $150 and platinum tier $200 and offer different exclusive VIP customer perks to each tier
  • Value-based pricing could be somewhat variable and depend on usage. For example, members who purchase $5000 per year pay $50 membership fee, while those that purchase less, pay $100 fee
  • Premium pricing that creates exclusivity through members’ financial commitment

4. Premium access beyond products

Today, customers expect more than just products and transactional experiences. Apart from products, there are many other factors that help in engaging them. And these other elements also drive revenue.

Here are some non-product based factors that can help you increase membership-based revenue:

  • Offer early access to members to sales and events
  • Create exclusive shopping windows for members. This can help increase membership sign-ups
  • Clearly communicate about the exclusive window
  • Use a Shopify membership app that allows seamless verification
  • Organize exclusive live streams and Q&A sessions for members
  • Create private forums and communities for members

Let’s look at some tips and cues to keep your Shopify exclusive membership program relevant for customers:

  • Keep your Shopify store updated with products in demand
  • Regularly update exclusive VIP customer perks
  • Frequently communicate with customers
  • Create a member community
  • Create members-only activities
  • Gamify your ecommerce membership program
  • Consistently follow up with members
  • Enable perks-sharing for members

How to set up exclusive member access on Shopify

There are many different ways to set up exclusive access memberships on Shopify. There are a number of apps designed to help brands set up membership programs. Shopify also has in-built features that support membership features.

For instance, Shopify customer accounts and tags for basic segmentation, password protection for exclusive collection pages, and discount codes specific to member groups, are some of these features.

Shopify apps, such as Appstle Memberships enable seamless set-up and managing for recurring billing and transactions. Moreover, Appstle also has customization features that can help brands tweak and integrate unique features to meet their specific requirements.

With Appstle Memberships app, you can set up various types of membership plans, offer different VIP customer perks, set up automated billing and notifications, offer customized perks, enable smart member tagging to associate the right perks with the right member plans, etc.

Another important aspect of membership programs is effective communication. Integrating and automating communication via SMS, email, WhatsApp, etc., can help brands communicate with members effectively.

Moreover, personalization is a must when you want to create exclusive membership experiences. It enhances the value perception of your program. For instance, with personalization strategies, you can share dynamic content with different member segments, offer personalized perks and benefits, etc.

Examples of membership programs with exclusive access strategies

In this section, we look at a few examples of successful membership programs and share key takeaways that you can implement in your Shopify membership programs.

1. Baking for Business

Baking for Business is an online membership model that caters to home bakers who want to launch their baking business. Apart from free courses and guides, members can sign up for the paid membership and get access to courses, recipes, social media templates, and business classes.

Key takeaways:

  • Simple membership model
  • Free access to courses
  • Exclusive content, courses, recipes, and business lessons for paid members
  • Offer a community experience to members

2. Vintage Sewing School

The online sewing school, Vintage Sewing School, offers online classes, courses, and a community of like minded members interested in sewing. The brand offers video courses, new courses every month, advanced lessons, and a community of members to support each other. The brand also organizes events and contests for members.

Key takeaways:

  • Affordable membership pricing
  • New content every month to keep members engaged
  • Advanced classes and courses add value to members

Get started with monetizing exclusive memberships

From paid membership benefits to exclusive content marketing for members to offering perks beyond products, there are a lot of ways you can monetize exclusive memberships on your Shopify stores.

However, for a seamless membership experience for your customers, you will need a smart Shopify app that supports various features, easy integrations, and automation.

You can implement these strategies with the help of Appstle Memberships App.

items.html:
Loyalty programs are one of the most common marketing strategies used by eCommerce brands.

Efficiently executed loyalty programs help brands in many ways, such as drive more sales, increase customer lifetime value, strengthen customer engagement and loyalty, among other advantages.

However, to maximize ROI from loyalty programs, eCommerce merchants must ensure they are strategically designed and efficiently managed.

This blog explores the Dapper Yankee Shopify rewards strategy breakdown, key takeaways, and tips you can use for your Shopify rewards programs.

What is the Dapper Yankee Loyalty Program?

Dapper Yankee is a premium men’s grooming and lifestyle brand that offers a range of high-quality products including beard care, hair styling, and men’s accessories. The brand focuses on natural ingredients and artisanal craftsmanship, delivering a premium experience for the modern gentleman.

Dapper Yankee Rewards is the brand’s loyalty program designed to reward returning customers and encourage repeat purchases. The program operates on a points-based system where customers earn points for various actions and can redeem them for discounts, free products, and exclusive perks.

Dapper Yankee Shopify rewards strategy breakdown and lessons

Loyalty & rewards programs are a must-have for eCommerce stores. Customers expect brands to offer points, and eCommerce brands can use these programs to drive engagement and grow their business. In this section, we breakdown Dapper Yankee Shopify rewards strategy and share key lessons, takeaways, and tips you could implement on your eCommerce loyalty programs.

1. Dapper Yankee Rewards is a points-based program

Dapper Yankee’s rewards program offers points for multiple actions. This encourages customers to keep transacting with the brand.

For instance, their customers earn points for making purchases, creating a customer account, on their birthdays, for referring friends, social media follow, and sharing product reviews.

This ensures their customers remain engaged beyond making purchases. Actions such as social media follow and sharing product reviews also earn points.

Let’s note some tips you could implement in your Shopify loyalty program:

  • Set up a straightforward and transparent rewards structure
  • Offer points for multiple actions, not just for purchases
  • Make it easy for customers to understand the points structure as well as to earn points
  • Create opportunities to communicate to customers about their reward points
  • Offer surprise reward points to keep customers excited

2. Multiple ways to earn reward points

Dapper Yankee has set up multiple ways for customers to earn reward points. Doing so encourages customers to engage more with the brand and makes them feel like progressing in the rewards program is possible for them.

Here are some tips to implement in your Shopify store:

  • Make points earning and collection an enjoyable activity for customers
  • Incorporate gamification to increase customer excitement and engagement
  • Personalize reward points, for example, give points on customers’ birthdays

3. Multiple ways to redeem points

Dapper Yankee’s Shopify rewards strategy also focuses on points redemption. By offering multiple ways to customers to redeem points, the brand drives more engagement, higher sales, and enhances customer satisfaction.

Here are some points you must consider:

  • The ways to redeem points should align with your brand values and customer preference
  • Clearly communicate with customers about their available loyalty points and how they can redeem them
  • Personalize points redemption. For example, consider personal requests by individual long-term loyal customers. Bend the rules for your most loyal customers
  • Keep monitoring points redemption and enhancing the experience for your customers

4. Integrated referral program within the rewards structure

Dapper Yankee has integrated its referral program into the rewards program. When customers refer their friends, they (customers) get 100 points and the referees get 20% off their first order.

This sort of merging two marketing strategies together has many advantages for the brand:

  • It drives organic customer acquisition via your loyal customers
  • Improves customer engagement and sales
  • Further strengthens customer loyalty

Now let’s look at some tips to make the most of such an integration:

  • Emphasize on your referrals program as much as the loyalty program
  • Offer significant rewards to your existing customers for sharing referrals
  • Highlight your value proposition to encourage organic customer acquisition

​5. Loyalty program integrated throughout the customer journey

Dapper Yankee has seamlessly integrated its rewards program within the customer journey without making it seem forced. For instance, the rewards program is visible to any visitor on the homepage. A dedicated page offers all the details about the loyalty program.

Customers can see the number of points they earned during checkout and how many points they have accumulated. This kind of transparency leads to instant satisfaction and gratification.

The brand sends regular updates on points balance, available rewards, and other offers, offering a personalized experience to customers.

Here are some tips you can use to effectively integrate your Shopify loyalty program within your eCommerce experience:

  • Highlight your Shopify loyalty program throughout your website
  • Show points earning potential on all the product pages
  • Display points balance and available rewards at checkout
  • Include rewards program information in the order confirmation email
  • Send regular updates on points balance and upcoming rewards

6. An FAQs section

The Dapper Yankee rewards page has an FAQs section that answers the most common questions asked by customers. Having an FAQs section and a live chat option ensures customers can find answers to doubts and common queries. Automating live chat can help you answer customers’ questions in real-time leading to a more satisfactory customer experience.

The section answers questions, such as:

  • What is the Dapper Yankee rewards program
  • How to join the Dapper rewards program
  • How to check accumulated points
  • Transfer of points
  • About Dapper rewards referral program
  • About Dapper rewards VIP program and tier

Here are some details you definitely must include in your Shopify rewards program page:

  • Clearly mention the points and rewards structure
  • How to earn points, how to redeem, and what other perks are available for customers
  • Any updates to your rewards and points policy
  • How customers could earn more points and maximize the benefits of the program
  • If they can transfer points to someone else
  • If points get lapsed and when
  • Contact information of the rewards customer care

7. Points expiry system

Another key aspect of Dapper Yankee Shopify rewards strategy is its points expiry system. If customers don’t redeem points or earn any points within a 6-month period, their accumulated points expire.

This system ensures repeat purchases and consistent activity by customers, ensuring long-term association between customers and the brand.

For instance, customers can engage in activities such as sharing product reviews, following on social media, etc. to keep their points and redeem them.

Here are some tips for your Shopify store:

  • Plan your reward points strategically
  • Monitor and revisit your points strategy periodically to enhance it
  • Set up expiry system to increase customer loyalty
  • Offer more rewards to long-term loyal customers

8. It has a tier-based Shopify rewards strategy

Dapper Yankee has a tier-based Shopify rewards strategy. Its VIP tiers are based on the total reward points customers accumulate within a year.

Customers who earn 500 points in a year, reach VIP status; those who earn 1000 points, reach Gold VIP status; and those with 2000 points, reach Platinum VIP status.

Each time customers unlock a new tier, they get access to exclusive discounts and special offers that are exclusively for specific VIP levels.

This tier-based structure adds excitement and increases engagement.

Here are a few tips for your to implement in your Shopify rewards strategy:

  • Incorporate gamification into your loyalty program to boost engagement
  • Design exclusive rewards for each tier, making it tempting for customers to earn more rewards to progress tiers

Key takeaways from Dapper Yankee Shopify rewards program

1. Create an engaging rewards program: Dapper Yankee rewards strategy has a mix of many engaging features, such as gamification, tier-based structure, VIP levels, referrals program, and more. This ensures consistent high-level engagement

2. Set up multiple ways to earn and redeem points via various activities, giving customers more opportunities to engage, earn, and redeem points through more purchases. This can help you increase customer lifetime value

3. Integrate other marketing strategies into loyalty and rewards programs, for example, referrals programs. This makes rewards programs more engaging.

4. Integrate the loyalty program throughout the entire customer journey, from homepage visibility to checkout point displays, creating transparency and immediate gratification.

5. Include an FAQs page and an automated live chat feature to address common customer questions about the rewards program.

6. Implement a points expiration system to encourage consistent engagement and prevent point hoarding.

7. Incorporate gamification via VIP and tiered structure. This adds excitement and exclusivity encouraging customers to earn more points to advance tiers.

8. Ensure personalization in both earning and redeeming points, including special considerations for loyal customers.

How to get started with your Shopify rewards strategy?

Loyalty and rewards programs can be game changers for Shopify stores. However, you have to plan and manage them efficiently. To do so, you need a smart Shopify app.

Appstle Loyalty & Rewards App offers a comprehensive set of capabilities and features. These include, customizable and user-friendly loyalty program design, personalized VIP perks, flexible points structure, and more.

With Appstle’s gamification and marketing features, you can leverage innovative features for various use cases for your rewards programs.
