items.html:
Many eCommerce brands include membership programs within their marketing plans.

When managed well, membership programs provide competitive advantage to eCommerce brands. For instance, brands offer a community feel to members, increase average order value, increase customer lifetime value, and boost customer engagement.

To maximize ROI from membership programs, brands have to ensure they are well-planned and managed.

In this blog, we look at the membership program of Banks Brewing, its distinct features, and takeaways.

This Shopify membership strategy breakdown will offer lessons, strategies, and tips you can apply to your membership programs.

What is Banks Brewing Banks Club?

Banks Brewing is an Australia-based family run brewery that offers a range of beers. The brand produces a range of beers and also sells merchandise. Alongside, it also hosts beer events, such as competitions and festivals.

The Banks Brewing Store runs a membership program called Banks Club. The membership has an annual membership fee and offers various perks to members. Some of the benefits include a free beer on joining the membership, 10% discount on purchases, and a free beer in the members’ birthday week, among others.

Banks Club Shopify Membership Strategy Breakdown

In this section, we look at the key features of the various strategies used by Banks Club membership program, and tips we can use.

1. Offers a discount on all purchases

A study by Harvard Business Review says smaller and more precise discounts could help brands increase sales. And for 3 out of 4 online shoppers, discounts are a key factor in purchase decisions.

One of the biggest factors that drives membership sign ups is discounts. Customers expect cost benefits and savings when they sign up for membership programs. When customers know that a membership program will lead to consistent savings, signing them becomes easier. Even if there’s a membership fee involved.

That’s what Banks Club does. The annual-fee based membership program offers a 10% discount on every purchase, online and offline.

Here are some tips to plan your membership discounts:

  • Offer a discount on every purchase. This helps members recover the membership fee they paid and also keeps bringing them back to your store
  • Offer surprise discounts on festivals and special occasions to keep members excited and interested
  • Find new opportunities to offer discounts. For instance, if you add a new product to your inventory, create a week-long launch campaign and offer a discount on the new product. However, ensure you do not overdo discounts as it can create a sense of diminished value of your products and membership program

2. Banks Club charges membership fee

To join the Banks Club, members have to pay an annual fee of $75. This fee is only for the first year. From the second year, members can renew their membership for $50.

Members can earn their money back by making purchases at a 10% discount. Additionally, they get other benefits, such as freebies and more.

Many eCommerce brands charge a fee for membership programs. Think Amazon Prime, Walmart, American Express, etc. That’s because serious members do not hesitate to pay a membership fee.

Let’s look at some factors about membership fees.

  • Serious and genuine customers don’t mind paying a fee
  • For brands, charging a fee is a way to keep away customers who are not interested
  • Having a fee-based membership structure also helps retailers focus their efforts on a smaller segment of select customers, rather than everyone

Here are some tips to run a fee-based membership program:

  • Once customers have paid a fee, ensure you consistently communicate with them about the benefits of the program to keep them engaged. This is because members’ interest tends to diminish as time passes
  • Design your membership fee payment model carefully. For instance, not all customers may be comfortable paying an upfront amount of $75 or $100. If a staggered payment model works better for your customers, try it out
  • Highlight the value of the other benefits. For instance, Banks Club offers free beers on at least two occasions – one for signing up and the other for members’ birthday

3. Multiple payment options

Today, there are several payment options used by customers. From online transfer to cards to mobile wallets to cash and more. Customers expect eCommerce brands to offer these various options.

Brands that offer multiple payment methods have advantages over those that don’t. For instance, offering multiple methods increases convenience for customers and leads to higher conversion rates. It improves customer satisfaction and reduces payment related issues.

Thus, enabling multiple payment methods brings in more cash flow and leads to an overall competitive advantage to the brand.

Banks Brewing Store offers multiple payment options, such as mobile wallets and cards. It’s Shopify checkout page has a minimal design with easy navigation and UX.

Overall, this aspect leads to a better experience for its customers and increases conversions. Moreover, the checkout page also highlights the fact that members pay lesser fees from the second year onward, improving conversion rates.

Let’s learn some tips for planning payments for memberships:

  • Integrate a Shopify membership app that allows multiple payment options
  • Choose payment methods that are popular and widely used to cater to a large customer base including various customer segments
  • Prioritize payments security when choosing your membership app security features
  • Choose payment methods that are efficient and economical for your membership model and for your Shopify business
  • Ensure you have payment methods that are suited for recurring payments, such as recurring cards, direct debits, etc.
  • Consider local payment methods if your membership program caters to multiple geographical regions. Enable payment methods from all regions to cater to a wider audience
  • Choose an efficient payment gateway that easily integrates with your Shopify store. Also look for features such as fraud detection, card upgrades, etc.
  • Conduct customer surveys to understand their preferred payment methods

4. Banks Club membership program is simple

The structure of the Banks Club membership program is simple and straightforward. It is easy for customers to understand and transact. For instance, the perks are clearly mentioned, so members know exactly what they can expect.

Customers prefer everything to be easy and simple, including payments. Banks Club offers multiple easy payment options to choose from. What is more, its members get first access to limited edition releases.

Here’s how you can make your Shopify membership program simple and easy:

  • Focus on easy management by integrating automated processes with the help of a smart membership app
  • Ensure the payment method is easy, there are multiple payment options, and the payments are secure and automated. This adds to member convenience
  • Members have committed to your brand for a long term, hence, you must ensure you give them premium treatment and make them feel special
  • Personalize your membership program experience with the help of customization and personalized perks
  • Work on building strong customer relationships via your membership program through consistent communication, feedback requests, etc.

5. Banks Club automates membership processes

Automation has numerous advantages for eCommerce stores. It increases efficiency, reduces costs, enhances customer experience, and helps brands make better use of data. Automation helps streamline processes and allows businesses to focus on strategic growth.

Banks Brewing uses Shopify membership app, Appstle Membership for its membership program. The brand automates various functions with the app.

Here’s how you can leverage automation for your membership programs:

  • Automate repetitive tasks and process things faster, such as order fulfilling, shipping, sending notifications, etc. By reducing manual processes, you can increase efficiency
  • Reduce operational costs and improve resource allocation by automating membership processes with the help of an app
  • Collect and analyze customer data and use the insights to personalize membership experiences
  • Automate communication and reduce wait time. This leads to enhanced customer experience
  • Create a seamless shopping experience for customers
  • Make informed business decisions based on customer data and analysis
  • Track inventory in real-time, reduce stockout, manage your inventory better
  • Scale your business operations easily with the help of automation features to meet increased customer demands

Key takeaways from Banks Club Shopify membership strategy

Here’s a recap of the key takeaways from the Banks Club membership strategies that you could consider when planning your Shopify membership program.

  • Offer value-based pricing to your Shopify members: Banks Club charges a membership fee but also offers a 10% discount to members on all purchases. This offsets the fee and creates value for members. Moreover, reducing the membership fee from the second year also encourages long-term commitment from members
  • Keep your membership programs simple. You can make your membership experience better by creating a straightforward structure and ensuring clear communication that helps customers understand the value proposition
  • Think about discount offers strategically. For instance, a consistent 10% discount to members can encourage repeat purchases, while surprise discounts can maintain excitement
  • Automating processes can help you enhance efficiency and performance. Use an efficient Shopify membership app such as Appstle Memberships
  • Ensure personalization, exclusivity, and customization based on your members preferences. Your Shopify membership app can help you with these features

Ready to set up your Shopify membership strategy?

You can take inspiration from these strategies used by Banks Brewing for its membership program. However, ensure you pick only those strategies that are relevant to your business goals and customer preferences.

You could start with one or two of these strategies and keep experimenting with new strategies from time to time. To plan and manage your Shopify membership strategies, you will need an intuitive app such as Appstle Membership.

The app has an intuitive merchant UI that makes it easy for merchants to manage their membership plans. Its tiered and customized membership perks and automated billing features take away the load of manual processes from merchants.

items.html:
Meal subscriptions have taken the food business by storm. Today, there are multiple options for meal subscriptions for all kinds of cuisines and diet preferences.

However, not all subscription businesses succeed. Those that are planned well and leverage the advantages of digital technology, tend to outdo the traditional subscription businesses.

In this blog, we look at the Shopify subscription strategy of frozen meal subscription by Fresh Chef.

If you’re looking for tips and Shopify subscription strategies for your business, get started with reading this blog.

What is the Fresh Chef Frozen Meals subscription?

Fresh Chef Frozen Meals is a frozen meal food brand. The New Zealand-based brand offers meals that are made with fresh ingredients and frozen at the peak of freshness, keeping nutrients and flavors intact. The brand offers one-time purchases as well as subscriptions.

Meals bought through subscriptions provide price benefits to customers. Apart from that, this Shopify subscription strategy focuses on convenience, flexibility, and customer satisfaction. The brand offers meals that cater to multiple diet types, including vegetarian, non vegetarian, vegan, and combos.

Fresh Chef Frozen Meals Shopify subscription strategy breakdown & takeaways

The food subscription market is projected to grow from USD 6.19 billion in 2025 to USD 11.78 billion by 2032, a CAGR of 9.63%. This rise in the market is also leading to increased competition within brands in the industry. Among the many brands that have got their subscription models right, is Fresh Chef. We dissect the brand’s subscription model features and share takeaways that you can apply to your Shopify subscription strategy.

1. A dedicated page for subscriptions

The Shopify website of Frozen Chef has a dedicated page for subscriptions. This page includes all the details about its subscription plans, how to place orders, among other details.

Having a dedicated page or space makes it easy for customers to find information and leads to a better customer experience. Believe it or not, but this simple Shopify subscription strategy can make a huge difference to customer experience. Moreover, it is also a way for brands to show that their program is an important part of their business.

2. Offers three subscription tiers to choose from

Fresh Chef offers three different frozen meal subscription tiers to choose from. The three tiers are based on the number of meals – 6, 8, and 16 meals. Here are some of the positives from this format:

  • Keeping the number of subscription tiers minimal and simple makes it easy for customers to choose. It keeps away decision fatigue
  • Features of the three plans remain the same; only the number of meals change. This makes it easy for customers to choose a plan
  • The pricing of the three plans differs. Plans with 8 and 16 meals have discounted pricing. The price benefits are mentioned under each plan

3. Detailed information on shipping

The page also includes detailed information about shipping.

Proper shipping and logistics is as important as the quality of products in subscription models. Delayed deliveries or damaged products can lead to poor customer experience. It can also increase the churn rate.

To ensure seamless shipping and transparency, Fresh Chef frozen meal subscription shared detailed information on the subscription page. The brand shares details about:

  • The shipping calendar for the current month
  • Days when deliveries are available and not available
  • Holidays and rural shipping availability schedule
  • Delivery timing
  • Cut off timing
  • Names and details of courier companies

4. Flexibility features

Flexibility is essential because it allows customers to tailor the subscription experience to their requirements. This Shopify subscription strategy leads to customer satisfaction and loyalty. Around 17% of customers say flexibility and 32% say convenience are factors that lead their subscription sign-up decision.

Fresh Chef frozen meal subscription allows customers a high level of flexibility. Customers can change, skip, or cancel subscription delivery when they want to. Customers can simply go to the Shopify store’s ‘Manage My Subscription’ function to make these changes.

Apart from this, subscribers can also choose their delivery frequency from every 1, 2, 3, or 4 weeks. Additionally, subscribers can also add a note with their orders, driving more customization and personalization.

5. Easy cancellation policy

Subscriptions have a high rate of cancellation due to many factors, including, subscription fatigue caused by too many subscriptions, increasing fees, rigid policies, etc. Having an easy cancellation flow and policy is a critical factor.

As customers sign up for long-term associations, they prefer to have easy cancellation if they wish to discontinue their subscription plan. Fresh Chef has made cancellation easy for subscribers.

A dedicated page for cancellation policy shares the following details:

  • Cancellation via website and email
  • Changes to meals
  • Order cut off day
  • Default recurring

6. Multiple meal options

The Fresh Chef offers multiple meal options for subscribers to choose from. This ensures different subscriber segments’ requirements are met and the brand can cater to a wide range of customers. Brands must set up Shopify subscription strategies to cater to multiple customer segments.

For instance, the brand offers veg only, veg and meat, seafood, and other options. Each frozen food option comes with a detailed description and meal label, including ingredient details.

When subscribers have many options, it keeps their subscription experience exciting. They can try new products in every delivery and keep boredom and monotony away. Boredom is another reason customers cancel subscriptions after a while.

7. Mobile optimized subscription experience

In a survey,73% web designers said non-responsive design is one of the key reasons why visitors leave websites. With an increase in mobile commerce, customers expect a seamless mobile experience. Hence, eCommerce brands should keep mobile users in mind when designing their subscription site.

Fresh Chef has a mobile optimized website, which enhances its subscription experience. The images, text, layout, and speed are optimized for mobile screens, which helps the brand attract traffic from mobile users as well.

8. Discount on higher tier subscription plans

One of the biggest advantages of signing up for subscriptions is discounted pricing. For brands, this is an effective marketing tactic. And Fresh Chef ensures it lets customers know about the discounts it offers.

From the three meal subscription options, two offer discounts, mentioned against the original price one would pay if bought individually. This is a great Shopify subscription strategy to attract subscribers.

Key takeaways from Fresh Chef Shopify subscription strategy

In this section, we put together key takeaways based on the points discussed above. These takeaways can give you an overview of how to plan your Shopify subscriptions.

Ensure cohesiveness and consistency

Plan your subscription program strategically before starting off. Ensure you use an efficient Shopify subscription app that allows you to have a comprehensive set of features, such as discounts and integrations.

Prioritize clarity and simplicity

Clear information, easy UX, and quick access to information can enhance your Shopify subscription strategy. It gives a good experience to customers, leading to higher satisfaction and loyalty rates.

Keep a customer-focused approach

Customers like brands that focus on them, understand them, and personalize their experiences. Fresh Chef ensures customer-focus by building trust via features such as transparent shipping information, clear communication, etc. Moreover flexibility and easy cancellation procedure, too, leads to a better customer experience.

Integrate an efficiency subscriptions app

With new and advanced digital features, eCommerce brands are not only competing with product quality, but also the digital experience of subscribers. This is possible because of intuitive subscription apps, such as Appstle Subscription App.

Create an attractive value proposition

Factors such as a wide range in the inventory, such as multiple meal options; tiered pricing structure and visible discounts; and mobile optimization ensure a seamless experience and attract customers.

Create sustainable revenue

Fresh Chef Shopify subscription strategy demonstrates how a well-designed subscription model can provide sustainable revenue, reduce churn, and maximize convenience for customers. By addressing your customers’ pain points, you can set up a successful subscription model.

Get started with your Shopify subscription strategy

The above frozen meals subscription strategies can help you give you tips and cues for your Shopify business. However, you may not want to apply all the strategies at one go. Rather, you could try out different strategies and identify the ones that work well for your business goals and customer preference.

To set up these strategies and automate your subscription business, you will have to partner with an efficient Shopify subscription app, such as Appstle Subscriptions.

items.html:
Gone are the days when eCommerce brands advertized products and customers simply made purchases.

Today, there are many factors that customers consider. Hence, transactional relationships are no longer sustainable for brands. Customers prefer long-term engaging associations.

This brings the spotlight on marketing and retention strategies. Subscriptions and loyalty programs are two key long-term customer retention methods. And when eCommerce brands combine these two strategies, it can result in maximum growth.

In this blog, we explore how subscription and loyalty strategy combined can help your business, and how to go about it.

Why combine subscription and loyalty strategy?

According to a report by Forbes, the cost of customer acquisition has gone up in the last decade. It is now $29 for every customer acquired. This puts the emphasis on retention strategies to reduce customer acquisition costs.

Now, subscription and loyalty strategies individually help with customer retention. But when combined, the two strategies can increase the value of the other. For instance, it can increase engagement, reduce churn, and lead to higher customer lifetime value (CLV).

Here are some examples of how brands combine these two Shopify retention strategies:

Example 1: Amazon Prime

Amazon Prime membership is both a subscription and loyalty program in one. Members pay an annual fee and enjoy benefits such as free shipping, Prime Video, etc., while also earning points.

Example 2: HelloFresh

HelloFresh food subscription offers Fresh Points program through which long-term subscribers can earn points, discounts, and free mean upgrades, among other benefits.

Source

How do loyalty-driven subscriptions improve customer retention?

Now let’s look into the details of how exactly loyalty programs enhance engagement and growth opportunities when combined with subscriptions, and some takeaways for your Shopify subscription and loyalty strategy.

By rewarding long-term subscribers

Offering loyalty points to subscribers can improve the value proposition of your subscription plans. Also, when subscribers see tangible benefits, they are less likely to cancel their subscription; and more likely to continue with your brand.

For instance, in addition to free shipping, gifts, discounts, early access, and in-person events, subscribers also get points. These points have monetary value and can be used to make more purchases. This gives subscribers one more reason to shop more from your Shopify store with their points.

Example: Chewy pet supply subscription offers “Paw Points” for scheduled deliveries, redeemable for future purchases or donations to animal shelters.

By encouraging renewals through tiered programs

Tiered loyalty program structures offer benefits based on levels or tiers. For instance, gold level members get more benefits than silver and bronze members. Thus, silver and bronze members strive to become gold members. With loyalty-driven subscription programs, you can incentivize higher spending and long-term loyalty, and customers tend to stay with your brand longer.

By increasing engagement

Loyalty programs can help you increase customer engagement opportunities for subscribers. For instance, offering points on every subscription order gives you the opportunity to interact and communicate with subscribers. When you use these communication opportunities smartly, you can increase the quality of your engagement with subscribers.

How to structure a successful subscription + loyalty model?

There are various ways you can structure your subscription and loyalty program. The subscription app you choose should provide options and customization features to create a unique subscription and loyalty program. Here are some structures you could consider:

1. Tier-based subscription and loyalty strategy

This subscription model is based on different levels or tiers. For example, bronze, silver, and gold are common tiers used by eCommerce businesses. Moreover, most brands create three or four tiers, as it is easy to manage.

So what can you do with a tier-based subscription and loyalty program?

  • Offer loyalty points towards subscription orders based on the tier or level
  • Encourage subscribers to increase their spend in order to progress to higher levels
  • Clearly mention the loyalty benefits for each tier and ensure the benefits are exclusive to each tier
  • Make it easy for subscribers to advance to the higher tiers

2. Gamification for subscription and loyalty strategy

There are numerous ways to engage customers beyond purchases, points, and transactions. If you want to create a unique and engaging subscription program, you will have to bring in exciting rewards and gamification.

What are some unique and engaging rewards you could consider?

  • Think of rewards that would be relevant to your products, services, and subscribers
  • For example, allow customers to use their points to support causes such as animal welfare, environmental initiatives, etc. This would attract conscious consumers
  • Offer points to subscribers that refer their friends or reshare your content on social media

3. Monetize subscription and loyalty strategy

Most brands offer free subscriptions. However, there are many brands that don’t shy away from charging a fee for their subscription programs. This has many benefits, such as an extra revenue generation stream, a KPI to measure year after year, and a pool of interested subscribers.

Here are some ways you can monetize your subscription and loyalty program:

  • Introduce paid memberships alongside traditional subscription plans
  • Increase the paid subscription fees every year or every few years, leading to recurring revenue growth
  • Allow customers to progress tiers by joining paid memberships

How does combining subscription and loyalty strategy impact business finances?

While you would need to incur some expenses to manage a subscription plan that has loyalty benefits combined in it, the monetary advantages this strategy will bring are way more than the expenses.

Let’s explore some ways in which your Shopify business can benefit with this combined strategy:

1. Increase in customer lifetime value (CLV)

Both subscription and loyalty programs have one common advantage. They improve CLV. Both these strategies involve long-term engagement from customers and hence lead to increased CLV.

A study by BusinessDasher found that loyal customers are 5x more likely to repurchase, 5x more likely to forgive, 4x more likely to refer, and 7x more likely to try a new offering.

Here’s how it helps increase customer lifetime value:

  • Long-term subscription sign-ups (6 months, 1 year) ensure more revenue for your business and more spends from customers
  • With tiered structures, customers tend to spend more to progress to higher levels, thus, increase CLV
  • When you focus on creating more engaging experiences for subscribers and loyalty members, they tend to stay more loyal to you. They also refer their friends, which adds to your revenue

2. Reduced churn rates

According to the Harvard Business Review, engaged customers are more likely to be loyal to brands. That’s because higher engagement with a brand leads to deeper emotional connections and satisfaction. These factors lead to repeat purchases and reduced churn.

Here’s why engaged customers are less likely to cancel subscriptions:

  • With more engagement, you can make customers feel more invested in their relationship with your brand
  • Loyal customers tend to make repeat purchases, increasing recurring revenue growth and profitability
  • Loyal customers are more likely to increase word-of-mouth referrals
  • Increasing customer retention by 5% can increase profits by 25% to 95%. With subscription and loyalty program together, you can increase retention

Example: DollarShave men’s grooming subscription model’s referrals program offers 500 points to subscribers who share referrals.

3. Higher average order value (AOV)

With subscriptions and loyalty programs, brands have more opportunities to upsell and cross-sell. This directly leads to an increase in the average order value. Consistent increase in order value can have a positive impact on profits.

Here are some ways to create upselling and cross-selling opportunities for subscription and loyalty strategy:

  • Upsell and cross-sell new products added to the subscription inventory and offer exclusive extra points
  • Offer exclusive loyalty rewards on specific recommended products
  • Promote subscribers to a higher loyalty and subscription membership tier when they spend more

Best practices for implementing subscription and loyalty strategy on Shopify stores

  • Choose the right platform for your Shopify store.It is critical to choose the best Shopify subscription and loyalty apps that provide comprehensive features. Your app should allow seamless experience for both subscriptions and rewards programs.
  • Appstle Subscriptions App and Appstle Rewards & Loyalty App is the best Shopify app preferred by merchants across industries.
  • Collect, analyze, and use customer data to personalize rewards. Create customer segments and offer subscription perks and loyalty points.
  • Utilize multiple communication platforms, such as email, SMS, push notifications to engage customers and drive retention. Automate subscription and loyalty strategy communication.

Example: The North Face, an outdoor gear brand, has a loyalty program called XPLR Pass. The program offers discounts, field testing options for gear, and dedicated customer support, along with points when customers return their old gear.

Ready to start your Shopify subscription and loyalty strategy?

Combining subscription and loyalty programs can be a game-changer for your business growth. From driving engagement to increasing loyalty and multiplying profits, a combination of the two strategies can set your business for success.

And the best part, you can set up and manage these strategies using Appstle apps. Appstle provides a suite of intuitive and comprehensive apps for Shopify marketing requirements.

items.html:
The maximum number of drop-offs occur at the checkout stage. And the reasons are many – from hidden costs to lack of payment options to lengthy forms.

Hence, a smooth checkout experience is essential to ensure higher subscription conversions.

In this blog, we explore subscription checkout optimization strategies, best practices, UX improvements, and ways to reduce friction.

Understanding the basics of subscription checkout funnels

Before we get into subscription checkout optimization strategies, we must understand the basics of the subscription checkout funnel.

The stages in subscription checkout

Here’s how a typical checkout works:

  • Subscription plan selection stage: At this stage, customers choose the subscription plan that suits their needs and budget
  • Cart review: Once customers zero-in on a subscription plan, in the next stage they review (pricing and other details) and confirm their chosen plan
  • Filling form with information: At this stage, customers share information about themselves, such as contact details, billing, shipping address, payment details, etc.
  • Subscription confirmation: Next, customers review and confirm their subscription sign-up
  • Order completion: In this last stage of subscription checkout, customers receive a confirmation about their subscription sign-up

At which stage do drop-offs happen?

Data reveals some patterns of customers dropping off from the subscription checkout process. By identifying drop-off points, we can implement better subscription checkout optimization strategies. Here are some common drop-off points:

  • At the stage of information sharing or form filling: There are a few reasons customers drop off at this point. They may not want to share personal details because of security and data privacy reasons, or they may find the form to be too lengthy and tedious.
  • Account sign-up: While it’s important for customers to sign up for subscriptions by creating an account, many customers do not want to sign up because they are already part of many subscriptions.
  • Unexpected or hidden costs: Hidden or surprise costs at the checkout process is one of the biggest reasons for drop-offs. If there are costs such as annual subscription fees or delivery charges that customers hadn’t anticipated, they might choose to drop off.
  • Complex checkout process: Another reason customers drop-off is when the process of sign-up is complex or lengthy. Customers want seamless subscription sign up. A complicated process might lead to frustration and drop-off.

Subscription vs. one-time purchase: checkout experience difference

Subscription One-time purchase
Payment commitment Customers have to be given clear information about billing frequency and terms as they get into a long-term association Customers make payment for products or services they purchase one time
Long-term relationship Customers enter into a long-term relationship with the business Customers have a single transaction and may not come back to make any more purchases
Cancellation Since customers get into a long-term contract, they may worry about cancellation policies and terms Since customers make a single purchase, they may only want to know cancellation terms or return policies for that single purchase
Value perception Customers look for the long-term value that the subscription plan would give them One-time purchases do not involve long-term value perception

How to reduce friction in the subscription checkout process

You can ensure subscription checkout optimization by using multiple ways that help enable a smooth checkout. Here are some ways:

1. Simplify the subscription checkout process

A complex and lengthy checkout process can lead to cart abandonment. Here are some things to do:

  • Minimize the number of steps in the checkout process
  • Use smart features, such as auto-fill and conditional logic to show only relevant fields
  • Use single-line address fields
  • Gather only essential information at this stage

2. Offer a guest checkout option

While this may seem difficult for subscriptions, you could try a guest-checkout option, making it easy for customers.

  • Highlight the benefits of account creation, such as order tracking and subscription management
  • Use social login features for a seamless subscription sign-up
  • Create an account automatically using email address

3. Display progress indicators

When you show customers how close they are to finishing the sign up process, it has a psychological effect on them, leading them to complete the process. Here’s what you can do:

  • Have a progress bar showing all checkout steps
  • Keep the number of steps minimal, to 3 or 4
  • Mention an estimated time to completion, for example, 1 minute

How to optimize the subscription pricing and plan selection

Here are some tips from our experts:

1. Provide clear pricing details

Apart from perks, people join subscriptions for cost benefits. And so, if they come across hidden fees and surprise charges, it can instantly put them off. That’s why transparency in pricing is critical. It helps build trust and reduce cart abandonment.

Some ways to ensure clarity in pricing are: Mention detailed and complete cost breakdown early on in the checkout process. Highlight savings in comparison to one-time purchase. Display shipping costs and taxes. Additionally, separate subscription costs and any one-time charges.

2. Allow customers to compare plans

Having to choose from multiple subscription plans can lead to decision paralysis, delaying conversions. One way to help customers to choose the best suitable subscription plan is to make it easy for them to compare plans. How do you do that?

Create side-by-side comparison tables highlighting features and benefits of each plan. You could use media, such as videos and images to recommend popular plans. Mention clear information for each plan, including a summary of who each plan is best suited for.

3. Offer flexible billing options

As subscriptions entail long-term commitments, customers may prefer flexible billing options. For example, monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, or annual payment options. By doing so, you can cater to different customer segments and their preferences.

Here are some things to do:

  • Offer multiple billing frequencies with discounts
  • Mention savings amount or percentage for different billing frequencies
  • Allow customers to switch between different billing frequencies
  • Offer EMI or sail payment options for higher-priced subscriptions

How to improve trust and transparency

Since customers are getting into a long-term and recurring billing commitment, it is essential to gain their trust and confidence. Long-term commitment anxiety can be a barrier to conversion. Here are some ways to build trust and transparency for your Shopify subscription checkout optimization.

1. Clear cancellation and refund policies

One of the first things customers tend to look for is the cancellation terms, in case they choose to unsubscribe. Hence, clearly mention the cancellation terms. You could offer free trial periods that do not require customers to share their card details. Make cancellation or pausing subscriptions easy. Additionally, share information about how customers can manage their plans by themselves.

2. Share social proof

It is human psychology; we feel more confident when we read reviews and see social proof shared by other customers. Here’s how you can improve trust and credibility via social proof:

  • Display customer testimonials and reviews about their subscription experience
  • Share ratings and review counts
  • Display subscriber statistics; for example, 1000 subscribers joined this month
  • Show real-time pop-up notifications of recent subscribers

3. Badges and trust signals

With rising online fraud and data security issues, customers are wary of signing up to multiple subscriptions. One way to reduce this customer worry and increase subscription conversions is to display badges and trust signals.

Display security badges that demonstrate compliance adherence. Show logos, supported payment methods, display money-back guarantee messages, among others. Display all these at checkout to reduce customer concerns.

Ensure a mobile- and multi-device-optimized checkout experience

Here are some best practices to follow:

1. Create a mobile-optimized subscription experience

An increasing number of customers prefer to use their mobile devices to transact with brands, including managing subscriptions. Hence, it is essential to ensure an efficient mobile experience for your subscription model. Some important factors for subscription checkout optimization on mobile are: design an experience for small screens by ensuring thumb-friendly buttons, and create a responsive design that adapts to different screen sizes. Ensure clear images and minimise horizontal scrolling.

2. One-click checkout

With digital payments gaining preference, offering digital wallet payment options can increase subscription sign-ups. You can make one-click checkout easier for customers by offering multiple options, such as Google Pay, Apple Pay, and other digital wallets. Incorporate biometric authentication, and reduce the number of steps or click for completing a subscription sign up.

3. Increase page loading speed

Customers tend to want everything within a few seconds. A slight delay can lead to abandonment rates. To avoid this, increase speed and reduce load time for the checkout process. Some ways to do this are: minimize page weight and optimize images, use predictive loading for the checkout process, and provide visual feedback and help during the checkout process to make checkout steps faster.

How to leverage upsells and personalization for subscription conversions

Here are some ways to drive higher conversions:

1. Offer upsells and recommendations

To enhance the checkout process and increase conversions, you can implement upselling and personalisation. When customers perceive more value from their subscription plans, the checkout conversion rates increase. Some ways to incorporate upselling is to recommend add-on products or services. You can offer one-time purchases along with the subscription plans, and share limited-period offers to encourage new sign-ups. Additionally, you can use data and analytics to offer personalized recommendations.

2. Personalize checkout experience

Another way to enhance the subscription checkout experience is to focus on personalisation at various stages of the journey. For instance, pre-fill information based on customer behavior, and use browser cookies to remember returning visitors. You can use smart features, such as dynamic features based on customer location. Further, offer personalized deals and incentives for seamless subscription signups.

3. Integrate loyalty and rewards

Another strategy for subscription checkout optimization is to combine loyalty and rewards benefits with subscriptions. There are many ways to do so; here are some: show customers loyalty points available for subscription sign-up. Offer exclusive perks to subscribers, highlight milestone rewards, and create tiered benefits that increase with subscription period. For example, more rewards for annual subscription compared to quarterly plans.

Monitor and analyze checkout performance

Here’s how to know if your subscription checkout is working well:

1. Implement A/B testing

By continuously monitoring and analysing the subscription checkout performance, you can keep improving the checkout conversion rates. One way to do so is to implement A/B testing. For example, try button placements, use different copy and CTAs. Try different form layouts and field arrangements, and try alternative pricing and discount messaging.

2. Track drop-off points and make improvements

To reduce drop-offs and increase conversions, you will have to understand the reasons your customers are dropping off during the checkout process. Some things you can do are: incorporate a step-by-step funnel tracking system, set up exit-intent tracking to identify the reasons for drop-offs. You can use session recordings and analyze subscription sign up completion rates and errors.

3. Collect and address customer feedback

To improve the checkout flow, gather customer feedback and address issues to enhance customer experience. For instance, collect feedback directly from customers via different channels. Implement automated post-abandonment surveys to understand reasons for drop-offs, use heatmaps to understand behaviour patterns, and analyze customer support inquiries related to checkout issues.

Ready to optimize your Shopify subscription checkout process?

Your Shopify subscription checkout process is as important as the first stage—the awareness stage—in the customer journey. It is the point that sees the maximum number of drop-offs. Hence, to ensure reduced drop-offs, and increased conversions, implement the subscription checkout optimization strategies shared above.

To apply these strategies, you will require a comprehensive and intuitive Shopify subscriptions app. Explore Appstle Subscriptions App, designed for Shopify and Shopify Plus stores. The app enables automation, different types of subscription plans, recurring payments, tiered structure, gamification, personalization, and many other marketing capabilities.

items.html:
Most eCommerce brands offer loyalty and rewards programs. Points and rewards are effective incentives to attract customers and increase sales.

However, over time, loyalty programs tend to become monotonous and boring. Loyalty members begin losing interest. And at some point, stop engaging with it.

There are few brands that do their loyalty programs right. One such brand is Brownie Heaven. In this blog, we explore what makes Brownie Heaven Shopify loyalty program strategy so successful and what we can learn from it.

What is the Brownie Heaven loyalty program?

Brownie Heaven is a UK-based online bakery. It specializes in brownies and offers a wide range of flavors and varieties. The brand also offers a brownie loyalty program called Brownie Points. The loyalty program helps the brand enhance customer retention and increase customer lifetime value (CLV).

The Brownie Points rewards program incentivizes repeat purchases with its points system. It offers rewards that encourage customers to make repeat and additional purchases.

The Brownie Heaven Shopify loyalty program strategy breakdown

In this section, you will learn many effective strategies used by the Brownie Heaven loyalty program that you can adapt and apply to your Shopify loyalty programs.

1. A dedicated page for the loyalty program on the website

The Brownie Heaven website has a page dedicated to the loyalty program. This page includes all the basic and important information about the rewards program. Customers who want to know any information about the loyalty program can simply visit this page and find the details.

This page includes:

  • CTA to sign in or create an account
  • Ways to earn reward points
  • Ways to redeem reward points
  • Referrals program
  • Frequently asked questions and answers
  • Customer reviews
  • Customer support chatbot

Key takeaway: Make customers’ loyalty experience easy and enjoyable through clarity, transparency, and ease. This is one of the most underrated eCommerce customer retention strategies.

2. A simple structure

Customers prefer things to be simple when shopping online and transacting with brands. Complicated processes can make people feel overwhelmed and

The Brownie Heaven loyalty program follows a points-based system. Customers can earn points for various actions, such as on purchases, for signing up for SMS, following on social media, etc. The brand allows multiple ways to earn reward points.

Moreover, the reward program is fully integrated into their Shopify platform, which streamlines and syncs all the processes, making it simple for customers to engage and transact.

Key takeaway: You can include gamification in loyalty programs to offer a tiered structure experience and increase engagement, but ensure clarity and simplicity.

3. Multiple ways to earn points

When brands make earning points difficult for customers, they might lose interest. While the opposite happens, earning points is easy. Customers start engaging more. Brownie Heaven loyalty program offers customers many different and exciting ways to earn points.

Some lessons from the Brownie Heaven Shopify loyalty program strategy to apply to your store:

  • Customers get points when they sign up for the loyalty program
  • For subscribing to the newsletter
  • On every product they purchase
  • Points on birthday
  • Points for subscribing to SMS
  • Referrals
  • Social media follows

Key takeaway: Offer personalized customer incentives to make the loyalty program more exciting and relevant for customers. This ensures longevity and long-term returns.

4. Ways to redeem loyalty points

The way you make it simple to earn points, it helps to make it easy for customers to use those points. Not being able to easily spend and redeem points can lead to frustration and disengagement.

The brand keeps it simple. Members can redeem points to get discounts. This way, the brand also ensures more sales and increased CLV.

Here’s how Brownie Heaven makes it easy for members to use points:

  • Redeem points against discounts
  • 2000 points to get £20 discount
  • 1500 points to get £15 discount
  • 1000 points to get £10 discount
  • 500 points to get £5 discount

Key takeaway: AI-powered rewards programs automate points redemption and other processes. This can help bring consistency, keep fraud risks at bay, and enhance experience.

5. Brownie Heaven loyalty program has a referral program

On average, businesses get 60% of their business from referral programs. People trust recommendations shared by their friends and families more than direct advertisements from brands.

Brownie Heaven Shopify loyalty program strategy has integrated its referral program. When existing loyalty customers refer someone, they receive 500 points. The referred customer gets a £5 discount when they make a purchase.

Referrals marketing strategy is effective for brands as it can increase the number of potential customers, and sales.

Key takeaway: You can further personalize the referral experience through personalized customer incentives for members that refer new customers.

6. It has a dedicated FAQs section

The Brownie Heaven has included an FAQs section on the loyalty program page. This makes it easy for customers to find information.

The FAQs section answers questions about:

  • What is the Brownie Points program?
  • How to earn points?
  • How to redeem points?
  • What do approved, pending, and cancelled statuses mean?

Key takeaway: Include features such as FAQ, live chat, easy communication options in your Shopify loyalty program strategy for a good customer experience.

7. Clear and straightforward structure

The Brownie Points loyalty program has a clear structure that is easy to understand for customers. Moreover, the brand explains its features with clarity on the website.

  • Customers can refer to the FAQs section to know details
  • Customers can also get instant answers to questions via the live chat feature
  • To increase trust, the brand shares customer reviews and ratings on the page

Key takeaway: Ensure you share as much information as possible on the dedicated loyalty program page and make it easy for customers to contact you to know more.

8. Many customer acquisition elements

Brownie Heaven has strategically designed its loyalty program to increase the potential of attracting and acquiring customers. Here are some of the aspects of the Brownie Heaven Shopify loyalty program strategy that help the brand acquire and retain customers:

  • A reward for joining the loyalty program. The brand offers 200 points for signing up for the program
  • Easy to join the loyalty program and immediate rewards upon signing up work as an effective value proposition for new customers
  • The brand rewards customers for social media following. This helps extend its reach

Key takeaway: Include personalized customer incentives to increase customer acquisition and retention. It can help enhance customer experience and satisfaction.

9. Many loyalty member retention strategies

A key element of success for eCommerce is customer retention. Existing customers helps brands increase revenue and CLV. Moreover, the cost of new customer acquisition is much more than retaining existing customers.

Here are some ways in which Brownie Heaven enhances customer retention and how you can enhance eCommerce customer retention:

  • Offers points for every purchase. This creates a value proposition for return purchases
  • Offers birthday rewards, creating an annual event and incentive for customers to look forward to
  • The point accumulation structure drives customers to reach reward threshold

Key takeaway: Give retention equal importance as acquisition. It will have a positive effect on your revenue and profits.

10. Offers a good customer experience

The Brownie Heaven offers an overall good experience to customers. From designing a customer-centric loyalty program to keeping it simple and straightforward, the brand has paid attention to a lot of details in its Shopify loyalty program strategy.

Here are some of the factors that lead to a good experience for their customers:

  • The Brownie Heaven Shopify loyalty program is easy to understand and not complex
  • The brand offers instant gratification by giving points for every purchase
  • Customers can easily access their balance points and get an overview in their customer account
  • Every element is integrated within their Shopify system, allowing a smooth experience

Key takeaway: The Brownie Points loyalty program ensures an overall good experience by keeping the program structure simple and things easy.

Key lessons from Brownie Points Shopify loyalty program strategy

  1. Clear communication via a dedicated page: Include all important information, such as how to earn, redeem points, FAQs, and customer support options in one place, like a page or a loyalty program app.
  2. Keep the structure simple yet engaging: Create a points-based or a tier-based structure keeping it simple and frictionless. Offer multiple ways to earn points to keep customers engaged.
  3. Make points redemption easy and valuable: Make rewards meaningful and valuable to encourage customers to make additional purchases as an eCommerce customer retention strategy.
  4. Integrate other marketing features in the Shopify loyalty program strategy: Leverage marketing strategies such as referrals to generate high-quality leads at lower acquisition costs.
  5. Implement retention strategies: Include exciting features such as purchase points, birthday rewards, and threshold-based incentives to keep existing customers engaged and returning.
  6. Use AI and automation tools: Use Shopify loyalty program apps to manage points, redemptions, gamification in loyalty programs, and personalized offers without adding operational complexity.
  7. Balance acquisition and retention efforts: Maximize customer lifetime value while optimizing your marketing spend by giving equal focus to acquisition and retention.

Set up your Shopify loyalty program strategy with these lessons

No matter the type of products you offer on your Shopify store, you can set up an effective Shopify loyalty program strategy that helps your brand grow and prosper.

items.excerpt: AI has immense potential for eCommerce. From marketing to design to content to sales – there are AI tools for every process. items.html:
AI has immense potential for eCommerce. From marketing to design to content to sales – there are AI tools for every process.

While an increasing number of Shopify stores are integrating AI into their systems, many fail to maximize its applications.

In this blog, we look at ways to use AI for Shopify sales growth, across your Shopify store processes, to enhance customer engagement, sales, and profitability.

Read on!

AI application for Shopify stores

Customer-facing: To drive engagement and conversion

One of the biggest advantages of AI is to understand your customers better based on data and analysis. This helps with AI-powered personalization, higher engagement and conversions. Here are some strategies to use AI for customer-facing processes.

Here are some statistics on the various use cases of AI in retail companies.

Source

1. Personalization and product recommendations

AI has changed the way brands interact with customers. While earlier, brands interacted with customers to understand their needs and preferences, now, AI does it for brands. Then, brands interact with customers by sharing personalized recommendations and telling customers what they must purchase.

Here’s how to integrate AI-powered personalization and recommendations:

  • To track customers behavior on the website
  • Collect data about past purchases, interests, preferences
  • Analyze the data to draw patterns
  • Get a better understanding of customers

2. Chatbots and virtual assistants

Customers can have different kinds of requirements from brands. Some may need assistance with shopping, while some might have issues that need the brand’s attention.

Their first instinct is to reach out to customer support. Ecommerce brands are now using AI chatbots and virtual assistants to provide customer service. 31% of eCommerce companies use virtual agents or chatbots.

Here’s how using AI-based chatbots and virtual assistants for eCommerce stores can help in many ways. It improves:

  1. Efficiency: Prompt and relevant responses to customers
  2. Scalability: Attend to multiple customers at the same time
  3. Customer satisfaction: Prompt and effective support lead to customer satisfaction
  4. Data collection: Collect and analyze data easily via AI tools

Here are some use cases for AI for Shopify sales growth:

  • To answer basic questions
  • Offer shopping assistance
  • To resolve customer issues
  • Guide customers for rewards, points, offers, etc.
  • Provide 24/7 AI-enhanced customer support and assistance

3. AI for dynamic pricing and smart discounts

AI-based dynamic pricing adjusts prices of products and services in real-time, based on potential customer actions. It has changed the way eCommerce businesses sell their products and services.

For example, when the demand for a particular product is low, maybe due to seasonal change, AI automatically reduces its price to drive more sales. Dynamic pricing helps increase sales and revenue, customer experience, inventory management, and adds competitive advantage.

Here’s how you can use AI for Shopify sales growth through dynamic pricing:

  • Use AI to adjust pricing based on competitor pricing, so you can offer the best price
  • Change pricing based on real-time demand and supply
  • Change pricing based on customer actions and behavior to encourage more sales

4. AI-based email and SMS marketing

Consistent communication is a must to keep customers engaged. Ecommerce stores are using AI to set up automated systems for email and SMS marketing.

AI can help speed up email and SMS campaigns, ensure consistency, timely communication, and free up marketing teams’ time with automation.

Here are some ways to use AI for email and SMS:

  • Segment email lists with data such as demographics, purchase history, and engagement levels
  • Use AI to determine optimal email open time to decide send time
  • Create personalized emails using AI
  • Create content using AI tools
  • Conduct A/B testing using AI
  • Automate emails and SMS with AI tools

5. AI-enhanced visual search and AR

AI-based search and augmented reality offer many advantages to eCommerce stores. For instance, it offers a faster and more intuitive experience. Customers feel instant satisfaction, and it can enable a personalized shopping experience.

Here are some ways you can use AI-based AR and visual search:

  • Use AI to analyze past purchase data and offer customized recommendations
  • Use visual search to match products with images uploaded by customers to understand their preference and taste
  • Use AI for Shopify sales growth to enable virtual try ons, for instance, for accessories, clothes, etc.

Here’s an example of Amazon’s Shop the Look AI feature.

6. AI-driven upselling and cross-selling

Upselling and cross-selling are effective strategies to increase sales. However, unlike physical stores where a sales representative can personally recommend products for upselling or cross-selling, for online stores, you can depend on AI tools to help you upsell.

Here’s how to incorporate AI-driven upselling and cross-selling:

  • Automate product recommendation based on customers’ recent purchase
  • Upsell and cross-sell products based on other customers’ purchase patterns
  • Bundle and combine products and offer dynamic discounts based on customer behavior

7. AI for loyalty programs

If you have a loyalty program on your Shopify store, you have to ensure your loyal customers are consistently happy and engaged. And this is where you can employ AI to enhance your Shopify loyalty program.

For instance, you can use AI to understand your loyalty members’ preferences and offer them personalized loyalty incentives. Your AI tools can be set up to provide special 24/7 assistance to loyalty members. Moreover, you can also use AI to optimize the rewards structure for your loyalty members, ensuring retention and higher customer longtime value.

Business operations: For efficiency and profitability

Most eCommerce businesses can benefit from using AI for customer-facing as well as internal and business operations perspectives. Here are some AI applications for business operations that can lead to higher efficiency and profitability.

11. AI for inventory and demand forecasting

AI has made inventory management easy, accurate, and predictive. With the help of AI tools, businesses can easily analyze sales data, sales patterns, market trends, and more. This data analysis and insights can be used to forecast demand and ensure proper inventory management.

For instance, an eCommerce fashion retailer can use AI to analyze purchase patterns based on locations and regions. AI can help predict the styles that sell more in specific locations, and automatically adjust the inventory.

Ways to use AI for Shopify sales growth based on inventory management:

  • Analyze data related to reorders to predict inventory needs
  • Identify slow-selling products before they become deadstock
  • Use AI for dynamic pricing based on demand

12. AI for supply chain and logistics management

Supply chain and logistics management can be quite complex. It has many aspects that have to work in sync; for instance, different locations may require different delivery services, real-time updates due to traffic or weather conditions, etc.

Businesses have proven that the use of AI for Shopify sales growth for supply chain and logistics management can bring efficiency, higher performance, and seamless operations.

Here are some ways to use AI for supply chain and logistics:

  • For customer support related to logistics and delivery
  • Identifying shipment delays and notifying customers
  • Real-time route optimization
  • Early risk detection for disruptions

13. AI-based order fulfillment and automation

Another crucial part of eCommerce stores is warehouse operations and last-mile delivery. And AI is helping streamline these processes, too. For instance, Amazon uses robots at its fulfillment centers to pick and pack orders. The computerized system identifies products and ML optimizes the processing time.

Some ways you can use AI for order fulfillment:

  • Automate warehousing and inventory placement based on order frequency prediction
  • Computerized quality control while packaging
  • Dynamic delivery time and schedule based on real-time conditions

14. AI for subscription management

Running subscription models involves many processes and tasks. Each of them are critical and have to work in sync with the others. This is where AI can help you. From managing your subscription plans to updating them to cancellation management, payments, and inventory management, AI can help you with all these tasks, and more.

In addition to these operations-related processes, AI can also help with customer-facing processes. For instance, personalized recommendations, AI-based dynamic pricing and discounts, AI-enhanced customer support, etc.

With AI, you can automate subscription management and recurring billing:

  • Automate adjusting delivery schedules based on consumption patterns
  • Identify cross-selling opportunities within subscription offerings
  • Identify at-risk subscribers before they cancel subscriptions
  • Optimize pricing tiers based on usage analytics and willingness-to-pay modeling

Source

15. AI for customer segmentation and insights

With AI, retailers can conduct advanced segmentation based on behavior patterns, preferences, and more. For instance, Sephora uses AI systems to analyze customers’ purchase history, and browsing behavior to create customer segments.

Some ways to use AI for Shopify sales growth via segmentation and insights:

  • Use AI to identify high-value customer segments with predictive lifetime value analysis
  • Detect customer behavior patterns to identify their needs before they express it
  • Create dynamic segments that automatically update as customer behavior changes

16. AI for A/B testing

AI can help you identify customer patterns that you may miss otherwise. For instance, you can run A/B tests of different kinds for multiple campaigns at the same time. AI-based analysis can help you with A/B testing at scale.

Here are some use cases for AI A/B testing:

  • Test communication variants for campaigns
  • Personalized testing that shows different variations to different segments
  • AI-generated test hypothesis based on user behavior analysis
  • AI testing for continuous adjustments based on real-time performance data

17. AI for SEO and content optimization

Digital marketing and SEO are key for eCommerce businesses to attract customers. AI tools can help with various processes related to SEO and content. For instance, to create content, optimize it, and to distribute it to the right potential audience.

Here’s how brands are using AI for Shopify sales growth for content and SEO:

  • Use AI for keyword research and to identify trends
  • Automate content optimization by using AI to suggest improvements
  • Conduct content gap analysis using AI
  • Automate internal linking strategies maximizing page authority

18. AI for fraud detection and risk management

With an increase in online fraud, it’s a must for eCommerce retailers to set up fraud detection systems and strategies. For instance, businesses can employ deep learning algorithms that can analyze multiple variables for every transaction to identify fraudulent patterns.

Here’s how you could implement risk management with AI:

  • Identify account takeover attempts via login behavior
  • Detect suspicious purchase patterns based on customers’ past behavior
  • Identify fraudulent shipping address changes
  • Assess transaction risk within seconds

How to get started with AI for Shopify sales growth?

There’s intense competition in the eCommerce market. But that shouldn’t scare you if you integrate the right AI tools on your Shopify store to help you with marketing and operations.

Ensuring your Shopify tools have AI features and the ability to continuously advance with the evolving AI technologies is the best way to get started.

items.html:
Loyalty programs have always been an essential part of a well-rounded loyalty strategy for eCommerce brands. When done well, loyalty programs drive profits and growth for brands.

With the widespread use of AI, there’s a lot that brands can do more, and better. AI can be used for marketing as well as for business processes.

In this blog, we look at all the ways in which to use AI for eCommerce loyalty programs.

Let’s get started!

Marketing and customer-facing AI use cases

Using AI in customer-facing processes, such as marketing, sales, promotions, and communication can help you enhance customer experience and improve the performance of your loyalty program. Here are some ways to use AI for customer-facing processes.

1. Personalized loyalty incentives

Every customer is different. One way AI is helping brands create more effectiveness with loyalty programs is by personalizing rewards.

By collecting and analyzing data, AI helps brands understand customer preference. AI analysis can throw light on customer behavior and purchase history, they kind of reward certain customers are more drawn to, etc.

For instance, consider a customer who purchases a lot of sports gear. Offering them AI-driven customer rewards related to sports will be more relevant to them. This hyper-personalization of loyalty rewards can lead to increased loyalty.

Moreover, AI can also help identify the time, period, moments when customers are more prone to and inclined to making purchases for rewards. For example, it could be during the sale and discount season.

Here’s how to use AI for eCommerce loyalty programs personalization:

  • Use AI to collect customer data
  • Analyze data to understand customers’ likes and interests
  • Know customers in a genuine manner
  • Identify rewards that match customers’ personalities
  • Integrate AI tools to offer personalized rewards via your Shopify loyalty program

Example:

2. AI-powered gamification

Rigid and transactional-only loyalty programs are limiting and do not lead to the kind of experiences customers look for. That’s where gamification can help create engaging rewards programs.

Incorporating gamification in your loyalty program can add an element of fun in it. Besides, it touches all sorts of emotions of your customers – a competitive spirit, instant gratification from winning, etc.

Here’s how to use gamification and AI for eCommerce loyalty programs

  • Add an emotional touch with gamification – make customers feel excited, happy, competitive, and engaged with gamified rewards
  • Use AI to offer personalized gamified experience, for example, offer personalized rewards

3. Chatbots for customer assistance

Another way to use AI for eCommerce loyalty programs is to set up AI-powered chatbots. They can help you stay connected and engage with loyalty program members 24/7. Since these are your special customers, you can make it easy to always stay connected via chatbots.

Here are some use cases of AI-powered chatbots for your loyalty programs.

  • Use AI to ensure your chatbot tool can access customer history and rewards information in real-time
  • Enable chatbots to respond to customer questions related to rewards, such as, checking their available points, explore how to earn rewards, ways to redeem points, etc.
  • Automate communication about customers’ expiring points via chatbots
  • Use AI to handover conversations to human agents when necessary

4. AI-optimised email and SMS notifications

Effective, timely, and targeted communication is essential for loyalty programs. AI tools can help brands send personalized messages, timely messages, and relevant communication.

For instance, if a loyalty member hasn’t logged in or engaged with your brand for over a year, your AI-optimised system will send an email to rekindle their interest and bring them back to your site by telling them about new rewards, expiring rewards in the customer’s account, etc.

Here’s how AI can help enhance loyalty program email and SMS communication:

  • Personalize messages based on customers’ individual engagement patterns
  • Adjust the frequency of emails and SMSes based on customer preference
  • Send timely notifications
  • Create dynamic content in real-time, for example customize rewards

5. Automated churn prevention

The average consumer is part of around 19 loyalty programs, but engages with just a few. Disengagement eventually leads to churn. But with so many customers, it’s hard for brands to track which customers are leaning towards churn.

AI-powered retention strategies can help brands with churn prevention. Detect disengaged customers and identify triggers that may lead to churn. Here’s how you can use AI for eCommerce loyalty programs and reduce churn:

  • Use AI to identify customer behavior that can lead to cancellation
  • Automate offering AI-driven customer rewards in real-time, to reverse churn
  • Use AI to re-engage customers before they churn, based on their past behavior

6. Use AI for social media engagement

AI can also be used for social media engagement for loyalty programs. Using AI, you can offer personalized loyalty incentives to create more engagement. By using AI, you can use your social channels more effectively to identify, reward, and retain customers.

Here are some AI based customer engagement strategies for social media:

  • Offer AI-based rewards for interactions, shares, likes, comments, etc.
  • Offer AI-based rewards for referrals
  • AI-based incentives to customers who share good reviews about your brand
  • Track brand mentions, product discussions, etc. via social listening
  • Use AI to generate personalized interactions for social media channels

AI for eCommerce loyalty programs: business process use cases

AI can help loyalty program internal processes become faster and more efficient, leading to more productivity for eCommerce businesses. In this section, we look at the many ways in which you can use AI to execute your loyalty program efficiently.

1. AI-based segmentation and tiering

AI can help you segment your loyalty program members in several different groups, giving you a more multidimensional view of customer behavior.

Here’s how you can use AI for eCommerce loyalty program segmentation:

  • Use AI for behavioral segmentation. Use AI to track customer browsing patterns, frequency, product categories they’re interested in, and their response to promotions.
  • Create macro and micro segments. Segregate customers into macro groups and also into micro groups based on their behaviors.
  • Enable real-time tier upgrades. Set up an AI system that upgrades customers to higher tiers in real-time, based on their behavior patterns.

2. Use AI to optimize reward structures

One of the most important tasks of loyalty programs is to offer relevant rewards to members. Members aren’t interested in expensive or the number of rewards as much as they are in their relevance. And to make rewards personalized, you can use AI.

  • Monitor which rewards drive more repeat purchases and offer more of those
  • Use AI to test and track which reward combinations are more profitable for your business
  • Set up an AI system that helps you personalize rewards – know which rewards are suitable to specific behaviors and preferences

Example:

3. AI-driven fraud detection

Loyalty and rewards program fraud is on the rise. To protect your customers and your business from fraud, it’s essential to set up automated fraud detection systems. This is where AI comes in.

  • Use AI to track and monitor sudden and unusual point accumulation or redemption patterns
  • Enable additional verification for high-value points redemption to keep fraudulent transactions at bay

4. Use predictive analytics for loyalty programs

One critical task for businesses is to retain customers, understand when customers might leave or disengage. With AI you can set up proactive strategies to identify different things, such as cancellations, churn, fraud, etc. Rather than waiting for these customer actions to occur and then finding a way to reverse them, you can use predictive analytics for loyalty programs to proactively detect them beforehand.

  • Set up AI-powered retention strategies. Your AI system should be able to identify signals many months before customers leave your loyalty program
  • Using AI, predict which customers could offer the highest lifetime value to your business, based on their spending
  • Automate offering AI-driven customer rewards to stop members from cancellations and churn

5. Manage your loyalty programs with AI

When you run a loyalty program, you will have a lot of tasks to manage – from onboarding members to offering personalized loyalty incentives to sending updates and renewal reminders – the list is endless. Performing all these tasks manually is impossible. This is where you can use AI to streamline your loyalty program management.

  • Set up an AI system that smartly allocates rewards based on the product margin, inventory levels, or other factors. This way, you can manage your program more effectively
  • Enable automatic tier adjustments based on members’ behaviors, such as upgrades when their spending increases, and downgrades when it decreases

6. AI-based pricing strategies

Effective pricing strategies are critical to loyalty programs. Customers expect financial benefits and savings when they join loyalty programs. But to manually gauge and assess the best strategies for different customer segments can be difficult. Use AI and algorithms.

  • Use AI to offer dynamic rewards based on product margins and customer value
  • Develop triggers that prevent too much discounting on high-margin products for price-sensitive customers
  • Use algorithms to identify how sensitive different customers are to various rewards

7. Enhance referral programs with AI

Typically, brands offer the same incentives for all referrals. But what if you personalized loyalty incentives or offered exclusive incentives to your loyalty program members? It would definitely enhance your referral and loyalty programs. Here’s how you can use AI for it:

  • Use AI models to identify customers most likely to make successful referrals based on social media activity, review writing, and previous sharing behavior
  • Create systems that offer different referral rewards based on a customer’s influence potential and the projected value of their referrals
  • Use AI to analyze when customers are most receptive to referral requests and automate outreach during these windows

8. Manage your supply chain with AI

Ecommerce stores not only have to manage their regular inventory, but they also have to track their rewards program inventory. If you promise rewards to customers, you must ensure they receive it. That is why inventory management is critical for loyalty programs. Use AI for your eCommerce loyalty programs supply chain management.

  • Use AI to create systems that predict reward redemption patterns based on point accumulation rates and seasonal factors
  • Integrate your inventory with your rewards program and use AI to automatically adjust rewards availability based on inventory levels
  • Set up AI systems that can suggest alternative rewards recommendations based on availability

How to employ AI for your eCommerce loyalty program

To use AI capabilities for your Shopify store, you must set up a strong foundation with smart features that use AI. One way to ensure this strong foundation is to use an efficient Shopify loyalty programs app, such as Appstle Loyalty & Rewards App.

With Appstle, you can build loyalty and rewards programs that are:

  • Highly engaging and attract members
  • Choose different types of loyalty programs
  • Scale based on in depth performance analytics
  • Gamify loyalty programs with exciting activities and rules
  • Personalize loyalty points redemption for higher customer engagement
