In today’s competitive eCommerce space, clothing brands are increasingly turning to membership models to build customer loyalty and create recurring revenue streams.

Umai Clothing has a well designed Shopify membership program that helps engage customers, increase customer lifetime value, and strengthen its brand positioning.

In this blog, we explore the structure, benefits, and strategies of Umai Clothing’s membership program called Umai+. We share effective strategies used by the brand and actionable points to apply to your Shopify membership programs.

What is the Umai+ membership program?

Umai Clothing offers a membership program called Umai+. The membership program offers discounts, store credits, free shipping, members-only exclusive products, and most of all, a member community.

Umai+ has built the program with a strategy to create strong emotional connections with its members, enabling them to be a part of a community of like-minded people, who receive exclusive perks from the brand.

Umai+ is priced at $99 annually. This annual billing cycle ensures long-term revenue and customer value.

Umai+ Shopify membership program features and takeaways

1. Offers a discount on all purchases for members

While most brands offer 5 to 10% discount to its members on all purchases, Umai+ makes discounts attractive by offering a substantial discount of 20%.

This high discount helps the brand to motivate members to make more purchases, makes the steady sales revenue flow a sustainability strategy for the business, and generates more engagement opportunities for the brand.

Moreover, the high discount nullifies the membership fee over a period. Members save much more than what they paid for the membership fee. With this strategy, the brand provides immediate satisfaction as customers get returns after making a few purchases.

Key takeaways:

  • Offer a significant amount of discount
  • Makes customers feel satisfied with the savings
  • Focus on your membership pricing and discounts strategy
  • Continuously optimize your pricing and discount strategy
  • Create dynamic pricing for membership models

2. Offers early access to new collections

When customers are made to feel special, their loyalty to brands increases. Moreover, this feeling of exclusivity enhances their experience. Members may even become brand ambassadors, referring new potential members and spreading a good word about the brand.

For clothing brands, an exclusive eCommerce membership perk is to offer early access to new collections. It can be an ongoing strategy. As fashion trends keep changing with seasons, clothing brands have an advantage of launching new collections, and maintaining excitement for their customers.

Umai+ members get exclusive early access to the new collections and limited-edition products. This brings a sense of privilege and insider status for its members. It also adds a feeling of urgency around the new products.

Key takeaways:

  • Make members feel exclusive and special consistently
  • Generate excitement by creating exclusive offers
  • Build a sense of urgency through these strategies to increase sales
  • Create early-access campaigns for members

3. Offers member-only products

To make their Umai+ members feel special, Umai clothing offers them limited-edition and members-only products. The brand ensures that customers outside of the membership program do not have access to these products.

This brings a heightened sense of exclusivity as well as becomes a key differentiating factor. The member-only products strategy adds FOMO by creating collectible items. It gives a sense of adding unique value that can’t be purchased elsewhere.

Key takeaways:

  • Offer limited-edition products making them more exclusive and desirable
  • Create a buzz about member-only products on social media, this will help attract more potential members
  • Offer personalized membership benefits exclusive to members

4. Offers free shipping

One of the biggest causes for cart abandonment is shipping costs. Customers tend to reverse purchase decisions when there are shipping costs involved. Umai+ members get free shipping on all orders. This reduces a significant amount of cost and encourages frequent purchases. It can also drive more impulse purchases.

Key takeaways:

  • Offer free shipping on all orders
  • Offer same-day shipping if possible
  • Ensure you partner with a premium logistics partner for your Shopify membership program to ensure a smooth experience

5. Offers dedicated customer support

With membership programs, customers engage with brands for a long-term, and hence they expect efficient customer support as they are special customers. By offering top notch customer support that is helpful, prompt, and seamless, brands can enhance brand perception.

Umai+ members receive a VIP experience when they reach out to the customer support. The brand wants to build stronger relationships with customers by providing personalized attention. By addressing their specific concerns individually, the brand ensures customer satisfaction.

Key takeaways:

  • Consider member support to be a key part of your Shopify membership program
  • Enable various communication channels for customer support
  • Create AI-driven member engagement by automating customer support using AI chatbots; train AI to know when to transfer chat to a human agent
  • Ensure a two-way conversation on all channels as a form of personalized membership benefit

6. Generates predictable revenue through membership fee

Umai Clothing’s Shopify membership program provides the brand with revenue through the monthly or annual fee. This predictable revenue improves cash flow, reduces dependence on fluctuating sales, and enables better financial forecasting.

Many brands prefer to offer memberships for free in order to increase sign ups. However, Umai+ does not hesitate to charge members. Members can pay monthly or annually. This ensures only serious customers sign up for their membership plan.

Key takeaways:

  • A membership fee ensures only serious customers sign up
  • Offer different tiers of memberships to cater to more customers
  • Billing annually can help reduce administrative costs and ensure predictable revenue

7. An FAQs section for clarity

The Umai+ membership page has an FAQs section that answers basic questions about the membership. Customers looking to sign up can easily go to the FAQs section to gather information and details about the membership program.

This section answers questions such as, how the store credit system works, how to cancel the membership, and how to become a member of Umai’s Shopify membership program, among others.

Key takeaways:

  • Make it easy for customers to find information
  • Add all important questions and answers in the FAQs section
  • Provide an option for customers to contact you if they have more questions

8. Data and insights from Shopify membership program

Umai Clothing uses Appstle Membership App for its membership program. The brand collects and analyzes data from the program to enhance customer loyalty and retention. Using AI for membership retention has many benefits.

Data and analytics help brands understand members preference and needs better and provide tailored and personalized recommendations and offers. AI retention systems in-built in Shopify apps help reduce churn by automating churn management.

Key takeaways:

  • Use a Shopify membership app that has AI capabilities
  • Set up automated AI systems to reduce churn
  • Ensure continued engagement with customers via automated marketing features
  • Offer personalized incentives and offers to encourage repeat purchases

9. Comprehensive checkout page

To become Umai+ members, customers simply need to add the membership to their shopping carts, make the payment and complete the process.

The brand shares multiple product recommendations on the checkout page. Adding the recommended products and merchandise is easy. Customers can simply add to cart and complete the checkout process.

Key takeaways:

  • Create an easy checkout process
  • Display recommendations, discount options, etc.
  • Offer multiple payment options

Key learnings from Umai+ Shopify membership program

Umai Clothing’s membership program offers many lessons that can be applied to not only fashion and clothing memberships, but other industries as well. Here are the key learnings you can apply to your membership strategies.

1. Have a strong value proposition

When planning your membership perks and benefits, ensure you have a mix of discounts, experiences, savings, and more. If you have a membership fee, balance it well with valuable benefits by offering exclusive eCommerce membership perks.

2. Ensure a strong ROI for members

Your Shopify membership program members should see tangible savings and monetary benefits out of their engagement with your membership program. Combine monetary and experiential benefits.

3. Keep the membership structure simple

Umai+ has a single membership tier. If you want to have multiple tiers, ensure it is simple, and customers do not get confused or face decision fatigue, even if there is dynamic pricing for memberships. Ensure you have an efficient Shopify membership app to help you manage a multi-tiered membership model.

4. Prioritize exclusivity

Umai+ members enjoy members-only products, early access to new collections, special customer support, and a community feel that makes them feel special and builds loyalty. Ensure you offer VIP treatment and experiences to your Shopify members.

5. Leverage AI and automation

In today’s fast-paced and highly competitive eCommerce space, AI-driven member engagement is a must. Utilize AI, automation, data and analytics. Create personalized experiences, reduce your administrative costs, and manage your membership program efficiently with the help of new and advanced technology.

6. Clear communication

Use features such as FAQs, chatbots, easy communication access, multiple communication channels, engagement campaigns and more for consistent communication. Moreover, ensure there’s clarity in communication.

How to set up an efficient and profitable Shopify membership program?

While you may have big ambitions and great ideas for your Shopify membership program, if you do not set it up well and if you do not manage it well, you might struggle to keep it afloat.

To efficiently and seamlessly manage your membership program, you will need to partner with a Shopify membership app that provides comprehensive features for marketing, customer management, communication, automation, easy integrations, etc.

items.html:
The skincare and beauty industry is booming. New brands are coming up and every brand is trying hard to attract and retain customers.

One marketing strategy that is effective is subscriptions. Beauty and skin subscriptions are on the rise.

In this blog, we look at the Skin Authority Shopify subscription strategy for its program called Facial Club. You’ll learn lessons and takeaways that you can apply in your Shopify subscriptions.

What is the Facial Club subscription?

Skin Authority is a brand that is passionate about skin health. The brand creates science-backed skin care products and treatments. The brand has a subscription program called Facial Club. This Shopify brand has aced its subscription program by making it truly unique.

The Facial Club is a premium subscription program that offers high-quality products, treatment, and skincare solutions to its subscribers. The subscription billed annually carries a premium price tag and a considerable discount for its subscribers.

An in-depth look at this Shopify subscription strategy reveals that the Facial Club is not just any subscription plan offering just discounts and free delivery, the brand takes its value proposition seriously. From customized skincare kits that change every season to at-home services, it offers much more than meets the eye.

Skin Authority Shopify subscription strategy breakdown and lessons

While 80% of brands offer some sort of subscription or membership program, only a few are able to sustain and really engage their subscribers. Most customers tend to disengage within a few months and leave. But here’s how Skin Authority has made Facial Club subscription program stand out from the crowd.

1. Dedicated section on the website

The way a brand presents its eCommerce subscription model can heavily influence the way customers perceive the program. And of course, the subscription program’s success.

Skin Authority has a dedicated page for Facial Club subscription, on their website. This page is useful and informative, giving all the important details about the subscription program. Customers who want to understand the program can simply go to this page and look for any information.

This clear organization of information communicates the subscription program’s importance and makes it easy for potential subscribers to find detailed information without digging through the site.

The page details out:

  • How the Skin Authority Shopify subscription program works
  • The benefits and perks subscribers can avail
  • FAQs that answer basic questions
  • Testimonials by subscribers
  • Details about pricing

2. Multiple benefits and perks

Another key factor of Shopify subscription strategy is the benefits or perks they offer. Why should customers become members? What value is the brand offering? Skin Authority details out the benefits and perks of its Facial Club Shopify subscription program.

  • High-quality products in personalized kits: Subscribers receive curated skincare products and kits that are delivered three times a year. Every delivery kit is valued at $498 and includes premium products that are tailored to address specific skin concerns and goals of the subscribers.
  • Professional skincare treatment: Apart from products, subscribers also receive professional treatments for skin or at-home skin care treatment kits. This can be availed three times a year and each treatment is valued at $125.
  • Personalized skin care coaching: Skin Authority Shopify subscription strategy offers personalized skin coaching sessions to subscribers. Each session is valued at $75. Skin care experts evaluate subscribers’ skin conditions and offer personalized advice and guidance.
  • Exclusive discounts: Subscribers of the Facial Club get a 15% discount on every purchase they make. This also applies to individual purchases they make outside of the subscriptions, improving sales for the brand. This ensures Shopify recurring revenue.
  • Birthday rewards: The Facial Club members get special treatment on their birthday with birthday rewards. This helps the brand strengthen emotional connection with the subscribers.

3. It works in an easy and straightforward way

Skin Authority has a straightforward approach for its subscription model. And believe it or not, but keeping things simple is a Shopify subscription strategy you must consider. The Facial Club provides a user-friendly experience with a simple and functional format. Even though the brand offers a comprehensive list of benefits, perks, and curated subscription boxes, it has set up clear instructions and expectations. Simplicity minus confusion and uncertainty for subscribers makes it easy for new and old customers to make purchases.

4. Subscription kits are curated to customers’ needs

A one-size-fits-all approach doesn’t work with subscriptions, and especially if the products are skincare and beauty. These products have to be used based on skin types, conditions, and goals. An effective subscription retention tactic is to offer personalized and customized subscription boxes.

The Facial Club subscription kits are curated to match each individual subscriber’s specific skincare needs and concerns. Moreover, each subscription kit is different from the other, carefully curated by the skin coaches based on individual subscribers’ needs. This enhances the subscription’s perceived value. This can be done with the help of AI in subscription management.

5. Clear pricing structure

Another critical Shopify subscription strategy is pricing. The price of this premium subscription offers significant savings to subscribers. The annual subscription membership costs $1,199 compared to the total value of products and services it offers, which are worth $2,500.

Skin Authority Shopify subscription program has an annual billing cycle, ensuring Shopify recurring revenue. By doing so, the brand ensures longevity and a longer commitment by customers, as well as it is able to offer them significant discounts. An annual billing cycle also helps reduce administrative costs for brands.

6. Social proof and trust

Social proof influences 90% of consumers. By displaying social proof on eCommerce websites, brands can impact consumers’ perception of their brand, increase sales, build trust, and confidence.

Skin Authority Shopify subscription strategy leverages customer testimonials by featuring videos of customers sharing their experiences. By sharing these authentic stories with customers’ faces and videos, the brand builds customer trust and confidence, leading to subscription sign-up decisions for many.

Moreover, Skin Authority highlights the fact that their skincare solutions are science-based and have professional experts working with subscribers to recommend the most-suited treatments to them. This also helps build trust and credibility for the brand.

7. The brand offers a community experience

Whether it’s the exclusive discounts and benefits or the personalized treatment approach, Skin Authority offers a community experience to its subscribers. They feel a sense of belonging to an exclusive community, which is a proven subscription retention tactic.

The Facial Club has an educational element provided by the coaching sessions with skin experts. These educational sessions and personalized curated kits make subscribers part of an exclusive community, and improve brand loyalty.

8. Clear and prompt communication

Skin Authority customers pay a premium price for the subscriptions. And the brand ensures seamless communication. The website has an FAQs page that answers basic subscriber questions. Alongside, the website also offers a live chat option – an excellent way to use AI in subscription management.

9. Seasonality and convenience factors

The Facial Club subscription emphasizes bringing professional-quality skin care experiences into the subscribers’ homes. This is an appealing strategy to busy consumers who value convenience without sacrificing quality.

Moreover, the delivery schedule of the subscription kits is every four months, which allows the brand to adapt products and treatments to seasonal skincare needs, providing relevant solutions throughout the year. This adds convenience and relevance to subscribers’ experience of the program.

5 key takeaways from Skin Authority Shopify subscription strategy

There are lots of lessons we can learn from Skin Authority’s Shopify subscription strategy. We’ve shared nine of the strategies we thought are effective and worth adapting for Shopify stores. And here, we have narrowed down five takeaways from its subscription strategy.

1. Offer value to your subscribers

The Facial Club subscription offers value beyond the typical perks that other subscription brands offer. For instance, most subscription models stop at discounts, quick delivery, and a few surprise gifts.

But Skin Authority Shopify subscription program offers much more that is exclusive to the brand. For instance, one-on-one skincare treatment coaching with experts, personalized skin care kits that change with seasonal changes, and at-home sessions.

2. Create exclusivity

By creating experiences and benefits only for your subscription members, you will be able to position your subscription experience as something unique and truly exclusive. Today’s customers want to feel special and exclusive. Build exclusivity into your Shopify subscription strategy by offering them unique experiences. This way you can also build an exclusive community for subscribers. This can help increase customer loyalty and increase the customer lifetime value.

3. Provide transparency

Just the way The Facial Club page clearly communicates with its customers about the premium pricing structure, the amount paid and saved, and other details, by ensuring transparency, you can build trust with subscribers. Trust and confidence are key to retaining customers and growing your customer base. Happy and satisfied customers often become your brand advocates, bringing in more potential customers to your brand.

4. Personalization is key

Whether you’re looking to build a skincare and beauty subscription, a food subscription, or an entertainment membership model, focusing on personalization is a must. There are at least five different generations of consumers you are catering to, and hence, their needs and preferences are going to be different. Personalization is the only way to keep all customers satisfied.

5. Bridge online and offline experiences

Even though online shopping is taking over in-store experiences, creating hybrid experiences that combine the two can truly enhance your subscription business. Including phygital experiences in your Shopify subscription strategy can help expand your customer base, increase sales and revenue, and increase the perceived value of your Shopify subscription program.

items.html:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is everywhere! AI-generated text, images, videos, AI-driven discounts offered by eCommerce stores, and data collected via AI. AI is omnipresent and it’s only getting more advanced.

Businesses are using AI tools and capabilities to improve their work, output, and performance. And why not! AI makes work faster, ensures more consistency, and accuracy.

So, have you wondered how you could use AI for Shopify subscriptions? This blog delves into the many ways AI can help subscription businesses work smarter and better.

Read on!

Customer-facing AI applications

There are multiple things AI can help you with. For instance, it can help you with customer-facing activities, and with processes that enhance your business operations. Let’s begin by exploring the ways in which you can use AI for customer-facing processes for your Shopify subscriptions business.

1. Personalized recommendations

71% of consumers expect brands to offer personalized experiences. But you might think personalization is not possible in subscriptions. Think about personalized product recommendations.

For instance, whether you offer fixed subscription boxes or curated boxes, you could share product recommendations with your subscribers. Here’s how AI-powered subscription management can make personalization easier for you:

  • Gather data about subscribers past purchases and browsing activities
  • Collect information about customers personal preferences
  • Know your customers better by simple details such as their gender, age, location, profession, spending capacity, etc.

The above information can help you come up with recommendations that match your customers personality and preference. And AI applications are the best way to know what products you must recommend to which customer segment.

2. AI-powered dynamic pricing and discounts

Discounts and pricing are among the key factors that influence customers’ purchase decisions. However, customers’ spending capacity and budgets vary. For instance, one customer segment may be more likely to buy a product at a lower price only, while another segment is willing to pay a higher price for the same product.

You can use AI to analyze these and other customer behaviors related to pricing and discounts, to increase sales. Let’s look at some ways to do so:

  • Collect data on customer behaviors and to segment customer groups
  • Predict when customers might cancel or leave a subscription, offer real-time discounts to retain the customers
  • Offer trial periods to leads that are hard to convince
  • Create offers and incentives, such as limited-period discounts
  • Gauge how much customers are willing to stretch based on their past purchase patterns and offer relevant pricing and deals

Example:

3. Automated customer support

86% of customers are willing to switch brands because another brand provides better customer support. With extreme competition between subscription businesses, you don’t want to lose customers to your competitors. To retain subscribers, ensure efficient customer support. Put AI on the job. Here’s how to use AI for Shopify subscribers support:

  • Automate customers support via chatbots
  • Integrate AI-driven assistants to handle common customer queries
  • Automate churn management, payment failure or billing issues, etc.
  • Use AI to enable customers to modify subscription plants, pause subscriptions, etc.

4. Automate churn prevention

Today, it’s easy for customers to leave one brand and immediately go to the next one, because customers are spoilt for choice. This makes it critical for your Shopify brand to integrate predictive analytics for subscriptions — identify at-risk subscribers beforehand and reduce churn.

Here’s how you can use AI for churn reduction:

  • Automate retention and churn management strategies with AI
  • Identify subscribes that show signs of fatigue and disengagement
  • Automate discounts and pricing strategies to retain these subscribers
  • Offer real-time discounts and incentives
  • Offer free gifts, free trials of new products, and exclusive incentives
  • Automate feedback forms and email communication to retain these customers

5. AI-optimized emails and SMS campaigns

80% of customers say the experience provided by brands is as important as their products or services. And just like how communication between two individuals creates an impression, the way brands communicate with customers influences how customers engage and feel about brands.

This is where communication via emails, SMS, and other campaigns comes in. And AI can play an important role in it.

  • Use AI for Shopify subscriptions to create personalized messages
  • Automate relevant messages for renewals, discounts, upselling, etc.
  • Create targeted campaigns based on your Shopify business goals by automating email, SMS, and social messenger campaigns

6. AI-driven fraud detection and prevention

Subscription fraud is on the rise; reports show it costs brands more than $2 billion each year. Online fraud and security is one of the biggest reasons that keeps customers away from transacting with brands. But with AI, you can keep your customers protected. Here’s how:

  • Choose a Shopify subscription app that has in-built AI fraud detection features
  • Automate AI fraud detection, for instance, your tool will detect suspicious subscription transactions
  • Use AI for real-time data tracking, proactive customer engagement, track unusual patterns, etc.

7. AI-generated product content

Another way to use AI for Shopify subscriptions is to generate content for subscriptions. AI-generated content can help brands enhance marketing and promotional campaigns. Here’s how you can use AI for generating content for your Shopify subscription business:

  • Generate AI-based text content, including product descriptions
  • Create AI-based images and videos for your subscription marketing
  • Automate product updates and details with the help of AI

Example:

Source

Business-oriented AI applications

Smart businesses know how to use the efficiency and capabilities of AI to make their business processes faster, more accurate, efficient, and cost-efficient. Now let’s explore the business-oriented use cases of AI for Shopify subscription businesses.

1. AI-powered subscription management

Managing a subscription model involves several activities. For example, managing subscriber onboarding, modifying plans, upgrading and updating subscriptions, managing cancellations, sending renewal reminders, and more. For this, you need a comprehensive subscription management system.

It is not practical to perform and manage these tasks manually. That’s where AI can help automate and manage subscriptions easily. Here’s how you can use AI for Shopify subscriptions.

  • Automate modification of subscription plan
  • Upgrade and update subscriptions
  • Cancellation management
  • Renewal reminders and notifications
  • Automate subscription inventory management
  • Automate billing and invoicing

2. Billing and payments optimization

With the recurring-billing nature of subscriptions, AI can make processes much faster and more efficient. Moreover, AI can ensure higher accuracy and reduced errors. Here’s how you can use AI-driven recurring billing for subscriptions:

  • Automate billing cycles
  • Manage revenue tracking
  • Manage multiple pricing tiers and usage-based billing
  • Handle dynamic pricing and discounts
  • Automate dunning for overdue payments

3. Inventory and fulfillment forecasting

An important element in subscription models is to ensure the right balance in your inventory. Overstocking could lead to unnecessary financial stress, and understocking will lead to failure in delivering orders. That’s why it’s critical to manage inventory efficiently. Here’s how to do it with AI:

  • Use AI to collect data, predict inventory requirements
  • Ensure you have stock levels to fulfill orders
  • Manage pricing and discounts based on inventory levels
  • Automate subscription delivery fulfillment tasks
  • Automate updates based on deliveries and orders

4. AI-powered data and analytics

Getting a better understanding of customers can drive more engagement, sales, and profits. But to manually gather information from and about customers can be a daunting task, especially for high-scale businesses. This is where AI’s efficiency in collecting and analyzing data comes in.

Here’s how you can use AI-powered subscription management for your Shopify business:

  • Generate data to help you understand customers better
  • Understand which actions will drive most value over time and increase customer lifetime value (CLV)
  • Generate AI-driven offers and incentives to increase customer loyalty and retention

5. Automate A/B testing for subscriptions

Like every business, subscription businesses also may need to experiment and run tests. For instance, your pricing model may not work for all tiers and so, you may have to tweak it. However, manual testing and experimentation may not be the best method. But you can definitely use AI for this. Here’s how:

  • Use AI to run experiments to assess pricing models
  • Try out different retention strategies using AI
  • Run automated communication campaigns for marketing
  • Assess what works and what doesn’t using AI’s data and analytics
  • Create different types of subscription boxes to understand which ones work best

6. AI-based logistics operations

Logistics is a key component of subscription businesses. It is critical to ensure that subscription deliveries reach on time, as well as in good condition. The success of subscription businesses is based on products as well as the overall experience, which includes subscription delivery and logistics.

Here’s how you can use AI for Shopify subscription logistics operations:

  • Use AI to manage logistics operations
  • Automate shipping and delivery updates and notifications
  • Use AI to predict delivery delays
  • Automate communication regarding deliveries
  • Integrate logistics in your subscription system for seamless operations

7. AI-based fraud and risk management

Subscription fraud can cause losses and derail businesses. It can also harm brand reputation. Hence, it is critical to keep fraud at bay and incorporate risk management systems into your subscription set-up. And this is where AI-powered subscription management can help.

  • Use AI to detect patterns of fraudulent sign-ups
  • Identify duplicate accounts with the use of AI
  • Detect payment fraud with predictive analytics
  • Identify suspicious behavior to stop fraud from occurring

Are you ready to integrate AI for Shopify subscriptions for your business?

AI has proven to be a game changer for subscription businesses. It can help you run subscription models more efficiently, leading to more sales. Not only can you use AI for customer-facing marketing processes, AI can be equally helpful for running and managing big and small tasks for your business.

If you’re looking for a Shopify subscription app that has integrated AI capabilities and features, explore Appstle Subscriptions. The app offers intuitive AI capabilities that can manage all your processes efficiently, allowing you to focus on more strategic parts of your subscription model.

items.html:
With rising competition in the market, brands are exploring various direct-to-consumer (DTC) marketing strategies. One such strategy is product bundling.

Brands across industries are experimenting with bundles, whether it is food or fashion.

In this blog, we explore the fashion brand pricing strategy of ASOS, what your brand can learn from it, tips, and best practices to ace your bundling strategy.

Let’s get started!

What is product bundling?

Product bundling is a marketing strategy in which many products are sold as one bundle. For example, a set of 5 t-shirts is a bundle, or a bundle of skin care products.

Product bundling increases the average order value (AOV) for brands and offers discounted prices to customers. Many different types of bundles are possible, depending on the product type and industry.

In the fashion industry, bundles such as sets of t-shirts, sets of socks, winter wear bundles, and accessories bundles are common. Bundling is an effective fashion brand pricing strategy that has many benefits for the business, such as, increasing the average order value (AOV), increasing sales, enhancing customer experience, and more.

Product bundle strategy breakdown of ASOS

ASOS is a fashion brand that caters to men and women’s fashion, clothing, accessories, footwear, and more. The brand houses multiple brands under one umbrella. A quick search for the words, ‘Bundle’, ‘Pack’, and ‘Set’, will bring up hundreds and thousands of options, ranging from cosmetics, clothing, and accessories.

In this section, we breakdown the brand’s bundling strategy and key takeaways that you could apply to your Shopify store.

1. Easy to find bundles

ASOS does not have a dedicated page for bundles. Perhaps that is because of the nature of the brand – it houses various brands under one roof and hence, bundling multiple brands together is not as easy as bundling products of the same brand.

However, this doesn’t deter the brand from offering bundles. The bundles are easy to find with the search tab. Words such as pack, set, multi, and bundle bring up all the bundle options.

This approach offers flexibility of choosing a single product or a pack. With this approach, the brand is able to create more excitement and increases AOV with bundles.

Tips and best practices:

  • Create various types of bundles
  • Make bundles prominent on your product pages
  • Make it easy for customers to find bundles

2. Bundles in different product categories

ASOS offers bundles in various categories, for instance, clothing, undergarments, accessories, cosmetics, and more. Items in these bundles can be purchased separately but are more appealing and cost lesser when bought together.

This approach not only enhances customer experience, it also simplifies customers’ shopping process. Brands that use this approach can increase the AOV, manage the inventory better, upsell, and create excitement for their customers.

Tips and best practices:

  • Create bundles across various product categories, for example, sustainable fashion bundles
  • Create mix and match product bundles
  • Bundle products for upselling and cross-selling

3. Fixed bundling

Certain products are best offered as fixed bundles, meaning, the products in the bundle are predetermined and cannot be changed.

One such example we found interesting on ASOS is the camera bundle. The bundle includes a camera, a case, and films.

The brand offers a discount on the bundle, however, increases AOV with these types of bundles. Fixed bundles also help manage inventory better, offer predictable pricing, and marketing opportunities

Tips and best practices:

  • Identify products suitable for fixed bundles
  • Determine a pricing strategy
  • Monitor and review the bundle performance
  • Promote the bundle to increase sales

4. Product recommendations with bundles

Another approach that is effective in increasing the AOV is product recommendations along with bundles. When a website offers thousands of products, it can get daunting for customers to go through everything.

That’s where strategies such as recommendations help customers discover more products. And this way, brands can introduce lesser-known or slow-selling items to customers.

For example, ASOS shares product recommendations in the product bundle pages — a pack of t-shirts can also be bought with a track pant — upselling and cross-selling.

Tips and best practices:

  • Upsell by suggesting product recommendations
  • Offer recommendations that add value to customers
  • Personalized product recommendations

5. Create FOMO and urgency around bundles

60% of consumers make impulse purchases after experiencing FOMO. Urgency and FOMO help brands increase sales. ASOS adds these tactics on its bundles.

For bundles, FOMO and urgency can be created in many ways. For example, by creating limited-period bundles, limited-edition bundles, seasonal bundles, etc. With this approach, you can not only increase AOV, but also increase the speed at which products get sold.

This tactic can be easily automated, so that as soon as products start getting sold-out, the product page automatically gets updated with a ‘Selling out fast’ sign. For instance, Appstle Bundles & Discounts can help with automation.

Tips and best practices:

  • Create limited edition bundles
  • Offer exclusive offers on bundles
  • Show scarcity or fast-selling out signs
  • Offer limited time free shipping on sets
  • Automate FOMO and urgency via your Shopify bundle app

6. ASOS keeps bundles simple

ASOS bundles and multi-packs are easy for customers to pick and choose from, because they are simple. Today, customers have multiple choices across brands and websites. And so, if you complicate their decision making, it may lead to your loss.

ASOS has created simple bundles and packs, minus any complication. For instance, the brand has a pack of 3, 5, or 7 pairs of socks. So customers can simply pick an option based on their needs.

Tips and best practices:

  • Simplify things that are complicated on your eCommerce website
  • From navigation to search to bundle options, make every experience simple
  • Write a clear description and details of each bundle to avoid confusion

7. Multiple types of bundles of the same product

Another bundling strategy that ASOS uses is to create multiple variations of bundles of the same product. For example, t-shirts of brand x available in a pack of 10, 7, 5, and 3. This offers more choices to customers, as they can pick a bundle based on their budget, needs, and preferences.

For the brand, this means more revenue and upselling opportunities. The strategy works for both. ASOS applies this strategy on mens and womens clothing and accessories. By creating these bundles, the brand differentiates itself from other brands and offers value-added purchase opportunities.

Tips and best practices:

  • Offer something for everyone
  • Offer what your customers want, for example, sustainable fashion bundles

8. ASOS offers starter bundles

ASOS smartly offers different types of bundles based on the products they offer. For instance, multi-packs of socks and t-shirts, and starter packs for cosmetics and wellness products.

For example, the brand offers a dental care starter pack. Most customers hesitate to try new products for their dental health. So, ASOS made it easy for customers to try the products with a starter bundle – an effective strategy for direct-to-consumer (DTC) marketing.

Tips and best practices:

  • Create bundles based on your products, not based on what other brands are doing
  • Keep the customers’ needs in mind when planning your bundles

Ready to start your fashion brand pricing strategy with bundles?

If you are a fashion brand, there are many ways to create and offer bundles to your customers. We have given you many ideas and tips on what all you could do with your fashion product bundles. And even if you aren’t a fashion brand, you could still try out bundling as a marketing strategy for your business.

items.excerpt: The eCommerce market is becoming more vibrant than ever. Brands are experimenting with multiple revenue generation models. For instance, subscription models, to bring in recurring revenue. But which model is better – one-time purchases vs. subscription? While many merchants debate that one-time purchases are better, subscription models have proven to offer more benefits to businesses.…
items.html:
The eCommerce market is becoming more vibrant than ever. Brands are experimenting with multiple revenue generation models. For instance, subscription models, to bring in recurring revenue.

But which model is better – one-time purchases vs. subscription? While many merchants debate that one-time purchases are better, subscription models have proven to offer more benefits to businesses.

One of the biggest plus points of subscriptions is the lower cost of customer acquisition. A Shopify report shows that in one-time purchase, the customer acquisition cost per customer may be anywhere between $20 to $400.

That’s a high price to pay for customers if they are only going to make a single purchase from your Shopify store. Isn’t it?

May, a better alternative would be subscription business models.

In this blog, we take a look at one-time purchases vs. subscriptions, the pros and cons of both, and which payment model is better for eCommerce stores.

Let’s get started!

What is a subscription pricing model?

A subscription pricing model is a recurring billing. Once a customer signs up to a subscription, the billing cycle repeats at a predefined interval. For example, Netflix, SaaS and AI products, such as ChatGpt, and grocery subscriptions work on this recurring pricing model.

Source

What is a one-time purchase?

A one-time purchase is when a customer makes a purchase and pays for that product. For instance, say you purchase groceries every other day and make payment for that on the spot.

Both these payment options have benefits and downsides. So, what is better: one-time purchases vs. subscriptions? Let’s find out by learning about the pros and cons of both.

Pros and cons of subscriptions

While many might argue that one-time purchases are better than subscriptions, this model offers many benefits that one cannot be overlooked. Let’s look at the pros and cons of subscriptions.

Let’s begin by learning some statistics around subscription purchases:

  • Between 80 and 90% of consumers prefer subscriptions when it comes to purchasing products and services in health & fitness, utility & productivity, photo & video, and education.
  • Approximately 75% of all direct-to-consumer businesses offer subscriptions.

Pros

1. Predictable income

Ecommerce brands can have a predictable income stream with subscriptions. As businesses know the number of subscriptions, and the revenue-generation dates. This also makes it easy for businesses to calculate customer lifetime value, plan business finances, and manage the balance sheet and expenses. These are some recurring revenue benefits associated with subscription models.

2. Cross-selling opportunities

As subscribers are associated with brands for a long period, it’s easier for brands to understand them and their preferences better. Over time, brands can recommend products that subscribers would want and appreciate. For example, upsell and cross-sell items based on subscribers’ shopping history.

3. Increase conversion rate

Subscriptions do not involve one-time large payments. Instead, the payments are broken down into small payments at regular intervals. This eases customers’ payment load. And so, it increases conversion rate for subscription businesses. The convenience and ease of small, regular payments makes it easy on subscribers.

For example, imagine if Netflix made it mandatory to pay the annual fee in one go, the platform may see subscriber numbers dwindling. One of the benefits of subscription payments is how it affects and helps with eCommerce profitability analysis.

4. Convenient for subscribers

One of the biggest benefits of subscriptions is the convenience factor. Instead of making repeated purchases multiple times, they can subscribe once, receive their subscription boxes on predefined dates, and their payments can be automated.

Subscribers do not need to get into the hassle of making repeated purchases every time. For brands, too, subscriptions bring convenience in the form of predictability, and better management and planning.

5. Improved customer retention

As customers get into a long term association with brands, brands get more opportunities to engage with customers. It also gives brands the opportunity to improve customer experience and increase loyalty. This leads to improved customer retention.

Moreover, brands can increase retention by various strategies, such as, offer more benefits, incentives, and discounts to retain customers. Subscription apps with churn management features also help retain customers.

6. Minimal manual tasks

Ecommerce subscription businesses automate a lot of their tasks via subscription apps. For instance, a lot of repetitive tasks such as billing, invoicing, payments, and discounts, are automated. Unlike one-time purchases, where every transaction is different, which may require manual intervention, subscriptions involve minimal manual tasks.

7. Reduces customer acquisition cost

Another recurring revenue benefit is the reduction of customer acquisition cost. With subscriptions, businesses do not have to spend on acquiring new customers as frequently. Subscribers engage with brands for a long duration via subscriptions. When subscription businesses acquire customers, they tend to stay for longer periods compared to one-time purchases. Hence, this affects the cost of customer acquisition.

8. Increase customer lifetime value (CLV)

Compared to one-time purchases, subscriptions help increase customer lifetime value (CLV). According to Gartner, it is essential to calculate CLV to drive customer retention. Subscribers associate with brands for a long period, ensuring they give revenue to the business from time to time.

Also, with subscriptions, businesses can increase the average order value with strategies, such as cross-selling and upselling. Some subscription businesses charge annual fees, which means subscribers get locked in for a year, ensuring a certain amount of revenue from subscribers. All these factors increase customer lifetime value.

Here’s an infographic that helps understand eCommerce profitability analysis on the basis of CLV:

Source

Cons

While there are many benefits of subscription models, there are some drawbacks as well. However, the benefits outnumber the drawbacks. Here are some cons of subscriptions.

1. Customer churn

With so many subscription options floating around in the market, it is hard for customers to keep up and use all their subscriptions effectively. Subscription fatigue leads to high churn.

Moreover, if customers do not see value or aren’t kept engaged in the subscription, they may lose interest and eventually leave or simply not renew. This can cause a high churn rate in subscriptions.

2. Need for continuous improvement

It is hard to keep subscribers engaged and loyal for a long time. Once the novelty of your subscription program wears out, subscribers may start dropping out. However, you can avoid this situation by ensuring you continuously improve your subscription offerings and experience. This may require resources, time, and effort.

Pros and cons of one-time purchases

One-time purchase or payment model is not a recurring revenue model. Here, businesses can generate instant revenue, but may incur high customer acquisition costs. In this section, we will look at the benefits and downsides of one-time purchases.

Let’s begin by learning some statistics around one-time purchases:

  • Between 30 and 70% of consumers prefer a one-time purchase and payment method when buying entertainment, sports, social media, and books.
  • Data from one-time purchases can provide valuable insights with proper analysis. These insights can be utilized for future marketing.

Pros

1. Immediate revenue

When customers make one-time purchases, they pay for it up front. This brings immediate revenue for the business. Unlike subscriptions where businesses generate revenue at intervals, one-time purchases bring instant cash into businesses. This makes it easy for businesses to plan and manage their balance sheet.

2. Reduced churn

Customers can make one-time purchases whenever they like. They are not bound by anything, such as in subscriptions. Moreover, subscription fatigue is common, given the number of subscriptions in the market. This gives customers more flexibility and they tend to return to your store when they want to purchase. However, this could mean they might return after a long duration.

Cons

1. Less predictability

With one-time purchases, there is less predictability because those customers may or may not return to your Shopify store. Thus, you may not have the security of recurring revenue benefits.

2. Low conversion rates

Customers have multiple options to choose any given product. Besides, there are multiple online stores to make purchases from. For instance, a quick search for a black diary will bring up many options. In such a situation, it’s difficult to attract customers to your site. You may require a lot of resources, leading to high customer acquisition costs.

3. Low long-term profitability

With one-time purchases, customers make one purchase. Their return to make more purchases may not be guaranteed. You may not be able to calculate customer lifetime value (CLV).

Let’s understand this with an example. Imagine if a business spent $20 in acquiring this customer. The customer made a single purchase of $22. The actual profit via this sale is just $2. If the customer never comes back to your store, your profits from this spend are quite low.

One-time purchases vs. subscription: what is better for your Shopify store?

With more than 75% of businesses offering subscription models, it is definitely worth a try for your Shopify business to try the benefits of this recurring revenue method.

From long-term profitability, high customer lifetime value to predictability, subscription businesses have many benefits. As the cost of marketing keeps rising, so does the cost of customer acquisition.

To ensure you lower your customer acquisition costs, subscription models are more advisable for businesses. However, to run your subscriptions smoothly, you will require a robust Shopify subscriptions app.

items.html:
As competition increases and marketing budgets get tighter, it has become critical that brands are able to persuade and influence customers into taking desirable actions. This applies to eCommerce subscriptions as well.

It is essential to map consumer behavior in subscriptions and thoughtfully build marketing strategies, if brands want to stay competitive.

Integrating psychology into your subscription marketing strategies can increase effectiveness in various ways.

In this blog, we look at 8 psychological concepts that can be integrated into your subscription marketing strategies, to drive success.

8 psychological concepts for subscription marketing strategies

Today, most marketers spend more time on understanding why and how their customers behave and take actions. Marketing is a lot about influencing, persuading, and driving desired actions by customers.

For subscription businesses, too, it is important to focus on customer behavioral science and psychology. In this section, we discuss 8 such psychological concepts that help influence subscribers and drive habit formation in eCommerce.

1. Commitment bias

Typically, subscriptions are for a long duration. When customers sign up, they know they’re getting into a long-term association. So, when customers sign up for subscriptions, they prefer to stay consistent with their decision. Their initial decision has a psychological effect.

Ecommerce brands can play with this commitment bias when planning their subscription models. For instance, unless there’s a major problem, customers would tend to continue with their subscriptions.

Brands can utilize this commitment bias in their favor by doing the following and influence consumer behavior in subscriptions:

  • Encourage customers to sign up for subscriptions
  • Offer the flexibility to unsubscribe at any point, making their decision to join easy
  • Offer a free trial of the subscription plan, encouraging them to subscriber
  • Offer discount on the first month’s subscription fee
  • Offer unique incentives to subscribe
  • Promise valuable perks and benefits, such as free gifts for long-term subscribers
  • Make the subscription plans valuable and irresistible making subscribers want to continue with their decision to subscribe

2. Fear of Missing Out (FOMO)

Gaining rewards is important for customers but more important than that is to avoid losses. This is where the psychology of fear of missing out comes in. When subscribers think that something may not be available for long, they feel more motivated to act on it.

For example, say you’ve launched a limited edition curated box and want the boxes to be sold-out fast. You could use FOMO techniques to encourage customers to buy them. Here are some ways to use FOMO for your Shopify subscriptions:

  • Limited time offers: Discounts and deals for a limited time to create urgency. This pricing psychology could be on subscription renewal fees or subscription boxes
  • Low stock alerts: Tell people a product is running out of stock to create a sense of scarcity and encourage them to add it in their subscription boxes
  • Social proof: Show reviews, ratings, and testimonials of products to show people that others have bought and loved the products
  • Abandoned cart reminders: Send reminders to customers who leave actions incomplete

Example

3. Instant gratification and dopamine triggers

Another way to influence consumer behavior in subscriptions is to use the psychology of instant gratification. In other words, use dopamine triggers to encourage customers to take actions.

In today’s competitive world, brands are trying to attract and engage customers by promising the moon. Apart from tangible perks, customers also find gratification in aspects such as convenience, knowledgeable help, and helpful customer support.

Let’s look at some ways to create a sense of instant gratification for customers:

  • Offer instant discounts or perks, such as fast shipping, vouchers, etc.
  • Personalize customers’ unboxing experience
  • Create flash sales on subscription boxes
  • Include a surprise gift in the subscription box
  • Quick delivery: 41% of shoppers expect a 24-hour delivery
  • Provide friendly and efficient customer service, adding a sense of satisfaction and good customer experience

4. The endowment effect

People have a tendency to value products they own. For instance, if they own a red sweater from brand X, they value it more even if it is expensive or common. That’s because they own it and hence, they feel it is good and valuable.

Here, there’s an endowment effect at play. This psychology can work well for subscriptions as subscribers are associated with brands for a long term.

For instance, subscribers would value your subscription more than your competitors because they themselves are a part of it. This could lead them to refer or recommend your subscription plans to their friends.

Now let’s learn a few ways to use the endowment effect psychology for subscriptions:

  • Offer free subscription renewals for the first month and auto charge from the second month onward
  • Incorporate build-your-own-box model in your subscription
  • Create a sense of ownership for customers, to justify the value of the subscription box
  • Use pricing psychology tactics on subscription boxes

Here’s an illustration that explains the endowment effect psychology:

Source

5. Social proof and herd mentality

Did you know a three or four-star rating can drop customers’ trust levels to 67%, while a five star rating can increase trust level to 95%? That’s how much reviews, testimonials, and user-generated content helps.

Sharing social proof, reviews, and ratings is not just a simple marketing tactic; it is a strategy that influences customer psychology. Here’s how you can use this psychological tactic for your influencing customers and habit formation in eCommerce:

  • Share subscribers’ experience on different channels to increase credibility
  • Include referral programs to encourage existing subscribers to refer friends; this helps increase your sign-ups
  • Share user-generated content by subscribers, on social media, your website, or app
  • Run special marketing campaigns to share subscriber reviews, videos, etc.

6. Personalization and the desire for uniqueness

We humans are drawn to experiences and information that seems more relevant to us, our interests, and needs. Personalization in marketing helps tap into this psychological principle and drive consumer behavior in subscriptions.

When subscribers experience a higher level of personalization, the value of the subscriptions increases as the products and services are more relevant to their needs.

Moreover, personalization also increases the sense of uniqueness. When subscribers receive an offer or a product that’s different from what others have received, they feel more unique and exclusive.

Here’s how you can use the psychology of personalization in subscriptions for the success of your eCommerce subscriptions:

  • Personalized recommendations of new products and services for subscriptions
  • Offer exclusive perks and benefits for long-term subscribers
  • Create deeper engagement via AI-driven personalization
  • Personalize content and communication for subscribers
  • Offer personalized subscription boxes based on customers’ interests and needs

Here’s an example of a personalization in subscription of a cosmetics business, where the brand gets subscribers to answer a detailed questionnaire to personalize their subscription box.

7. The scarcity principle

It’s a common feeling we all go through – when something is scarce, rare, or limited, we want it more. Rather, we get into a mode of loss aversion. Loss aversion in marketing is a common psychological framework used by eCommerce brands.

Why does this psychological strategy work? Scarcity increases the perceived value, the fear of missing out drives urgency and action, and limited time and quantities help reduce procrastination.

Here’s how you can use the scarcity principle to influence consumer behavior in subscriptions.

  • Create limited-time offers for subscribers
  • Create subscriber-exclusive offers and deals to encourage non subscribers to sign up
  • Include tactics such as count-down timers and display the quantity left, for example, ‘Only 1 left’
  • Create limited-edition premium subscription boxes; for example, limited edition wine subscription

8. The peak-end rule

When customers have a bad experience with a brand, they easily move on to the next best brand. One negative experience is enough for customers to make a decision to leave a brand.

This is something that is related to the peak-end rule psychology. People evaluate their eCommerce shopping experience based on their peak experience. For instance, an intensely good experience or a very bad experience impacts the overall perception or experience of customers.

So, how can this psychological rule be applied to and influence consumer behavior in subscriptions?

  • Create memorable unboxing experiences for subscriptions
  • Offer surprise gifts or surprise products in your subscription boxes
  • Organize exclusive events for subscribers
  • Take personalization to the next level for subscribers with one-on-one interactions to cater to individual needs

items.html:
Ecommerce brands are exploring new ways to engage customers and increase revenue. One such strategy is memberships. Brands across various industries are setting up membership models to generate recurring revenue for retail businesses.

Whether B2B or D2C, all types of businesses are exploring membership models. B2B membership benefits include more customer engagement, increased sales, and higher sustainability.

In this blog, we focus on the B2B membership model of the stationery brand, Staples. We look at how the brand has set up its membership model, its key features, and the takeaways for other brands.

Let’s get started!

What is Staples membership?

Staples is an American office supply brand. It offers traditional office supplies, such as paper, ink, printers, clearing products, technology, furniture, and all things office. The brand has designed a B2B membership model called Staples Advantage.

Staples Advantage offers multiple plans for businesses to choose from. Businesses can choose plans based on the number of employees they have. For instance, there are plans for businesses that have 20 or less, between 20 and 500, or enterprises that have more than 500 employees.

The membership plans are designed to cater to various types of business needs, from stationery to furniture to food, and more.

Staples membership strategy breakdown and takeaways

In this section, we look at the many features and factors that make Stapes membership plans so sought after by businesses. From the type of plans to how the brand offers flexibility, and more, you’ll learn the ins and outs of the Staples membership strategy.

1. Two membership plans

When it comes to membership plans, it is better for brands to keep it simple and easy. Offering too many choices may leave customers confused and lead to decision fatigue.

Earlier, Staples offered two different membership plans – one for small businesses, and the other for mid to large sized businesses.

1. Staples Plus: This plan is designed for small businesses. Small-sized businesses have lesser employees, and require less office supplies.

2. Staples premium: For mid and large businesses, this plan allows multiple users and locations, and is designed for businesses that require more supplies and administrative tools.

2. Staples Business Advantage membership

Staples Business Advantage has three different membership plants to choose from. The three plans are differentiated by the number of employees the plans are suitable for. Apart from that, the plans’ benefits differentiate them.

3. Three plans offering different benefits

To make the three tiers different and exclusive, Staples offers different benefits under each membership plan.

It’s three plans are differentiated by the number of employee it is suitable for:

1. For up to 20 employees: In this membership plan, members can avail everyday low business prices, fast and reliable next day delivery, and access to category and industry experts. Customers can sign up and save 20%.

2. For 20 to 500 employees: In this plan, members can enjoy custom pricing programs, flexible payment terms, and account support.

3. For 500 plus employees: This plan offers eProcurement system integration, spend controls and approval routing, and dedicated account management.

4. Staples membership plans are free

With so many membership plans available, businesses do not want to keep signing up for multiple memberships. Not only is it expensive, it can also be a security threat. Businesses prefer to stay away from sharing their business details and credentials because of the risk of fraud and data theft.

All three Staples membership plans are free. This membership strategy helps increase members and ensures membership model sustainability.

5. Tier-based benefits

Staples membership plans are tier-based. The brand offers B2B membership benefits based on the different tiers. Tier-based membership models have many benefits:

  • There’s an element of exclusivity for each tier
  • There are gamification features, making members want to climb to the next tier
  • Members can choose which tier they want to join based on their needs
  • Because there are options, members tend to stay longer

Staple tier-based plans offer these benefits:

  • Benefits such as 10% discount, fast delivery, and access to experts are common to all tiers
  • The lowest plan (for 20 employees) does not get the flexibility to schedule deliveries, while the other two plans get flexibility
  • The lowest plan cannot have custom pricing option; the middle plan (20 to 500 employees) only eligible businesses get custom pricing; the top plan gets custom pricing

6. A wide variety of products

The more products and services brands offer, the more customers they can cater to. When there is a wide variety of products, you can cater to various customer needs from different customer segments.

Staples understands this well and offers more than 20,000 products across categories, such as office supplies, print, paper, ink, school supplies, furniture, electronics, and more. The brand also offers different types of solutions. Having a wide range of products also ensures recurring revenue for retail stores.

7. Efficient customer support

Reports show that 87% of customers appreciate proactive solutions by brands, boosting satisfaction and loyalty. Staples offers efficient customer service options to its customers. Customers and members can get their questions answered via live chat within 30 seconds.

Efficient customer service reduces customers’ wait time and provides speedy answers and resolutions to their queries. Fast and efficient customer support helps enhance customer experience, satisfaction, and loyalty towards the brand.

8. Staples provides a dedicated account management team

Today, it’s a must for businesses to understand their customers and needs. However, for businesses that have a large clientele, it’s not easy to interact or engage at a one-on-one level.

But Staples has an effective membership strategy that helps the brand enhance customer engagement. The brand has a dedicated account management team that looks after customer preferences and requirements. This team gets to know customers and their businesses and helps them solve complex procurement needs. This is one of the biggest benefits of this B2B membership model.

Read more: Ecommerce membership marketing strategies + Examples

9. Discounts and savings

There are many things businesses require in order to function smoothly. For instance, offices require furniture and stationery, printers, and a pantry for employees. All these things can add up to a big cost to the company.

And hence, businesses prefer to buy from brands that offer discounts. Staples Advantage membership plans also offer discounts and savings to its members. Discounts and cost-effectiveness is amongst the top B2B membership benefits that businesses look for.

10. Staples membership caters to various industries

items.excerpt: You will find subscription box models everywhere, across products and services. Book subscriptions are nothing new. Remember local book libraries? items.html:
You will find subscription box models everywhere, across products and services. Book subscriptions are nothing new. Remember local book libraries?

However, with changing times, a lot has changed in the publishing and book industry. While many online bookstores offer subscriptions as it offers recurring revenue in the publishing industry, some subscription models stand out.

In this blog, we take a look at the Book of the Month subscription model. We breakdown its many features, and understand why it is so effective and why subscribers love it so much!

Read on!

What is Book of the Month subscription model?

Book of the Month is a subscription service for books. The monthly subscription fee is $ 17.99. This monthly book club subscription sends subscribers one book a month. The brand selects five to seven books every month. Of these books, subscribers can add one to their monthly box. The selection includes various genres and titles, from new releases, upcoming titles, and early book releases, among others. The brand ships the books within a week for free.

However, these are just the basic features and benefits of this book subscription. A more intense look at this subscription model offers insights into many more marketing strategies for the publishing sector and lessons on how to increase recurring revenue in publishing.

Book of the Month Subscription Box Model Breakdown

Starting from cost benefits to discounts to additional perks to easy cancellation and customer retention strategies, the Book of the Month has many effective features to talk about. Let’s go through each one, in this section.

1. The subscription model offers various genres

When planning subscription box models, brands have to ensure they cater to different segments of their target audience. Catering only to one or two segments may not be sustainable.

When it comes to books, there are many different genres. And when it comes to readers, there are all kinds, reading different genres. Book of the Month understands this well.

Its book club subscription offers books in many different genres, including thriller, mystery, contemporary fiction, romance, young adult, fantasy, and more. This ensures:

  • Higher engagement
  • Higher sales
  • More marketing opportunities
  • A large customer base
  • Subscribers get to discover new book titles

2. Book recommendations for subscribers

Book of the Month has a section called ‘Members Most Loved’. Just like lifestyle brands display recommendations on their website, ‘Most Bought’, ‘Bestsellers’, etc., this book subscription also offers recommendations for books that are most loved by other readers.

Apart from this, the subscription website has many other recommendation sections. For example, there’s a section that lists currently popular books. Another section shows the most popular new titles.

How do these recommendations help?

  • If subscribers don’t like the titles shared by the brand, they can choose from recommendations
  • Subscribers do not feel bound with limited choices
  • It keeps subscribers engaged as they can discover new titles to read
  • It’s an effective customer retention strategy for the publishing industry
  • It plays with customer psychology, making them feel that there’s a lot the brand has to offer and a lot they can discover

3. Personalization and customization

If subscription box models are too rigid and limited, it may put off subscribers. Everyone wants to have the freedom and flexibility to shop the way they want — studies show that consumers are willing to pay more for flexibility.

So, what happens when subscribers of the Book of the Month subscription box model want more than one book per month? The brand has incorporated personalization and customization features.

Subscribers can add one or two more books for an additional charge. They can choose these books from previous Book of the Month tiles. This feature offers flexibility, freedom, and enhances customer experience.

4. The subscription box model offers flexibility and freedom

Another aspect worth talking about is that members of this subscription box model have the freedom and flexibility to skip a month if they want to.

For instance, when subscribers are busy or traveling and do not want a book in a particular month, they can choose to skip that month. When subscribers skip, their credit gets forwarded to the next month.

This feature ensures customers feel comfortable signing up and do not lose money and continue their subscription for a long time.

Similarly, if subscribers forget to pick a book before a specific date, they are changed but the credit is forwarded and they can use it in the next month.

5. Gifting books made easy

Book of the Month also allows customers to gift books. Customers can choose a Book of the Month subscription of three, six, or twelve books for gifting. This feature is especially effective during the holiday gifting season.

The process of gifting a subscription is easy. Customers have to simply choose one of the three membership plans and make the payment in a few simple steps.

This process of gifting is hassle-free, convenient, and easy. No calls or follow ups; customers just have to follow a few, simple steps online.

This subscription box model sends the gift in three different ways:

  • Print-at-home card
  • Email
  • BOTM gift card

6. The subscription box model is cost-effective

Customers can join the Book of the Month subscription club at an affordable rate. The cost of the monthly book club subscription is $17.99. However, new subscribers can get their first book for $9.99 by entering a discount code during checkout.

Most customers sign up for subscriptions for the cost benefits and discounts. Book of the Month offers attractive pricing for the subscriptions, making it easy for customers to sign up.

7. Other benefits offered to subscribers

Apart from benefits such as convenience and discounts, the Book of the Month subscription box model offers many other perks to subscribers. When customers get something extra, it enhances their experience and they tend to stay loyal to brands.

Here are some of those perks that keep their subscribers engaged and loyal and customer retention strategies you can try for your subscription models:

  • A free gift with the first purchase
  • A tote bag after the first year
  • A free add-on during subscribers’ birthday month
  • One free book from the top five ‘Books of the Year’

8. Easy customer support

79% of customers expect a self-service option when it comes to customer service. Self-service provides a better experience, as customers do not have to wait.

Book of the Month has a dedicated section on its website, for customer support. Customers can either search for their specific query via a few quick links, or click open dedicated sections that explain how the subscription box model works, information about charges and credits, and more.

9. Easy cancellation policy

For customers, subscriptions can be tricky. Many brands make subscription cancellation difficult. In other instances, customers end up paying fees because of direct payment debit systems without even knowing. With so many subscriptions floating around, subscription fatigue is something that eCommerce brands have to strategically deal with.

These are some of the main reasons why customers do not sign up for subscriptions easily. But Book of the Month has made it easy for subscribers to cancel subscriptions. Customers have to call them up and initiate the cancellation process. This adds value and flexibility, which mean a lot to customers.

10. It has a loyalty program for the subscription

The Book of the Month loyalty program is called ‘Relationship Status’. Through this integrated loyalty program, the brand recognizes and rewards long term subscribers with gifts and additional benefits.

For instance, ‘Friend’ status can be achieved once the subscriber purchases three boxes in a single continuous subscription. The ‘BFF’ status can be achieved when customers purchase 12 boxes in a single continuous subscription.

11. It offers a wide selection of books

Ecommerce stores have the benefit of catering to a wide customer base. And when it comes to books and publishing, customers’ interests can be varied. And that is something that the Book of the Month is ready to cater to.

The brand offers a wide variety of genres — thriller, history, young adult, true crime, memoir, romance, fantasy, horror, sci-fi, and more. The brand also offers audiobooks – an excellent example of how brands need to adapt and tweak their offerings with changing times and market trends.
