items.html:
Whether it’s grocery, automobile, airlines, or live streaming – there are multiple subscription options available for all kinds of products and services.

Moreover, consumers took to the subscription boom and have signed up to more subscriptions than they can manage.

This overdose can cause subscription fatigue. Subscribers get bored or tired of subscription plans. And this can be lethal to subscription businesses.

So, if you’re a subscription business eager to learn how to prevent subscription fatigue, this blog is a must-read for you.

What is subscription fatigue?

Today, there are multiple subscription options for every product or service. For instance, may it be grocery, magazines, music, movies, or automobiles, it’s easy to find subscription options.

People too, have taken to joining subscriptions because they are convenient, offer price benefits, and other benefits. However, studies show that an average millennial has between six and 11 subscription plans.

It’s highly unlikely that people use all their subscriptions on a regular basis. Thus, subscriptions become an expense to them. Besides, there are too many subscription options. And the average consumer is tired of so many options.

This is subscription fatigue — a feeling of being tired, bored, and exhausted of having too many subscriptions. And as an increasing number of brands start subscriptions models, consumers’ fatigue is going to rise.

How does subscription fatigue impact business?

It’s understood that subscription fatigue is not a good thing for businesses. In this section, we look at a few ways in which subscription fatigue can negatively impact businesses.

1. Subscription churn

When subscribers get tired of having too many subscriptions or a subscription plan that stops adding value to their life, the first thing they think about doing is canceling the subscription. Subscription churn can negatively impact businesses, as it would mean loss of business and customers. Moreover, acquiring new subscribers to fill that gap is a cost-intensive activity that can add to business expense.

2. Loss of revenue

Subscription fatigue can either drive customers to leave or they start transacting less with the brand. In both cases, it leads to a loss of revenue. When subscribers leave, it has a direct impact on the business revenue. When subscribers start transacting less or when they shift to a lower tier subscription plan, it leads to a loss of revenue for the business.

3. Loss of touch with customers

Subscription fatigue can also lead to lower engagement levels. When subscribers do not see value in subscription plans, they tend to withdraw and engage less with the brand. For brands, this leads to a loss of touch with customers and decreased opportunities to interact and engage with customers.

4. Poor brand perception

If customers are not happy with your subscription plan, they may talk about it to their friends, family, and colleagues. This can adversely affect your brand perception. Also, it is known that when customers are not happy with something, they tend to be more vocal about it, as opposed to when they have good experiences with brands. Subscription fatigue can have a negative impact on your brand image.

How to prevent subscription fatigue?

For a subscription business to thrive and succeed, it must be able to keep customers engaged year after year. Moreover, the brand must ensure customers do not cancel subscriptions. Here are five best strategies to prevent subscription fatigue for your Shopify subscription business.

1. Focus on value

Gone are the days when customers only looked at low prices when buying from brands. Today, customers want value, convenience, community, and much more from their favorite brands.

One way to prevent subscription fatigue is to focus on value. A McKinsey study shows that 62% of subscribers prioritize value when signing up for subscriptions.

Source

Here are some ways to enhance the value of your subscription plans:

  • Personalize subscription plans: When the products and services you add in your subscription boxes are relevant to customers, they would find more value in it, rather than receiving products that aren’t of much use to them
  • Community experience: Make your customers feel exclusive by building communities for like minded subscribers. When your subscribers meet others with the same interests, engage in activities and interact with them, they feel like they belong to a community. This enhances their experience and lowers subscription fatigue
  • Quality and variety: When it comes to value, the quality of your products and services and the variety you offer are key considerations for customers. For example, food and meal kit subscriptions often promote freshness, nutrition, and a wide range of ingredients to attract subscribers
  • Apart from these, flexibility, competitive pricing, efficient customer support, and a seamless app experience are also some factors that enhance the value of subscriptions

Explore Appstle Subscription App for your Shopify subscription business for a seamless experience.

2. Identify market gaps to focus on essentials

Understanding the gaps to fill with your subscription offers is crucial, not only for your success, but for customer satisfaction.

For instance, say you’re a brand that sells automotive parts and accessories. Your research reveals that customers are facing an issue with services related to automotives, such as maintenance, cleaning, timely repairs, hardware upgrades, etc.

The solution: offer service subscriptions with your subscription plans.

When you offer the most essential products and services required by consumers, it’s unlikely that your subscribers would want to cancel or might feel disengaged. That’s because these are essentials that consumers cannot do without.

Here are a few cues to help you get started with filling market gaps and offering essentials:

  • Conduct market survey and find out what customers are desperately looking for
  • Find the product or service that can help your subscription plan take precedence over your competitors
  • Consistently ask your subscribers and customers what more you could offer to them in your inventory

Example: Volvo’s Flexible Car Subscription

3. Prioritize customer retention

Studies show that acquiring new customers can cost five times more than what you’d spend on retaining customers. Not only does retaining subscribers prove to be cost effective, you can even reduce subscription fatigue by focusing on customer retention.

Let’s find out how.

When you focus on customer retention, your customer experience improves. For instance, whatever your customer retention strategies are, you will keep the customers’ needs and preferences at the center. Thus, these strategies will directly impact how customers feel about your brand and how they perceive the subscription experience.

Here’s what you can do to focus on subscriber retention in order to reduce subscription fatigue:

  • Create a feedback loop with your subscribers: To ensure your customers continue to be happy and satisfied with your subscription offering, keep asking for their feedback. Run surveys, ask them to join focus feedback groups, consistently collect ratings and reviews to understand subscriber needs
  • Provide flexibility: Customers do not want to get into subscriptions where they get stuck. They expect flexibility and freedom. For instance, they may want to pause or skip deliveries, or change delivery addresses and intervals. When you make it easy for them to make these changes, they feel a sense of freedom, enhancing retention rates
  • Acknowledgement and rewards: When you acknowledge your subscribers as unique individuals, talk to them, care to understand their needs, they feel good about your brand. Consistently acknowledge and reward customers with incentives, such as discounts, subscriber-only offers, events, etc.

4. Offer competitive pricing

With most brands offering subscription options, across industries, it is extremely important to offer a competitive pricing for your Shopify subscriptions. Poor pricing strategies can single handedly derail your subscription business model.

So what are the pricing related strategies that can help reduce subscription fatigue in customers?

  • Reevaluate your pricing strategy from time to time to ensure you’re on track
  • Offer rewards and points for multiple actions, such as during sign up, on anniversaries, during sales, etc., so customers see more monetary value
  • Conduct subscriber and customer research to understand how your pricing affects customer experience and perception
  • Collect data on subscriber behavior, past purchase, etc. to refine your subscription pricing structures
  • Tiered pricing structure can enable subscribers to periodically reset their subscription plan to higher or lower tiers based on their needs

5. Provide novelty and variety

Another reason many subscribers continue or cancel subscriptions is the novelty or variety factor. Is your subscription model able to hook customers year after year? Are you introducing new products and new experiences for subscribers?

Consider this: Around 30% of customers say the lack of fun or new experiences is a factor in their decisions to cancel subscriptions. With so many brands offering so many different options of products and services, customers tend to get bored if you fail to offer them something new every now and then.

Here’s what you can do to ensure your subscription plan remains vibrant and exciting for subscribers:

  • Conduct market research to see what your competitors are offering via subscriptions
  • Use customer feedback, AI, ML, and data to provide tailored subscription experiences
  • Ensure you add new products and services in your inventory from time to time
  • Collaborate with complementing brands to offer something new to your subscribers
  • Include fresh and fun experiences that are enjoyable and engaging for subscribers

Example: Adidas Creators Club creates fun and engaging events for its subscribers

How to prevent subscription fatigue for your Shopify subscriptions

While you may have decided to apply some of the strategies we’ve shared in this blog, you will need to incorporate a subscription tool that can help you prevent churn and fatigue.

items.html:
Food subscription boxes have almost become a necessity for many people, especially those in urban cities.

For customers, food and grocery subscription boxes are convenient, cost-efficient, and hassle-free. For brands, the subscription model provides stability, predictable revenue, and long-term customers.

But even though there are so many food subscription options in the market, there are hardly a handful that succeed.

One brand that has got its food subscription box model on point is HelloFresh. This blog looks at why HelloFresh meal kit subscriptions are loved by customers.

Continue to read HelloFresh food subscription box breakdown.

What is the HelloFresh meal kit?

HelloFresh is one of the most popular and liked food subscription boxes in the US. HelloFresh sends fresh, nutritious, and healthy meal kits regularly for customers to cook their desired recipes.

The USP of this grocery subscription box is a wide variety of options for fresh and nutritious ingredients to make cooking easy. The brand offers meal kits of various types, ranging from a combination of meat and veggie to only veggie, and pescatarian.

Most customer reviews about HelloFresh particularly mention the wide variety and convenience factor.

While there are many meal kit subscription brands out there, few have been able to garner the engagement and loyalty that HelloFresh has. Let’s look at what makes this subscription box business so special.

HelloFresh food subscription box strategy breakdown

Why is it that some subscription brands take a while to succeed, some never make it, and some are able to turn profitable soon enough? A breakdown of HelloFresh subscription model reveals many learnings and takeaways that you could apply to your Shopify subscription business. Here are the key features that help HelloFresh succeed:

1. Highlights benefits of the subscription box

A lot of food subscription boxes are well designed and offer many benefits. However, the brands fail to make those benefits known to customers.

But HelloFresh has smartly mentioned the key benefits of the box, the first thing on the home page.

The brand has taken a customer-first approach by telling customers how they can benefit from the subscription box.

From the convenience of making homemade meals to the cost benefits to the need for nutritious meals and also the ease of pausing and cancelling the subscriptions anytime – all the benefits are mentioned clearly.

Alongside, there are appealing images that complement the text. HelloFresh has put together the perfect recipe to draw potential customers in right at the beginning of the home page.

2. Mention of reasons to choose HelloFresh

To further emphasize on the benefits, HelloFresh has created a separate section on the homepage to tell customers why they must choose the HelloFresh food subscription box.

Here are the benefits mentioned:

  • Nutritious meal kits: the brand ensures their meal boxes include quality protein, an essential component for balanced diets.
  • Freedom and flexibility: customers get the freedom and flexibility to skip, pause, or cancel their subscription whenever they want, with ease.
  • Variety of options: customers can choose from a huge recipe selection.
  • Fresh and affordable: HelloFresh promotes its meal kits as being cheaper than takeouts, apart from being fresh and nutritious.

3. HelloFresh offers seasonal and special food subscription boxes

A survey revealed that 74% of customers say quality is the most important factor in keeping them loyal to a brand.

HelloFresh has made their product offers exciting by including a range of plans to choose from. For instance, customers can choose from sections called, ‘Most popular plans’, ‘Veggie and plant-based meals’, ‘Kid-tested recipes’, ‘Fit & wholesome’ ‘Quick & easy’, and ‘Pescatarian’.

Offering multiple options not only makes it exciting and appealing, but it also gives options for customers to choose meal kits based on their dietary preferences.

4. Information about what’s inside each box

HelloFresh enhances customer experience further by offering a curated selection of meal kits. In the box are many other components that make the subscription experience even more exciting. Let’s look at everything else there is in HelloFresh curated subscription boxes.

  • Fresh vegetable and fruits for all kinds of dishes
  • Recipe cards with step-by-step guides for nutritional cooking
  • Protein-packed ingredients
  • Customization option for add-ons, such as snacks, savory sides, additional proteins
  • Eco-friendly packaging that can be recycled and reused

Also read: Ecommerce subscription trends and predictions 2025

5. Collects and displays social proof

99.9% of consumers look for reviews and proof before they make purchases. It builds brand trust, increases sales, and has many other benefits. And HelloFresh doesn’t shy away from sharing social proof on their homepage.

The homepage displays user generated content (UGC) shared by customers on Instagram. The brand encourages more customers to post their reviews and experiences of HelloFresh food subscription boxes and tag the brand.

6. A dedicated FAQs section

Not only new, potential customers, but even existing subscribers tend to have a lot of queries. And especially when the product is related to food and consumables. And one of the best ways to answer basic and routine questions is to have an FAQs section.

If customers have to reach out to your customer support team or write to you for every question, it can get annoying for them and daunting for you to answer each and every query.

That’s why an FAQs section helps. HelloFresh answers all kinds of questions in the FAQ section. In this section, you will find answers to questions related to redeeming special offers, how the food subscription box model works, whether the meal kits provide nutritional information, how customers can recycle the packaging, and whether customers can skip a delivery, among other questions.

7. Allows food subscription box plan personalization

Every individual has their own preference for food. And hence, a one-size-fits-all meal kit subscription won’t work. This is where personalization helps to enhance customer experience and satisfaction.

Personalization is all the more critical in subscriptions as customers associate with brands for a long term, and customization can keep things relevant for customers.

HelloFresh understands that, and hence, the brand allows individual customers to personalize their plan.

Subscribers can choose from meat & veggies, only veggie, family friendly, fit & wholesome, under 20 mins, and pescatarian meal options and create their own personalized plan. Additionally, subscribers have access to all the recipes every week.

8. HelloFresh subscription is simple yet comprehensive

When brands provide too many options and a lot of variety, customers often get into decision fatigue. Even though HelloFresh offers many different plans and kits to choose from, the brand has figured a way to still make the selection experience simple and straightforward.

Providing a less complex subscription system not only makes it easy for subscribers but also has many other benefits. For instance, happy customers tend to spread the word for your brand, and when making purchases is easy, customers tend to spend more on your website.

9. Customers can try new food items via the subscription

One of the best advantages of subscriptions is that brands can introduce new products to subscribers, and subscribers get to try new products every now and then.

With HelloFresh food subscription box, subscribers can not only try various meal kit options based on themes, such as veggie, pescatarian, etc., but also try out new products. For instance, the brand has more than 100 weekly menus and products every week.

Also read: How to launch a food subscription box model

10. Discounts on every order

One of the reasons customers choose subscriptions is the discounts. Retailers offer consistent discounts when customers sign up for subscriptions. For customers, this can add up to a huge amount of savings. For brands, recurring revenue ensures sustainability and profitability.

HelloFresh offers a discount on every subscription order. Groceries are an ongoing requirement with a short shelf life. Not only do grocery subscription boxes make customers’ lives easier, they also offer price benefits and savings to customers.

On the HelloFresh subscription site, subscribers do not have to apply a special discount code. Rather, the discount is automatically applied during checkout. This hasslefree process enhances customer experience.

Key takeaways from HelloFresh food subscription box breakdown

  • Highlight benefits of your subscription box – HelloFresh does it over and over again, makes it customer-focused
  • Emphasize on your USP and the value you add to customers lives
  • Bases on your products and industry, offer many options for customers to choose from
  • Clearly explain the contents of each subscription box
  • Have an FAQs page and efficient customer support for subscribers
  • Personalize the subscription boxes for better customer satisfaction
  • Keep it simple, easy, and uncluttered
  • Introduce subscribers to new products via subscription boxes
  • Offer discounts and price benefits to make your subscription plans enticing

items.html:
Your subscription and membership plans can succeed only if you are able to retain subscribers year after year.

A high churn rate would mean loss of revenue and an increase in new customer acquisition costs. Both these aren’t good for any subscription business.

However, not all subscribers who intend to cancel actually go through the cancellation. Thanks to effective cancellation flows.

In this blog, we look at effective cancellation flow strategies to incorporate into your Shopify and Shopify Plus subscriptions and memberships.

Let’s get started!

What are cancellation flows?

Customers showing an intent to stop their relationship with your brand by cancelling subscriptions or memberships is not a positive feeling. It can hurt your revenue and customer loyalty rate.

So when customers initiate a cancellation request, eCommerce brands typically run a series of steps to try and stop them. Brands try to convince customers to change their mind.

The steps brands take when customers’ show intent to initiate cancellations is called cancellation flow.

This flow involves brands offering assistance to customers, collecting feedback, offering incentives for continuation, or alternative solutions to improve the chances of customers not cancelling their subscriptions.

A cancellation flow starts from the time customers display an intent to cancel their subscription. And it can last even after they go through with cancellations.

Why are cancellation flows important?

Whether yours is a SaaS, online streaming, eCommerce or mobile app subscription and membership business, cancellation flows can be the factor that can make or break your business. Here are the reasons why cancellation flows are critical for your business.

1. Reduce churn

Acquiring new customers costs five times more than retaining old ones. And hence, it’s critical to reduce churn. Having well-designed cancellation flows on your Shopify store can help reduce churn, retain more customers, and reduce your dependency on new customers. By reducing churn, you can ensure long-term relationships with subscribers and members.

2. Better customer understanding

When you associate with customers over a long period of time, you can get to know them better. Having a cancellation flow that helps reduce cancellations can lead to long-term relationships with customers, helping you understand them better.

3. Revenue retention

Shopify subscriptions and memberships are also sources of recurring revenues for customers. For example, paid plans generate regular revenue. Moreover, the recurring nature of subscriptions and perks offered via memberships drive more sales. Hence, effective cancellation flows help retain revenue flow into the business.

Read: Customer Acquisition VS. Retention – What To Focus On?

Cancellation flows to have in place for subscriptions and memberships

The cancellation flow you design for your subscription or membership business will depend on your products and services, industry, and other generic aspects. Here are 9 cancellation flow strategies you must consider for your Shopify business.

1. Show them subscription or membership benefits

Over time, as your customers join other subscriptions, they may start seeing less value in your subscription. Hence, when customers show cancellation intent, direct them to a page where you have listed all the benefits of signing up. This page should remind them of why they joined and how the subscription or membership is benefiting them.

Here are a few things you could do:

  • Use data from the customers’ history to highlight the benefits
  • Use customer testimonials and reviews to highlight benefits
  • Highlight any new benefits that are going to be added in the future
  • Show all the exclusive benefits they enjoy as part of the plan

2. Collect feedback, reasons for cancellation

Your subscribers might be cancelling because they might have faced some issues. But that shouldn’t be the reason they disassociate from your brand. You can turn those reasons into learning and opportunities for improvement. Identify the reasons. Try to fix the issues to retain subscribers.

Do this:

  • Have a feedback form as part of your cancellation flow
  • Ask them specific questions about their subscription and membership experience
  • Conduct an exit survey via a form, a call, via chat, or other communication channels
  • Address customers’ issues and problems with the best possible solutions. Make them feel heard

Source

3. Offer alternatives to cancellation

If you want to stop your customers from cancelling subscriptions and memberships, think strategically. Most times customers aren’t sure about their decisions. They may wonder if they should cancel or not? Or continue for some more time and then decide?

This is when you must catch their attention by offering alternatives to cancellation. Here are some cues:

  • Coax them to pause their subscription or membership for a short period and then restart it
  • Offer them options to upgrade or downgrade their subscription or membership plan
  • Offer a discount to retain them. For example, one month free subscription upon renewal
  • Incorporate an intuitive membership app in your Shopify store to automate real-time personalized incentives to customers

4. Personalize your offers and incentives

Today, customers expect personalized experiences from their favorite brands. And most brands try to incorporate personalization strategies into their marketing plans.

So imagine, if you fall short in creating personalized offers, your customers might not get the same feelings they get from other brands. The result – they may not want to continue with your subscriptions and memberships.

Here’s what you can do to personalize cancellation flows:

  • Offer personalized discounts by speaking to individual subscribers and asking them how you could make them stay
  • Personalize offers based on subscribers’ preference and history
  • Make your offers relevant and exclusive, making them want to stay
  • Use personalized details, such as address them by their name, mention how long they’ve been subscribers, and other special details

5. Add a human touch to the cancellation flow

78% of customers prefer human customer support. Customers know when they’re chatting with a bot and when there’s a real person on the other side. And when it comes to something as sensitive as cancellations, it’s critical that you bring in a human touch to convince them to stay.

Here are a few ways to take a human-to-human approach in cancellation flows:

  • Instead of a chatbot, have a real person conversing with subscribers
  • Offer them personalized offers, talk to them, meet them if possible, engage in video conversation, if you need to
  • Send a message from the CEO or founder to convince them to stay
  • Understand the subscriber’s sentiment and respond accordingly. Only a human can really understand customers’ emotions

6. Share a feedback survey form

At times, when subscribers and members have already made up their mind to go ahead with cancellations, there is not much you can do. However, it’s critical to make their cancellation experience smooth and easy.

Providing a good experience during this time can increase the potential of these customers returning to sign up again in future. Here are some tips to follow to win back customers in the future:

  • Add a pop-up feedback form when a subscriber clicks on the cancel button
  • Ask customers the reasons for cancellation
  • Keep the feedback form short and to the point
  • Provide space for customers to share their own thoughts
  • Ask targeted questions that can help you gather information about them
  • Offer real-time incentives and offers to stop cancellations

7. Segment customers based on survey responses

Subscribers can have many reasons for cancelling, for example, maybe the payment gateway isn’t secure, or deliveries were delayed. To create the next steps for these different issues, incorporate segmentation. Create relevant cancellation flow steps for each segment.

Let’s understand how to go about segmentation for cancellation flow:

  • Segregate the different issues into different segments, for example, high subscription fee, poor customer service, etc.
  • Create personalized messages and offers to address these unique issues so that customers feel heard
  • Offer alternative solutions, offers, and incentives based on the unique concerns

Source

8. Collect data on common reasons for cancellation

Some of the most common reasons for subscribers and members cancelling their plans are: high subscription fee, poor customer experience, low value from benefits, and boredom.

An effective cancellation flow strategy is to identify common reasons. By doing this, you can address the most common reason subscribers are cancelling your subscriptions.

For instance, maybe subscribers are not happy with the way your subscription platform or app functions. A solution for this could be to explore a more efficient subscription app for your Shopify store. Providing a smooth digital experience can help you reduce churn.

Read: How To Reduce Shopify Subscription And Membership Churn During The Holidays

9. Re-engage ex-subscribers in the future

Let’s face the truth – you may not be able to retain some subscribers even with the best strategies in your cancellation flow. But that doesn’t mean you have lost them forever. You can attempt to encourage them to join your subscriptions or memberships again.

Here’s how you do this:

  • Use data from individual subscribers past activities
  • Create personalized and targeted campaigns to entice them to rejoin your subscriptions and memberships
  • For example, send them discounts and exclusive perks during the Christmas or New Year season telling them how much you miss them and all the new things they are missing out on

items.html:
Imagine you sign up for a curated subscription box from your favorite cosmetics brand. You receive a box of products on a designated date every month.

And even though it’s a curated subscription (surprise products), all the items in your boxes match your taste, needs, and are personalized to your likes.

Personalized subscription boxes have taken the subscription industry by storm. Customers love them because they offer discounted prices, carry a surprise element, and yet meet their needs.

Personalized subscription boxes have taken the subscription industry by storm. Customers love them because they offer discounted prices, carry a surprise element, and yet meet their needs.

This is the beauty of curated subscription boxes!

This blog explores curated subscription commerce, its benefits, and how your Shopify brand can profit from this business model.

What is a curated subscription box model?

A curated subscription box offers a personalized experience. The products, services, or experiences put together in the “box” are selected by the brand. But the selection is based on individual customers’ preference, taste, and needs. The appeal of curated boxes is the surprise and discovery element.

For example, TheraBox, an award-winning subscription box, sends monthly curated boxes around self-care. Each themed box could include products ranging from toners to teas, creams, candles, and more. Each month, a new surprise!

Image of TheraBox’s homepage featuring a new self-care subscription box.

Benefits of curated subscription boxes

From recurring revenue to more opportunities to engage customers to increased customer lifetime value (CLV) – curated subscription commerce provides a lot of benefits to eCommerce businesses. Here are some of the benefits.

1. Higher average order value

Subscription boxes lead to a higher average order value (AOV) as each box contains multiple products, as opposed to a single purchase. Moreover, you can include exclusive or new products in the boxes to increase the AOV.

2. Easily introduce new products to customers

Curated subscription boxes are an easy way to introduce new products to customers. For instance, when you add a new product to your inventory, seasonal products, or products by other brands during brand collaborations.

3. Improved customer experience

Curated subscriptions help enhance customer experience in many ways. For instance, you can create more opportunities to engage customers via new offers, regular updates, by offering seasons boxes, etc. A seamless delivery structure can also enhance customer experience.

Components of curated subscription commerce

A curated subscription box model is made up of several components or features that make it worth customers’ money and interest. Here are some of those components you must consider for your Shopify curated subscription boxes.

1. Curated selection of products

The curated subscription boxes model is based on the concept of curation – the brand puts together hand-picked products for customers based on their preferences, market trends or a specific theme. For example, a winter skin care for dry skin type curated subscription box.

2. Subscription model

Subscription models work on the concept of regular deliveries, for example, weekly, monthly, quarterly, or other intervals. Ecommerce brands can ensure consistent revenue for a long term. Additionally, higher customer loyalty.

3. Personalization

Businesses can drive 40% more revenue by offering personalized experience. Most customers expect brands to offer some sort of personalization. And curated subscription boxes are no exception. Brands offer personalized curated subscriptions based on customers’ preferences, demographics, interests, etc.

4. Boxing or bundling

Another aspect of subscriptions is bundling or boxing – products and services put together in a box or a bundle. This makes it easy for customers to receive curated items that match their preferences.

5. Pricing structure

The curated subscription box model functions on a tiered pricing structure. Customers can choose from different levels based on their budget and needs. Typically, higher tier subscriptions offer more value, benefits, and exclusivity to customers. This also makes high-tier boxes more enticing.

6. Customer engagement and community

Building a community around your curated subscription box model helps engage customers and offers more value to them. Communities through social media, offline and online events can help strengthen relationships.

7. Logistics and fulfillment

A big part of your subscription business is the efficiency of your logistics and delivery system. Partnering with reliable logistics partners, incorporating a subscription app that offers logistics management features, etc. is critical to the success of subscription models.

8. Vendor partnerships

Another important component of subscription businesses is vendor partnerships. For instance, partnerships with other businesses, packaging vendors, influences, product suppliers, etc. can add value to your curated subscriptions.

Read about the key components of a subscription management system.

Set up your Shopify curated subscription box business

The technicalities of setting up a curated subscription box model for your Shopify store are easy when you have a reliable subscription tool such as Appstle Subscriptions App. However, your subscription box concept has to align your business type, goals, and personality. Here are the steps to help you get there.

1. Define your niche

To know what to curate, you must understand who you’re curating the box for — your target audience. One of the first steps is to identify your potential buyers based on the products you are offering.

  • What are the demographics of your target audience – age, gender, location, etc.
  • What are their interests and likes – fitness, beauty, fashion, technology, etc.
  • What are their needs and problems, and which of your products can solve them? This will make your curation more relevant
  • Identify the gaps in the subscription market that your products or services can fill for these customers

2. Choose the subscription model

Subscription models have many other aspects that need to be figured out when setting up curated plans. Here are some of the basics to get started with:

  • The frequency of deliveries you want to offer – monthly, quarterly, weekly, or others.
  • The pricing structure of your subscription model – tiered pricing, basic pricing, flat pricing, etc.
  • The type of curated subscription plans you want to offer – fixed, personalized, etc.

3. Create a curation process

There are many ways to curate a subscription box. And so, you will have to narrow down your curation process based on your products, customers’ preference, etc. Here are some factors to curate your offerings:

  • Identify the products you want to offer in the curated subscription box. For example, these could be products you produce, a mix of products and services, or those sourced from third parties
  • Develop a curation process, for example, select products based on customers preferences, based on trends, and also ensure a good balance of consistency and discovery
  • Incorporate personalization strategies to make the subscription boxes relevant and appealing to individual customers

Read our e-book on getting started with eCommerce subscriptions

4. Create a brand identity

With so many subscription options in the market, customers expect something unique and meaningful when they shop. Uniqueness and value are elements that help build a strong brand identity. Here’s what you can create a brand identity for your subscription business:

  • Create a unique value proposition by defining what makes your curated subscription boxes special. For example, sustainable packaging, exclusive products, etc.
  • Build a community of your subscribers via channels such as social media, email, and in-person events to make your subscriptions more valuable and meaningful

5. Plan your logistics and operations

69% of customers are less likely to shop with the same retailer again after a delayed delivery or some issue with the delivery. Managing logistics and ensuring smooth operations is critical for curated subscription commerce, as these can make or break your business.

  • Create a system to track inventory, forecast demand, and manage supply
  • Choose reliable logistics and delivery partners
  • Use a subscription management tool, for example, Appstle Subscription that has comprehensive features

6. Create a marketing strategy

Once your curated subscription box model is set up, it’s time to get started with marketing it. Effective marketing can help you get a good start and set you up for success. Here’s what you can do:

  • Create a content market plan for your subscriptions business – include social media, blogs, email marketing, newsletters, influencer marketing, etc.
  • Put together a referral program – your loyal customers can help you get more subscribers
  • Use tactics such as FOMO and urgency by creating limited edition subscription boxes
  • Collect customer reviews, testimonials, and user generated content, for example, unboxing videos by subscribers

7. Provide efficient customer support

Your customers may have many queries and might need some explaining about how your subscription plan works, the benefits, etc. Also, your existing subscribers might need help from time to time. This is where an efficient customer service system can help you enhance customer experience. Here are a few things you can do:

  • Set up different communication channels for ease and speed
  • Make it easy for subscribers to perform some actions on their own, for example, change delivery schedule via the dashboard, initiate payments, etc.
  • Make it easy for customers to change their subscription plans, pause, or cancel subscriptions.
  • Incorporate loyalty and reward programs within your curated subscription commerce set up

8. Monitor, measure and optimize

Like any other business model, subscription businesses are not a one-time fixed set-up. You will have to consistently monitor and optimize your curated subscriptions to ensure you stay competitive. Here’s what you can do:

  • Use the analytics features of your Shopify subscription app to monitor the performance of your subscriptions – track customer behavior, churn, profits, etc.
  • Collect customer feedback to understand their preferences, gaps, etc.
  • Optimize your curated subscription boxes by making changes and adjustments based on trends, customer needs, seasons, etc.

9. Scale you curated subscription box business

To ensure consistent profitability from your curated subscriptions, you will have to scale your business. Incorporating a subscriptions tool helps scale easily as it automates tasks. Besides, it also offers other features such as marketing and promotions to help with business scaling. Here’s what you can do:

  • Expand your offerings to cater to a wider customer base, diversify products, services, introduce themed curated boxes, etc.
  • Collaborate with influencers to increase your brand awareness, partner with other brands to offer exclusive curated boxes
  • Use AI and data analytics tools to understand customer preferences, and streamline your curated subscription box management

Examples of curated subscription boxes

1. Maple Box

The Maple Box is a curated box subscription of organic products sourced from various brands. This subscription box is offered by Maple Magazine. Part of the subscription is a copy of the magazine.

2. Whiskey Loot

The liquor brand, Liquor Loot, offers a curated whiskey subscription box. The box contains custom glass bottles of whiskey and tasting notes. The brand encourages its subscribers to share feedback, reviews and unboxing videos and share them on their social media channels.

3. Bespoke Post

This themed subscription box for men by Bespoke Post offers a curated selection of products, ranging from accessories to grooming to home items. The brand asks subscribers to answer a quiz to personalize the curation process.

Cosmetics and beauty subscriptions are quite common and popular. Customers love them because of convenience and cost benefits, among other reasons.

For eCommerce beauty brands, subscription models bring stability, predictable revenue, decrease customer acquisition costs, and help the brand build long-term relationships with customers.

Although many cosmetics brands offer subscriptions, few are able to make it a successful venture and sustain it.

In this blog, we look at the subscription model of Dermalogica, a skin care products brand based on Shopify Plus.

What is the Dermalogica subscription?

Dermalogica is a skin care brand that was started in 1986. The brand offers a subscription option. Customers can get their skin care products delivered at their doorstep at a regular schedule. Customers can choose the delivery frequency.

Dermalogica subscription provides flexibility to its subscribers. Subscribers can change the delivery frequency or quantity. They also get to purchase products at the best prices along with free shipping. Additionally, subscribers earn 2x points with subscription orders.

A breakdown of Dermalogica skincare subscription on Shopify

In a sea of skincare and beauty subscriptions available online, Dermalogica stands out for many reasons. Not just the brand’s products, but also for the way the brand has set up and manages its subscription business model. In this section, we look at the many features of its subscription program and lessons to learn from it.

1. A dedicated subscription page

Visitors who come to your Shopify store might take a few seconds, if not minutes, to figure out your home page, the navigation, the different sections, and tabs.

So one of the most critical things to do is to have your subscriptions page tab on the home page. Better if you can highlight it or give it a prominent spot so customers don’t miss it.

Dermalogica has a dedicated subscription page.

Here are some takeaways from the Dermalogica subscription page:

  • Neat page with minimal text
  • The introductory text cleverly talks about three key benefits of joining the subscription
  • It shows graphically how the subscription work
  • Shares product recommendations with customers to get started
  • The page has a FAQs section

2. An FAQs section dedicated to the subscription model

Customers might have many questions before they sign up for the subscription. Even new subscribers might have questions.

Now, if they have to reach out to your customer support team with questions, it can become a rather long process. Besides, it adds to your costs. Many people might give up the idea of reaching out to you if the process is difficult.

That’s why having an FAQs section helps. You can answer all the basic and important questions via the FAQs.

In the Dermalogica subscription FAQs section, you will find questions such as, how to join the subscription, what happens after one joins, how to make changes to the subscription order, and other questions.

FAQs are a common and simple way to improve customer experience and make shopping easier and faster for customers. It is a section where customers can easily find information, and hence, it also helps increase sales and conversions.

Here’s Dermalogica’s FAQs section:

3. Dermalogica subscription plan is simple

Many eCommerce retailers think it helps when they offer more choices to customers. For example, offering three or more subscription plans to choose from. But did you know, this can actually lead to confusion, decision fatigue, and end in lesser subscription signups?

The subscription market is overloaded with options, and hence, you must try to make it easy for customers. That’s something that Dermalogica understands. Hence, the brand offers only one standard and simple subscription plan.

Customers are not put through the confusion of choosing from multiple subscription plans. Keeping the subscription plan simple has many benefits:

  • Less confusion for customers
  • More signups
  • Less cart abandonment
  • Makes subscription management easy
  • Brings more satisfaction for customers
  • Less competition and FOMO for customers

4. Explanation of how the subscription plan works

Keeping it simple, minimal, and easy to understand, the page shows a graphic explanation of how the subscription works, in three steps.

1. Shop: customers can purchase the subscription on the product page or add it in their cart

2. Schedule: Subscribers select the delivery frequency based on their individual preference

3. Enjoy: Customers receive the delivery, shipped free, 2x reward points and a bonus gift

6. Personalization options

Personalization leads to profits for businesses, say 90% of eCommerce marketers. Dermalogica offers personalization by allowing subscribers to choose products for subscription, change delivery frequency or dates, etc.

When brands allow customers the flexibility and freedom to choose, make changes, and adjust their subscription options, subscribers feel more confident about signing up. They trust the brand more.

Customer confidence and trust are also factors that lead customers to share referrals and recommend brands to their loved ones, thus driving more traffic and leads to your eCommerce store.

7. Customers can easily try new products via subscription

Dermalogica keeps its customers’ needs at the center by enabling them to try new skin care products. The brand has a wide range of skin care products to choose from but customers can select the ones they want in their subscription.

By having a wide variety of products, Dermalogica not only caters to a wider audience, but also allows subscribers many choices. Moreover, when the brand adds new products to the inventory, customers can try it via subscriptions.

Subscriptions make it much easier for the brand to introduce new products to their subscribers. As the brand is in touch with the subscribers frequently, it’s easier to engage them with new products, communicate, share product recommendations, and other content.

8. Reward points with every subscription order

One of the biggest reasons customers sign up for subscriptions is the price benefit and discounts. Dermalogica gives its subscribers 2X reward points on every order. Subscribers can use the reward points to make more purchases from the Dermalogica website. This not only benefits subscribers, but it also leads to more sales for the brand.

9. Scalable subscription plan

It is essential to keep scalability in mind when designing a subscription plan. Dermalogica has this factor covered!

The brand is an international brand and has eCommerce websites for various countries. Thus, it caters to a wide range of customer base and offers its subscription plan to them.

Having a wider audience also helps the brand collect more data and deep dive into analytics and metrics that help the brand with scalability factors.

10. Customer reviews and ratings

Today’s customers consider reviews and ratings when purchasing products. Dermalogica understands this well.

The brand adds ratings and reviews of products on each of the product pages. This helps subscribers make purchase decisions.

Not only does the brand show what customers say about the products, but the brand also doesn’t miss replying to each and every customer review, showing how much they care for their customers.

11. Easy live chat option

To ensure reliable customer service, the brand has a live chat option. Visitors, customers, and subscribers can ask any question and get answers within seconds.

Customer service is a key differentiating factor between brands that helps customers decide whether or not to transact with a particular brand.

The Dermalogica website provides the live chat option on each page of the website. Shoppers can ask any question and instantly get answers, making the interaction faster, easier, and communication seamless.

Takeaways from Dermalogica subscription breakdown

Here’s a recap of the key features and lessons we could take away from the Dermalogica subscription business model.

  • Having a dedicated page for subscription makes it easy for customers to find information
  • Simplicity helps avoid confusion and complexities, thus a simple and straightforward subscription plan wins
  • Minimal text with well-written copy is more impactful that text-heavy pages and long explanations
  • Flexibility and personalization are critical factors that help enhance customer experience

The app offers a set of comprehensive features for Shopify and Shopify Plus stores. If you’re looking for an intuitive and smart subscription app for your Shopify or Shopify Plus store, you’re in luck with Appstle Subscription App.

The eCommerce market is brimming with loyalty and reward programs. Every brand is offering points and rewards.

This has led to loyalty fatigue amongst customers. Even though customers join multiple rewards programs, they end up using just one or two. They disengage with most programs over time.

But Frank And Oak, a clothing and accessories brand, has created an effective and well-designed loyalty program that is worth checking out.

This blog dissects the many features that make Frank And Oak loyalty and rewards program one of the best loyalty programs.

Let’s learn from it!

What is Frank’s Club Loyalty Program?

Frank and Oak is a brand that makes conscious clothing for men and women. The brand’s purpose is to inspire a better way of living through their garments and accessories. The Canada-based brand was started in 2012. Over the years, the brand shifted its focus to responsible fashion. The brand now ensures it sources sustainable materials, fair labor practices, and sells products that are good for the planet.

Why does the Frank And Oak customer loyalty program stand out?

Frank and Oak is a clothing and accessories brand that promotes planet-friendly living. It has a loyalty and rewards program called Frank’s Club. The brand offers benefits and perks that go beyond monetary transactions, that makes its loyalty program worth talking about. In this section, we breakdown the different features of Frank’s Club loyalty program.

1. A dedicated page for Frank’s Club

Customers prefer everything to be easy and convenient when they’re shopping online. For instance, easy navigation and information they’re looking for. This is something that Frank and Oak has accomplished for its loyalty page.

Frank’s Club has a dedicated page for the loyalty program. It shares all the information related to the program. Here are the different elements on this page:

  • Prominently displays the benefits of joining the program – earn points, special perks, and free to join
  • CTAs that make it easy for shoppers to join the program
  • Explanation of how the loyalty program works
  • Ways to earn points
  • Ways to redeem points
  • Choose from three different tiers
  • Referral program information
  • Frequently asked questions

2. Frank and Oak prioritizes its loyalty program

When you make navigation easy, it leads to good customer experience. Frank and Oak has made its rewards program visible by having a dedicated page and a tab on the home page, which makes it easier for customers to find information about the program.

How does it help?

  • Customers can easily look for the loyalty program tab
  • Customers and members can find all the information on one page
  • Members know that the brand takes its loyalty program seriously

3. Frank’s Club loyalty program is free

One of the biggest factors that keeps customers away from loyalty programs are its joining fees. Customers do not want to pay a one-time or a recurring fee.

Unless the perks and benefits you offer are extremely irresistible, customers might not pay to join a loyalty program.

Frank And Oak loyalty program is free. Free joining makes it enticing for customers to join. Once hooked to the program, they can also move to higher tiers by spending more during a year. All that customers need to do to be a part of Frank’s Club is join for free.

4. Easy explanation of how the loyalty program works

Customers can easily understand how the program works by looking at the three steps, easily explained on the page.

The brand encourages customers to be part of the ‘Club’ by telling them how simple it is. They can simply sign up without paying any fee, start earning points on every purchase they make, and enjoy many special perks and benefits.

This simple explanation helps give clarity to customers and simplifies their decision making.

5. Multiple ways to earn points

Loyalty programs that make it difficult for customers to earn points often struggle to keep customers engaged. Frank and Oak understands this. Hence, the brand has provided many ways for customers to earn points.

Here are some of the ways loyalty members earn points:

  • Points on every dollar they spend
  • Sharing reviews
  • Sharing photo reviews
  • Referring a friend
  • Following on Instagram
  • Some products offer double points
  • Birthday gift
  • Following on TikTok
  • Signing up for SMS
  • Signing up for newsletter

6. Multiple ways to redeem points

Many loyalty and reward programs allow customers to earn points easily but they make it extremely hard to redeem the points. Oftentimes customers are confused or aren’t aware about the many ways they can use or redeem their points.

This leads to lower engagement rates and less interest from customers. But Frank and Oak has made it easy for customers to redeem points. Not just that, the brand also offers many different ways to redeem points.

For instance,

  • Customers get 20% discount on 200 points
  • 30% discount on 300 points
  • 40% discount 400 points

7. Three tiers in the loyalty program

Frank and Oak has designed its loyalty program with three tiers. Customers can join the program for free and as their spending per year increases, they move to higher tiers.

This is a smart and strategic way to make customers spend more and increase the brand’s revenue. The three tiers are:

1. Community – free to join

2. Crew – spend $350

3. Inner circle – spend $1000

The higher tiers offer more benefits and perks to customers, hence, customers try to spend more and be a part of the higher tiers.

8. Frank’s Club X Referral Program

Frank and Oak has smartly combined its referral program with the loyalty program. When customers refer a friend with $15, the customers receive $15 worth of Frank’s Club points.

Here are some takeaways from this feature:

  • A strategic way to encourage customers to pay for their friends and receive an equal amount of points themselves
  • The brand has enabled customers to share the referral form via different channels, such as WhatsApp, Messenger, Facebook, Twitter, and a simple link

9. Comprehensive member dashboard

As soon as a customer joins the loyalty program for free, they get access to their personal account. The dashboard provides all the details clearly.

  • The account is personalized with the customer’s name
  • It shows the free $20 points earned for signing up
  • It has a CTA to see rewards history and perks
  • A CTA to redeem points
  • A CTA to encourage members to spend more to jump to a higher tier
  • Information about how to earn more points and how to redeem points

10. An FAQs section for the loyalty program

Lastly, the page also answers all the common questions that customers might have through an FAQs section.

When customers are new to a loyalty program or when they are contemplating joining one, they typically want to know more details before they join.

Frank’s Club FAQs include questions such as:

  • How does Frank’s Club work?
  • What happens to points if customers return products?
  • When do the tier and points expire?
  • Can they get points for previous orders?
  • Can customers transfer or combine points of two accounts?
  • Can points be redeemed along with discounts and offers?

Key takeaways from Frank’s Club loyalty program

  • Frank’s Club loyalty program is well designed, which is the first and foremost requirement for the success of any rewards program. The brand has provided three tiers in the program and customers can reach higher tiers only if they consistently shop on the website, year after year. This ensures consistent revenue to the brand.
  • The brand offers points for different types of activities, not just on sales and spends. For instance, members receive points on their birthdays, on the brand’s anniversary, and for following the brand’s different social media accounts. This increases customer engagement and interest in the brand.
  • The brand is able to offer the best digital experience and a seamless flow of communication, offering discounts, etc., because it uses an efficient Shopify Plus loyalty program app.

items.html:
According to Statista, the eCommerce market is going to surpass eight trillion USD by 2027.

2025 is going to see more growth, thanks to advancing technology, digitalization, and increasing consumer comfort with shopping online.

But with the growth of the eCommerce industry will also grow competition among brands. And so, Shopify brands will have to work a little extra hard to ensure growth, customer retention, and profitability.

This blog explores 10 growth strategies for Shopify stores for 2025.

Ecommerce and Shopify statistics 2025

Before we dive in the growth strategies, take a look at these eCommerce and Shopify statistics that throw a light on the vibrant eCommerce market, the opportunities and possibilities:

  • The global eCommerce market is expected to reach $4.8 trillion in 2025
  • By 2027, 23% of the total retail sales will take place online
  • The global retail sales will reach $9 trillion by 2032
  • Social commerce will grow as part of eCommerce
  • Artificial intelligence (AI) will help enhance eCommerce
  • There are around 5 million Shopify websites worldwide
  • 30% of websites in the US are on Shopify platform
  • 66% of Shopify website owners are small businesses

10 Growth strategies for Shopify stores for 2025

Ecommerce brands use several growth strategies to ensure consistent traffic, sales, customer engagement, and more. However, there are some growth strategies that perform extra well for eCommerce. Apply these growth strategies on your Shopify store in 2025.

1. Subscription

While you might strive for adding new and more customers to your database, having recurring business strategies can truly benefit your Shopify brand.

For instance, having a subscription program can ensure stability, recurring revenue, enhance your business management, and more.

Come 2025, the kind of brands offering subscriptions is also going to expand. From automobiles to medical to dental care, customers will have subscription offers for everything.

Here’s what you can do for your Shopify subscription program in 2025:

  • Design a subscription plan that aligns with your business goals for 2025
  • Make your subscription program relevant to your products and services, rather than copying other brands’ subscription strategies
  • Install an efficient Shopify subscription app to help you manage your subscription business model
  • Make your subscription model stand out by offering unique perks and benefits
  • Consistently monitor and optimize your subscription plan with better marketing strategies, such as SEO, content marketing, etc.

Also read: Best practices for subscription customer portal to increase conversions

Example of an automobile subscription model:

2. Membership

Just like subscription models, Shopify membership programs are also going to be a preferred growth strategy for brands.

Membership plans help eCommerce retailers build long-term customer associations, add value to customers, earn recurring revenue through membership fees, and build stronger customer communities of members.

While many brands offer membership plans, few are able to sustain it and benefit from it. Here are some ways for you to ensure an effective membership program:

  • Design a unique and meaningful membership program that adds value to members
  • Build member communities, personalize their experience, create relevant experiences for members
  • If your membership plan is old and outdated, give it a shake up with new features
  • Install a Shopify membership app to help you automate tasks, use AI, data and analytics to offer a better experience

3. Referrals

For eCommerce brands, some of the most valuable leads come from existing customers through referrals. And referral leads drive 30% higher conversion. That’s because leads that come through existing, loyal and happy customers are of a better quality.

With high competition amongst brands and everyone trying to grab customers’ attention, people tend to avoid falling into marketing gimmicks. Instead, they trust their friends and family members and recommendations that come from their close ones.

Incorporating a referral marketing strategy for your Shopify store can help your brand grow. Even word-of-mouth referrals from your existing customers can help you bring more genuine leads. Imagine if you strategically make it one of your marketing strategies.

Here’s an example from AirBnB

4. Loyalty

Ecommerce marketers know the value of customer loyalty. Repeat customers not only increase your profits, reduce your customer acquisition costs, but also boost the average order value.

That brings us to loyalty and rewards programs — one of the best Shopify strategies that drive growth. But with every other brand offering loyalty and rewards programs, customers are facing loyalty fatigue. They are participating in only those loyalty programs that add value to their experience.

Here are a few cues to help you design an effective loyalty strategy:

  • Design a loyalty program based on the requirements of your business
  • Use an efficient Shopify loyalty program app, such as Appstle Loyalty & Rewards
  • Offer benefits and perks that differentiate you from other brands
  • Ensure consistent communication and engagement with customers
  • Automate your Shopify rewards program to offer discounts, reduce churn, and increase repeat purchases

5. Influencers

69% of customers trust influencers. In 2025, customers are not only going to look at influencers for good recommendations, but they will also be able to make purchases via the influencers’ social posts and websites.

While only big brands used influencer marketing earlier, now, small and micro brands are also able to integrate influencer marketing. Besides, influencer marketing works for both D2C and B2B brands.

Let’s look at some influencer trends for 2025:

  • Artificial intelligence (AI) influencers will become more popular and accepted among consumers
  • Depending on your business and needs, choose from micro or macro influencers
  • Be selective when choosing influencers and the number of influencers. Collaborate with only those that resonate with your brand
  • Use digital tools and technology to manage your influencer marketing. For instance, enable sales of your products via the influencer’s social accounts

Here’s an example of an AI fashion influencer:

Source

6. User generated content

User generated content (UGC) is created by customers, not brands. However, brands do share UGC on their channels. UGC can be in the form of reviews, photos and videos posted on social media sites, blog posts, articles, unboxing videos, etc.

UGC works well because it is authentic content that comes from consumers and is not marketing content created by brands. Here are some ways you can test user generated content as a marketing strategy for your Shopify brand in 2025.

  • Source UGC from various online sources such as review platforms, social media, by searching your brand name, etc.
  • Invite customers to submit their content by running contests, giveaways, etc.
  • Encourage customers to tag your brand name, share your hashtags, among other ways to generate UGC
  • Ensure you ask for customers permission before reposting or resharing their content
  • Share UGC via email, newsletters, your social platforms, etc.
  • Offer rewards to customers who share UGC
  • Integrate UGC strategy with various elements of your Shopify store, for example, subscriptions, membership programs, etc.

7. Integrated marketing

With business and workflows becoming more complicated, it is a must for eCommerce brands to prioritize integrated marketing. It involves syncing various channels across departments. For instance, integrate email, SMS, WhatsApp, social media, etc. so as to create a seamless flow of information within your organization.

Also, integrated marketing helps enhance customer experience. For instance, all customer data gets collected under one umbrella, giving a more accurate understanding of customers needs.

Here’s what you can do:

  • Understand your target audience, their problems and needs
  • Set your Shopify goals and objectives for 2025 and align your marketing plan with your goals
  • Choose the channels you want to incorporate within your marketing strategy and how you will integrate them
  • Use a comprehensive Shopify app that helps you integrate various marketing tools
  • Consistently monitor your integrated marketing systems and adapt for better ROI

8. Proactive customer support

No matter how digitized your Shopify website is with the most advanced tools, you will still need to prioritize customer support. Brands that offer better customer experience will have a greater advantage.

According to Gartner, 75% of businesses will prioritize customer experience over product and price. A big part of customer experience is the quality or customer service you provide.

Here’s what your customer support should include in 2025:

  • Power Shopify customers support with AI and digital tools
  • Integrate various channels for a seamless experience
  • Incorporate tools that help you collect and analyze data, predict customer wants, and deliver personalized and relevant experiences matching individual preferences
  • Provide a mix of AI bots, digital tools, and human intervention when necessary
  • Offer a personalized customer service experience
  • Prioritize post-purchase customer support to ensure customers come back for repeat purchases

9. SEO

The need for an effective SEO plan is even greater in 2025. However, with new algorithms, new and advanced technologies, and changing consumer behaviors, Shopify retailers need to take a fresh approach with SEO in the coming year.

SEO helps brands drive traffic, improve brand awareness and visibility, offer personalized experiences to customers, and make brands more relevant to target customers.

Here’s what you must prioritize in your SEO marketing strategy in 2025:

  • Integrate AI and ML into your SEO strategies to make the most of data
  • Base your marketing plan on a deep understanding on how algorithms work
  • Hire an expert SEO and content marketing agency to help you navigate this section of your marketing plan
  • Aim to generate more engagement, clicks, and interactions through your SEO activities
  • Conduct advanced keyword research based on your target audiences needs
  • Invest in content creation, content marketing, and a long-term content plan for 2025

10. Automation

While automation is nothing new, in 2025, its use is going to become more strategic. Companies and brands are now more comfortable using automation and AI. Consumers are more accepting and expect brands to provide relevant experiences.

Here’s how you can integrate automation and offer a more intelligent experience to your Shopify customers in 2025, while growing your business:

  • Create an integrated system and flow within your company so that all the departments have information collected through customer data
  • Incorporate real-time data collection and analysis to enhance customer experience
  • Predict product demand, customer needs, identify problems before the arise with the help of automation and ML
  • Automate communication with customers to always stay connected with them
  • Ensure a secure online shopping experience for customers

Get started with your Shopify growth strategies for 2025

items.html:
Whether it’s value meals at McDonalds or insurance bundles covering home, automobile and health, product bundles have taken over every market segment.

However, the different strategies that eCommerce retailers use for product bundling vary based on their goals, products, services, and industries.

But as with most marketing strategies, there are some trends that stand out for product bundling. This blog explores producing bundling trends for 2025 that you can use for your Shopify bundles.

Let’s get started!

What is product bundling?

Product bundling is a strategy where retailers sell multiple products as one set. The products could be the same or different. Whether it’s grocery, online entertainment, insurance, or online gaming, product bundling is a marketing strategy used to increase average order value (AOV), sales, improve customer loyalty, and provide more value to customers.

There are many types of product bundles, for example:

  • Fixed bundle
  • Mixed bundle
  • Mix and match bundles
  • Make your own bundles
  • Cross-sell bundle
  • New product bundle

Product bundles offer many benefits to retailers — increase the average order value (AOV), help clear inventory, reduce marketing costs by spending on marketing bundles rather than individual products, etc. For customers, bundles provide convenience and cost benefits.

Here’s an example of product bundling.

Source

8 product bundling trends for 2025

While there are many strategies for product bundling that you can apply and experiment with, here are eight product bundling trends that will help your Shopify store stand out and win in 2025.

1. Personalized bundling

Brands are using AI and data in more sophisticated and advanced ways to provide better eCommerce experiences. These technologies are being adapted for personalized bundling or build-your-own-bundle as well.

For instance, brands allow customers to choose products for their bundles from a curated selection. This curated selection is based on the customers’ past purchases, interests, and budget patterns.

Research by McKinsey shows that brands offering personalization generate 40% more revenue. So, what does personalizing bundles entail?

  • Understand your customers through data – their shopping history, browsing behavior, preferences, likes, average order value (AOV) of past purchases, etc.
  • Identify the products that customers tend to buy together
  • Curate a selection of products that match customers’ preferences
  • Use a bundling tool that allows you to easily adapt to different product configurations
  • Keep one high-value base product as static around which customers can choose other products. This will help maintain AOV of bundles
  • Ensure you highlight the personalization factor in your communication, promotions, and marketing, so that customers become aware of this personalized offering

2. Sustainability in bundling

The sustainability factor is becoming more relevant day by day. And consumers are becoming more aware and supportive of it. For instance, 86% of online shoppers are willing to delay delivery to improve sustainability; and 24% of consumers are prioritizing eco-friendly packaging.

Ecommerce brands are addressing sustainability through various measures, whether for individual orders or bundles. Let’s look at some sustainability bundling trends you could incorporate for your Shopify bundles.

  • Use eco-friendly packaging for your Shopify bundles
  • Include products that promote sustainability
  • Include products from conscious brands
  • Highlight the environmental benefits of your bundles
  • Offer subscription-based bundles — they lead to a lesser number of orders, decrease in logistics and packaging requirements, etc.
  • Implement sustainable delivery of your product bundles
  • Incorporate recycling and reusing practices wherever possible

3. Use of augmented reality (AR) in bundling

AR allows brands to provide real-world environment visualizations digitally. Customers can make purchase decisions based on AR versions of how the products look.

For instance, when buying furniture, customers can see how the furniture looks in their house and space.

The use of AR in bundling can enable customers to view how the bundled products function together. For example, for a skin care product bundle, customers could use AR to understand how different products might work on different skin types, etc.

Here’s how you can use AR for your Shopify bundles:

  • Explore AR based on your Shopify products and services, for example, virtual try-ons for clothes, cosmetics, accessories, etc., furniture placements, etc.
  • Experiment on a small-scale to begin with and keep expanding the use of AR
  • Use AR to personalize customers’ bundles based on their choices

4. Value and benefits beyond monetary

Today’s consumers prioritize quality and value over cost and pricing. And eCommerce brands recognize this. When customers feel satisfied and see value in your products, they not only come back for more, but also spread the word and drive more customers to your site.

For example, brands are highlighting many other benefits of bundles apart from cost or price. In fact, cost-based comparison could backfire for your bundles. Hence, a better strategy is to highlight the other benefits of your bundles.

Let’s see some ways enhance your bundle value proposition:

  • Talk about the convenience factor of purchasing bundles. For example, customers can buy house cleaning solutions in bulk, avoid repeated orders, save time, etc.
  • Highlight factors such as sustainability – when customers order a product in bundles, they avoid repeat deliveries, multiple packaging for each delivery, lower carbon footprint, etc.
  • Enable customers to view how products look and perform in real-life to help make their purchase decisions easier. For example, if you sell cosmetics, display different looks and sell those products as a bundle
  • Highlight non-price attributes of the products in your bundle, for example, durability, quality, strength, etc.
  • The products in a bundle should work well together and be useful as a set. This enhances bundle value

Here’s an example:

Source

5. Bundling for gifting

Throughout the year, there are many occasions and opportunities for eCommerce retailers to promote and market products for gifting. One trend that is picking up is gifting bundles — retailers offer bundles for gifting.

For example, a bundle of cosmetics for women or men, a stationery gift bundle for kids, or a set of five onesies for babies.

Here’s an example:

Now, let’s look at some strategies and tips for gifting bundles:

  • Create bundle gifting options for diverse customer segments, for example, based on gender, age, location, etc.
  • Create bundles based on festive themes, for example, Christmas, New Year, Diwali, etc.
  • Create seasonal bundles for gifting, for example, summer bundle, winter bundle, etc.
  • Allow customers to customize their gifting bundles, for example, allow them to select the products for bundles, maximizing customer choice

6. Experiment with pricing

When it comes to bundling, one aspect that is closely related to it is pricing the bundles correctly. If priced strategically and thoughtfully, your bundles can be a gamechanger for your business. However, if not thought-through, poorly priced bundling strategy can derail your business.

Let’s look at some pricing experiments for bundling in 2025:

  • Bundle high-value slow-moving products along with best-sellers. This way you can ensure AOV of the bundle, as well as clear inventory of less popular products
  • For each bundle, calculate the total of the bundle, the profit margin and then apply a discount. This will ensure you do not incur losses in any of the bundles
  • Monitor your bundle discounts and analyze its performance and impact on your business and profits. Optimize and adjust if there’s a need for it

7. Customer-centric product bundling

Bundling is an excellent strategy to retain customers and to attract future customers. However, for bundles to have this effect, it’s important for brands to build customer-centric bundling strategies.

Here’s how to ensure a customer-centric bundling strategy for 2025.

  • Create bundles that cater to customers’ different needs and outcomes. For instance, customers may be looking to buy a set of t-shirts to last them for a year. Hence, you must ensure quality and durable products that meet their needs
  • Highlight not just discounts and pricing, but also features of products, add-on services, and deliver measurable results that help retain customers for long-term
  • Prioritize after-sales services, such as customer service, grievance addressing, post-purchase services, etc.

8. Combining products and services in bundles

Real estate bundles combine homes and insurance, automobile bundles combine car, insurance, and servicing, and water purifiers with regular cleaning services — combining products and services in bundles is a trend that is here to stay in 2025.

Combining products and services not only offers convenience to customers, it also enhances their purchase experience. Here are some ways to go about combining products and services for bundles:

  • Ensure the services and products are related and go hand in hand
  • Display and highlight the price benefit of the bundle so customers see the value in it
  • Ensure excellent customer service. For example, if you bundle software and hardware, ensure you provide technical customer support in service to ensure a seamless customer experience
