items.html:
Bundles have been an effective strategy for eCommerce stores. They help brands increase the average order value by selling more products in one go compared to individual products. One such bundles strategy is upsell product bundles.

In this blog, we focus on upsell product bundles. This comprehensive guide will tell you the benefits, best practices, and how you can create upsell bundles on your Shopify store.

Let’s get started!

What are upsell product bundles?

Upsell product bundles are designed to drive customers to make additional purchases than the products they were going to purchase initially. For instance, say a customer was interested in purchasing one t-shirt but you recommend a bundle that has a t-shirt, a trouser, and a belt to them at a discounted price. Upsell product bundles help increase the average order value (AOV). Moreover, these bundles enhance customer experience as they not only get to buy products at a discount, but also offer convenience, help customers shop better and add value to their shopping experience.

Key features of upsell product bundles

Let’s look at the key features of upsell product bundles and some aspects related to these features and how these features impact customer experience and eCommerce brands.

1. Complementary products

By offering upsell product bundles, you can drive customers to buy complementary products. For instance, if a customer is about to buy a yoga mat, you could offer a bundle that includes a yoga mat, a towel, and a yoga mat bag. This upsell bundle at a discounted rate can enhance customer experience. Moreover, customers may not have thought of buying complementary products but the bundle made their purchase decision easier.

2. Higher value

Upsell bundled products help eCommerce retailers increase the average order value. Typically, the upsell product is more expensive than the original product. Besides, the upsell product should also add more value to customers and make their purchase valuable. By packing higher-value products and services together, retailers can attract customers with more comprehensive bundles.

3. Discounts or added value

Upsell product bundles typically have a discount on them because that is one of the factors that appeals to customers. This gives customers a perception of getting financial benefit as they have to pay less. Apart from discounts, upsell bundles may also offer other benefits, such as warranties, a discount code for the next purchase, free upgrades in future, etc. All these add more value to their purchase.

4. Convenience

Today’s customers expect brands to help them shop. Offering upsell bundled products is one way to enhance customers’ shopping experience. Wondering how? It simplifies purchase decisions. When customers see they can get more value by buying a bundle, they are most likely to go for the bundle. This also leads to satisfaction and they get a good perception of the brand. Moreover, it saves customers’ time as they do not spend time looking for different products separately.

Here’s an example of an upsell product bundle from Samsung:

Source

Benefits of upsell product bundles

Here are some benefits of upsell product bundles:

1. Increased revenue

Upsell product bundles offer more than one product to customers. This increases the AOV of orders. Upsell bundles help especially where the profit margins are low. Retailers can club different products together to ensure higher margins.

2. Enhanced customer experience

You can enhance customers’ overall experience with upsell product bundles that are carefully and thoughtfully put together. By curating personalized upsell bundles, you can save customers time and effort in browsing and selecting multiple products. Relevant products put together in a bundle makes customers’ shopping experience convenient, satisfying and smooth.

3. Higher AOV

Upsell bundled products are typically of higher value compared to a single product. This leads to increased AOV, which in turn boosts overall sales and profits. Ecommerce sales can be unpredictable as they rely on seasons, sale periods, festive times, etc. During such times, maintaining AOV can help businesses ensure steady revenue, thus making AOV one of the most important metrics for eCommerce retailers. And having upsell product bundles ensures this.

4. Improved inventory management

When planned strategically, upsell bundles can also help with inventory management. For instance, bundles are an effective way to clear extra stock. Bundles also help in promoting slow-moving products. For example, if you sell gardening products and garden scissors are a slow-moving product, you could bundle it together with fast-moving items such as compost and seeds. This will help you clear scissors stock.

How to set up upsell product bundles

Here’s a step by step we follow to set up upsell product bundles on Shopify stores:

1. Identify potential bundles

How well your bundles perform depends on how appealing they are. Here’s how to put together enticing bundles:

  • Look for products that complement each other and could be bought together
  • Use past sales data to identify patterns of items being bought together
  • Choose products that offer more value to customers compared to buying a single product separately
  • Understand which complementing products would solve customers needs
  • Put together high-value and low-value products to ensure an effective AOV

2. Decide bundle structures

Once you have clarity about which products you want to bundle together, the next step is to decide the structure of your bundles. Here are some cues to help you with it:

  • Choose from different bundle types, such as tiered bundles, advanced bundles, premium bundles, etc.
  • Offering multiple bundle types will allow you to cater to diverse customer segments, hence, understand your potential customer segments and their needs, spending capacity, etc.
  • Offering multi-tier bundles also increases the potential of customers upgrading to higher-value bundles
  • Use an upsell bundle products Shopify app that offers a wide range of bundle structures

3. Set upsell product bundle pricing strategies

One of the most critical factors of bundles is its pricing strategy. It is what attracts customers and drives sales. However, pricing bundles is a bit tricky. There are many factors to consider. Here are some cues to guide you.

  • Price the bundle in such a way that customers see value in it
  • The pricing should be beneficial to customers at the same time ensure doesn’t eat into your profit
  • The bundle price should be lower than the combined price of individual products
  • Monitor pricing and profit margin continuously as prices of products may change
  • Offer tiered pricing – premium bundles at a higher price but with more discounts and savings

4. Create bundle listings

Once the pricing strategy is in place, the next step is listing the upsell product bundles on your Shopify store so that your bundles get noticed. Here’s what you can do:

  • Make the bundles simple and less complicated so customers can understand them easily
  • Make the listing visually appealing
  • Write a clear and concise description
  • If a bundled item goes out of stock, a back in stock app Shopify helps notify interested shoppers and recover potential lost sales.

Here’s a product bundle listing example:

5. Promote your upsell product bundles

Your potential customers may be spending time on different platforms. The best way to promote your bundles is to create campaigns for those platforms to promote your upsell bundles. Here are some ideas to get you started:

  • Promote bundles on various pages on your website
  • Create pop up notifications on your website
  • Promote bundles on third-party websites via web notifications
  • Create social media campaigns using tactics such as quizzes, sales, etc.
  • Use other methods, such as paid ads, etc.

6. Monitor and optimize

The market is always changing and so are customer needs and preferences. To ensure success with your upsell product bundles, monitor their performance consistently and make adjustments for best results.

  • Measure the basic KPIs, such as sales, conversions, profits, etc.
  • Monitor which bundles are performing well and which ones aren’t
  • Make changes to the ones not performing well by changing products, pricing, etc.
  • Collect customer feedback and reviews to understand customer sentiment
  • Compare your bundles with competitors via market research

Also read: 15+ E-Commerce Product Bundling Metrics You Need To Maximize Profitability

Best practices for upsell product bundles

  • Monitor and analyze customer purchase behavior and preferences
  • Segment your audience to personalize upsell product bundles for them
  • Select complementary items for bundling together to make them more appealing
  • Offer premium upgrades in bundles, for example, with tiered bundles
  • Ensure and highlight clear value and savings compared to individual purchases
  • Consider flexible, tiered pricing options to cater to diverse customer segments
  • List bundles with clear, high-quality images and descriptions
  • Highlight savings and added value prominently
  • Display bundles on product pages, during checkout, or as recommendations
  • Use cross-selling and upselling techniques to promote bundles
  • Promote bundles with email marketing, social media ads, and website banners
  • Create limited-time offers or exclusive deals to boost sales
  • Monitor performance metrics, such as conversion rates and average order value
  • Test and optimize upsell bundled products with A/B testing
  • Manage inventory levels for products and bundles
  • Plan for efficient shipping and handling
  • Offer support and guidance to customers for bundle selection
  • Follow up with customers to ensure customer satisfaction and a better customer experience
  • Gather, review and address customer feedback
  • Refine bundles based on insights and data from your Shopify store

Ready to start your Shopify upsell product bundles?

Follow the above steps and best practices to get started with a robust upsell product bundles strategy for your SHopify store. To make the strategy more successful, use an efficient Shopify product bundle app.

items.html:
Multipack bundles are a favorite among customers. A pack of three t-shirts, a bundle of five soaps, and a family pack of two icecreams—multipack bundles often offer great discounts and the convenience of shopping more in one go.

Multipack product bundles offer many benefits to eCommerce retailers too. In this blog, we explore multipack bundles, its benefits, strategies, and how to set up the best multipack bundles on your Shopify store.

Let’s get started!

What are multipack product bundles?

Multiplack product bundles, also known as wholesale product bundles, are bundles that include multiple numbers of the same or related products. In short, these bundles do not include single units, but multiple units of the same product. Wholesale product bundles enable customers to purchase larger quantities of a product at discounted rates and additional benefits.

For example, essentials that people purchase regularly, such as soap, shampoo, home cleaning products, can be easily offered and multipack product bundles. Another example is a multipack of t-shirts or socks offered at a discount.

Here’s an example of a multipack bundle:

Key features of multipack product bundles

If you’re looking to set up wholesale product bundles on your Shopify store, this section will help you understand the basic features of this bundle model.

1. Quantity-based bundling

Multipack product bundles offer multiple units or numbers of the same product in a single bundle. For example, a pack of 10 bottles of a soft drink. Customers can buy a product that they use recurrently at a discounted rate with multipack bundles. Most often, the larger the quantity, the more the discount amount.

2. Discounted pricing

Wholesale product bundles offer products at discounted rates compared to buying a single product. This makes multipack bundles cost effective and more attractive for customers. Discounted pricing helps retailers attract more customers and increase leads.

3. Convenience

For products that customers buy recurrently, for example, groceries, wellness items, or house cleaning products, multipack product bundles are more convenient for customers. They can buy products at a discounted rate and stock up for a longer duration. This eliminates the hassle of making purchases often.

4. Increased sales volume

For eCommerce retailers, Shopify product bundles are an effective way to increase sales. Retailers can apply attractive discount strategies on bundles, and benefit from higher AOV per transaction. Moreover, creating multipack bundles is also an effective way to clear inventory.

5. Enhanced marketing opportunities

There are many different ways to market and promote your multipack bundles. For instance, market them as bulk purchases, as bundles that offer value and convenience, highlight their price benefit, etc. Moreover, you can combine multipack with other sales and marketing strategies too, for example, during your annual sale.

Examples of multi-pack product bundles

Here are some examples of this type of product bundle:

1. Consumer goods

Consumer essentials such as household products are often sold in multi-pack bundles. Items such as toilet paper rolls, shampoos, house cleaning products, are fast-selling consumer goods bundles. Customers can buy recurring products at discounted prices and avoid the need for repurchasing every now and then. This adds convenience to their life and shopping habits.

2. Food and beverage

Food items with considerable shelf life are often sold in packs. This brings convenience to customers as they do not have to make purchases repeatedly. For example, a pack of five biscuit packets or a three pack potato chips bundle. Another bundle inspiration for food and beverage is a pack of six beer bottles.

3. Beauty and personal care

Another example of a multipack product bundle is beauty and personal care products. People tend to use specific products on their body and hence often buy the same product repeatedly. Instead, wholesale product bundles of personal care items can eliminate the need to make repeated purchases of the same products.

4. Office supplies

Another product that gets used up on a regular basis is office stationery. When bought in wholesale bundles, office supplies can be purchased in bulk at a lesser price. For example, a box of 10 pens or a multi-pack of printer paper or envelopes.

Benefits of multipack bundles

Multipack bundles offer benefits such as convenience and discounts to customers. But retailers also prefer this sales model because of various benefits. Here are some of the benefits.

1. Cost savings

When you offer discounts on multipack product bundles to customers, it not only provides cost benefits to them, but also increases customer satisfaction. This leads to repeat purchases, which indirectly means cost savings for eCommerce retailers. You can save on marketing costs.

2. Inventory management

Wholesale product bundles help businesses manage inventory well. For instance, retailers can move larger quantities of inventory by creating multi-pack bundles. Additionally, retailers can manage stock levels more efficiently and avoid overstocking or stockouts. Efficient inventory management helps streamline business.

3. Customer loyalty

When customers buy more with every purchase, the average order value goes up. When they experience cost benefits, they prefer to buy the same products from the same brand. This leads to enhanced customer loyalty and lifetime value. A 5% increase in customer retention can increase revenue by up to 95%, which can help boost business profits.

Considerations when setting up multi-pack bundles

Setting up Shopify product bundles can be highly beneficial to your business. However, it has to be well planned. Here are some factors you must consider when setting up multipack bundles:

1. Pricing strategy

An effective pricing strategy for multipack bundles should offer a balance between perceived value to the customer and profitability to the eCommerce brand. Here are some cues to help you price your bundles in the right manner:

  • The multipack bundle price should show the savings for customers
  • Tiered pricing strategy can help increase AOV. For example, a pack of 5 at a higher discount compared to a pack of 3
  • Avoid offering high discounts as it can devalue the products
  • Conduct competitor research to understand the pricing standards in the multipack market
  • Ensure your bundle reflects the value it offers so that it appeals more to your customers

2. Inventory management

Multipack product bundles could end up complicating inventory management for you but it can also help you manage the inventory more efficiently. However, you can avoid complications by following some best practices.

  • Track and monitor demand and sales for individual products and bundled products. This will help you plan your stock in a way to avoid overstocking or stockouts
  • Use past sales data to understand product demand and forecast inventory stock requirements
  • Create separate inventories for individual products and multipack product bundles for better management

3. Marketing wholesale product bundles

Today’s customers do not care too much about price. They want to see how a product solves their problem and fulfills their needs by adding value. That’s why, when marketing your Shopify product bundles, you must consider positioning your bundles in a way that highlights its value proposition. Here’s what you can do:

  • Highlight factors other than price and cost benefits, such as convenience, quality, durability, ease of shopping, and other perks attached to bundles
  • Create campaigns on various channels to highlight the value proposition. For example, websites, social media, email, advertisements, etc.
  • Display comparative value between individual product and multipack bundle
  • Highlight all benefits, such as reduced packaging making it eco-friendly, saving time, etc.

4. Product selection

When choosing products for multipacks, you must consider a few points. For instance, if the product is something customers would buy in a pack, if its discounted pricing will benefit customers as well as not eat into your profits, etc. Here are some other things to consider:

  • Choose products on which you are able to offer a discount
  • Pick products that are fast-selling and preferred as packs
  • Ensure the multi-pack offers more value than just the price
  • Choose products based on past sales data, market trends, etc.

How to create multipack bundles on Shopify

There are multiple aspects to setting up and running a bundles model. To get your multipack bundles strategy started, follow these actionable steps.

1. Define a clear strategy

One of the first steps is to create a clear strategy for your multipack product bundles. Some things to consider are:

  • What is your goal – increase AOV, clearing out slow-moving inventory, or targeting customers looking for cost savings?
  • Once you narrow down your goal, you will have clarity about selecting products, pricing, how to market your wholesale bundles, etc.

2. Select the right products for your bundles

Selecting the right products is critical because you may create bundles with products you think are great but what if customers aren’t interested in them? Here are a few factors to consider when selecting products.

  • Use past sales data to determine which products are in high demand and are bought multiple times by customers
  • Create personalized product bundles. For instance, if customers buy a multipack of beverages, offer them a multipack of snacks to go with it
  • Another type of products to select are slow-moving items. By putting them into a wholesale pack, you can offer discounts and entice customers to buy them, thus, ensuring the products get sold faster

3. Determine multipack product bundle pricing

Pricing your Shopify product bundles strategically is critical. Not only should the pricing be beneficial and attractive to customers, it should also be profitable for your business. Consider these pricing strategies and best practices.

  • Calculate the total cost of products in the multipack, including shipping, packaging, storage, etc. This will help you do a thorough analysis of the product cost and guide your pricing strategy
  • Next, determine the amount of discount you must offer. Ensure your discount doesn’t eat into your profits and does not lead to losses
  • Price the multipack bundle in such a way that there is a noticeable discount compared to when a single product is bought separately

4. Promote your wholesale product bundles

Once your product bundles are set to be sold, promote them for better visibility and sales. Use these strategies:

  • Create campaigns to highlight the bundle benefits and value proposition
  • Create different campaigns for various platforms
  • Optimize SEO by adding keywords relevant to multipack and wholesale to improve visibility of your bundles

5. Track and monitor bundle performance

The market, customer preference, and trends are continuously changing, and hence, your multipack product bundles may not remain relevant forever. Here’s what you can do to keep them relevant:

  • Monitor your product bundle sales, identify trends, and gaps so you can make adjustments
  • Collect customer feedback and reviews to enhance your bundles
  • Keep making adjustments and changes to pricing, products, marketing campaigns, etc.

Get started with multipack product bundles for your Shopify store

Offering wholesale product bundles is a great way to attract customers and increase AOV. However, there are a lot of aspects to consider when running a multipack bundle offer. From planning and identifying products to pricing and promoting them correctly.

items.html:
Product bundles are becoming a favorite amongst customers and retailers. Bundles not only offer discounts and convenience to customers, they help retailers increase AOV and speed up sales. There are different product bundle types.

In this blog, we focus on fixed product bundles – one of the most common types of bundles, yet profitable for eCommerce brands. If you want to learn what fixed product bundles are, how to plan fixed bundles for Shopify, how to market and optimize them for profits, and which is the best fixed product bundles app, this blog is for you.

Read on!

What are fixed product bundles?

Fixed product bundles include a set of predetermined products or services sold together as a bundle. The products or services in fixed bundles cannot be changed or customized. Fixed bundle format is commonly used in industries such as Software as a Service, D2C, B2B, retailers selling products and services, etc.

Fixed bundles simply purchase for customers, and offer convenience and price benefits to them. For eCommerce retailers, this bundle type helps increase and speed up sales, increase average order value, and enhance competitiveness. An example of fixed product bundles is McDonalds combo of burger, fries, and coke offered at a discounted rate compared to buying these three items individually.

Here’s another example of a fixed product bundle:

Source

What are the benefits of fixed product bundles?

According to the National Bureau of Economic Research, product bundles can increase profits by up to 30%. In this section, we look at more benefits of fixed bundles and how they impact eCommerce businesses.

1. Streamlined inventory management

With fixed bundles, you can get a sense of demand for particular products and hence forecast and predict your inventory requirements. This helps reduce stockouts, overstocking, and streamlines inventory management. You can use past data and purchase history to forecast inventory needs. Streamlining inventory management can also help reduce warehouse storage costs, and avoid supply chain inefficiencies.

2. Predictable pricing for customers

Creating fixed product bundles helps offer consistent pricing, making it easy for customers to make purchase decisions and purchases. Customers do not spend time evaluating prices of individual products or bundles as they are aware of the fixed pricing. This has benefits — customers build trust in the brand. This also helps build long-term associations between brands and customers.

3. Enhanced customer experience

Fixed product bundles help enhance customer experience in many ways. For instance, customers get to buy bundles that include complementary products or services together, hence they do not need to buy products individually. In a market that is overloaded with options and choices, ensuring easy purchase decision-making is a key factor in driving sales and customer satisfaction.

4. Boost average order value

For online businesses, maintaining AOV is critical in ensuring consistent revenue and profits. That’s another plus point of product fixed bundles. Compared to selling individual products, you can sell a curated selection of products together, increasing the order value. Moreover, bundles are often offered at discounted pricing, which encourages more customers to buy them.

5. Easy marketing and promotion

Instead of marketing and promoting individual products, you can market and promote whole product bundles. This has many benefits – lesser marketing costs, reduced efforts, and a more simplified marketing process. As fixed product bundles offer higher perceived value, it is easy to attract customer attention and drive sales. Use a Shopify bundles app that enables automating marketing and promotion via the app.

How to plan your fixed product bundles?

No matter which industry you belong to and what products you offer, you can come up with an effective fixed bundle for your brand. Follow these steps to get started with setting up a fixed bundle strategy for your Shopify store.

1. Identify products

Different customer segments have specific requirements and preferences. A one-size-fits-all approach may not work when planning fixed product bundles. Hence, one of your first steps should be to put together the right products in different bundles. Here are some strategies to apply when identifying products:

  • Create different bundles for different customer segments
  • Choose products based on past data, research, and market trends
  • Put together high-value products with

Here’s an example:

Source

2. Decide bundle configuration

Planning product fixed bundles is not as simple. To make your bundles a success, you have to think strategically. Here are a few factors to consider:

  • The number of products in each bundle
  • The specific products in each bundle
  • The perceived value of each bundle
  • Pricing of each bundle

3. Decide pricing strategies

One of the most critical factors of fixed product bundles is its pricing. If the price does not offer enough value or discounts, customers may not find it attractive. Moreover, your pricing strategy should also be profitable and make business sense. Here are some common pricing strategies for product bundles.

  • Offer a fixed discount on the entire bundle
  • Apply value pricing strategy that highlights the value of the bundle
  • Keep adjusting pricing strategies based on the market and product pricing

Also read: Best Pricing Strategies For Ecommerce Product Bundles on Shopify

4. Assess customer preference

Customer preferences and market trends keep changing. And hence, it’s important to ensure that your product bundles remain relevant to market needs and trends. Here’s how you can ensure it:

  • Continuously assess market trends and customer preferences
  • Conduct customer surveys to understand what customers want
  • Keep an eye on market trends and be flexible enough to adapt to changes

Best practices for managing fixed product bundles

1. Monitor and review bundle performance

Tracking and monitoring the performance of your product fixed bundles is critical as it gives you an understanding of sales, customer satisfaction, and whether you need to address any gaps. Here are some key performance indicators (KPIs) you must monitor:

  • Monitor which bundles are selling more and which are selling less
  • Monitor customer feedback and sentiment on your fixed product bundles
  • Review the profit margin on the bundles so you can optimize your pricing strategies to ensure more profitability

2. Adjust bundles based on trends

To stay relevant to customers and in the market, you must ensure you’re changing your product fixed bundles based on trends. Here are three trends you must monitor:

  • Customer preferences and needs change based on market trends. Hence, keep an eye on customer behavior, ask for feedback, and adjust your bundles based on their needs
  • To stay competitive in the market, you must keep an eye on what your competitors are offering in their product bundles
  • Monitor seasonal trends, the larger market trends, and products that are in high demand to adjust your bundles from time to time

3. Ensure inventory and pricing management

Inventory and pricing are two of the most critical factors for fixed product bundles. You cannot change products in fixed bundles, hence it is important to ensure you have enough stock of products to fulfill sales. Here are a few things you can do:

  • Manage product inventory to ensure there are no stockouts
  • Change pricing of product bundles based on price changes of products to ensure profitability and value to customers
  • Use a Shopify product bundling app to notify about diminishing inventory to avoid stockouts

4. Highlight and promote bundles

Even if you’ve created the best bundles in the market, unless and until consumers know about them, your bundling strategy won’t succeed. That is why promoting and marketing your bundles is important. Here’s how you can do it:

  • Promote and highlight your fixed product bundles on your website and landing pages
  • Create targeted and personalized email campaigns to promote bundles
  • Apply cross-selling and upselling strategies across channels such as social media, messaging, etc.

Tracking and optimizing your fixed product bundles

To ensure success of your fixed bundles on Shopify, continuously tracking and optimizing is a must. This will ensure that your fixed bundles are relevant to customers and you’re able to satisfy customers. Here are a few things you can do:

  • Monitor key metrics such as the number of sales, the number of conversions, customer feedback, return rate, drop in sales from previous periods, etc. monitoring these will help you determine where adjustments are needed
  • Once you collect data from key metrics, look for insights that can help you optimize bundles. For instance, identify high-selling product bundles and use these as benchmarks to optimize other bundles. Similarly, you can identify bundles that are not performing well and make adjustments of products and pricing to drive more sales
  • One of the best strategies is testing different product fixed bundle configurations and pricing. You could try A/B testing to see which bundles are performing better. For pricing, you could try strategies such as premium pricing, added discounts, reducing discounts, etc.

items.html:
Product bundles have become a favorite of both customers and eCommerce merchants.

And why not! Bundles offer discounts to customers and for merchants, they drive an increase in the average order value (AOV).

There are different types of product bundles for Shopify. One type is ‘nested product bundles’. This blog deep dives into nested product bundles, what they are, and how your Shopify store can make the most of it.

Let’s get started!

What are nested product bundles?

Nested product bundles refer to a strategy in which there are bundles within a bundle. Each nested bundle includes a specific set of products. Nested bundles offer a wide variety of products to customers, combining products in different ways to meet specific customer needs.

For example, in an electronics bundle, there could be multiple bundles within the overarching bundle. Here’s what it could look like:

1. Basic bundle: smartphone + charger + earbud

2. Bundle 2: Basic bundle + screen guard + phone case

3. Bundle 3: Bundle 2 + warranty + charging pad + bluetooth speaker

What is the difference between nested and simple product bundles?

Benefits of nested product bundles

Ecommerce stores that want to grow and increase revenue must definitely explore the many advantages that Shopify product bundles can offer. Here are some:

1. Enhanced customer choice and customization

Nested bundles on Shopify offer multiple tiers of products to choose from. Compared to a single bundle that customers have to either buy or leave, nested bundles provide more choice to customers. Customers can choose from different tiers of bundles based on their needs and budgets. For instance, a yoga nested bundle could have these options:

  • Bundle 1: Yoga mat, yoga wear
  • Bundle 2: Bundle 1 + meditation cushion + yoga towel
  • Bundle 3: Bundle 2 + online yoga class subscription + aromatherapy diffuser

Ecommerce brands can offer more choices and customized bundles to customers through nested bundles.

2. Increased sales and average order value

Maintaining sales and average order value (AOV) is a must for businesses to ensure profitability and growth. This can be achieved through strategic steps. One such strategy is nested product bundles.

Nested bundles offer multiple choices. Additionally, it provides an opportunity for upselling. With high-value bundle tiers that offer enticing products in a set, customers can easily get attracted to buying these Shopify product bundles, thus, increasing the AOV.

3. Improved inventory management

The competency with which you manage your Shopify store’s inventory can make or break your business. This is another area where nested product bundles help make inventory management easy.

With nested bundles, tracking and managing stock becomes quite easy as you are aware of how much stock you’d require. It reduces the complexity associated with inventory management. Some of the benefits are streamlined order fulfillment, reduced stock discrepancies, faster processing time, and more efficiency. All these aspects also lead to an increase in customer satisfaction.

4. Increased customer satisfaction and loyalty

What do today’s customers want when shopping online? Convenience, ease, and personalization are some factors customers look for. Nested product bundles combine complementary products and offer options to choose from. This saves time and effort in searching for single products, making customers’ shopping experience easy and convenient.

Moreover, cost savings due to discounts make it a good deal for customers. What is more, brands often enable customization of nested bundles. This enhances customer experience to another level as customers can purchase products that are relevant to their needs and likes.

How to plan your nested product bundles?

Follow these actionable steps to ensure your nested bundles are based on a strong foundation with all the basics in place.

1. Identify products for nested bundles

Select products for your bundles strategically so that both your customers and your business benefit. Here are some cues to help you identify the right products for your bundles.

  • Choose products that complement each other
  • Bundle up products in such a way that bundles add value to customers
  • Mix up high-value and low-value products in each bundle tier to maintain AOV
  • Introduce newly launched products in nested bundles

2. Analyze customer needs and preferences

When planning your Shopify product bundles keep your customers at the center. You may put together the best products and create bundles, but if they don’t match your customers’ needs and preferences, you find it hard to sell them.

Here’s what you can do:

  • Analyze past data to understand customer preferences
  • Run customer surveys asking them about their needs and preferences
  • Conduct market research to understand what consumers want
  • Look at your competitor brands and what are they offering in their Shopify bundles
  • Segment customers so you can create relevant product bundles

3. Set up bundle pricing strategies

People prefer bundles and get attracted to bundles for the price benefits and discounts. And hence, it’s a must to strategically think about pricing. Proper pricing can help you stand out in the crowded bundles market. Here are some pricing strategies for nested product bundles:

  • Offer fixed amount discount on each nested bundle
  • Offer a percentage discount on each bundle
  • Take a cost plus pricing approach — calculate the total of each bundle and then add a predetermined profit margin on each bundle
  • Use value-based pricing strategy — price each bundle based on the value it offers
  • Use psychological pricing strategy — introduce a less attractive bundle to make the other high-value bundles look more attractive

4. Determine nested product bundle structure

One of the most critical steps is to decide the structure of your nested bundles for Shopify. For instance, there may be various complementing products that you might want to include in the bundles, but which ones should you pair in which bundle? Let’s explore some strategies.

  • Decide what will go in the parent bundle (the big, high-value bundle that includes all the smaller bundles) and in the child bundles (the smaller nested bundles)
  • Your strategy may change based on your goals, such as the need to maintain AOV or the need for variety in each bundle, or value provided to customers in each bundle, etc.

Best practices for managing nested product bundles

Ensure you follow these best practices to make the most of your nested bundle strategy on your Shopify store.

1. Regularly reviewing and updating bundles

Just like any other business strategy, you must monitor the performance of your Shopify nested bundles. Use Shopify apps that allow you to automate collecting data about which bundles are selling, and which are not. Based on the insights you gather, keep making necessary changes and optimizing your bundle strategy. For instance, you might require to change a few products in some of the bundles, or add an additional tier, or introduce a new product in one of the bundles.

2. Monitor customer feedback

One of the best ways to optimize your nested product bundles is to keep your customers at the center. There are many ways to do so, including customer feedback. Here are some things you can do around feedback.

  • Consistently collect customer feedback
  • Collect customer feedback via other methods, such as social listening, customer reviews, etc.
  • Address customer feedback and ensure you incorporate it into your bundle strategy

3. Ensuring accurate inventory and pricing updates

Managing your product inventory with bundles can be a bit more complex than not having a bundle strategy. The reason is because there are multiple products involved, and multiple bundles, too. A slight change in the price of one of the products would require you to make changes in the inventory and pricing updates to all bundles.

Here are some practices to follow:

  • Review inventory and prices on a regular basis
  • Automate inventory and pricing updates
  • Set up notifications for stockouts and low inventory
  • Set up automated messages to inform customers about pricing changes, etc.
  • Use an intuitive Shopify bundle app for seamless operations

4. Optimizing bundle presentation on your eCommerce store

The effectiveness of your nested product bundles relies on how they are presented on your Shopify store. For instance, if the information mentioned is confusing, or if the design is poor, it could mislead customers. Here are a few factors to keep in mind for optimizing your Shopify product bundles.

  • Write clear headings, subheadings, and descriptions
  • Highlight benefits, value, and discounts/ savings
  • Use high-quality, attractive images
  • Make the checkout process easy

Marketing your nested product bundles

Unless you market your nested bundles well, you may not be able to achieve your goals. Here are a few tried and tested marketing strategies:

1. Create effective bundle promotions

Even though nested bundles are attractive and engaging for customers, retailers still have to focus on promoting these bundles via various strategies. The average person comes across hundreds of advertisements every day and hence, without promotions, customers might soon forget about your bundles. Let’s look at some promotion strategies for nested bundles.

  • Offer attractive prices on bundles. Highlight savings and the percentage of discount on each bundle
  • Create limited-time nested bundles to make them more enticing and to encourage FOMO-driven buying by customers
  • Create seasonal bundles based on customers’ needs according to different seasons

2. Leverage email and social media marketing for bundles

Depending on your product type and industry, you must make use of email marketing and social media to promote your nested bundles for Shopify. With 4.48 billion email users the world over, it’s no surprise that 81% of companies continue to use email marketing. Meanwhile, more than 5 billion people use social media, making it one of the best platforms for promoting products and services.

  • Create personalized nested bundle email campaigns based on customers’ past purchase data
  • Create upselling and cross-selling campaigns to be shared on social media and emails
  • Offer exclusive discounts for email subscribers and social media users

3. Use targeted ads and retargeting strategies to increase visibility

Data is one of the best assets for eCommerce stores. It enables you to craft targeted and relevant marketing campaigns that bring better results. Here’s how you can create targeted ads and retargeting strategies for your Shopify store:

  • Use data from customers’ past purchase patterns
  • Understand and predict customers through their current actions on your site
  • Use different platforms to meet customers with targeted strategies

Get started with nested product bundles for your Shopify business

Nested bundles benefit both customers and your eCommerce business. With multiple options to choose from, more convenience to customers, better value-add, and higher engagement opportunities, it is a strategy worth exploring, if you haven’t already. And to get you started, Apple Bundles offers the most comprehensive set of features.

items.html:
Product bundling is a tried-and-true strategy in e-commerce, and for good reason—it can significantly increase average order value and boost sales.

But simply setting up bundles isn’t enough. To truly capitalize on bundling, you need to continually fine-tune your approach.

This is where tracking the right product bundling metrics comes into play.

In this blog, we’ll dive deep into all the essential product bundling metrics you need to know to maximize profitability.

18 Metrics to Determine Which Products You Should Bundle

To create product bundles that truly connect with your customers, the first step is to gather comprehensive information about them.

Below are 18 essential product metrics to monitor to keep your bundling strategy ahead of the competition.

1. Top and Worst Sellers

Keep a record of your product catalog to know what items sell well and which ones are your worst performers. This aids in crafting good bundles to offer.

Here are some tips to track this:

  • Keep track of the revenue earned from the items in the inventory that give a profit to the company
  • Seek out certain items with record-low sales that are constructive to others
  • Combine faster-moving items with items that are moving slowly
  • Reduce dead stock and holding costs
  • Market new items concurrently with widely compatible and highly sought-after items

Bundling high-performers with underperformers helps achieve a net positive sales outcome as well as destroys the stagnated inventory.

Pro tip: Employ this strategy to introduce a new product line and at the same time gain market traction by availing the products along with favorite items.

2. Annual Growth

Annual growth is the measure of how much value the product has changed in the period of one year. Use this metric to:

  • Track year-over-year growth of individual items
  • Decide if a product should be in a bundle
  • Identify potential bundle anchors (high-growth items)
  • Find products needing a sales boost through bundling

Analyzing annual growth helps you make smart bundling decisions based on real sales data.

3. Profitability Analysis on SKU Basis

SKU profitability indicates the extent to which an individual product does better as compared to all other products. This metric:

  • Removes non-controllable costs
  • Shows profitability for each unit sold
  • Highlights defects in the selling technique
  • Enables you to react swiftly

By focusing on SKU profitability, you can create bundles that maximize your profit margins and customer satisfaction.

4. Listing Profitability

Listing profitability includes evaluating the performance of a certain item on a particular sales channel. You’d use this metric in deciding which areas to focus your bundles on for maximum impact.

By studying this data, you can:

  • Explore opportunities in specific products and their best channel
  • Create products that are best suited across different bundles
  • Work on the customer engagement levels in those channels that are doing poorly
  • Improve conversions in all sales channels

Use this knowledge to adjust your multichannel selling strategy.

For instance, a bundle that is performing well on your site may require some changes before it gets listed on a marketplace. So, you should not ignore the value of this metric in finding the best way of bundling the products for different channels.

5. Trending Profitability

Trending profitability is most useful in identifying the best period to push for bundles. With time to reverse engineer and track product trends and synergies, one can;

  • Discover times of the year with specific demands
  • Offer well-structured fast-moving bundled products
  • Lure people to buy gifts during the holiday seasons
  • Anticipate customer needs

For example, booksellers may place together items in the same genre or series, expecting that customers would be willing to buy other products in the same genre. There is evidence in the market to support that selling this move will tremendously increase sales.

Remember, effective bundling isn’t just about product selection—it’s also about timing. Use the metrics provided by profitable transactions to provide the customers with resulting bundles at optimal moments enhancing sales and satisfaction at the same time.

6. Sales Volume

Sales volume measures the total number of bundles sold over a specific period. This is an objective index measure of the acceptance and demand of bundles from customers.

By counting sales volume specifics of customer bundles that are successful can be acknowledged and what adjustments are needed can also be determined:

  • Benchmarking the bundle sales performance against the sale of standalone products
  • Analyze time trends of bundle sales for seasonality patterns
  • Advising on the volume of inventory to procure bundled packages
  • Discovering bundles that do well in sales and can be made into more

7. Revenue

Revenue computation for bundled packages highlights the sales that bundles generate in a particular period. This is necessary in assessing the effectiveness of the bundling strategy employed.

It is also possible to evaluate the impact of the promotion by looking at the sales from the bundling and comparing it with standalone item sales.

Now, you can:

  • Utilize the revenue generated from a package to see more engaging combinations
  • Study growth in revenue derived from the bundles and compare with growth in overall sales
  • Determine the price of these bundles in the future
  • Study the profitability of these bundles in terms of types (complementary bundle versus same category bundle)

8. Average Order Value (AOV)

Average order value measures the amount of money spent for a purchase between orders that are bundled with other items and orders that are not bundled. An increase in AOV in bundled orders signifies that your packing strategy is working since it persuades customers to spend more.

With this data, you can:

  • Track trends in AOV over a long time to determine if bundling has any long-term effects on the behavior of the consumers
  • Segment AOV by customer types to identify which groups respond best to bundles
  • Use AOV insights to guide marketing efforts for bundles
  • Experiment with bundle compositions to optimize AOV

9. Conversion Rate

Conversion rate measures the percentage of visitors who purchase a bundle compared to those who visit the bundle page.

This metric is important for evaluating how effective the bundling strategy has been in turning non-customers into customers. A high conversion rate suggests that shoppers find your bundle offers attractive and appropriately targeted.

Here’s how this data can help:

  • Compare conversion rates for different bundles to identify top performers
  • Analyze conversion rate trends over time to assess bundling strategy changes
  • Use conversion rate data to optimize bundle page design and layout
  • Experiment with bundle incentives (e.g., discounts, free shipping) to boost conversion rates

10. Bundle Profit Margin

Bundle profit margin analyzes the profitability of each bundle by subtracting the cost of the bundled items from its selling price.

This metric is particularly relevant in evaluating whether your bundling strategy is going to be financially viable. Understanding the profit levels will help us know what bundles can comfortably be promoted or which ones need to be adjusted.

11. Cost of Customer Acquisition (CAC)

This metric indicates the proper physical investment required to attract new clients with bundled offers rather than on individual items. A less favorable value of CAC being attributed to bundles means that the acquisition is much cheaper.

12. Customer Lifetime Value (CLV)

CLV looks into the long-term economic activity associated with those customers who purchase bundles of products compared to those who purchase individual products.

This metric helps in understanding the extent to which bundling benefits customers and retention.

  • Assess customer CLV for both customers who buy bundles and customers who buy individual products
  • Research and list the bundles with the highest revenue and include them in marketing activities
  • Apply CLV to analyze the customers and customize offers for bundles to them

13. Bundle Redemption Rate

Bundle redemption rate is the measure of how frequently discounted bundles or promotional bundles are redeemed compared to other promotional incentives. This metric assists in analyzing the success of sales generated by bundle-related promotions.

When the bundle redemption ratios are at the higher end, then it means that the promotions based on the cupboards are reasonable to the users.

14. Bundle Engagement Metrics

Bundle engagement metrics, such as click-through rates (CTR) on bundle promotions and interaction with bundle-related content, provide valuable insights into how well your bundles are being marketed.

High engagement indicates that your bundles are appealing and compelling to your audience. Tracking these metrics helps you refine your marketing strategies to better capture customer interest.

15. Inventory Turnover

Inventory turnover shows the rate of how quickly bundled products get sold against stand-alone items.

A quicker inventory turnover per bundle suggests that such combinations fly off the shelves, meaning customers find them valuable. This metric is vital for effective inventory management, reducing carrying costs and enhancing liquidity.

16. Return Rate

Return rate measures the percentage of bundles returned by customers, providing insight into the effectiveness of your bundling strategy.

Here’s what you need to do:

  • Examine the differences in return rates for various bundles, as well as whether any problems arise
  • Determine the causes of return in order to reconfigure bundle contents or amend bundle descriptions
  • Compile data on return rate to help orient approaches to managing quality and customer feedback
  • Deal with bundle variations that are expected to reduce return rates while maximizing profitability

17. Customer Feedback and Reviews

Customer feedback and reviews specifically related to bundles provide direct insights into how well these offerings meet customer needs and expectations.

Bundling feedback can assist e-commerce merchants in strategies that work while negative feedback assists in diagnosing pitfalls. Such feedback should be received and assessed often since such information helps in improving customer bundles’ satisfaction and retention.

18. Repeat Purchase Rate

Repeat purchase rate (RPR) is the ratio of customers who come back to buy the bundles again.

It serves as an indicator of how satisfied or loyal the customer is. A high repeat purchase rate indicates a higher relevance of the bundles to buyers and a higher probability of making another purchase on-site.

You can use this valuable product bundle metric to:

  • Compare repeat purchase rates across different bundles to identify the most popular combinations
  • Use repeat purchase data to segment loyal customers and create targeted marketing campaigns
  • Analyze factors driving repeat purchases, such as bundle composition, pricing, or promotions
  • Optimize bundles to increase repeat purchase rates, focusing on customer favorites and high-performing combinations

items.html:
Product bundling is the new e-commerce obsession. And, for all the right reasons!

According to a Harvard Business School Study, Nintendo uses mixed bundling to boost unit sales by as much as 100,000 units with a single campaign.

Source: ScienceDirect

But do you ensure you still remain profitable when providing bundled items at such steal deals to your customers?

That’s where the bundle pricing strategy comes in.

The pricing strategy of your product bundles can either help you double your revenue or start cutting into your profits.

What is Bundle Pricing?

Source: Omnisend

Bundle pricing is when merchants take two or more products and sell them together at a lower price than if they were purchased separately. This tactic prompts consumers to buy bundles as they offer a good deal over single purchases.

By selling product bundles, retailers can increase their order value per sale and move closer to their revenue goals. For instance:

A computer store sells these items:

  • Laptop: $800
  • Mouse: $30
  • Keyboard: $50
  • Laptop bag: $40

The store makes up a “Work–From–Home” bundle that comprises all of these items and offers it for sale at $875. Customers find this particular bundle attractive for various causes:

It encompasses everything required to set up an office at home.

It’s convenient for customers not to search for individual pieces of things.

When the bundle is bought, customers save forty-five bucks.

Additionally, by bundling slow moving goods like laptop bags with popular ones, the store also benefits.

Although bundle pricing may cut profits initially, Shopify stores can make it up by selling more bundles hence increasing long-term revenues.

Why Is Bundle Pricing Effective?

According to McKinsey, 35% of all Amazon purchases come from the product recommendation section, which often includes the “buy it with” bundles.

Source: Amazon

Product bundling is a great way to grow your business and give customers something they can touch. The key is to find the right mix of products that will benefit both parties involved – this means more sales for you and better value for them.

Let’s look at some of the benefits of bundle pricing in detail:

1. Offloading Less Popular Products

Retailers can use bundle pricing to rid themselves of slow-moving inventory. This involves bundling slow-moving items with the best-selling ones so as to get rid of dying stock. In this way, a customer is introduced to something that he or she would not ordinarily consider purchasing.

2. Increasing Customer Spend

The value of bundles usually makes customers buy more than what they had intended.

Instead of just buying one thing, customers may go for a package that contains many items at an affordable price. This helps retailers increase their average order values by effectively using the technique of upselling customers.

3. Simplifying Shopping Experience

Product bundles make shopping easier.

By grouping complementary items, retailers save customers time and effort.

For instance, gift bundles are designed to make gift-giving easier, these curated sets often revolve around themes or occasions.

They save shoppers time and decision-making stress, especially during busy gift-giving seasons. These bundles often come in attractive packaging, adding to their appeal as ready-to-give presents.

4. Attracting Deal-Seekers

Did you know coupons and discounts (39.3%) are the second most encouraging factor for people to shop online?

Bargain hunters love bundles.

Attractive bundle deals should be able to lure in even non-traditional bargain shoppers into your doorsteps; hence expanding your market base and increasing total sales volume for any season.

5. Launching New Products

Bundling helps introduce new products in the market quickly and efficiently. By doing this, a retailer will be leveraging popular products that are available already so as to attract attention towards the new ones.

The idea reduces risks involved in rolling out completely new products lowering initial sales numbers at an early stage.

How To Calculate Bundle Pricing?

Calculating effective bundle pricing involves strategic decision-making based on data analysis. Here’s a step-by-step guide:

1. Select Products for Bundling

Rely on data as you decide which products to pair together.

Check customer behavior, purchase history, and product metrics of performance. This eliminates guesswork and identifies combinations that can push sales.

The following key factors should be considered:

  • Complementary products
  • Popular items coupled with slow-moving stock
  • Seasonal relevance

2. Determine Optimal Pricing

It is a given that the price of bundles must be less than the cost of individual products.

Here, the magnitude of the discount has significant implications on sales. For instance:

  • 10% discount: Most customers would rather buy separate products.
  • 45% discount: Bundle preference goes up sharply.

Find a sweet spot that draws customers while remaining profitable.

3. Set Bundle Size

The number of items in a bundle should correspond with the pricing strategy. But, generally speaking:

  • High-priced goods: Smaller bundles work best
  • Low-priced goods: Bigger bundles perform better

4. Analyze Competitor Strategies

Research competitor offerings in bundles and discounts provided by them on their websites. That information will help you refine your approach and keep you competitive in the market.

5. Use Data Analytics

Combine browsing information and shopping cart data for analysis purposes. This provides insights into what customers prefer and how effective your bundle is.

6. Trial and error

So as you put into place a bundle pricing strategy, monitor how it is performing. Be ready to alter your tactics based on what sales figures and customer feedback say.

7. Profit margin considerations

Make sure that the offering of bundle discounts does not reduce the profit of the company significantly. Do a thorough analysis of how much different combinations could impact overall margins.

Different Bundle Pricing Strategies You Should Look Into

It is commonly assumed that bundling is just simply adding 2+ products in a pack and your sales will magically multiply. But there are so many different kinds of product bundle pricing types –

1. Fixed Discount Pricing

This strategy involves providing a fixed amount of discount in relation to the costs of individual items.

For instance:

A laptop ($800), wireless mouse ($50), and laptop bag ($70) are bundled in an online electronics store.

  • Individual total: $920
  • Bundle price: $850
  • Fixed discount: $70

The method is simple and easy to grasp the value by customers.

2. Percentage Discount Pricing

Applying a percentage discount on the total value of items in the bundle.

For example:

Three supplements (all priced at ₹780 each), have been bundled by an e-commerce health and wellness retailer.

  • Total value: ₹2340
  • Bundle discount: 10%
  • Final bundle price: ₹2106

This approach can provide more perceived value for money to customers, especially in cases of high-priced bundles.

3. Tiered Pricing

Offer multiple options at different price ranges for bundling.

For example:

Online fitness shop provides equipment bundles such as;

  • Basic ($99): Resistance bands, jump rope, workout guide
  • Standard ($199): Everything in Basic + dumbbells and yoga mat
  • Premium ($299): Everything in Standard + kettlebell and foam roller pair

In this way, different customer requirements and budgets can be served through this pricing model hence potentially boosting overall sales.

4. Buy One, Get One (BOGO) or Buy One, Get More

This is a simple strategy – giving free or reduced-priced products when another one is bought.

As per a survey by AMG Strategic Advisors, 93% of customers prefer Buy-One-Get-One (BOGO) bundles.

For instance, buying any bestseller and getting a classic novel free is what an online bookstore has.

This will increase sales of particular products or expose customers to new ones.

5. Mix and Match

Customers can combine products from a range of choices to make their own packages. The idea here is to first find the total cost of packaging all items, then add a margin.

Example:

A skincare e-commerce site offers “Choose any 3 products for ₹999” from a curated list.

This allows customers to have more control and might boost perceived value.

6. Psychological Pricing

Use different prices and promotions to make bundles more attractive.

For example:

Rather than selling it at 500 dollars, an online electronics store prices a smart home bundle at 499.99 dollars.

Different examples include:

  • Charm pricing: instead of 10$ they use 9.99$
  • Prestige pricing: Instead of 999.99$ for deluxe bundles they utilize $1000 for luxurious ones

In any type of combination, this method can be used to improve perceived value and stimulate buying behavior.

7. Dynamic Bundle Pricing

Adjust bundle prices based on real-time factors like demand, inventory levels, or competitor pricing.

For instance, an online travel agency dynamically prices flight + hotel bundles based on current demand and availability.

This strategy maximizes profitability and can help manage inventory in e-commerce.

Did you know Amazon is a pioneer in dynamic pricing and makes over 250 million price changes every day? The average product’s price will change once every 10 minutes based on demand and search volume.

8. Subscription Bundles

These create ongoing relationships with customers.

A gourmet food shop might offer a monthly “Chef’s Selection” box of ingredients. Subscription bundles provide predictable revenue for businesses and convenience for customers.

They often include an element of surprise or curation, keeping customers engaged and looking forward to each delivery.

9. Freemium Bundling

Include a free or heavily discounted item in the bundle to increase perceived value.

Example: An online beauty store offers a skincare bundle:

  • Cleanser, toner, and moisturizer: $80
  • Plus a free sample-size serum (usually $15)

This strategy can introduce customers to new products and increase the bundle’s appeal.

Source: Nykaa

10. Cross-Category Bundling

Combine items from different product categories to encourage diverse purchases.

Example: An online bookstore bundles a bestselling novel ($20) with a branded bookmark ($5) and a small reading light ($15):

  • Individual total: $40
  • Bundle price: $32

This approach can introduce customers to new product categories and increase overall sales.

items.excerpt: Choice is everything for the consumer and when it comes to product bundles, providing this choice can make a significant difference. items.html:
Choice is everything for the consumer and when it comes to product bundles, providing this choice can make a significant difference.

Build Your Own Bundle or BYOB is a popular and effective bundling strategy that allows businesses to provide customers with the flexibility to choose their favorite products while availing additional benefits from bundling these products.

In this blog, we will delve into everything that you need to know about the Build Your Own Bundle model, from its benefits to the steps needed for creating them.

What is build your own bundle (BYOB) product bundling strategy?

“Build Your Own Bundle” or BYOB is a product bundling strategy that lets the customers choose their favorite/ desired products and create custom bundles by themselves, often at a price that is much lower than what would cost when purchasing each item from the bundle individually.

This custom bundle creation strategy is highly effective as it combines the strengths of product bundling with flexibility and freedom of choice, thus offering customers precisely what they want at a much better price.

What are the benefits of BYOB for businesses?

Offering bundle builders on E-commerce stores often comes with a lot of benefits making it one of the most viable and effective product bundling strategies. These are some of the major benefits of Build Your Own Bundle product bundles for businesses:

Increased sales

DIY bundles by providing customers the ability to pick multiple products and buy them at a discounted price, encourage them to purchase more and get the best value from the bundle. This way BYOB strategy can greatly improve the average order value while also increasing the number of orders.

Enhanced customer loyalty

With the customizability that businesses can provide with a DIY bundle model, customers will have a much more personalized shopping experience where that perfectly aligns with their needs and interests. These positive customer experiences can greatly improve customer loyalty and result in stronger long-term customer relationships.

Improved inventory management

By letting customers choose from a variety of products, the risk of overstocking or stockouts of specific products can be greatly minimized. This way enabling custom bundle creation can positively help businesses in moving and managing inventory better.

Higher conversion rates

By letting customers choose their own products rather than showcasing a specific set of products in a bundle, they are more likely to place an order. In other words, by allowing customers to tailor their bundles based on their own preferences, brands can see a substantial improvement in their conversion rates.

Increased market differentiation

Among brands that offer pre-set bundles, you can provide customers with flexibility and choice, making for a unique experience. Furthermore, a unique DIY product bundle model can help you differentiate your brand from your competitors.

Enhanced data insights

Having a bundle builder on your website gives you a way to access valuable customer data that will provide you insights into the customers’ preferences and interests. These insights can help your brand refine its product offerings and fine-tune your marketing strategies for the best results.

What are the benefits of BYOB for customers?

Besides the benefits and perks that E-commerce bundle builders provide to businesses, they can be greatly advantageous to the customers as well. Here are some of the major benefits of BYOB product bundles for customers:

Personalization

The ability to personalize their purchases online offers customers a significant advantage, as it lets them choose what best meets their individual tastes and preferences. Thus, customizable bundles help customers get only the products that are relevant to them. This way they are bound to feel in control of their purchases and have a more tailored and satisfactory shopping experience.

Perceived value

One of the major benefits of Build Your Own Bundles for customers is the perceived value that it offers. Customers will be drawn towards the added value or the discounted price at which they can get their preferred products by bundling them, compared to the higher cost of buying each product separately. For customers, this perceived value will not just be about saving more money but also about getting more for less.

Flexibility

Build Your Own Bundle strategy’s fundamental philosophy is that of providing customers flexibility. Customers rather than having to go for preset bundles where there might be an unwanted item, can simply mix and match products to suit their individual tastes. Hence BYOB can accommodate diverse customer preferences while offering a tailored, satisfactory experience.

Convenience

The Build Your Own Bundle model can effectively simplify the shopping process by letting customers find and purchase the products of their choice in one go, instead of having to look for each product separately. In a climate where customers value time-saving options, the added convenience reduces the friction in the shopping experience.

How to create a BYOB product bundle on Shopify store?

These are the steps involved in creating a Build Your Own Bundle product bundle on your Shopify store:

1. Plan your bundle offerings

The first step to creating a bundle builder for your Shopify E-commerce store is to define your bundle categories. This involves deciding on the type of bundle you want to offer and product categories such as beauty products or tech gadgets, or specific themes like gift sets, starter packs etc.

At this stage, also choose the products that will be available for customers to be added to their custom bundles. It is ideal to include a mix of products ranging from new arrivals, slow-moving products and best-sellers to have a diverse offering.

2. Set up bundle rules

The next step is to establish clear rules for your Build Your Own Bundle on Shopify, to ensure flexibility and manage expectations. Start by deciding the pricing structure.

The pricing can be a fixed discount, a tiered discount based on the number of products or a set price for an entire bundle. The minimum or maximum limits for the number of products customers can select should also be decided.

3. Configure your E-commerce platform

Ensure that your Shopify or Shopify Plus platform supports BYOB (Build Your Own Bundle) functionality. Shopify users can utilize the Appstle Bundles app for an easy and effective setup.

Appstle Bundles offers robust features to create customizable bundles that enhance the shopping experience and drive sales. If native support is not available, Appstle Bundles provides a comprehensive solution to seamlessly integrate bundle functionality into your Shopify store.

4. Create Bundle templates

After you have the right tools in your hands, it is now time to create the actual bundle templates. This entails the development of specific pages or product listings where the customer can create their bundles. Usually, this will involve establishing a convenient interface that will enable the customers to choose items from the specified categories.

Moreover, you should allow customers to select options for the product within the bundle, for example, color, size or any other option. A good bundle template not only improves the usability of the bundle but also motivates the customers to use the BYOB feature.

5. Test the bundle functionality

Before launching, test the bundle creation process to see if the creation of bundles is intuitive and user-friendly. Review the customer experience and verify that pricing and discounts are applied correctly. This step helps identify and resolve any issues that may hinder the implementation, ensuring a smooth launch.

6. Promote your bundles

Advertise your BYOB bundles through email, social networks, and your website. Emphasize the advantages of customization and the value being offered. It is also important to adequately and cleverly introduce certain offers or discounts that would make the customers interested in the new bundle option.

7. Monitor and optimize

After going live with your bundles, you should always keep track of their performance. Monitor the sales data and the feedback received from the customers to adjust the bundle offers, the prices, and the promotions. Adjusting and optimizing your BYOB strategy periodically based on real-life data will assist in improving customer satisfaction and increasing sales.

Examples of BYOB product bundles for eCommerce

These are some of the popular Build Your Own Bundle examples:

BirchBox

BirchBox, the popular beauty brand’s BYOB is unique in that the personalization happens way beyond just letting customers add products to a bundle. BirchBox asks customers a few questions about their beauty goals so as to match them with the right products, thus ensuring only the most relevant products reach the customer.

The Gourmet Box

The Gourmet Box understands that BYOB cannot be effective without any real options so they have a diverse range of products to offer. They let customers personalize Gourmet gift boxes with products of choice, while also letting customers add a custom gift message in the box.

Tula Skincare

Tula Skincare kits are a fine example of how clever Build Your Own Bundle strategies can be implemented with a bit of playfulness to easily catch the customer’s interest. Each kit is displayed along with a clear mention of the discount percentage along with a badge saying “Customize Me!” Tula offers different types of product kits all of which can be customized to suit the needs of customers with different preferences and needs.

Conclusion

The Build Your Own Bundle (BYOB) product bundling model offers customers flexibility and can significantly enhance conversion rates and sales for businesses.
