items.excerpt: Product bundling is a highly effective way in which brands can sell more from their store and increase the average value of each customer’s orders. With a curated collection of products that complement each other, businesses can nudge average buyers to go big with their shopping. However, product bundles are hard to sell if they…
items.html:
Product bundling is a highly effective way in which brands can sell more from their store and increase the average value of each customer’s orders. With a curated collection of products that complement each other, businesses can nudge average buyers to go big with their shopping.

However, product bundles are hard to sell if they cannot capture the interest of customers or manage to excite them.

But don’t worry! If you have been struggling to make your product bundles stand out to customers, here are some of the best product bundling examples from the real world to inspire you!

Let’s begin.

Real-life brand examples of product bundles

Below we have listed some of the best product bundle examples from across different industries, that manage to capture customer interest and increase average order value for these brands.

Fashion and apparel

1. Nordstrom

Popular apparel and jewelry e-commerce website, Nordstrom’s approach to product bundling is a great example of how to capture the attention of every kind of shopper. Nordstrom has a separate page dedicated to offering carefully picked and matched to suit different customer tastes.

The website has sets bundled for both men and women, curated differently for different seasons, occasions, holidays and preferences. By promoting matching fits as a bundle, Nordstrom cleverly inspires its customers to purchase more.

2. M.M. LaFleur

New York-based women’s fashion brand M.M. LaFleur, known for its innovative Power Casual clothing, has a unique way of bundling products. The brand allows customers to use a curated build-your-own capsule wardrobe collection named “The Always Capsule” that they regularly update. The added offer of 15% that customers get from buying two or more pieces from the capsule, further incentivizes and encourages bigger purchases.

Beauty and skincare

3. Kylie Cosmetics

Popular across the globe, Kylie Cosmetics intrigues its store visitors with cleverly curated product bundles to welcome customers. These products are showcased as bundles of the month with discounted prices to attract customers. Customers can easily navigate through the bundles page and find the offered bundles to get the products that they want to complete their look with. The products are already matched, making it easier for customers to repeat this makeup in the future as well.

4. Volition

Volition Beauty, the California-based collaborative beauty brand conveys their value from the outset to promote its cosmetics and beauty accessories. This is a fine product bundle example as it cleverly uses both the actual price and the bundle discounted price to directly communicate how much customers can save from opting for the bundle, thus encouraging customers to grab the opportunity instantly.

5. NUXE

NUXE is a popular and preferred skincare brand for many and has been around since its founding by Aliza Jabès in 1990. As the tourism and travel industry steadily rose post-pandemic, NUXE came out with its Travels Essential Kit which was able to capitalize on this rebound, quickly adapting its bundle strategy to the changing market. A perfect cherry on top of the bundle was NUXE’s discounted price making the traveler’s kit a great deal, irrespective of whether one is traveling or not.

Food and beverages

6. Death Wish Coffee

Death Wish Coffee, established in New York in 2012, not only has an intriguing brand personality and innovative product lineup but also an intuitive approach to its product bundling. The brand offers a separate category of product bundles, that offer special holiday season bundles that include its best-selling flavors. By diversifying its offerings with unique combinations Death Wish Coffee effectively manages to capture customer interest with every holiday special bundle.

7. McDonald’s

McDonald’s Happy Meal is one of the best and most iconic product bundling examples, where creative advertising meets the appeal of convenience and value. The Happy Meal was first conceived in 1979, targeting younger demographics, with a child-size portion of a burger, fries, a drink and a toy. By creating an engaging and joyful dining experience the Happy Meal became a revolutionizing strategy that has greatly changed the fast-food industry.

8. Cuisinery

Cuisinery Food Market is an online specialty food platform that is popular for its unique breakfast bundles. The bundle named “At Home French Bakery” comes with delicious items like butter croissants, apple turnovers, waffles, French crepes etc. This product bundle works by providing food lovers with combinations of authentic European tastes in their quick and freshly delivered breakfasts.

Health and wellness

9. iHerb

For the popular natural healthcare products and supplements brand, iHerb, product bundling is an essential part of its strategy. For each chosen product the brand displays a combo of products on the sidebar, along with the discounts or savings they can make by purchasing the product in a bundle. By offering more products for better pricing, customers automatically are inclined to go for the bundle rather than saving less by purchasing a single item.

10. HVMN

The nutrition and supplement company HVMN offers a great example of a build-your-own bundle type of product bundling with its mix-and-match bundles. Here customers can choose their preferred flavors of Keto Collagen or MCT oil powder to create a custom bundle. With this highly effective product bundling the brand was able to see a significant improvement in its average order value.

Pet care

11. Wild Ones

Wild One is a pet goods retailer that has strategically implemented related product bundles to combine popular items with less popular items together and sell them. The Harness Walk Kit, for example, combines a dog leash, harness and a complementary waste bag carrier together as a bundle, this way effectively selling more bag carriers than was possible before.

12. BarkBox

BarkBox is another popular pet essentials brand that has a unique and effective approach to product bundling. They offer subscription-based product bundles containing pet accessories, pet wellness products and more, that will be delivered to the customers’ doorstep every month. The bundles can even be customized based on the breed of the dog, known allergies, the dog’s preference for toys and more, showcasing how tailored deliveries and experiences are crucial for building a loyal customer base.

Entertainment

13. Hulu and Spotify

Launched first in 2018, this unique product bundle combined Spotify’s premium music streaming service with Hulu’s video streaming at very attractive pricing, allowing customers to enjoy the benefits and services of both these platforms. Currently being offered to only students, this bundling strategy was able to combine the strengths and the audience base of both these platforms to effectively enhance the reach and customers for both of them simultaneously.

Electronics

14. Samsung

Product bundling can necessarily go beyond just “products.” Global tech giant Samsung, instead of offering another product, offers premium support coverage known as Samsung Care+ as a bundle. Customers can simply pay a bit more when purchasing a product and thus get coverage of expert support and protection against liquid or physical damage on their devices.

15. Best Buy

In a highly competitive market of consumer electronics, Best Buy manages to stay on top because of its highly affordable prices. Its product bundles come in the form of expert recommendations that allow customers to purchase to whole bundle for a single price. Customers can also add all the products from the recommendations to the cart or deselect products as they prefer. This form of product bundle not only appears credible but also can effectively increase AOV.

16. Apple

The leading tech company Apple also sets a great example of inventive product bundling that nudges customers to purchase more than just a single product. Customers purchasing an Apple product such as an iPad, iPhone, Mac etc. can customize the products, add personalized engravings and bundle the product with accessories and gadgets that are compatible and complementary to the product.

Sports and outdoor gear

17. New Balance

The athletic apparel and footwear giant, New Balance, has been strong in the game since 1906, and their product bundling game has only gotten stronger. When a customer browses for a single product, they are recommended a bundled look that includes sportswear or accessories that complement the product they are looking for. This way the brand utilizes bundled product recommendations to enhance the experience while nudging users to buy more.

18. The North Face

The renowned outdoor apparel and high-performance gear brand, The North Face also employs a very effective product bundling strategy that perfectly caters to its adventure-loving customers. The Advanced Mountain Kit offers different layers that in combination provide enhanced moisture management, waterproofing and protection against extreme weather. This product bundle example shows how practicality and meeting customer needs are also key to successful product bundling.

Gaming

19. PlayStation

Sony Interactive Entertainment’s gaming brand PlayStation has been a behemoth in the gaming industry since 1994. PlayStations gaming bundle is highly successful as most buyers often prefer it over standalone product purchases. The company’s VR bundle, for example, includes a VR headset, camera, PlayStation VR Worlds and more, which evidently seems to be a better and more comprehensive deal for most customers

20. Nintendo

Nintendo’s mixed bundling model offers customers choices of bundles with their console and video games at discounted prices. Customers easily saw the value in purchasing bundles rather than having to spend more on buying these products individually. Nintendo increased its sales by more than 100,000 units, just by allowing customers to save money with customizable bundles!

Conclusion

Product bundling is undeniably a very effective way of improving the quality of user experience while simultaneously bagging more sales. And from the examples we have seen above, we can rightly say that with the right implementation, you can seamlessly make the difference you want to see from your upselling and cross-selling strategies.

Appstle lets you employ different bundle types from classic, combo advanced and more, and use different discount types and conversion-optimized templates. With its capability to seamlessly integrate with different Shopify apps, it is one of the most dynamic and flexible tools for product bundling that you can get your hands on.

items.html:
Forrester’s research states that upselling and cross-selling contribute to around 10–30% of eCommerce revenues. Interestingly, product bundles significantly increase Average Order Value (AOV) by 20-30%, as customers spend more per transaction when they perceive a better deal.

Customers that leverage product bundles have 2.7x higher lifetime value (LTV). This is because they are usually introduced to a broader range of products, increasing the likelihood of repeat purchases.

Okay, that’s interesting. But what are e-commerce product bundles? What are its benefits and do you set them up on your Shopify store? In this blog, we’ll discuss all this and more.

What is Product Bundling?

Product bundling is an e-commerce marketing strategy where multiple complementary products are sold together in a single package.

It’s a win-win situation: customers get more value, and companies earn higher average order value (AOV) while exposing their range of products to buyers.

Common examples of product bundling include meal combos in fast-food restaurants, beach kits with frisbees and towels in one bag, or shampoo and conditioner sets.

Some brands only offer certain best-sellers as part of bundles to encourage customers to try other items. This works well for catching both the scrollers and the shoppers.

There are different types that product bundling can take such as upsells (offering a premium version) or cross-sells (suggesting related items). This can be easily implemented using Shopify apps like Appstle Bundles that provide merchants with tools necessary for effective execution so businesses can create attractive packages that make sense from a customer perspective thereby improving sales on their online store.

Benefits of E-Commerce Product Bundling

According to McKinsey, 35% of all Amazon purchases come from the product recommendation section, which often includes the “buy it with” bundles.

Product bundling is a great way to grow your business and give customers something they can touch. The key is to find the right mix of products that will benefit both parties involved – this means more sales for you and better value for them.

Benefits of product bundles for customers

  • Cost Saving: Usually product bundles deliver better worth than buying single units.
  • Convenience: Buying several related things at once saves the time and energy required rather than making separate purchases for each item.
  • Simplified decision-making process: Pre-assembled sets help reduce the paradox of choice which often leads people to make no decision at all due to being overwhelmed with so many options available in the market.
  • Product discovery: Customers get introduced to other items that they may not have thought about before but which go well with what they are already buying or using.
  • Enriched experience: Some bundles can solve more customer problems than individual parts would do separately thus giving them complete satisfaction in terms of meeting their needs fully as identified during the purchase process analysis stage.
  • Value perception: Even without significant discounts, bundles can create a perception of getting more for your money.
  • Gift-buying ease: Bundles simplify gift shopping by offering pre-selected combinations suitable for various occasions.

Benefits of product bundles for business

  • Sales and revenue growth: This marketing strategy can put more goods in the hands of customers thereby increasing overall sales volume. According to a study by the National Bureau of Economic Research, product bundling can increase profits by up to 30%.
  • Higher Average Order Value (AOV): By combining multiple products, businesses can increase the amount spent per transaction.
  • Inventory management: Packaging together slow-moving items with fast-moving ones helps prevent dead stock.
  • Improved product awareness: Not-so-popular or new products gain visibility when sold alongside bestsellers.
  • Competitive advantage: A good combination of products could make a business different from others thus attracting customers looking for value deals.
  • Simplified marketing: It is cheaper to advertise a package than individual items separately.
  • Customer loyalty: When people are satisfied with useful sets, they buy from the same seller again and become loyal to that brand name.

Common Types of Product Bundling for Shopify Stores

It is commonly assumed that bundling is just simply adding 2+ products in a pack and your sales will magically multiply. But there are so many different kinds of product bundle types – each with its use case and benefits. Let’s look into these.

1. Pure Bundles

These are all-or-nothing packages. Businesses use them to showcase a complete product line or solution.

For example, a skincare brand might offer a bundle with cleanser, toner, serum, and moisturizer, available only as a set.

This strategy can boost sales of less popular items and encourage customers to try a full routine. It’s particularly effective for products that work best when used together.

2. Mix-and-Match Bundles

This approach puts customers in the driver’s seat.

A clothing store might offer “Any 3 shirts for $50.” Customers enjoy the flexibility to create personalized sets, while businesses benefit from increased sales volume. It’s an excellent way to clear varied inventory and satisfy different tastes.

The key is to set a threshold that encourages larger purchases while still offering value.

3. New Product Bundles

This strategy uses established products as a launchpad for new ones.

Did you know using an upsell product bundling strategy can be 68% more effective than trying to grab a new customer?

For instance, a tech company might bundle its new wireless earbuds with its popular smartphone.

This tactic leverages customer trust in existing products to promote new offerings. It can significantly boost initial sales and awareness of new items, helping them gain traction in the market.

4. Cross-Sell Bundles

These bundles connect the dots between related products.

An outdoor gear shop might package a tent with sleeping bags and a camping stove.

By offering complementary items together, businesses increase average order value and provide a more complete solution. It’s like suggesting the perfect sides to go with a main course, enhancing the overall customer experience.

5. Gift Bundles

Designed to make gift-giving easier, these curated sets often revolve around themes or occasions.

A spa-themed bundle might include bath oils, scented candles, and a plush robe.

They save shoppers time and decision-making stress, especially during busy gift-giving seasons. These bundles often come in attractive packaging, adding to their appeal as ready-to-give presents.

6. Inventory Clearance Bundles

This is a smart way to move aging stock.

A kitchenware store might bundle last season’s placemats with discounted cutlery sets. It helps businesses free up warehouse space and recover some costs on slow-moving items.

For customers, it’s an opportunity to snag deals on products that might otherwise be out of their price range.

7. Buy-One-Get-One (BOGO) Bundles

BOGO offers are straightforward and highly attractive to bargain hunters. A beauty store might offer “Buy one lipstick, get another 50% off.”

As per a survey by AMG Strategic Advisors, 93% of customers prefer Buy-One-Get-One (BOGO) bundles.

This strategy can quickly boost sales volume, introduce customers to new products, and create a strong perception of value. It’s particularly effective for products with higher profit margins or those nearing expiration dates.

8. Tiered Bundles

This approach caters to different customer needs and budgets.

A software company might offer Basic, Pro, and Enterprise packages with increasing features and support levels. It allows customers to choose their ideal price point while encouraging upgrades.

For businesses, it’s a way to capture different market segments with a single product line.

9. Subscription Bundles

These create ongoing relationships with customers.

A gourmet food shop might offer a monthly “Chef’s Selection” box of ingredients. Subscription bundles provide predictable revenue for businesses and convenience for customers.

They often include an element of surprise or curation, keeping customers engaged and looking forward to each delivery.

How To Get Started With Product Bundles

Now that we’ve looked into the benefits and types of product bundling in e-commerce, let us dig into how exactly can you set it up in your Shopify store. Here’s a step-by-step breakdown –

1. Analyze Your Product Catalog

Start with taking in all the data about your inventory and sales reports to find out which items sell most. You can then quickly analyze and recommend other products that would go well together.

2. Get Into The Heads of Your Customers

Don’t just go with your gut feeling. Use your sales data to identify common buying habits and preferences among customers.

3. Set Out the Purpose for Bundling

To get the maximum results out of your product bundling strategies, you need to have a clear goal to work towards. Decide whether you want to increase sales, dispose of stock or launch new product lines. This will help you immensely in outlining the right pricing and bundling strategies

4. Select the Bundle Type

Based on your goals as well as your product mix, choose the most suitable bundling strategy. You can choose one of the types mentioned in the previous section. Remember, the type of bundling you choose will be heavily dependent on your goals and objectives.

5. Determine Pricing Strategy

Find out at what discount level customers will perceive value while maintaining profitability.

6. Design bundles presentations:

Craft compelling product descriptions and visuals to showcase your bundles effectively.

7. Implement in your Shopify store:

Start using a trusted application like Appstle Bundles to manage your bundles seamlessly and with ease. This app lets you create different types of bundles, set up discount rules, and manage offerings effectively.

8. Test and Launch

Begin with a few bundled items and closely monitor their performance rates.

9. Promote Your Bundles

Make sure people get to know about these new packages through all available marketing channels you use such as email marketing, social media networks as well as search engine optimization techniques.

Best Practices For Product Bundling: Everything You Need To Know To Boost Sales

  • Understand your customer/client: Utilize data analysis to identify consumer purchasing patterns and tastes.
  • Ensure that the items go together: Make pairs of products that make sense together. For instance, makeup brushes with foundation or woolen socks with mufflers.
  • Maintain value perception: Offer a clear price advantage over individual purchases.
  • Do not make them complicated: Don’t confuse customers with excessive choices or intricate bundles.
  • Show savings: Clearly state the worth and savings made on the purchase of such bundled products. An easy to do this is to show savings in percentage.
  • Offer customization opportunities: Let customers change bundles as they want them so that they suit individual needs.
  • Test different combinations: Constantly experiment using diverse product pairings in order to see the best combination.
  • Leverage seasonality: For vacations, seasons and special occasions create timely combos.
  • Use attractive packaging: Make bundled products visually appealing, especially for gift bundles.
  • Implement dynamic pricing: Adjust bundle prices based on demand and inventory levels.
  • Provide detailed descriptions: Clearly explain what’s included in each bundle and its benefits.
  • Offer deals for limited periods: This can be done through time-bound discounts on package deals which creates an atmosphere of urgency necessitating an immediate decision by the customer since these packages are only available within a specified period or while stocks last.
  • Launch using bundles: You could introduce your new products alongside already established favorites through this method.
  • Monitor performance: Regularly analyze bundle sales data to refine your strategy.

How To Measure The Success Of Product Bundles

Crafting a high-converting product bundle requires you to dig into the data. Numbers rarely lie. A close eye on conversions and sales metrics can reveal your overall sales growth and conversion rate of specific bundles.

To evaluate the effectiveness of your product bundling strategy, focus on these key metrics:

  1. Average Order Value (AOV): Track changes in AOV after implementing bundles. An increase suggests successful bundling.
  2. Bundle vs. Individual Sales: Compare the performance of bundled products against their individual counterparts.
  3. Conversion Rate: Monitor how bundle offers impact your overall conversion rate.
  4. Customer Lifetime Value (CLV): Assess whether bundles are contributing to increased CLV over time.
  5. Inventory Turnover: Evaluate how bundling affects the speed of inventory movement, especially for slow-moving items.
  6. Customer Feedback: Gather and analyze customer reviews, ratings, and survey responses about bundle offerings.
  7. Repeat Purchase Rate: Measure if customers who buy bundles are more likely to make repeat purchases.
  8. Profit Margins: Ensure that while offering value to customers, bundles maintain healthy profit margins.
  9. Bundle-Specific Metrics: Track the performance of individual bundles to identify top performers and areas for improvement.

Common Challenges Merchants Face With Product Bundling

Although e-commerce product bundling is a sure-shot way to increase your sales in most cases, it comes switch its own set of challenges and roadblocks. In this section, we’ve briefly outlined these challenges, so you can avoid them for maximum profitability.

Let’s dive in.

  • Inventory Management: Balancing stock levels for bundled items can be tricky. Mismatched inventory can lead to bundle unavailability or overstocking of individual components.
  • Customer Expectations: Bundles may create unrealistic expectations about product value. Customers might expect similar discounts on individual items or become resistant to non-bundled pricing.
  • Pricing and Profit Margins: Finding the sweet spot between attractive discounts and sustainable profits is challenging. Overly aggressive bundle pricing can erode margins, while insufficient discounts may fail to attract customers.
  • Bundle Flexibility: Offering customization in bundles can complicate operations but may be necessary to meet diverse customer needs.
  • Cannibalization: Bundles might reduce sales of high-margin individual products, potentially impacting overall profitability.
  • Tracking Performance: Accurately measuring the success of individual products within bundles can be complex, making it difficult to assess true product performance.

Trends To Watch Out For in E-commerce Product Bundling

The future of product bundling is moving towards more personalized and flexible offerings. Personalized bundles are growing popular, tailored to individual customer preferences based on their purchase history and browsing behavior. These smart bundles use AI and machine learning to suggest highly relevant product combinations.

There is also a rise of build-your-own bundles, which allow customers to design personalized packages that best fit their needs. This strategy can increase customer satisfaction as well as average order value.

Subscription bundles are becoming increasingly popular, offering customers convenience and regular value while providing businesses with predictable recurring revenue.

Tools like Appstle Subscriptions are making it easier for e-commerce businesses to implement and manage these subscription bundles, allowing them to stay competitive in this growing trend. As bundling strategies continue to evolve, the focus will be on creating more dynamic, customer-centric offerings that balance value, flexibility, and profitability.

items.excerpt: Subscriptions are taking over the world of eCommerce. There are subscriptions for all kinds of products, services, and in all industries. But not all subscriptions are sustainable. items.html:
Subscriptions are taking over the world of eCommerce. There are subscriptions for all kinds of products, services, and in all industries.

But not all subscriptions are sustainable. For subscriptions to succeed, they need to be managed well. That’s why having an efficient subscription management system is critical.

In this blog, we deep dive into subscription management systems. You’ll learn what it is, why it is important, what are its key components, and which subscription management system is the best for your business.

What is an eCommerce subscription management system?

Managing eCommerce subscriptions involves a lot of tasks. From setting up subscription plans to billing cycles to deliveries, etc. Apart from these, there are other tasks such as sending regular updates to customers, attending to their requests for delivery swap, halt, etc. There’s a ton of small tasks that need to be in sync.

A subscription management system or platform or app, helps businesses perform all these tasks. Ecommerce businesses can set up, manage, and monitor their subscription business model with the help of eCommerce subscription management apps. The system lends efficiency and streamlines subscription management.

Why is a subscription management system important?

Subscriptions are on the rise. In the past year, 54% of consumers have subscribed to eCommerce subscription boxes and 15% have subscribed to service-based subscriptions. As competition in the subscription industry rises, there’s an increasing need for businesses to have comprehensive and smart subscription management systems integrated into their eCommerce businesses. Here are some reasons why you it’s important:

1. Streamline operations

Subscription operations involve many tasks. Streamlining subscription operations is one of the basics of subscription management. Performing every task manually is not possible if you want to scale your business. Having a subscription management system can help you streamline operations efficiently. For instance, you can automate billing and payments, manage the inventory, prevent stock outs or overstocking, have your customer relationship management (CRM) system integrated, collect data, reports and analysis, among other tasks.

2. Enhance customer experience

Customers sign up for subscriptions for convenience, ease of shopping, and to make their life easier. If they find certain aspects difficult, it directly impacts their experience. eCommerce subscription management system helps enhance customer experience. Data collected and analyzed by the system can provide important insights that can be used for personalization. Other factors that impact customer experience are a seamless onboarding experience, flexibility, automated communication, seamless customer support, etc.

A McKinsey study found customers consider experience when signing up for subscriptions.

3. Scalability

Scalability is an essential factor of subscription businesses. And having a management tool supports business growth through easy scalability. For instance, as the number of subscribers increase, your tasks will also multiply. Having a management tool will help handle the increasing volumes and transactions. Moreover, your tool will help adapt to changing business needs with flexible plans.

4. Better customer retention

Even though customers sign up to subscriptions for long-term, there are high chances of churn. Most customers do not fully realize the benefits of subscriptions or find it repetitive and hence choose not to renew their plans. But with a subscription management tool, you can implement proactive strategies to retain customers and reduce churn. For instance, set up dunning management so customers who are about to unsubscribe can be retained by offering real-time incentives and discounts.

8 essential components of an eCommerce subscription management system

Customers sign up for subscriptions for various reasons—for instance, personalized experience (28%), convenience (24%), value for money (23%), among other reasons. If you’re looking for a Shopify subscription management system for your business, here are a few factors you must consider.

1. Automated billing and invoicing

Subscription models have more predictable transactions that occur on predefined dates. A subscription management system makes billing and invoicing related tasks easy to manage. For instance, some features of a subscription billing software are: recurring billing cycle, applying discounts, managing promotional offers, etc. Here are a few ways automated billing and invoicing help:

  • Manage recurring billing cycles on time – weekly, monthly, annually
  • Reduce errors related to calculation
  • Improve cash flow management
  • Follow compliance and reporting procedures
  • Collect data and analytics reports for insights on subscriber behavior
  • Simplify transactions
  • Reduce tedious tasks
  • Manage payment methods and security

2. Subscription plan management

Businesses that want to create engaging subscription plans need to put in a lot of effort in creating and managing subscription plans. And that’s what management systems help with. Here are a few factors:

  • Set up different types of subscription plans to cater to different customer segments
  • Customize subscription plans to meet customer preferences
  • Set up different pricing models – monthly, quarterly, annual, etc.
  • Apply automated discounts and promotional offers to increase revenue
  • Enables plan modification, upgradation, downgrade, etc. allowing flexibility to subscribers
  • Dunning management and cancellation management to improve retention rate

3. Customer management

Customers commit to subscriptions for a longer duration and hence you must ensure you understand customers’ changing preferences. Customer management is key and you can integrate it within your subscription management system. Here’s how it helps:

  • Maintains accurate customer information in one place to enhance customer experience
  • Customer segmentation to improve marketing and promotion relevance
  • Helps with personalization of deals and offers
  • Streamlines regular communication, notifications, and updates with subscribers
  • Enables self-service so subscribers can manage their subscriptions via the portal
  • Manages customers support, timely responses, ticketing, and quick service
  • Tracks and collects customer data based on customer behavior patterns
  • Provides data analytics for insights to help with personalization
  • Automates customer retention strategies

4. Renewals and retention

Given the competition and changing customer preferences, it is hard to retain subscribers year after year. But there are a few related tasks that you can automate with the help of an intuitive subscription management system and improve retention rates. Here’s how the management system helps:

  • Send automated renewal reminders and notifications in a timely manner
  • Set up retention strategies, such as offering discounts for renewals, incentives, etc.
  • Predict cancellations and offer incentives to retain customers
  • Manage churn by assessing reasons for cancellation and provide real-time solutions to retain subscribers
  • Set up dunning management throughout customer touchpoints
  • The features of subscription billing software include automated renewal prompts, reminders, etc.

5. Analytics and reporting

Subscription businesses have multiple aspects that need to be monitored and tracked. With proper report generation and analytics, businesses can gain valuable insights to help optimize their subscription business. Here’s how a subscription management system helps with analytics and reporting.

  • Monitor and track metrics such as monthly revenue, churn rate, average order value, customer lifetime value, engagement rate, etc.
  • Generate reports on subscription performance, customer behavior, financial health, etc.
  • Make data-driven decisions to optimize subscription strategies
  • Customer behavior insights to have an understanding of changing customer preference—63% of people expect brands to use their purchase history to provide personalized experience
  • Financial reporting such as revenue, profit, expenses, losses, etc.
  • Predictive analytics to identify patterns so businesses can proactively take the necessary actions

6. Integrations

You may require additional functions and features outside of your subscriptions app. Hence, subscription management systems must integrate with third-party applications and tools that can help support and enhance your subscription experience. Here are the different types of integrations and how they help:

  • Integration with multiple payment gateways for seamless transaction
  • Integration with CRM, ERP, and other business tools for better management of your subscription plans
  • API integration for customization of functionalities and workflows

7. Compliance and security

40% of customers do not want their data shared with third parties. Moreover, 75% of customers like to be in control of the data they’ve provided to brands. This makes privacy and security compliance one of the basics of subscription management. Here’s how your subscription management system can help:

  • Compliance with industry standards, such as GDPR, PCI DSS, etc.
  • Protect customer data and privacy through in-built or integrated security measures
  • Update customers about data and privacy compliance and policy changes

8. Customization and flexibility

Today’s customers look for flexibility and customization potential when they look for brands for long-term association. These factors bring confidence and trust as customers know they can change things around if they want to. A good subscription management system should have customization and flexibility capabilities.

  • Customized subscription plans based on customer segments and their preferences
  • Flexibility in subscription plan pricing to adapt to pricing strategies to increase profits
  • Custom billing cycles to cater to customer needs
  • Multi-currency and multi-language support for better communication and subscriber ease
  • Customizable workflows based on different delivery schedules, etc.
  • Flexibility in changing plans, pausing deliveries, changing delivery dates, products, etc.

Why choose Appstle Subscription Management System for Shopify?

There are many Shopify subscription management apps in the market, but Shopify merchants prefer Appstle over other apps. That’s because of the app’s unmatched features and capabilities.

Appstle Subscriptions App keeps the customer (Shopify merchants) at the heart. The app is designed to help merchants set up multiple types of subscription plans based on their industry, products and services, and customer preferences. This gives merchants across industries the flexibility to try, change, and set up multiple types of plans. For instance, subscription box, tiered subscription plans, etc.

Merchants can control their customers’ experience via the dashboard that allows easy management features. Merchants can themselves make the changes, set up automations, personalization features, etc. This gives merchants complete control over their subscription business.

items.html:
Rewards and loyalty programs are among the top marketing tactics that help attract and retain customers.

Today, most eCommerce brands offer some sort of rewards or loyalty programs. However, few are able to sustain the program.

Most rewards programs fail to engage customers beyond a certain period of time. Members start losing interest and disengaging.

Why so?

That’s because a rewards program has to be well-designed, beneficial to customers, and enticing.

One such customer loyalty program example is the Ulta Beauty Rewards program. In this blog, we breakdown its various elements to learn what makes it so successful!

What is the Ulta Beauty Rewards program?

Ulta Beauty is an American chain of cosmetics stores. The brand offers cosmetics products from multiple brands under one umbrella. The brand has physical stores, an online store and an app where customers can shop from. The Ulta Beauty Rewards program, one of the best reward program examples, offers multiple benefits to members. Its perks go beyond points and discounts. Members get to enjoy exclusive communication, gifts, and more. Being a brand that offers different cosmetics and beauty brands, its multi-brand rewards program offers a lot more than other single-brand loyalty programs.

1. Ulta Beauty prioritizes its rewards program on its website

Easy website navigation is essential for good customer experience. To make its rewards program visible, Ulta Beauty has created a dedicated page for it. Not only that, the website prominently displays and advertises the rewards program on the home page, and has a tab on the top-left corner, making it easy for visitors to navigate to the page.

How does this help?

  • Makes it easy for members to participate and engage with the loyalty program
  • Shows customers that the brand prioritizes the loyalty program and takes it seriously. This makes customers interested in it

Ulta Beauty Rewards program page includes the following information:

  • How members can earn rewards points
  • The number of points and its equivalent discount
  • The three rewards program tiers and their benefits
  • FAQs and terms and conditions
  • More perks and benefits

2. Three types of rewards tiers

Ulta Beauty Loyalty program offers three levels or tiers to its members.

  • The first tier, called Member, is free.
  • The second tier, Platinum, includes members who spend more than $500 per year.
  • The third tier, Diamond, includes members who spend more than $1200 per year.

By offering three levels, the brand does two things—keeps the rewards program simple for customers and adds an element of gamification. This keeps customers excited and engaged. Gamification can be a game changer in rewards programs, so it is advisable to choose a Shopify rewards program app that supports gamification features, such as Appstle Rewards and Loyalty App.

Customers in the free tier tend to buy more in order to progress to the Platinum level. Similarly, those in the Platinum level try to reach the Diamond level.

Each of these levels also offer exclusive benefits. Having multiple levels has many benefits, such as:

  • Offers exclusivity to customers
  • Creates a community experience for members at different levels
  • Adds an element of gamification, competition, and progress

3. The rewards program offers exclusive benefits

A quick Ulta Beauty Rewards program breakdown shows how the brand creates exclusivity for loyalty program members by offering benefits and perks that are not available to non-members. This makes loyalty program members feel special and encourages them to return to the brand more often to avail exclusive benefits.

4. Multiple ways to use points

A critical factor in the success of rewards programs is how easily members can earn points. Ulta Beauty has ensured that earning points is easy and straightforward, and members can get points quickly.

Members earn points on every dollar they spend. Additionally they can earn weekly bonus points. The more points members earn, the better deals they get on future purchases. For example, when they accumulate 100 points, they get a $3 discount; for 250 points, an $8 discount; etc. This element of gamification adds excitement and instant gratification for members, making them want to earn more points.

5. Answer to frequently asked questions

Ulta Beauty customers can find the answers to all their basic queries on the Ulta Beauty Rewards program page. The FAQs section on the page is elaborate. Questions are divided in the following sections:

  • Program information
  • Earning points
  • Managing profile
  • Enrolment
  • Redeeming points
  • Platinum program
  • Diamond program

Having answers in different sections makes it easy for customers to find information relevant to their query and gives a better understanding of the rewards program.

6. Customer support

A study by Harvard Business Review found that when loyal members come across issues on websites while shopping online, they feel more upset compared to customers who aren’t part of a rewards program. This means it is extremely critical to keep your loyalty and rewards program members happy and satisfied.

So, when Ulta Beauty’s rewards program members encounter a problem on the website, the brand ensures their issues are addressed through top-notch customer support. Here are some support features:

  • A comprehensive contact us page with various types of contact options
  • Help topics to browse, like Order placement, order tracking, order cancellation, etc.
  • Contact details for chat, text, call and email

7. Ulta Beauty offers a co-branded credit card

Ulta Beauty offers a credit card – the Ulta Beauty Rewards Credit Card. It can be used at Ulta Beauty stores and on the website. Card holders earn one extra point for every dollar they spend. Members can check their credit card balance in their customer account. The credit card makes the rewards program more engaging for customers as they can earn and redeem more points. With the Ulta Beauty Rewards program credit card, customers get 20% off their first order.

Also read: A Complete Guide On Customer Loyalty Programs For Beauty, Cosmetics, And Skincare Brands (2024)

8. Mobile optimized website

People are now used to doing everything on their mobile devices, including shopping and managing their reward points. Ulta Beauty addresses this with a highly-optimized mobile site. Apart from a mobile-optimized website, the brand also has an app through which customers can perform any action they want to.

All the features available on the web version are available on mobile as well. What is more, Ulta Beauty Rewards program follows great practices for its mobile version, making it easy for customers to shop and engage with the rewards program on the go.

9. Multiple reasons to join the rewards program

Ulta Beauty offers multiple reasons for customers to join their rewards program. The brand offers perks that go beyond monetary benefits. Here are some of the reasons why the Ulta Beauty loyalty program is one of the best loyalty program examples.

  • It’s free to join
  • Members earn one point for every dollar spent
  • Members can redeem points on any product or service in-store, in the app or on the website
  • Member-exclusive offers and communication
  • Double points during members’ birthday month
  • Diamond and Platinum members get exclusive birthday gifts
  • Members can combine points with other discounts and special offers

10. Rewards program terms and conditions

Ulta Beauty Rewards program page has a section dedicated to terms and conditions. This feature shares more information with customers, making them more confident about the loyalty program they’re getting into.

For instance, the terms and conditions section shares detailed information on aspects of membership, such as the joining fee, eligibility, information about privacy, etc. There are different subsections for the membership levels explaining how customers can join them and what the respective benefits are.

Other information in this section:

  • Cancellation
  • Account maintenance
  • Earning points
  • Gift cards
  • Birthday gift
  • Exclusions
  • Returns
  • Bonus points
  • Redeeming points

Key takeaways from the Ulta Beauty Rewards program

  • Having a well-designed rewards program is the first and foremost requirement if you want a successful loyalty program that helps generate engagement and profits. Ulta Beauty has not only ensured it’s one of the best loyalty program examples, but the brand makes sure its program is promoted for maximum awareness and engagement.
  • Ulta Beauty creates deeper engagement with members through non-transactional elements. For instance, the brand sends exclusive communication and content to its members, first access to special discounts and deals, etc.
  • The brand shares all details with customers, leaving no room for doubt or ambiguity. This builds stronger trust and confidence in the rewards program and customers engage with the program knowing all the details.
  • Ulta Beauty Rewards program offers the best digital experience on the website, on mobile devices, and on its app. The key to running a successful rewards and loyalty program is using an efficient Shopify loyalty program app.

Apply these lessons to your Shopify rewards program

With competition in the rewards and loyalty market increasing, it’s hard to keep your customers engaged for a long time. However, if done well, you can make your rewards program a game changer for your brand, just as we see in the above rewards program example.

items.html:
Coffee subscription models are quite popular amongst consumers and eCommerce retailers. While customers love the convenience and cost benefits offered by subscription models, eCommerce merchants benefit from predictable revenue systems, lower retention spends, and long-term customer relationships.

But not all coffee subscription models are able to sustain. Many fail because they’re poorly planned and managed.

One coffee subscription brand that stands out is Lavazza coffee subscription. In this blog, we breakdown every aspect of its strategy to learn what makes it so successful.

What is Lavazza coffee subscription?

Lavazza is a coffee brand that provides coffee to customers across the world. It offers coffee subscriptions of various types. For example, customers can choose from different types of coffees, different roasts and grounds, etc. Subscribers get a discounted rate with every subscription as well as price benefits. Apart from that, the brand offers educational content, and other benefits to subscribers.

Breaking down Lavazza coffee subscription strategy

A quick search for coffee subscriptions is sure to bring up Lavazza. The secret to its popularity is the way the brand has set up and managed its subscriptions.

In this section we look at the many factors that make it one of the best coffee subscription models.

1. A dedicated subscription page

Lavazza has a page dedicated to subscriptions. The page is simple and minimal, sharing basic information about its three subscription plans:

  • My Way Capsure Subscription
  • My Way Ground & Beans Subscription
  • My Way Classy machine & Capsule subscription

Even though the page provides minimal information, the brand has ensured visitors know the cost savings offered in each of the three subscription plans. They instantly take away the most enticing factor about the subscriptions—the percentage discount and cash savings.

2. Keeping it simple with three subscription plans

In this overcrowded space of eCommerce where customers are spoilt for choice, it’s important to remove decision fatigue for them. That’s something that Lavazza coffee subscriptions has addressed well. The brand offers only three subscription plans. Customers can choose any plan they like based on their preference and needs. Each plan further offers more options to choose from. While two of the three plans are purely for coffee, one plan offers coffee and a machine.

Also read: The Complete Guide To Setting Up A Coffee Subscription Business Online

3. A dedicated page for each of the three subscription plans

Instead of cramming information about all three plans on one page, the brand has created three different pages, one for each plan. Each page has the following sections:

  • Title
  • Options of plans to subscribe
  • Benefits of choosing this subscription
  • How it works
  • FAQs
  • Live chat
  • Accessibility adjustment settings tab

Having a separate page for each plan makes it easy for customers to understand each plan. It also makes purchase decisions easy. Moreover, having a one-page-for-one plan allows the brand to share all the information in detail.

4. FAQs section to answer customer questions

Signing up for subscriptions is a considerably long-term commitment, and hence, customers may have a lot of queries before committing. But getting in touch with the customer support team can seem like a task. The alternative? Set up a comprehensive FAQs section.

Lavazza has an FAQ section on each of the subscription pages. The section answers common questions such as which regions the Lavazza coffee subscription service is active in, how to change personal details, how to schedule deliveries, etc. Having an FAQ section clears customers’ doubts and increases sign-ups.

5. Detailed explanation of the subscription plan

Each subscription plan page has an easy visual explanation of how the plan works. Keeping it simple and minimal with three to four steps, each step is explained with text and illustration.

Research conducted by Harvard Business Review shows that the single biggest driver of customer stickiness is ‘decision simplicity’— the ease with which consumers can gather trustworthy information about a product and confidently and efficiently weigh their purchase options.

Lavazza coffee subscription pages keep it simple, minimal, and easy to understand, making customers’ purchase decision journey easy.

6. Benefits of Lavazza coffee subscription explained

There are thousands of coffee subscription models on the internet. Lavazza makes sure customers know why theirs is worth signing up for by mentioning the benefits of the subscription plan to customers.

Customers like to know how a product or service would benefit them. Now, customer benefits can be both abstract and concrete, so Lavazza mentions both kinds of benefits. For example,

  • How many dollars customers save
  • The percentage of discount
  • Customization possibilities
  • Flexibility

These benefits demonstrate the value customers can get from Lavazza coffee subscriptions, making their purchase decisions easier.

7. Price benefits prominently mentioned

Coffee is a product that customers need to buy on a recurring basis, and hence, customers will look for discounts and cost benefits in coffee subscriptions. A McKinsey study shows ‘value for price’ is the top-most motivation for customers to sign up for subscriptions. And Lavazza offers cost benefits in all its subscription plans.

  • Lavazza My Coffee Subscription plans offer a 25% discount
  • Lavazza My Ground and Beans Subscriptions offer a 25% discount
  • Lavazza My Way Machine and Capsules Subscription provides 25% discounts and $130 savings on the machine

Displaying cost benefits and discounts prominently makes it easier for customers to make purchase decisions and compare subscriptions by different brands.

Did you know the top reasons for subscriber churn are value for the price and a lack of pricing options? Lavazza subscription addresses these with flexibility and customization for deliveries, making it one of the best coffee subscription model examples. With the Lavazza subscription, subscribers can easily reset their subscriptions and adjust their pricing based on the products they select.

8. Easy live chat option

For customers, customer service is a key differentiating and deciding factor for whether or not they must transact and continue with a brand. In short, a brand is only as good as the quality of its customer support.

The Lavazza coffee subscription website provides a live chat option for customers and subscribers to ask questions and instantly get their queries answered. This makes customer interaction easier and provides seamless communication.

9. Website accessibility adjustment (inclusivity)

Another reason why Lavazza is one of the best coffee subscription model examples is the way the brand prioritizes its website’s accessibility. The brand ensures that all its visitors have an easy experience regardless of their different abilities.

For instance, visitors can adjust settings to seizure safe, vision impaired, ADHD friendly, cognitive disability, keyboard navigation profiles, etc. According to WHO, one in six people have a disability. This makes it important for eCommerce stores to make their websites accessible to people with all levels of abilities. Lavazza applies the best practices in this regard.

10. Mobile-optimized website

Today, a large number of consumers prefer to use their mobile devices to shop and manage orders, and subscriptions. Lavazza addresses this with a highly-optimized mobile site. All the features and information available on the web are available in the mobile version as well.

The brand follows best practices for its mobile site version, such as visible text size, attractive images, suitable font style, and easy-to-navigate features.

11. Easy customization of subscription deliveries

Lavazza’s coffee subscription model allows customers to customize their subscription deliveries based on their preferences. This makes it one of the best coffee subscription model examples to learn from. Customers can choose:

  • Delivery frequency
  • Coffee and coffee machines
  • Delivery date
  • Delivery address

Easy customization options and flexibility add more convenience, value and personalization for subscribers. Flexibility and personalization are key factors for 17% and 12% of subscribers, respectively.

12. Subscription terms and conditions explained

Lavazza subscriptions website has a whole page dedicated to the subscription’s terms and conditions. The page includes explanations and conditions for activities such as changing orders, payments, products and pricing, shipment and delivery, cancellation, privacy policies, applicable law, among other details.

13. Many more reasons to choose Lavazza subscriptions

Apart from these features directly related to Lavazza’s subscription plans, the brand offers many more reasons for customers to choose Lavazza coffee subscription. Here are some of the many reasons why customers and subscribers love the brand:

  • The brand prioritizes sustainability
  • The brand participates in several social, economic, and environmental initiatives
  • Lavazza participates in and collaborates with many sports activities and events
  • They share recipes, coffee hacks and educational information about coffee
  • They conduct in-store events
  • Lavazza initiates projects in music, design, art and entertainment

Key takeaways from Lavazza coffee subscription

Let’s summarize Lavazza coffee subscriptions that make it a successful business model for the brand.

  • The brand has created dedicated subscriptions pages, prioritizing its subscription business
  • Lavazza has kept the subscription model simple with minimal plans
  • Customers are provided with all the important information in detail and with clarity
  • Subscription plans offer discounts, price benefits, and savings in each plan
  • Apart from monetary benefits, the brand offers many features that may appeal to different types of customers
  • Customization, flexibility, and personalization make the subscription model more appealing to customers

items.html:
There’s immense competition in the eCommerce world. Customers have many brands to choose from. Hence, there’s high churn.

eCommerce membership models however, provide added value to customers in this crowded space. Gamification strategies for eCommerce can signifcantly benefit your membership model.

In this blog, we explore how to use gamification for your membership models.

Defining gamification in eCommerce

Gamification involves using game-like and fun elements to encourage customers to engage more with your brand. For instance, motivating customers to buy more products to earn more points and rewards. The idea behind gamification is to add an element of fun through games, interactive activities, and the idea of winning. Customers are encouraged to participate in specific behaviors to enjoy added benefits and perks.

Here’s an example of gamification in eCommerce.

Rip Curl sells surf wear and has a membership program, Club Rip Curl. The program connects members who are passionate about surfing. Members get to earn points for surfing, making purchases, registering, etc. The program has a membership app that tracks every time members go surfing and adds points to their accounts.

Gamification strategies for eCommerce membership models

Gamification has many immediate and long-term benefits for eCommerce brands’ membership models. From adding an element of fun, to enhancing your brand reputation and increasing customer satisfaction — there are many reasons to gamify your eCommerce membership program. Here are a few strategies to apply.

Set up points and rewards system

The more opportunities you give members to earn points and rewards, the more they’ll engage with your brand. Create chances to earn points on purchases, writing product reviews, sharing feedback, making referrals, engaging on social media, etc.

As well as making it easy to earn points, enable members to easily redeem points. From time to time, recommend ways in which they can use points, such as for discounts, during sales, to send gifts, etc.

In gamified membership programs, you can create multiple tiers and encourage members to progress tiers by earning more points. This way you can incentivize continuous engagement via gamified experiences.

A few key points:

  • Make it easy to earn points for performing different actions
  • Tell customers how they can redeem their points
  • Create gamified experiences for members to engage more

Badges and achievements

We humans are wired to want things immediately. That’s why achievement badges work well as gamification strategies in membership. Gamification badges are digital tokens given to customers for completing specific actions and milestones. For example, when members make purchases, cross a certain threshold of purchases or points earned, make referrals, etc. Achievement badges work because they make members feel good, promote engagement, showcase recognition, and are fun and exciting.

Another way to increase engagement via badges is to allow members to showcase their badges on their profiles. This encourages them as well as other members to compete and earn more badges. This brings in playfulness and a culture of competition and winning.

Additionally, you could also offer rewards to members who have earned multiple badges. This boosts engagement.

Challenges and contests

Another engagement strategy for your eCommerce membership model is running contests and creating challenges for members. These help engage customers and earn rewards and points. For instance, you could run regular weekly or monthly challenges. Another effective way to run challenges is to use your social media channels.

An effective gamification tip is to display leaderboards. Studies show that customers tend to engage more with eCommerce programs that have leaderboards. That’s because leaderboards rank members, provide gratification, create competition, and engagement, and drive members to take actions.

Also read: Ecommerce Memberships Marketing Strategies And Examples

Personalized gamification

Membership programs offer multiple opportunities to brands to personalize customers’ experience. As membership is a long-term association with customers, you can get to understand a lot more about your customers. Analyze data, run surveys, and ask customers to share information about themselves so you can personalize their membership experience.

For instance, personalize challenges based on customers’ behavior, activities, likes, and interests. Create different segments of customers and tailor challenges for different groups.

To personalize this further, provide personalized feedback as members progress through challenges.

Quests and missions

You can get as creative as you like when it comes to gamification strategies for eCommerce. Create missions and quests depending on your products and services. For example, you can create thematic missions around festivals, specific seasons, or months.

Another way to boost engagement in your eCommerce membership model is to have step-by-step missions. You can break down bigger missions into smaller milestones for members. For example, create a big mission that members can complete over a long period of time, while earning rewards.

Creating narratives or stories is another way to boost engagement with your membership plans.

Social and community features

Online customer communities are one of the best ways to offer experiences to your members. Communities offer added value to members, where they can meet other like minded people. Communities also align with the long-term approach of membership programs.

Involving members in creating gamification experiences is also a way to get them engaged. When members are more involved, they automatically feel more interested. For instance, ask members to create challenges and invite their friends and family to participate. These challenges could be online or offline.

Conversely, you could set up community or collective goals—involve a segment or group of members to achieve a collective goal. For instance, encourage a group of 10 members to earn X number of points within X time and give them free gifts when the target is achieved. Also, get members to interact with each other through comments, likes, shares, etc.

Exclusive access and content

Another gamification strategy for eCommerce is to offer exclusive content to members. However, they’ll have to complete a certain task to unlock access to content. For instance, you can create special tutorials, articles, behind-the-scenes videos, early product release content, etc. Bring in gamification so members have to perform certain actions to unlock content.

Tiered programs enhance eCommerce membership experience. It has different levels, offers different perks and benefits, and has an element of higher engagement. VIP and premium tiers offer higher levels of perks and benefits and value to members, making the experience more exclusive.

Gamified onboarding for eCommerce membership model

Did you know 83% of people uninstall apps within a day of installing them? And that is why you need to make your eCommerce membership process exciting and ensure their first impression hooks them to your brand. How do you do that? By gamifying the onboarding process.

Create interactive onboarding experience. For instance, ask members to answer a few questions about them. Research shows that gamified onboarding experiences lead to members feeling that the process is useful as the brand will offer more value to them, and hence, they tend to engage more. For instance, you could have a progress bar in the process, or ask customers to set a personal goal for their membership, etc.

Through your onboarding process, you could also provide interactive tutorials to members. Make it educational and fun for them to understand your brand and membership plan better.

Example: Nike Training Club adds many forms for members to answer during the onboarding process so as to personalize their membership experience

items.html:
According to a McKinsey report, 80% of customers expect personalized experiences online.

Tailored experiences such as personalized product recommendations, discounts and deals on products of customers’ liking have transformed the online shopping experience for customers.

Ecommerce brands are leveraging personalization for all aspects of their business, including membership programs. Considering eCommerce memberships create a long-term engagement opportunity with customers, personalization becomes more relevant and effective as a strategy.

In this blog, we explore personalization techniques specifically for eCommerce membership programs.

Recap: What are eCommerce membership models?

Ecommerce membership models enable customers to become members of a program to access exclusive benefits, offers, services, discounts, and perks. For example, Amazon Prime is one of the most common references to understand eCommerce memberships. Some of the common perks offered via memberships are gift vouchers, birthday gifts, special member discounts, property access to new collections, members-only savings, member community experiences, etc.

Different ways to personalize eCommerce memberships

Today’s eCommerce customers are more aware and savvy, and have high expectations from brands. Typically, customers stop engaging with brands that do not offer personalized experience across their buying journey. In this section, we look at how to offer personalized eCommerce membership experiences on your Shopify site.

Personalized onboarding

Your first impression is the last impression, so why not set the tone for your brand from the moment new members sign up? eCommerce membership businesses are following some simple and powerful techniques to personalize onboarding experiences. Here’s how:

  • Tailored welcome messages: When you address customers with their first name, you instantly build a friendly connection with them. However, eCommerce personalization is more than just adding first names to welcome messages. Along with it, look for ways to say more in the welcome message. For example, based on customers’ data, send them a product recommendation, or content they’d like to explore.
  • Customized onboarding pathways: When onboarding customers, ensure you don’t make the mistake of sending one standard message to all members. Segment your customers based on data, and create multiple pathways based on their past activities on your site, purchase behavior, and preferences and interests.

Personalized product recommendations

Recommend products, share suggestions, and entice customers by introducing new products, but narrow down your approach based on customers’ preferences and likes. Here’s what to do:

  • Behavior-based recommendations: Customers engage in many different ways on your eCommerce membership website. And all their actions are useful information for you. For instance, if customers tend to shop more during sales, you know how to target them the next time you have a sale. Similarly, look for cues from customers’ behavior patterns to recommend products.
  • Collaborative filtering: One of the best examples of personalized product recommendations is Amazon. The website uses customers’ past data to share different types of recommendations. For instance, ‘Customers who bought this also bought’, ‘Recently viewed’, ‘What other customers are looking at now’, etc. For your Shopify memberships, you can use customers’ past purchase and browsing history to recommend products.

Source

Customized content and offers

You might think content cannot be personalized to meet each individual customer. True. But what you can do is share only relevant content with different customer segments. Let’s look at how to do that:

  • Personalized discounts and promotions: To make your eCommerce membership customers feel special, keep track of their special days such as birthdays and anniversaries, and offer them a discount code or deals on these days. Another way to offer personalized discounts is to create offers on products in their wishlists or shopping carts.
  • Exclusive content: A brand is only as good as its content. Content is one of the aspects that attracts and retains customers. And when it comes to your Shopify membership program, there’s a lot more you can do to leverage content. For instance, provide members access to exclusive content such as articles, videos, webinars, etc.

Source

Dynamic website content

Use your website to create personalized experiences by way of creating dynamic pages. This means different customer segments get to see a different version of your website. Here’s how to do it:

  • Personalized homepage: Dynamic personalized homepage means the content on your homepage is tailored to individual customers, and is not static and the same for all customers. For instance, some ways to personalize homepage content is to show product comparisons based on customers’ browsing history, show products based on the member’s delivery zip code, show a discount code pop up to new members, etc.
  • Personalized search results: Another way you can create dynamic content for your eCommerce membership customers’ experience is by personalizing search results. When customers search for a product on your website, show them a selection of tailored products based on their likes, interests, past purchases, and preference.

Tailored communication

Factors such as how you communicate with your customers, at what time, and on which channel, play a key role in customer experience. Try these personalized communication tactics:

  • Segmented email campaigns: Another eCommerce personalization technique that’s effective is sending personalized emails. 72% of consumers say they only reply to messages that are aimed directly at them. So, what can you do to personalize emails? Start with segmenting customers into different categories. Create email drip campaigns for each segment to drive them through their respective funnels. Add a personal touch, and share the right message, at the right time.
  • Customized push notifications: Another channel to apply personalization tactics to is push notifications or pop up messages that customers can click. Send personalized messages based on your members’ recent activities and preferences. Share relevant offers and discounts to make the message enticing.

Personalized loyalty programs

Loyalty programs help build a personal and stronger connection with customers, which can be further personalized by applying these strategies:

  • Custom rewards: Consider customized rewards for your Shopify membership personalization. Understand customers’ preferences and interests, and offer rewards that matter to members on a personal level. Bring in diversity when you offer custom rewards, meaning, different types of rewards – experiential, monetary, points, gifts, events, etc. Another aspect of eCommerce personalization through rewards is the flexibility to redeem rewards. Allow members to choose when and how to use their rewards.
  • Tiered memberships: One of the best methods to personalize loyalty programs for your eCommerce memberships is to create tiered membership programs. In tiered plans, members belong to different tiers and enjoy specific perks and benefits of that tier. Rewards can be personalized to members’ engagement levels, activities, and preferences. Exclusivity adds to the personalization experience of customers.

Personalized customer support

Think beyond the standard customer support experience, make customers’ interaction with your brand meaningful, and add value to customers when they reach out to you. Here’s how:

  • AI-powered chatbots: Offering personalized customer support goes beyond simply addressing customers by their first name. Instead, it’s all about providing personalized solutions to unique problems at the individual level. 80% of customers who receive valuable service tend to repurchase from the same brand. Utilize the power of AI to understand members’ past data and offer real-time AI-powered responses via chats. Customers who receive personalized and timely resolutions tend to be more trustworthy of brands and loyal.
  • Dedicated support: Imagine having to share your query multiple times every time you reach out to customer support. Your Shopify membership program customers are special and deserve premium treatment. Consider offering them dedicated support —personal, one-on-one, human-to-human customer support. Moreover, ensure omnichannel customer support. This will not only enhance their membership personalization experience, but also boost their loyalty towards your brand.

Also read: How To Measure The Success Of Your Ecommerce Membership Program

Data-driven personalization

In today’s complex eCommerce membership world, data is the aspect that can help you gain a deeper understanding of customers to offer tailored experiences. Here’s how to go about it:

  • Behavioral analytics: Your Shopify memberships program can give you data about customers’ behavior, activities, interests, and motivations. Ensure you continuously collect this data, analyze it, and expand your understanding of your customers. Use Shopify membership apps and tools that enable you to collect and analyze data in real time.
  • Feedback integration: Another way to enhance eCommerce personalization is to involve customers at a deeper level. For instance, ask them for feedback to improve your membership model. This way, you can track their evolving needs and preferences, and stay abreast with membership market trends.

Personalized eCommerce membership renewal offers

How you ask members to renew their eCommerce membership plans can make or break the deal. That’s why you need to personalize this critical activity. Do this:

  • Customized renewal incentives: Keep your members at the center when crafting incentives. Make membership renewal incentives personalized and relevant to members. Ensure it’s more than just transactional discounts. Offer them exclusive products, additional perks, and something new to keep them interested in your program.
  • Reminders and updates: When you send reminders and regular updates to your eCommerce membership customers, send them personalized messages. Add in incentives and highlight features that are more relevant to your members.

Also read: Understanding Value-Adds That Would Make Your Ecommerce Membership Worth It

Community building

Today, eCommerce brands are all about their communities. However, your community should exist around helping your customers and facilitating connections between them. Here’s what you can do:

  • Personalized community engagement: Create online and offline communities, spaces for your eCommerce membership customers to engage, meet, and discuss topics of their interest. For example, each tier of your membership program can be an exclusive community.
  • Exclusive events: Host online and offline events, webinars, and engagement opportunities that cater to the interests of different segments of your members. For instance, these could be a workshop or learning experience related to your products or something completely non-related, for instance, volunteering for a social cause.
