items.html:
Learn how to create a personal care subscription model for your Shopify store.

Have you ever wondered why some subscription businesses thrive and others fail miserably?

Subscription businesses grow and thrive based on the value you offer to customers. Value-addition boosts customer brand loyalty, and profits.

This is why if you’re in the personal care retail business, you must not ignore a personal care subscription model for your Shopify store.

There are hundreds of personal care brands on Shopify, including skin care, hair care, oral care, beauty, and cosmetics.

And with so much competition in this industry, you have to ensure you’re doing subscriptions the right way!

In this blog, you’ll learn how to set up eCommerce subscriptions for personal care products for success.

What are personal care eCommerce subscriptions?

A personal care eCommerce subscription is a model through which customers can buy products on a recurring basis. Products are delivered to customers at predefined intervals, and customers pay fees based on the type of subscription model. Personal care products can be segmented into a few broad categories, such as skincare, hair care, cosmetics and makeup, and oral care.

Consider these figures from the industry:

  • The beauty subscription market has projected a 26.6% CAGR from 2023 to 2033
  • Currently, the beauty subscription market is valued at $964.1 million
  • The number of users in the personal care market is expected to reach 1.52 billion by 2027
  • More than 50% of consumers subscribe to subscriptions

Here is a graph that shows revenue projection in the personal care market:

Source

Types of subscriptions for personal care

There are different types of subscription models. eCommerce brands tend to choose the type of model based on the products, customer preferences, and pricing. Let’s look at some of the most common types of subscription models used for personal care products.

Curated subscription box

A curated subscription box model functions on the principle of surprise. Customers get different products in each delivery box. Curated subscriptions are suitable for personal care products such as beauty and makeup. This model provides a better opportunity to introduce new products and samples to customers.

Benefits:

  • You can send personalized products based on customer preferences
  • Easily introduce new products in delivery boxes
  • Gather customer reviews and feedback for new products
  • Add new products frequently to keep customers interested and engaged

Example:

Customized subscription box

In the customized subscription box model, customers can choose the products they want. Some customized boxes also offer flexibility, allowing customers to change, add or remove products from the boxes. This is a popular type of subscription used by personal care brands on Shopify.

Benefits:

  • Increased customer satisfaction as a result of the ability to select preferred products
  • Boost the lifetime value of each customer
  • Provide customers with freedom and flexibility

Replenishment subscription model

Personal care products such as body care lotions, soaps, shampoo, conditioner, etc., must be replenished occasionally. Replenishment subscription models automatically send refills on the scheduled date or when customers notify brands about it.

Benefits

  • Gives personal care brands a competitive advantage by offering convenience to customers
  • Generate a steady stream of income
  • As demand is predictable, it makes inventory management easier
  • Get subscribers to sample new products easily

Example:

Benefits of personal care subscription models?

Ecommerce subscriptions for personal care products have many benefits for customers and brands. We’ve listed some below:

Convenience

Subscriptions make it easy and convenient for customers to get their required products delivered to their doorstep at specific intervals. Personal care products are recurring purchases. In addition, people prefer to stick to the same products, so getting a subscription works better than placing the same orders repeatedly.

Upselling and cross-selling

It is easier for personal care brands on Shopify to know their subscribers’ preferences as the engagement is typically for long periods. Therefore, it is possible to upsell and cross-sell. You could use data to know which products to recommend to customers.

Customers can try new sampler products

There is immense competition in the beauty and personal care industry. Personal care subscription boxes make it easy to introduce new products to long-term customers. For example, you can send surprise samplers in the deliveries or offer discounts on them. You could request product reviews and offer more discounts.

How to set up a personal care eCommerce subscription model for your Shopify store?

Follow this step-by-step guide to set up your personal care subscription box. Apart from the following steps, there are many more aspects that you will have to factor in. However, these are the building blocks that will get you started.

Step 1: Choose the type of subscription model

The first step to setting up your personal care subscription model is to choose a suitable subscription model type. Here are some factors you must consider when selecting the type of subscription:

  • Consider your customers’ preferences. If you’re launching a new subscription model, you could conduct a survey with your existing customers
  • Identify which type of subscription model would work best for your products
  • If you already have a subscription model running and want to change it, identify the aspects that are working well. Then double down on what’s working and change the elements that aren’t. This will help you create your unique subscription model

Step 2: Identify your products

Every vertical within the personal care industry is sizable. Therefore, focusing on a smaller selection of products is crucial when starting ecommerce subscriptions for personal care products.

There are many benefits of narrowing down and identifying products. For example, it helps you manage the inventory better.

In addition, you must also identify ‘star products’ — items that are fast-selling, popular, and generate considerable revenue for you. Additionally, you can roll out your subscription services and products gradually. Meaning keep adding new products slowly and steadily.

Here are a few cues for choosing the ideal products for your subscription business:

  • Ask customers to take a survey and list their preferred products
  • Determine your star products—the best-selling products—based on past data
  • Add new products or discontinue existing ones based on sales and customer feedback

Step 3: Determine the delivery frequency

Subscription deliveries can be made daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, etc., depending on your goods/services. You must choose the delivery frequencies when setting up your personal care subscription model.

Most personal care products last a few months, for example, if it’s cosmetics, skin care products, etc. Hence, quarterly or half-yearly deliveries would be more suitable.

However, the delivery duration would also depend on the type of subscription model. For example, you would send surprise items if it is a curated box subscription for makeup. In this case, the delivery frequency could also be monthly, bi-monthly, etc., as people use new makeup products regularly.

Although you may choose the delivery frequency options yourself, asking your customers what they prefer is a good idea. Conversely, you could have many delivery options when you first launch your subscription business and make adjustments based on what’s more in demand.

Another strategy is to make it straightforward by only providing two or three delivery options, then add more later to serve your customers better.

Step 4: Know your subscription value proposition

The market for personal care products is flooded with subscription options. And so, you must ensure your subscription model stands out if you want to flourish in the market. At this point, introduce your distinctive value proposition—the perks and advantages you provide.

How to create a value proposition:

  • Before you begin promoting your subscription business, define your value proposition
  • Define your objectives, goals, and brand voice
  • Recognize what your intended audience wants and expects from you
  • Examine the value, advantages, and benefits you can provide to customers

Your value proposition will depend on the following factors:

  • Financial advantages including savings and discounts
  • Community involvement, special events, etc.
  • Exclusive access to promotions, new collections, etc.
  • Feedback and reviews from customers so they feel like a part of the brand

Step 5: Bring in flexibility and freedom

At times customers may want to alter their deliveries. For instance, when traveling or, they may want to take a break from the subscription, or just change a few products in their subscription box.

You can improve personal care subscription box experiences by being flexible. Flexibility can be added throughout the customer experience. Let’s look at some ways to do so:

  • Give customers the option to select the plan they desire and make it simple for them to change their plan
  • Allow customers to add or remove the products and services
  • Make it simple for customers to reach customer service
  • Give customers the freedom to choose their preferred communication channel
  • Make it simple to cancel subscription

Step 6: Determine pricing for your subscriptions

One of the critical factors for the success or failure of subscriptions of personal care brands on Shopify is the pricing. And it takes work to get your subscription pricing strategy right. For example, you might set a low price only to acquire customers, but it could result in losses in the long run.

Your products, services, and business objectives will determine your fees and pricing. For example,

  • Fixed cost: fixed cost pricing is a simple pricing strategy where prices remain constant
  • Tier-based pricing: varying costs for various customers. The tier-based pricing structure performs well when you have a wide range of customers
  • Variable cost: determined by the products and delivery components. Prices of some personal care products may vary depending on factors including availability, season, freshness, expiration dates, etc. The variable pricing strategy works effectively for personal care products. For instance, customers can be charged more when they add additional items

Some factors to consider when pricing your subscription:

  • Consider your competitors’ pricing structure and see how you could beat it
  • Work out your costs and add a profit to it
  • Change your pricing structure frequently to reach pricing that works for you

Step 7: Set up dunning management

Once you figure out the pricing strategy for your personal care subscription model, it’s time to set up dunning management.

But what is dunning management: When a customer’s payment is declined for whatever reason, including expired cards, card decline, payment failure, etc., dunning helps send messages and instructions to customers to take the appropriate action.

Dunning management helps generate more income, save time, and experience less churn. You require an efficient subscription app that includes dunning management features, for example, Appstle Subscription and Loyalty app.

Step 8: Figure out the shipping and delivery requirements

You will need competent shipping partners to manage your personal care subscription model well. Shipping and delivery are crucial elements of subscription businesses. Because no matter how good your products are, your shipping and delivery need to be excellent to ensure good customer experience.

Take into account the following aspects when selecting a shipping carrier partner:

  • Proper handling and product safety
  • Accountability and prompt delivery
  • Company standing and dependability
  • Location and coverage specialization
  • Technological prowess. For example, do they use apps and can their app integrate into your subscription app
  • Pricing
  • Their capacity to scale as your business grows

Step 9: Set up automated communication

Personal care brands on Shopify with subscriptions aim for long-term customer relationships. Proper communication is a crucial component for retaining customers. Customers expect brands to inform them about their orders, deliveries, new product introductions, etc. To ace communication, you require a subscription app that has automation features.

And these are some of the messages you could automate:

  • Automate messages about order status
  • Install an automated dunning management system
  • Reminders for payments
  • Message about delivery time and changes
  • Thank-you messages

Step 10: Create a landing page for your personal care subscription model

Landing pages help bring traffic to your website and share information with customers. For example, say you have social media posts in which you have added a link to your landing page. Through the link, you can drive customers to the landing page and provide useful information about your personal care subscription.

Include the following elements on your landing page to increase conversions:

  • Information about subscription plans
  • Content that helps consumers in deciding whether to subscribe or not
  • CTA buttons to drive actions
  • Create different sections that gather data, such as geography, demographics, etc.

Step 11: Create a marketing plan for your personal care subscription box

You’ll need to create a marketing strategy to attract new subscribers and retain the current ones if you want to run a profitable subscription business. Include the following elements in your plan for personal care subscription marketing.

  • Offer incentives to new customers, such as offers and discounts
  • Create a rewards or loyalty programme and combine it with the subscription model
  • Create campaigns using a variety of platforms, including social media, SMS, and push notifications
  • Share user-generated content on various platforms, such as social media
  • Collaborate with micro and macro influencers in the personal care industry
  • Run a referral campaign for your current customers
  • Plan offline gatherings exclusively for your subscribers
  • Monitor and optimize your marketing plan

Get started with your personal care subscription model

With the industry growing, you must ensure your personal care subscription model is set up for growth and can withstand the hurdles that may come along the way as you scale. It is essential to have a Shopify subscription app that provides the required features and scalability capacities.

Merely setting up a good subscription model is not enough. It has to be constantly monitored and optimized. Moreover, you must be able to add new features as and when required. To ensure your Shopify subscription model has all these features, explore Appstle Subscriptions and Loyalty app.

items.excerpt: The e-commerce subscription industry has experienced remarkable growth in recent years, with the global subscription box market, including mystery boxes, reaching a staggering value of USD of USD 26.9 billion in 2022. As the world of e-commerce evolves and expands, subscription boxes have emerged as an exciting trend, captivating the curiosity of consumers worldwide. These…
items.html:
The e-commerce subscription industry has experienced remarkable growth in recent years, with the global subscription box market, including mystery boxes, reaching a staggering value of USD of USD 26.9 billion in 2022.

As the world of e-commerce evolves and expands, subscription boxes have emerged as an exciting trend, captivating the curiosity of consumers worldwide. These carefully curated packages of surprise goodies have taken the industry by storm, offering an unparalleled and thrilling shopping experience.

Among the diverse array of subscription box models, one trend has particularly caught our attention—the mystery box subscription model. In this blog, we will delve into the world of mystery box subscriptions, uncovering the reasons behind their popularity, exploring different types available, and sharing tips on how to make the most out of this captivating retail phenomenon.

What are Mystery boxes?

A mystery box is a curated package filled with undisclosed items, typically centered around a specific theme or interest and designed to provide an element of surprise and anticipation for the recipient. The contents of a mystery box are often kept secret until they are opened, adding an exciting and suspenseful element to the unboxing experience.

Today, the world of mystery boxes has evolved to cater to a wide range of interests and passions. Whether you’re a fashion enthusiast, a beauty aficionado, a gaming fanatic, or a connoisseur of gourmet treats, there’s a mystery box subscription tailored to your preferences, making it an exhilarating way to discover new products and experiences. The exponential rise of social media and the widespread phenomenon of unboxing videos have further fueled the intrigue surrounding mystery boxes, amplifying the sense of excitement and sparking curiosity among consumers.

How do mystery boxes work?

Mystery boxes operate on a simple yet very functional concept – offering a unique shopping experience for customers. Here’s a breakdown of how mystery boxes work:

1. Selection and Curation

Businesses curate a selection of products specifically chosen to be included in the mystery box. These products are typically centered around a specific theme or interest, ensuring variety and appeal to the target audience. The curated themes can span various categories, such as beauty, fashion, gaming, food, or even a mix of different product categories.

2. Surprise and Anticipation

The real magic of mystery boxes lies in the element of surprise and anticipation they offer. Customers purchase a mystery box without knowing the exact contents inside, creating an exciting experience. The undisclosed nature of the items generates a sense of adventure, keeping customers engaged and eager to receive their surprise package.

3. Unboxing Experience

The joy of unboxing is a crucial aspect of the mystery box experience. Once the mystery box is delivered, customers get to unveil the hidden contents and enjoy the process of opening their surprise package. As the box is opened, a range of carefully selected products is revealed, adding to the excitement. Businesses can enhance the unboxing experience through thoughtful packaging, personalized messages, and even additional surprises within the box.

4. Value and Exclusivity

Mystery boxes often provide customers with a sense of value. The combined worth of the items in the box typically exceeds the purchase price, creating a feeling of getting more for their money. Furthermore, including exclusive or limited-edition items in the box enhances the perceived value and adds an element of exclusivity for customers. The surprise element and the potential for receiving high-value items create a unique selling proposition for mystery boxes.

By offering unique and engaging experiences, mystery boxes have gained popularity as an effective marketing and sales strategy, especially in the e-commerce industry.

How do mystery boxes help brands?

The mystery box subscription model holds immense potential for brands, providing a gateway to enhance visibility, engage customers, and fuel business growth. Let’s explore how brands harness the power of mystery boxes in the dynamic landscape of e-commerce:

1. Increased ‘Organic’ Brand Visibility

Embracing the mystery box trend can spark a wildfire of buzz, propelling brand visibility to new heights. Customers eagerly share their unboxing experiences on social media platforms, generating valuable user-generated content that showcases the brand and its products to a wider audience. This organic exposure amplifies brand recognition and establishes a vibrant online presence.

2. Customer Engagement

Mystery boxes ignite a spark of anticipation and excitement, compelling customers to actively engage with the brand. The allure of the unknown and the thrill of unboxing create a powerful emotional connection, fostering a deeper level of customer engagement and loyalty.

3. Product Exposure and Cross-Promotion

Brands leverage mystery boxes as a strategic tool to introduce new or lesser-known products to customers. By carefully selecting items that align with the brand’s ethos and incorporating them into the mystery box, brands can showcase the breadth and depth of their product offerings, driving increased exposure and enticing customers to explore beyond their usual choices.

4. Data Collection and Insights

Mystery boxes offer a treasure trove of data for brands. By monitoring customer preferences, feedback, and purchase behavior related to mystery box offerings, brands gain invaluable insights into consumer preferences and trends. This data-driven approach enables brands to fine-tune their customization efforts, target specific customer segments more effectively, and optimize future marketing endeavors.

5. Brand Differentiation

The element of surprise and the curated experience of mystery boxes create a lasting impression in customers’ minds. By delivering a distinctive and memorable brand encounter, brands differentiate themselves from competitors and carve out a unique position in the market. The allure of mystery boxes becomes synonymous with the brand, leaving an indelible mark on customers’ perceptions.

5 Brands that have redefined the eCommerce game with their mystery box subscription models

Many e-commerce businesses have re-pivoted their sales and growth strategy by introducing mystery boxes; some have done a credibly good job at it. Here are the five mystery box subscriptions we love:

1. The Munch Bag Collections Mystery Box

Munch Bag calls itself the one-stop shop for goodies from across the world. Their mystery boxes are a handpicked collection of Internationally popular snacks ranging from Oreos, Cheetos, and Pringles to M&Ms and Nutella. People seem to love the fact that Munch Bag chooses exclusively for you and includes new exciting products that aren’t even listed yet to give them an exclusive first taste!

2. The Meesho.com Mystery Box

Particularly designed to appeal to women, this mystery box by Meesho has a collection of carefully selected makeup goodies. Right from makeup brushes to sponges and eyelash curlers, this box contains makeup tools that are handy for any woman and are available to them as a collection with major price savings.

3. The Knitroot Mystery Box (3-pack baby onesies)

Targeted at parents, this mystery box by The Knitroot contains a collection of three onesies at a much discounted overall price. While the designs are chosen by their team, customers can customize the onesies to have various initials like ‘mom,’ ‘dad,’ ‘aunt,’ etc, and also choose the age of their kids to ensure a snug fit.

4. The Craighill Mystery Box

Craighill, a trailblazer in the world of mystery box subscriptions, has captivated consumers with their innovative approach. Renowned for curating a collection of funky and functional items, Craighill’s mystery boxes are a treasure trove of daily utility products. With their Standard Mystery Box featuring at least three items valued at $175, including a standout piece worth $65, and a larger mystery box showcasing a remarkable value item worth $98, Craighill has redefined the game by offering unique and delightful surprises to their customers.

5. HEAT Mystery Box

Catering to the ever-growing Gen-Z audience, HEAT has captured the hearts of fashion enthusiasts with their highly sought-after mystery boxes. Renowned brands such as Alexander McQueen, Off-White, JW Anderson, Maison Kitsune, Maisie Wilen, Nanushka, and MMissoni have eagerly contributed their coveted products to these enigmatic packages.

Why does the mystery box subscription model work?

The mystery box subscription model works because it delivers the desired “aha” moment, satisfies consumers’ quest for unique experiences, fosters a sense of discovery and surprise, and builds customer engagement and loyalty. By capitalizing on these factors, brands can leverage the appeal of mystery boxes to stand out in a competitive market and create long-lasting relationships with their customers. Here is why the model works so well:

1. Delivers the “Aha” Moment

Studies indicate that approximately 62% of consumers actively seek surprises, and mystery boxes provide that exhilarating experience through the anticipation and reveal of undisclosed products. The element of surprise triggers a positive emotional response, creating a memorable moment that customers enjoy.

2. Focus on Experiences Over Discounts

In today’s saturated market, consumers are no longer solely motivated by discounts. They crave unique and memorable experiences that go beyond just a price reduction. Mystery boxes fulfill this desire by offering curated selections of products, allowing customers to discover new and exciting items. The thrill of uncovering hidden treasures adds a sense of adventure to the shopping experience.

3. Drives a Sense of Discovery and Surprise

By removing the burden of choice and introducing an element of surprise, mystery boxes cultivate a sense of discovery, allowing customers to explore new brands and products they may not have encountered otherwise.

4. Builds a Sense of Connection

The mystery box subscription model actively engages customers from the moment of anticipation to the unboxing experience. Customers often share their unboxing experiences on social media, fostering a sense of community and deepening their connection to the brand.

How to plan your mystery box subscription model?

Planning your mystery box subscription model involves careful consideration of various factors. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you navigate the process:

1. Identify Your Target Audience

First and foremost, clearly define your target audience based on demographics, interests, and purchasing behavior. Understanding your audience will help you curate products that resonate with their preferences and increase the chances of customer satisfaction.

2. Identify Product Preferences

Even though the contents of your mystery box are a surprise, it is crucial to research and identify the types of products your target audience is likely to enjoy. Conduct surveys, analyze market trends, and gather feedback to ensure the products you include align with their tastes.

3. Set Value Options

Offer customers the flexibility to choose the value of the mystery box they want to purchase. Provide different price tiers or subscription levels that cater to various budget preferences, allowing customers to select the option that best suits their needs.

4. Create Engaging Packaging

Design visually appealing and enticing packaging that adds to the excitement of unboxing. Consider incorporating branding elements and personalized touches to create a memorable unboxing experience for your customers. The packaging should reflect the theme or concept of your mystery box and enhance the overall customer experience.

5. Set Buying Frequency Options

Give consumers the option to choose how frequently they want to receive the mystery box. Offer different subscription plans, such as monthly, quarterly, or seasonal, allowing customers to select the frequency that suits their preferences and budget. This flexibility ensures that your subscription model accommodates a wide range of customer preferences.

6. Find a Reliable Logistics Partner

Partner with a reputable logistics provider to ensure timely and efficient delivery of the mystery boxes. Reliable shipping and tracking processes are crucial to maintain customer satisfaction and keep the excitement intact. A reliable logistics partner will help you deliver the mystery boxes in a timely manner, ensuring a positive customer experience.

By following these steps, you will be able to effectively plan your mystery box subscription model, ensuring that it aligns with your target audience’s preferences, provides value options, creates an engaging unboxing experience, and delivers a seamless customer experience from start to finish.

Ready to roll but don’t know what to do next?

Mystery boxes have gained popularity for their ability to deliver the sought-after “AHA” moment to consumers. However, creating a successful mystery box subscription model requires careful planning and execution. From identifying the target audience and their preferences to designing engaging packaging and ensuring timely delivery, each step plays a vital role in delivering a memorable customer experience.

items.html:
Choosing the ideal discount app for your Shopify store might be difficult with so many alternatives available. To assist you in making a wise choice and growing your Shopify store, we’ve put together a list of the 19 best discount apps for Shopify.

These apps provide everything you need to incentivize your customers and increase profits, from automatic discounts to product bundles, BOGO offers, volume discounts, stackable discounts, wholesale offers, upsell offers, post-purchase offers, cart discounts, tiered pricing, and creating flash sale opportunities.

Let’s take a closer look at these best apps for Shopify…

How to Choose the Best Discount App for Your Shopify Store

As a Shopify store owner, it’s important to find ways to attract customers and increase sales. One way to do this is by offering discounts and promotions. However, manually managing discounts can be time-consuming and difficult to keep track of. This is where discount apps come in handy.

Discount apps are software programs that allow you to create and manage discounts, promotions, and deals on your Shopify store. These apps can help you attract more customers, increase sales, and grow your business. However, with so many apps available, how do you choose the best one for your Shopify store?

Here are some tips to help you choose the best discount app for your Shopify store:

  • Firstly, make sure you choose an app with seamless integration into Shopify. This will save you time in setup and ensure that the theme and design of your store are cohesive.
  • Secondly, be sure to select an app that offers features specific to your needs; for instance, if you’re offering tiered discounts, look for an app that can accommodate this feature easily.
  • Then, read reviews from other store owners who have used the same app; this will provide valuable insight into how well the discount works and whether it’s worth the money or not.
  • On top of these considerations, make sure that the customer support is sufficient should any issues arise; be aware of what kind (email/phone/live chat) is available before committing to a purchase.
  • Finally, make sure the balance between cost and benefits aligns with what you need out of the discount app before making a purchase decision.

Advantages of Using Discount Apps for Your Shopify Store

The goal of an online store owner is to maximize income while reducing costs. Using Shopify for your store is one approach to doing this. With the help of these discount apps, you can provide discounts and promotions to your clients, enticing them to buy from you and increasing your sales.

Some benefits of integrating discount apps into your Shopify store:

  1. Improved Customer Retention: They can aid in cultivating customer loyalty by offering incentives and rewards for repeat business.
  2. Increased Sales: By leveraging discounts and promotions, you can spur sales and revenue growth for your Shopify store.
  3. Enhanced Customer Interaction: They facilitate the creation of interactive campaigns and personalized offers, bolstering customer engagement and elevating brand awareness.
  4. Competitive Edge: Through the implementation of discount apps, your Shopify store can distinguish itself from the competition by delivering promotions and deals that set it apart.
  5. Economical Marketing: They represent a budget-friendly marketing solution, helping to attract new customers and retain existing ones without incurring costly advertising expenses.

Main Features:

One of the standout features of AIOD is its ability to provide valuable insights into the performance of your discounts. This helps merchants make data-driven decisions and adjust their promotions for maximum impact.

In all, AIOD is an incredibly useful tool for merchants that enables them to easily provide discounted pricing and reach a wider group of customers. AIOD takes away the need to share discount codes, as it has automated processes for applying those discounts. The app makes it easier for businesses to manage their discount offers without putting extra effort into the process, so they can focus on other aspects of running their business.

items.html:
Learn All About Setting Up A Food And Beverage Subscription Model

Food and beverage is one of the most popular in subscription business models. As they are fast-consumption and recurring purchase products, food and beverage bring high regular revenue.

With high growth potential, it’s no surprise more food and beverage businesses want to join the subscription model wave. But is it that easy to start a subscription model?

In this blog, we tell you how to set up your Shopify food subscription business model for success.

What is a food and beverage subscription business?

A food and beverage subscription business is a recurring revenue model in which customers sign up, pay a fee and receive products and services at regular periods. There are different types of subscription models. Once signed up, customers don’t need to place orders every time; rather, they receive their products and services on their chosen dates.

Some examples of food and beverage subscription models using Appstle Subscription and Loyalty app.

Ortaliza

Lisa’s Popcorn

The benefits of food and beverage subscriptions

While all kinds of subscription models provide the basic benefits of convenience (for customers) and predictability and recurring revenue (for eCommerce businesses), subscriptions in the food market have many more advantages.

Recurring revenue

Subscription business models bring recurring revenue and hence, brands can predict the revenue month after month. Recurring revenue is also more stable and helps businesses plan their finances better. Recurring revenue can help speed up business growth. It helps increase customer lifetime value (CLV).

Better customer engagement

Subscription models are based on long-term relationships between brands and customers, and hence, this model provides many opportunities to engage customers. For example, you can:

  • Send updates and notifications about deliveries
  • Give freebies, new product testers, etc.
  • Offer more personalized customer support
  • Regularly collect feedback
  • Offer exclusive discounts

Get customers to try new products

Getting customers to try a new product or service is much easier via subscriptions. When customers sign up for subscriptions, they enter a long-term relationship. This form of association builds trust faster. Besides, subscribers already like your brand and products. And so, they’ll be more open to trying your new products.

Do this:

  • Slip new products into the regular deliveries as freebies
  • Offer discounts on new products and services

Improve customer lifetime value

The longer customers engage and transact with your brand, the better the chances to boost sales and improve customer lifetime value. For example, you can encourage customers to upgrade their subscription plan to a higher level. Moreover, if you offer a good experience, customers will renew their subscription plans year after year. This way, you can also ensure higher customer loyalty.

How to set up a food and beverage subscription business model?

If you’re looking to start your food and beverage subscription business, we’ve made it easy for you. Follow the below steps to set up your food and beverage subscription business model.

Step #1 Know the different types of subscription models

There are many types of subscription models, but which one should you choose for your food and beverage business? To determine that, you’ll first need to understand the different types and how they work.

Replenishment subscription model

As the name suggests, this type of model is suitable for reordering items on a recurring basis. Food and beverage products are consumables with a limited shelf life, and hence, they get consumed fast. They need to be restocked and replenished recurrently.

The replenishment subscription model suits food and beverage products. Customers don’t have to go through the process of selecting items and placing orders every time. The replenishment subscription model helps in many ways:

  • Adds a competitive advantage to your F&B business—customers will choose your brand for the convenience
  • Creates a consistent stream of revenue
  • As the demand is predictable, it helps you manage the inventory better
  • Boosts customer retention
  • Customers get to try new food items

Build-a-box subscription model

Build-a-box subscription model allows customers to choose the products they want for every delivery. Customers may not want to buy the same food items. This type of subscription gives customers the freedom and flexibility to choose products, the quantity, delivery frequency, date, etc.

A build-a-box subscription helps:

  • Boost customer satisfaction as customers can choose their preferred products
  • Increase the customer lifetime value
  • Offer freedom and flexibility to customers

Curation subscription model

Curated box subscriptions have an element of surprise. Customers receive boxes that include curated products. For example, in a grocery curated box subscription, the box could contain a mix of vegetables and fruits. Every delivery may have different items.

Benefits of curated box subscription model:

  • Can be personalized—curate products based on individual preference
  • Introduce new products through the curated box
  • Collect feedback and reviews from customers
  • Keep customers engaged and interested by adding new products every time

Step #2 Identify your food and beverage products

Food and beverage is a vast industry, and every vertical under it, too, is huge. And hence, when you’re launching a new food subscription retail business, it’s important to narrow down your product list.

Why? So that it’s easy for you to manage your inventory and subscription business model. Moreover, you can launch your subscription plans and products in phases.

Some tips to identify the best products for your subscription business:

  • Conduct a survey, ask customers their favorite items
  • Based on past sales, identify your star items—the most-selling products
  • Add new products, discontinue products based on sales and customer feedback

Step #3 Decide subscription time frame details

Depending on the product and service, subscription deliveries can be daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, etc. You must decide the time period, when you set up your Shopify subscription model.

For example, vegetables and fruits should have more frequent deliveries, while items like sauces and butter could have less frequent deliveries.

While you could decide the time frames on your own, a good way to go about it would be to ask your customers their preference. Conversely, you could have many options when you start your subscription business and bring changes based on what’s more in demand.

Another way is to keep it simple by offering only two or three delivery times, and later introduce more options to serve your customers better.

Step #4 Identify your subscription value proposition

The food and beverage market is brimming with subscription options. To succeed in the market, you have to ensure your subscription model stands out. That’s where you must bring in your unique value proposition—the perks and benefits you offer.

Steps to set up your value proposition:

  • Define your value proposition before you start promoting your subscription business
  • Define your goals, brand voice, and mission
  • Understand what your target customers want and expect from you
  • Analyze the value, benefits, and costs that you can offer to customers

Factors that will determine your value proposition:

  • Financial benefits, for example, discounts and savings
  • Community experience, exclusive events, etc.
  • A feeling of belonging to an exclusive group
  • Exclusive access to sales, new products, etc.
  • Feedback and say in new products, etc.

Step #5 Incorporate flexibility and freedom in your subscription plans

Although food, beverage, and groceries are regular items, it’s possible that customers might want to make such changes in their subscription deliveries. For example, they might want to take a break, change products, quantity, delivery dates, etc.

With flexibility, you can make subscribers’ experience better. You can bring in flexibility across the customer journey. Let’s look at some ways to do so:

  • Allow customers to choose the plan they want
  • Allow them to change their plan with ease
  • Let them add or remove the products and services they prefer
  • Make it easy for them to contact customer care
  • Enable flexible payments
  • Allow flexibility to choose the type and form of communication customers prefer
  • Allow the freedom to cancel subscriptions easily

However, setting up flexible subscriptions is not easy. For it, you need an efficient Shopify subscriptions app with technology capability.

Step #6 Set up payment and dunning management

Your subscription payments and pricing will depend on your products, services, and business goals. There are different types of pricing formats.

  • Fixed price: a predefined fixed price. A straightforward pricing method where the pricing does not change.
  • Tier-based pricing: different prices catering to different customers. When you have a wide range of customers, the tier-based pricing format works well.
  • Variable price: based on products and items in deliveries. Food and beverage product prices may differ based on availability, season, freshness, expiry dates, etc. The variable pricing model is well suited to food and beverage items. For example, when customers add more products, they get charged more accordingly.

Once you set up the food and beverage subscription pricing, you can move to setting up dunning management.

What is dunning management? Dunning management involves sending the messages and prompts to customers to take the necessary action when their payment does not go through due to any reason; such as, expired cards, card decline, payment failure, etc.

Dunning management helps reduce churn, save time, and boost revenue of your food and beverage subscription business.

You can set up dunning management by using an efficient subscription app for Shopify.

Step #7 Choose the best shipping solutions for subscription deliveries

One of the main components of your subscription business is the shipping carrier. Because no matter how good your products are, if they do not reach customers on time or in good condition, your business is set to go downhill.

To choose a good shipping carrier partner, consider these factors:

  • Proper handling and safety of products
  • Delivery speed and accountability
  • Company reputation and reliability
  • Coverage and location
  • Specialization
  • Technology capabilities
  • Pricing
  • The ability to scale

Also read: How To Choose The Right Subscription Box Shipping Carrier

Step #8 Set up automation

Subscription businesses are designed to build strong customer relationships. And one of the key aspects of these relationships is communication. Customers expect brands to keep them informed about their orders, deliveries, new products, etc.

And that’s why Shopify food and beverage subscription businesses need the capabilities of automation.

Here’s how you can automate:

  • Install an efficient automation tool
  • Automate order status messages
  • Set up automated dunning management
  • Send automated payment reminders
  • Send automated delivery notifications
  • Thank you messages
  • Automated payment and billing notifications

Step #9 Set up a landing page

A landing page is where you can guide traffic from your content. For example, for your social media posts, promotional ads, blogs, etc. This is the page that provides helpful information to your potential customers.

To ensure your landing page converts, include these components:

  • Information about your food and beverage subscription plans
  • Content that helps customers decide whether they should sign up for the subscription plan
  • Call to action button/s
  • Separate landing pages for different customer segments
  • Segments that collect customer information, for example, demographic, location, etc.

Step #10 Put together a marketing plan

To run a successful subscription business, you’ll need to craft a marketing plan to help you acquire new customers and retain the existing ones. Here are some aspects to include in your food and beverage subscription marketing plan.

  • Incentives such as discounts and offers to first-time customers
  • Set up a loyalty or rewards program
  • Create campaigns on different channels such as email, social media, SMS, push notification
  • Run influencer marketing campaigns by collaborating with micro and macro influencers relevant to the food and beverage industry
  • Share user-generated content on different channels such as social media, etc.
  • Run refer-a-friend campaign for your existing customers
  • Organize offline events exclusively for your subscribers

Step #11 Monitor and optimize your food and beverage subscription

From onboarding customers to payment and post-purchase, there are many touchpoints in subscription businesses. And hence, it’s important to monitor each and every step in the journey.

Metrics to measure:

  • Customer acquisition rate
  • Customer retention rate
  • Average duration of customers
  • Customer churn rate
  • Customer lifetime value
  • Subscription renewal rate
  • Net promoter score
  • Monthly recurring revenue
  • Active engagement rate

Only when you measure these metrics, will you be able to identify aspects that need your intervention and optimization.

Ready to launch your eCommerce subscription business?

It’s a good time to set up a food and beverage subscription business. Subscription model has been on the rise. Food and beverage being one of the fastest growing markets. And so, there’s immense competition in the business.

Hence, it can be difficult to reach your subscription business goals. To ensure success, you have to set it up well. Follow the above steps with the help of a comprehensive Shopify subscriptions app.

Appstle Subscription and Loyalty app is designed for Shopify eCommerce subscription businesses. The app provides comprehensive features to set up and market subscription plans.

items.html:
Learn The Best Tips And Takeaways From Membership Examples Of Ecommerce Brands

There are 12 million to 24 million eCommerce sites across the globe!

Can you imagine the competition between brands? Competition paves the way for growth, for trying new marketing strategies, and putting forth consistent effort to engage customers and drive sales.

One such strategy that’s catching on like wildfire is membership models.

All kinds of businesses are experimenting with membership plans as a model to generate revenue and engage customers.

In this article, we look at 20 eCommerce membership examples that are worth a look and lessons you can learn from them to apply to your Shopify membership models.

Ecommerce membership examples with key takeaways

There are several eCommerce businesses that are experimenting with the membership business model. But let’s take a look at some eCommerce membership examples that are leading in this space:

1. Malt The Brewery

A brewery based in the UK, Malt, offers an annual brewery club membership, called The Maltsters. Members pay a fee and get a 10% discount on every order, members-only events, loyalty and rewards points, among other benefits.

Takeaway: The brand has combined the loyalty and rewards program into the benefits of the membership plan—an excellent way to boost sales and cross-promote marketing programs.

2. Coming Inflatable Slide

Coming Inflatable Slide is an inflatable slides and games brand. Its membership program offers members discounts and exclusive invitations to events for an annual fee. The fee gets offset by the amount of discounts customers receive. The brand cleverly displays three price options on every product page, including the price for members. In addition, every page also has the ‘Join Membership’ CTA button to boost sign ups.

Takeaway: The website has the CTA button to join membership on every product page, which helps boost sign-ups.

3. Lilac & Pine

Another eCommerce membership model to talk about is by Lilac & Pine. It is a creative design brand that sells designs such as door hangers, signs, boards, decoration, hangings, etc. The L&P SVG Club is the brand’s membership program that offers a limited number of members access to design bundles.

Takeaway: The L&P SVG Club membership allows a limited number of customers to join as members. This makes the membership program more exclusive and sought after.

4. Marquis Wine Club

Marquis Wine Club is a membership model that delivers wines to the doorstep. The membership is free. Members can choose monthly or quarterly plans and receive carefully selected wines, tasting notes, food pairing suggestions, discounts, exclusive access to tastings, events and seminars.

Takeaway: The brand keeps everything customer-centric for good customer experience, something that every eCommerce membership model should follow—no membership fee, easy cancellation with no cost, and provides excellent customer service.

5. Desired Landscapes

A magazine about urban experiences, spaces and places, Desired Landscape publishes a pocket-sized magazine every nine months. It also organizes walks and sells maps and guides. Desired Membership gives members 10% discount on all products and 20% discount on walks.

Takeaway: Desired Landscapes has kept its membership plan simple, resonating the brand essence. On the website, the brand has given its membership feature prominence by having the membership tab first in the navigation bar.

6. Metolius Artisan Tea

A wholesale brand for teas, Metolius Artisan Tea runs a membership plan that offers discounts, free shipping and priority fulfillment. In addition, members get to try products before the launch and share product development inputs.

Takeaway: Metolius Tea offers free shipping on wholesale orders within the country. Free shipping can be a huge benefit for businesses that can improve profits.

7. Nakunako Oy

A baby clothing rental brand, Nakunako Oy has three membership plans to choose from—monthly, tri-monthly, and semi-annually plans. Members can choose 10 second hand baby clothes in every delivery.

Takeaway: The brand provides a wide range of sizes so as babies grow they can keep increasing the sizes of the garments in the membership boxes. This motivates members to continue memberships for a longer duration.

8. Moda Confidential

Another excellent eCommerce membership example is Moda Confidential—a community-oriented platform that helps women embrace the Parisian way of life and transform shopping habits for a more sustainable life. It offers two annual membership plans. Members receive boxes of products, playbooks, online consultation, and get to be part of an exclusive community.

Takeaway: The brand has included a subscription box as a perk in the membership plan—an excellent way to cross promote different programs of the brand.

9. Rachel’s Texas Kitchen

Rachel’s Texas Kitchen is a small, home-based jam business. It’s monthly membership plan at a fee of $8 includes perks such as free shipping, 15% discount, and access to their traditional recipes.

Takeaway: The small and simple business vibe resonates in its membership plan, too—one standard membership plan with straightforward perks.

10. Fabric Bash

A brand that provides all things quilting and sewing, Fabric Bash has both an online and physical presence. The brand offers, on rent and sale, material, accessories, machines, and tools to the brand’s community of sewers and quilters. The monthly membership plan called Longarm Club offers perks such as discounts on rentals and products.

Takeaway: The brand keeps it simple and offers only one standard membership plan.

11. Maker’s Fantasy

A brand for acrylic jewelry creators, Maker’s Fantasy offers designs, jewelry stands, etc. Its membership plan called Fantasy File Club offers members exclusive design files every month, 40% discount on products that aren’t part of the membership plan, access to a private Facebook community, and access to the past month’s files.

Takeaway: The Shopify website has a page that shows a comparison of the different membership plans making it easier for members to pick the best plan.

12. Freeze Drying Cookbook

A freeze drying cooking website, Freeze Drying Cookbook offers three membership plans—monthly, semi-annually, and annually. Customers can also join the free trial one-day membership plan to get a taste and then commit for a long-term membership plan.

Takeaway: Since it’s an online cookery website, its membership plan is available to customers globally. The localized pricing feature makes it easy for customers across the world to sign up. What is more, the brand has added memberships under its products section, giving memberships the focus it deserves.

13. Innate Macros

Health and wellness brand Innate Macros offers three membership plans – Bronze, Silver, and Gold. The membership plans include training programs, recipes, check-ins and evaluation, and personalized 24/7 support.

Takeaway: The perks are personalized based on members’ goals of health, nutrition, and training. The brand further personalizes member experience by being available to them one-on-one over phone and message.

14. Meat Mekanik

The online meat store, Meat Mekanik offers one standard semi-annually membership plan for a fee. Members get discounts, free shipping, and exclusive access to monthly clearance products.

Takeaway: A simple membership plan for regular, recurring consumable items—ensures long-term members and recurring revenue.

15. Arts@302

An arts class center, Arts@302 provides multiple membership options for customers to choose from. Members get discounts on art classes, gifts, priority access to special events, newsletters, and mention on collaterals such as websites, newsletter, etc.

Takeaway: Memberships are available for individuals and family, which boosts sign-ups.

16. Remy Lane Designs

Another good example of membership eCommerce model is the children’s design brand, Remy Lane Design offers two types of membership plans—finished design membership and clipart membership. Members can sign up for monthly, quarterly or yearly memberships. The brand also offers lifetime memberships. Lifetime members get access to all the membership plans. Members get access to new designs every week and exclusive collaborations.

Takeaway: The membership plans are limited to 100 members every month. This makes it more exclusive.

17. A Stitch A Half

A Stitch A Half is a machine embroidery design brand offering Gold Membership plans. Members get to choose from a wide range of embroidery designs and download eight designs every week.

Takeaway: The membership page on the website explains every detail, making it easy for members to sign up and use the membership plan.

18. Everyday Vegan

Ecommerce memberships and subscriptions work particularly well for everyday, routine, recurring products such as groceries. That’s what Everyday Vegan has done with its VIPea Pass eCommerce membership model. Members get free deliveries, can shop online and in-store, shop retail at wholesale rates, and earn Planet Points for more savings.

Takeaway: Everyday Vegan promotes the idea of being kind to the Earth via the membership plan, which helps emotionally connect with customers.

19. Chimera Planet

A design and lifestyle brand, Chimera Planet sells digital art, accessories, gifts, and more. Its monthly Premium Membership plan allows members free downloads, gifts, discounts, welcome discount, priority support, and exclusive access.

Takeaway: The brand offers a welcome discount every year, making it attractive to members to renew their memberships year-after-year.

20. Oukside

A wellness and fitness services brand, Oukside offers its members tips and advice on dieting, targeted guides, personalized content, and more, via monthly and yearly memberships.

Takeaway: Oukside offers a 7-day free membership for customers to get a taste before they sign up for a long-term membership plan.

Key learnings from these eCommerce membership examples

Here’s a quick recap of learnings from key takeaways from the above membership business examples:

  • Combine other marketing features such as loyalty program and subscription with membership plans
  • Have ‘Join Membership’ option on every product page
  • Put a cap on the number of members to make the membership plan more exclusive
  • Keep the customer at the heart of your membership perks
  • Give a prominent spot to the membership page in the navigation bar
  • Offer free shipping to encourage customers to sign up
  • Make it worth for customers to join for long-term
  • Incorporate localization depending on the region your memberships serve
  • Keep the membership plan and perks simple for customers to understand
  • Personalize the membership plans as much as possible
  • Allow family members to use memberships and perks
  • Weave in emotional connections within the membership plans
  • Offer a free trial option

Wrap up

There are so many eCommerce membership examples and there’s so much to learn from each one. Even though there’s high competition in the membership market, there’s also opportunities to set up unique membership plans.

seo.title: Luxury Subscription Box: Does The Model Really Work?
seo.description: Does the luxury subscription box model work in upscale eCommerce? Uncover its potential with Appstle Subscription's comprehensive guide.

items.excerpt: The French design house, Hermes, has a tie subscription model. The fashion brand, Ralph Lauren, rents out clothes. Lifestyle brand, Eleven James, has a subscription model for watches. What is common between the above examples? All these are luxury brands catering to high-end customers. The subscription model in luxury eCommerce is catching up across industries—from…
items.html:
The French design house, Hermes, has a tie subscription model. The fashion brand, Ralph Lauren, rents out clothes. Lifestyle brand, Eleven James, has a subscription model for watches.

What is common between the above examples?

All these are luxury brands catering to high-end customers.

The subscription model in luxury eCommerce is catching up across industries—from cars to jewelry to fashion.

And it’s no surprise why.

Studies reveal 25% of global luxury sales are expected from eCommerce by 2025 (Statista). And with subscriptions gathering momentum, luxury brands want a slice of the cake too.

But is running a subscription model in the luxury space the same as in other industries? How does a luxury subscription model work? And how can a luxury eCommerce brand set up a subscription model?

In this blog, we deep-dive into understanding the what, why, and how of luxury subscription services.

Let’s get started!

What is a subscription model?

A subscription business model is where customers sign up/ subscribe to receive products and services on a recurring basis at pre-defined periods. Subscription models can have a subscription fee or can be free.

There are different formats of the subscription model, for example, subscription box, replenishment model, bargain subscription model, fixed price model, etc. Each of these types have specific benefits depending on the different industries.

For example, for grocery subscriptions, free deliveries would make a considerable difference to customers as the deliveries would be more frequent, and they can save on delivery charges.

However, for luxury subscriptions, a discount or a surprise product might be more valuable and enticing for customers. And so the benefits and perks of luxury subscriptions might be different.

So, what is a luxury subscription box? And how different is it from regular subscriptions? Let’s find out.

What are luxury subscription boxes?

Luxury subscription boxes are a curated set of luxe, designer, high-end goods. The contents of each luxury subscription box may differ based on the brand, type of products/services, and other factors.

In the luxury subscription business the curated box and bargain model are quite common. Apart from these, brands set up their unique subscription formats, too. Let’s understand a bit more about some of the common luxury subscription models.

Curated box subscription

A curated box subscription works on the element of surprise. Here, customers do not know exactly what product they’d receive. The products are put together to match customers’ preferences and tastes.

This type of subscription format works particularly well for the luxury eCommerce market because subscribers want to try out new and latest products. Moreover, most luxury items are related to lifestyle, fashion, and trends, which aren’t necessities but more to do with desire.

Bargain or access subscription model

Since luxury products have a significantly higher price, brands often use discounting strategies to attract customers. This discount strategy is applied via the subscribe and save subscription model.

In this type of subscription model customers subscribe to receive a special discount and a bargain deal on products. This makes it easy for luxury shoppers to sift through luxury products available at discounted prices. So, they can pay less for their luxury items and services.

The bargain subscription type works on the element of exclusivity. Customers feel good when they have access to exclusive products at discounted prices.

Pay-as-you-go subscription

Luxury customers aren’t all in a position to afford expensive luxury boxes. Similarly, brands that launch luxury subscription services, too, try to first experiment to test the waters. That’s where the pay-as-you-go subscription model comes in.

Here, customers pay only for the amount of products or services they use. They can choose which and how many luxury products/services they want in every delivery. This way, they do not have to pay extra.

Let’s peek into some of the best luxury subscription boxes to understand more.

Examples of the best luxury subscription boxes

Ipsy Glam Bag X

Ipsy Glam Bag X is a glamorous makeup subscription. Subscribers receive five products, and exclusive access to discounts, among other benefits. Subscribers can upgrade their subscription to the Icon Box, which includes eight products.

Hermes Tie Society

Another brand offering top-notch luxury subscription services is Hermes. Customers can subscribe to the Hermes Tie Society to receive a new tie every month, quarter, or two months. Subscribers get benefits such as free delivery, professional laundering, tie reshaping, repairs and access to in-person events at the Hermes store.

The Opulent Box

Another brand that has adopted the subscription model in luxury eCommerce is jewelry brand, Opulent. The Opulent Box subscription gives customers custom designer jewelry boxes delivered four times a year. Subscriptions start with a survey to understand customer preferences to provide tailored experiences and luxury surprises.

Cigar By Vices

Cigar By Vices is a cigar subscription that delivers an assorted collection of cigars every quarter. The subscription box also includes cigar accessories, a booklet about stories of cigar makers and other tools that complement the experience.

How is the luxury subscription model different from the non-luxury?

Apart from the products and prices, too, there are many ways in which luxury subscriptions differ from the non-luxury subscription market. Here are some factors that differentiate the two.

1. Niche customer base, lower sign-ups

Subscription models in industries such as food and beverage, publications, online streaming services, etc. cater to mass consumers because these products and services are a necessity for all.

But that’s not the case in the luxury subscription model. Luxury items are not needs; they are wants. And because luxury products are expensive, they cater to a small consumer segment.

A niche customer base means lower sign ups compared to other sectors such as consumer goods, online publications, etc.

2. Higher levels of personalization

Compared to subscription models in non-luxury markets, luxury subscriptions offer a higher level of personalization.

How? First, the number of customers in this segment are lesser, and hence, brands can pay more attention to each individual or every small group of customers within their client list.

And second, customers pay significant amounts for products and services and hence, they’re more demanding. They expect nothing less than VIP treatment and individual attention.

3. Higher virality

Most consumers sign up for luxury subscriptions because they want to be seen associated with the brand. Luxury subscription customers feel proud of the subscription products they use or carry. And hence, they readily spread the word amongst their social circles.

Brands can use this opportunity to motivate them to share reviews or talk about the subscriptions in return of incentives. When subscribers are impressed with their luxury subscriptions, they easily share the sentiment with more consumers.

4. Higher churn

Since the price tags attached to luxury subscription services are high, customers often expect VIP treatment and leave no room for errors. Even a small bad experience could result in the cancellation of subscriptions.

According to a study by McKinsey, 15% of consumers sign up for subscriptions. Since subscription brands are niche and cater to one type of products only, most luxury subscribers end up subscribing to more than a few subscription boxes. For example, one each for clothes, shoes, watches, etc.

In such a scenario, they may not want to continue paying for subscription services that do not meet their demands of VIP experiences. And hence, the churn rate in the luxury subscription business space is high.

Consumer psychology plays a vital role in the subscription model in luxury eCommerce. If you’re a luxury brand wondering how to set up a luxury subscription service, you must first get into the psyche of your target audience.

Luxury subscription models and its target audience: the secret sauce

Typically, luxury brands have one type of consumer—those who are willing to shell out a big amount for a significantly high priced product.

But what leads this consumer segment to do so? Here are some of the psychological factors behind luxury subscriptions and subscribers:

1. High-end products increase self-esteem

Many luxury consumers regard luxury brands and products as superior to non-luxury items. So, when they buy expensive, luxury products and services, they feel assured, proud, and confident. Buying premium products helps boost the buyers’ self-worth.

2. Provides subscribers a sense of belonging

Many luxury consumers buy premium goods in an effort to belong to a specific social group. It’s not necessary that all the customers who buy luxury subscription services have the financial capacity to afford it. They may be in debt but still choose to buy luxury subscriptions under peer pressure. Luxury brands use FOMO and urgency as strategies to entice such customers to buy their subscriptions.

3. A belief that high price equals better quality

Some luxury consumers believe that the more expensive products are, the better their quality.

  • Many customers buy luxury goods to belong to a specific social group
  • Buying luxury products gives customers a sense of accomplishment
  • Some customers believe high price equates to better quality
  • Luxury products provide a sense of uniqueness

Benefits of subscription model in luxury eCommerce

1. Predictable revenue

Revenue can be predictable, thanks to the subscription model. And this is an advantage, especially during phases of uncertainty and market slowdowns. The recurring, predictable revenue can help you plan your company finances better.

2. Better customer engagement

Customers choose subscription models for convenience and better experiences. As they get into an exclusive relationship with your brand, you can create multiple engagement opportunities to strengthen your long-term association.

3. Easy to get customers to try new products

Since customers are in an exclusive association with your brand, you can promote your newly launched products to them with greater success. For example, offer them a discount to try a new product or add the item as a surprise in the subscription luxury box.

4. Lower retention cost

Subscribers have signed up for regular purchases and hence, you won’t need to spend money on marketing campaigns to bring them back to your eCommerce store frequently. You can utilize your budgets to run loyalty campaigns for your subscribers.

5. Subscription model is more sustainable

In a subscription model, revenue is cyclical—brands lock customers into long-term models. This offers revenue guarantee to brands. Moreover, brands can improve their products and services to match their customers’ changing needs and grow their business in a much thought-through way alongside customers.

6. Stronger customer relationships

Customers choose subscription options as it provides convenience—they can get products that match their preference delivered to their doorstep without having to place orders at regular intervals. In addition, subscriptions ensure personalized experiences. Brands can scale their offerings with evolving trends and customer preferences.

How to set up a subscription model in the luxury space?

In a study, researchers emphasized on the criticality of luxury brands to keep up with the latest technological advances. Online advertising is changing at fast speed. Data utilization offers several opportunities to luxury brands to generate more sales, as well as challenges.

However, to stay ahead in the luxury market, brands need to have to pick an efficient subscription tool that enables them to evolve and scale. And that’s where Appstle Subscription And Loyalty App’s capabilities come in.
